# Standards Audit — Recommendations
**Repo:** learning-tracker @ `4018a91c` (branch `dev`) · **Yardstick:** `docs/coding-standards.md` rev 2026-07-02 · **Date:** 2026-07-03
**Method:** 125 batch finders over every tracked file (full-file reads), adversarial verification of all 1,008 raw findings (3-vote consensus on P0/P1, single+second-opinion votes on P2/P3), completeness critic, supplemental round. Deliverables: this document, `findings.json` (machine input for the Linear ticket pass), `_LEDGER.md` (per-file coverage). Voice: the chair writes plainly; the adversarial posture lives in the method, not the adjectives.

---

## 1. State of the Codebase

### What this codebase is trying to be

An offline-first, multi-profile Torah-study tracker for children: local Drift databases are the source of truth, Firestore syncs across devices, parents supervise through a PIN-gated mode, and tutors get scoped cross-account access. The development model is unusual and honest about itself: the code is built largely by AI agents in waves, and the standards document's Rule 0 — *a standard ships with its checker* — is the load-bearing idea holding that model together. Judge everything below against that ambition, because the codebase does.

The good news first, and it is genuinely good: the architecture the docs promise is mostly the architecture the code has. `flutter analyze` is clean at zero issues. The 22-check audit passes. EN/HE ARB parity holds at 1,421 keys. Firebase symbols stay confined to their sanctioned modules (Rule 3 holds everywhere but one already-baselined backlog), raw Talker is contained, the single-writer patterns (`CompletionWriter`, `StreakReducer`) are respected at every call site the audit traced, and the append-only ledger design is intact. Of 2,063 audited files, 783 cleared with no findings at all. This is not a codebase in crisis. It is a codebase whose *stated* discipline is real — and whose *enforcement machinery* has quietly rotted underneath it.

### The five systemic problems

**1. The guardrails are broken, and nobody noticed — because the guardrails are how you notice.**
This is the audit's most consequential theme. The nine custom lints enforce nothing anywhere: `dart run custom_lint` crashes outright on the analyzer-9 pin (AUD-guardrails-03), and CI runs it warn-only, so a whole tier of the enforcement stack — layering, RTL geometry, `e.toString()`-in-UI, color literals, raw `logEvent` — has silently been prose for some time. Worse: `make audit` check 15/15, the cross-feature-import gate, is *structurally incapable of firing* — its awk compares a feature name extracted from the file path against a regex match over the whole grep line, which always finds that same file path first; the comparison is self-equal by construction (AUD-guardrails-02, independently discovered by twelve finder batches). It has never caught anything, and real deep imports sailed through it (AUD-tutoring-*, AUD-notifications-*, AUD-scheduler-*). The profileId-in-PK checker silently skips the `Goals` table (AUD-guardrails-01). The custom-lint test suite runs nowhere (AUD-guardrails-17). Committed codegen is stale because the freshness gate is still pending (AUD-core-labels-03). And the error-handler installer that the logging tests pin — `AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers` — is dead code; production wires its near-duplicate twin inline in `crashlytics_bootstrap.dart`, so the tests verify a path the app never runs (AUD-core-logging-01). For a codebase whose whole development model rests on "agents conform to what fails their loop," a fence that looks solid from the house but has no wire in it is the single most dangerous thing this audit found.

**2. profileId scoping — the product's core invariant — leaks at the edges.**
Multi-profile isolation is not a style rule here; it is the difference between one child's data and their sibling's. The invariant holds in the schema for most tables, and then leaks exactly where the checker doesn't look: `LearningOrderDao` reads and deletes by `curriculumId` alone, so on any household with two profiles sharing a curriculum, one child's custom learning order is served to — and silently deleted by — the other (AUD-core-database-02, a P0 found independently by four batches). Six tables lack the FK+CASCADE that their siblings have, so a tutored-mirror wipe orphans a mirrored child's rows (AUD-core-database-01). `PointsLedger` and `RewardRedemptions` lack `UNIQUE(profileId, ulid)`, so a sync merge can double-credit a child's points (AUD-core-database-03). And `DataExportImportService.importData()` clears sixteen tables *device-wide* before importing one profile's data (AUD-settings-03). None of these are exotic: they are the same defect — scoping enforced by convention instead of by key — appearing wherever the composite-PK rule wasn't mechanically checked.

**3. Child privacy holds at the center and leaks at the seams.**
Beyond the two known, baselined gaps (analytics params, unconditional Crashlytics), the audit found the same class of defect in new places: the outbox dead-letter path ships `entityKey` — literally `profileId:sefariaRef:stage:...` — into Firebase Analytics (AUD-core-analytics-01, P0), and the transactional-email logger writes the full plaintext body, child's name included, through a redactor that only matches on key names it has been told about (AUD-core-email-01, P0). The tutor-invite Cloud Function grants access on an email match without verifying `emailVerified` or the invite token (AUD-firebase-01, P0). The pattern to internalize: PII discipline is enforced at the named choke points and assumed everywhere else — and "everywhere else" is where it fails.

**4. The sync path fails politely and silently.**
The offline-first design is correct on paper and mostly in code, but its failure branches are soft. `ProfileRepositoryImpl` swallows tutor cloud-push failures in a blanket `catch (_) {}` on the assumption that "the outbox will retry" — and for the tutored facade, it won't (AUD-profiles-02, P0). LWW ordering fields are written from the client clock, not `FieldValue.serverTimestamp()` (AUD-core-sync-13), which makes cross-device conflict resolution owner-of-the-fastest-clock. One malformed payload aborts an entire outbox drain (AUD-core-sync-*), a mid-merge crash can strand a stale LWW shadow timestamp (AUD-core-sync-*), and the account-removal path deletes local data without verifying the outbox is drained (AUD-account-01, P0) — for an offline account, that is the user's only copy. Individually these are edge cases; together they describe a sync layer whose happy path is engineered and whose unhappy paths are hoped.

**5. The test suite is wide and soft in the middle.**
TQ-8 is the largest single rule bucket in the register (102 findings): tests that assert what the mock returns, tests pinning stale hand-copied widgets, tests that grep source text instead of exercising behavior, a "regression test" for batch chunking that never calls the chunking code. Forty-seven TQ-6 findings (plus a 377-site deterministic backlog) put wall-clock and real sleeps inside the suite. The user-visible consequence is already in the register: the "Archive (keep history)" flow **wipes** the history it promises to keep, and its test didn't notice (AUD-profiles-01, P0). A suite this size that can't catch that defect is providing coverage, not confidence.

Two smaller currents run through everything: **English leaks into a bilingual app** (21 AX-2 clusters of hardcoded strings and raw `e.toString()` surfaced to Hebrew users — this app's most recurring historical defect class, still recurring), and **the documentation lies in places agents read** (the architecture doc's dependency graph names four features that don't exist and omits two that do, AUD-docs-15; a 993-line superseded standards doc still sits at the repo root contradicting the real one, AUD-docs-04; schema "v14" vs the real v32).

### What to stop doing

1. **Stop adopting rules without checkers.** The register's meta-section lists ~60 rule families with confirmed violations and pending checkers. That backlog *is* the standards debt.
2. **Stop letting agents fork canonical flows.** The profile-delete dialog forked from `deleteProfileFlow` re-introduced a fixed bug (AUD-profiles-*); duplicated `PaceCalculator`/`PinFlowMode` classes drifted (AUD orchestrator AG-4). One definition, one flow, enforced by the AG-4 script.
3. **Stop trusting green tests as evidence.** Verification evidence must exercise the production path (TQ-8); a test of dead code is worse than no test.
4. **Stop treating docs as write-once.** Doc drift misleads the next agent wave; AG-8's pairing rule needs its checker.

The verdict: sound bones, rotten fences. Fix the enforcement machinery first — everything else this audit found is exactly the kind of thing working machinery would have caught.

### core/analytics  (4 findings — 1 P0 / 0 P1 / 1 P2 / 2 P3)

#### AUD-core-analytics-01 · **P0** · CONFIRMED · Constrain AnalyticsService.logEvent to the AnalyticsEvent catalog — LogEvents-sourced calls leak profile_id and content identifiers to Firebase Analytics
- **Rule:** PV-1 · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 22 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** AnalyticsService.logEvent(String name, ...) accepts any bare string, so nothing stops a caller from importing LogEvents — documented in its own header as 'structured log event names' for AppLogger, not an analytics catalog — and piping it straight into real Firebase Analytics. Grepping every `.logEvent(` call site in lib/ shows ~15 places do exactly this, bypassing the audited 12-event AnalyticsEvent catalog and its PV-1 review entirely. At least 7 of those sites attach identifying data: outbox_processor.dart fires sync_outbox_dead_lettered with entity_key = '${profileId}:${sefariaRef}:${stageId}:${trackType}:${curriculumId}' (confirmed composition in completion_writer.dart:747) for every dead-lettered completion row — combining the per-child profile id with the exact Torah/Mishnah reference the child was studying in one string; pull_pipeline.dart fires sync_merge_router_halt with a bare profile_id; tutor_pin_service.dart fires tutor_pin_set with a bare profile_id; tutor_audit_log_writer.dart fires tutor_action_recorded with a 'target' field whose own documented shape is a resource path like 'profile/42.displayName' (line 130) — i.e. the profile id again, now attached to a description of what was changed; sync_orchestrator.dart fires sync_pull_failed and sync_listener_error with the raw exception's `.toString()`, which for Firestore permission/not-found errors routinely embeds the full document resource path (profiles/{id}/completions/{ref}). In release/profile builds analyticsServiceProvider resolves to the real FirebaseAnalyticsService (analytics_provider.dart), whose logEvent forwards `parameters` verbatim with zero redaction (firebase_analytics_service.dart:29-32) — so every one of these fires a real event to Google's servers. This is materially worse than the two baselined single-field leaks (bare sefaria_ref, bare profile_id in analytics_service.dart) because several of these sites combine per-child identity with content/action detail in one uncatalogued, unreviewed string, and remains a live COPPA/GDPR-K risk independent of the separately-baselined PV-3 consent-gating gap (fixing consent gating controls whether these fire at all, not what's inside them once a user has consented).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/analytics/analytics_service.dart:45` — “Future<void> logEvent(String name, {Map<String, Object?>? parameters});”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/logging/log_events.dart:3` — “// Typed string constants for structured log event names.”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/learning/data/completion_writer.dart:747` — “'${cmd.profileId}:${cmd.sefariaRef}:${cmd.stageId}:${cmd.trackType}:${cmd.curriculumId}';”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/outbox/outbox_processor.dart:267` — “'entity_key': row.entityKey,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/outbox/outbox_processor.dart:372` — “'entity_key': row.entityKey,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/pull_pipeline.dart:437` — “'profile_id': profileId,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/sync_orchestrator.dart:967` — “'error': e.toString(),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/sync_orchestrator.dart:1401` — “parameters: {'channel': channel, 'error': error.toString()},” _(+14 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Change AnalyticsService.logEvent's name parameter from bare String to a closed type sourced only from AnalyticsEvent (e.g. an extension type/sealed wrapper), add a Rule-0 grep/lint that fails CI on any `.logEvent(` call whose first argument isn't `AnalyticsEvent.<x>`, and triage the 7 cited sites: either drop the identifying parameter and keep these as AppLogger-only structured logs (most already have a parallel LogEvents-based AppLogger call right next to the analytics one), or promote them into AnalyticsEvent with PV-1-safe parameters (counts/enums/booleans only) and route error detail through a stable EH-5 error-code enum instead of `.toString()`.
- **Done when:** A checker (grep in make audit, or a working custom_lint rule) fails with file:line on any AnalyticsService.logEvent(...)/.logEvent( call whose event-name argument is not an AnalyticsEvent member · entity_key/profile_id/target/error-text parameters are removed, hashed, or replaced with a coarse enum at all 7 cited call sites · A regression test asserts FakeAnalyticsService-captured params for outbox_dead_lettered, merge_router_halt, pull_failed, listener_error, tutor_pin_set, and tutor_action_recorded never contain a raw profileId, sefariaRef, or exception string · docs/coding-standards.md PV-1 known-gaps list is either cleared for these sites or explicitly extended to name them
- **Labels:** privacy, coppa, analytics, P0, child-privacy · merged 3 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 4 batches · verifier corrections: TutorAuditLogWriter (tutor_audit_log_writer.dart, the 7th site, 'target'/'grant_id' leak) has no constructor call anywhere in lib/ or test/ — it is currently dead/unwired code, not reachable in production today. The find

#### AUD-core-analytics-02 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Inject an overridable clock into streakMilestoneAnalyticsObserverProvider instead of hardcoding SystemLocalDayClock
- **Rule:** TQ-6 / Feathers testability lens · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The observer instantiates `const SystemLocalDayClock()` directly rather than watching an injectable clock — the codebase already has this seam elsewhere (e.g. outbox_providers.dart reads `ref.watch(localDayClockProvider)`). Because the observer can't be handed a fixed clock in tests, the happy-path test has to anchor seeded data to real `DateTime.now()` and then poll every 20ms for up to 5 real seconds waiting for the milestone to fire, instead of asserting deterministically against a fixed instant. The test's own comment documents this was already a source of past flakiness ('silently breaks the moment the calendar advances', 'failed in isolation') — the current polling approach is less likely to fail, not deterministic, and burns up to 5 real seconds per run.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/analytics/streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart:47` — “clock: const SystemLocalDayClock(),”; `learning_tracker/test/core/analytics/streak_milestone_analytics_observer_test.dart:129` — “final todayUtc = DateTime.now().toUtc();”; `learning_tracker/test/core/analytics/streak_milestone_analytics_observer_test.dart:168` — “while (DateTime.now().isBefore(deadline) &&”
- **Fix:** Thread a LocalDayClock through the provider (watch a clock provider, mirroring outbox_providers.dart) so tests can override with a fixed clock and assert the milestone fires on an exact expected tick without polling.
- **Done when:** streak_milestone_analytics_observer_test.dart's happy-path test uses a fixed/injected clock instead of DateTime.now(), with no wall-clock polling loop · Test runtime for that test drops from a up-to-5s poll to near-instant
- **Labels:** testability, P2, flaky-test, analytics · verifier corrections: StreakStateProvider.watch() drives the wait via a Drift .watch() stream plus async restoreIfEmpty, independent of clock source. Injecting a fixed clock fixes the DateTime.now() seed-anchoring (real, valid benefit) but li

#### AUD-core-analytics-04 · **P3** · SUSPECTED · Type streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart's two catch blocks to Exception — bare Object catches swallow Error subtypes as warnings
- **Rule:** EH-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** Neither catch has an `on X` clause, so both also catch Dart Error subtypes (NoSuchMethodError, TypeError, RangeError, StateError) that signal genuine programming bugs, not recoverable runtime conditions — exactly what EH-4 says never to catch. A bug in StreakStateProvider or an unexpected state shape gets downgraded to a single logger.warning(...) call (not even error/critical) and the loop or stream quietly continues or ends — no crash, no Crashlytics report, nothing but a line in a 2000-entry ring buffer nobody reviews outside 'Send Diagnostic Logs'. This provider runs unconditionally in the app shell every session (per its own doc comment), so a regression here has zero blast-radius signal to catch it.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/analytics/streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart:74` — “} catch (e, st) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/analytics/streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart:83` — “} catch (e, st) {”
- **Fix:** Narrow both catches to `on Exception catch (e, st)` (or the specific exception types StreakStateProvider/AnalyticsService can throw) and let Error subtypes propagate to the zone's onError handler like the rest of the app.
- **Done when:** Both catch clauses in streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart use `on Exception catch` (or a named typed exception), not bare `catch (e, st)` · streak_milestone_analytics_observer_test.dart's existing R6-3 tests still pass unchanged (they throw plain Exception, not Error)
- **Labels:** error-handling, P2, analytics · verifier corrections: Ran a probe test: querying a closed Drift NativeDatabase throws StateError (e is Error==true, e is Exception==false) — the exact scenario R6-3's stream-error test triggers via db.close(). Narrowing line 83's catch to `on

### core/auth  (6 findings — 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 3 P2 / 3 P3)

#### AUD-core-auth-01 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Add a getIdToken(forceRefresh) primitive so a synced write hitting permission-denied/unauthenticated can recover
- **Rule:** AU-5 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** AU-5 requires exactly one getIdToken(true) forced refresh plus a single retry when a synced write fails with permission-denied/unauthenticated. A repo-wide grep for 'getIdToken' returns zero hits in lib/. Neither FirebaseAuthGateway/FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl nor AuthRepository/AuthRepositoryImpl — the only classes layering Rule 3 permits to touch FirebaseAuth for this feature — expose any way to force-refresh the cached ID token; the closest method, reloadCurrentUser()/User.reload(), only refreshes profile fields (displayName, emailVerified), not the JWT/claims. A stale token (e.g. after a custom-claims change) therefore has no dedicated recovery path; a failing synced write can only retry against the same stale token via the outbox's generic exponential backoff until it dead-letters, and the only user-facing fix is a full sign-out/sign-in.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/auth/firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart:47` — “if (user == null) return null;
    await user.reload();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:9` — “/// Delegates to the auth gateways in `lib/core/auth/`. Per layering rule 3,
/// this file MUST NOT import the firebase_auth SDK”
- **Fix:** Add Future<String?> getIdToken({bool forceRefresh = false}) to FirebaseAuthGateway/AuthRepository as a thin pass-through to User.getIdToken, and wire the outbox/push-pipeline's permission-denied handler to call it once with forceRefresh: true plus a single retry before falling through to the existing backoff.
- **Done when:** FirebaseAuthGateway/AuthRepository gain a getIdToken(forceRefresh: true) method with a unit test against the fake/mock gateway. · Outbox/push-pipeline regression test: inject permission-denied on first attempt, assert exactly one getIdToken(true) call plus one retry occurs before falling back to normal backoff.
- **Labels:** auth, AU-5, sync, resilience

#### AUD-core-auth-02 · **P2** · SUSPECTED · Guard FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl link/reauth methods against silent no-op on null currentUser
- **Rule:** AU-1 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [3x3] · filed P1, revised
- **Why:** If currentUser is null when these fire (expired/revoked anonymous session, or a UI race), the `?.` swallows the call and the method returns a normally-completed Future<void> — no exception, no signal that nothing happened. The one real caller (features/account/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:129-140 `linkGoogleProvider`/`linkEmailProvider`/`reauthenticateWithGoogle`) just awaits and reports success with nothing to double-check. That directly undercuts AU-1: linking must actually run against the anonymous uid so its offline data carries over; a silent no-op leaves the account anonymous while the user believes it's now permanent, and Identity Platform auto-deletes unlinked anonymous accounts after 30 days (AU-3's rationale), which can permanently orphan the child's offline learning history. Every sibling precondition check in this same file (deleteCurrentUser:172-176, updatePassword:181-186, reauthenticateWithEmail:192-199, sendEmailVerification:100-104) throws `StateError` instead of silently no-op'ing; the one genuinely-intentional no-op in the file (`updateDisplayName`) is declared as such by an explicit 'is a no-op when no user is signed in' test — these three methods have neither the guard nor a test declaring the no-op intentional, which is the tell that it's an oversight, not a design choice.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/auth/firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart:218` — “await _firebaseAuth.currentUser?.linkWithCredential(credential);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/auth/firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart:226` — “await _firebaseAuth.currentUser?.reauthenticateWithCredential(credential);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/auth/firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart:238` — “await _firebaseAuth.currentUser?.linkWithCredential(credential);”
- **Fix:** Add the same `if (user == null) throw ...` guard used elsewhere in this file before calling linkWithCredential/reauthenticateWithCredential in all three methods (ideally throwing the typed exception recommended in the companion EH-5 finding rather than another StateError). Add regression tests mirroring the existing 'throws when no user is signed in' pattern for linkWithGoogleIdToken, linkWithEmailAndPassword, and reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken.
- **Done when:** linkWithGoogleIdToken, linkWithEmailAndPassword, and reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken throw (not silently no-op) when currentUser is null. · New red-first unit tests in firebase_auth_gateway_impl_test.dart cover the null-currentUser case for all 3 methods and pass. · Existing 'links credential when signed in' tests for the same methods stay green.
- **Labels:** auth, AU-1, child-privacy, silent-failure · verifier corrections: The "one real caller ... just awaits and reports success" framing is wrong for 2 of 3 sites: linkWithGoogleIdToken/linkWithEmailAndPassword are dead code with no UI entry point in lib/ (only exercised by unit tests). The

#### AUD-core-auth-03 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Replace hardcoded English StateError messages in FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl with typed error codes
- **Rule:** EH-5 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** EH-5 requires domain/data errors to carry a stable code/enum, never a pre-formatted human sentence, because the app ships EN+Hebrew and a raw exception.message/.toString() renders untranslated and un-RTL-shaped. This StateError carries no `.code` field at all — contrast with the codebase's own established pattern for exactly this kind of condition: 4 presentation files (account_actions.dart, sign_in_controller.dart, signup_screen.dart, account_picker_screen.dart) all switch on `GoogleSignInException.code`, never `.message`. The one caller I traced for this specific StateError (sign_in_controller.dart `_extractFirebaseCode`) happens to fall back safely to a translated generic string because its `[plugin/code]` regex doesn't match a StateError's toString() — but that's incidental to that call site's defensive regex, not a guarantee, and the other 3 call sites (deleteAccount/changePassword/reauthenticateWithEmail flows in features/account) are outside this batch and unverified. The lint meant to catch a raw .toString() reaching UI (no_e_to_string_in_ui) is currently non-functional (custom_lint crashes — baselined), so nothing today would catch a future regression at those sites.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/auth/firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart:103` — “throw StateError('No authenticated user found');”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/auth/firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart:175` — “throw StateError('No authenticated user found');”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/auth/firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart:184` — “throw StateError('No authenticated user found');”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/auth/firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart:198` — “throw StateError('No authenticated user found');”
- **Fix:** Introduce a small typed exception (e.g. NotAuthenticatedException) or a stable error-code enum instead of StateError('...'); have presentation resolve display text via AppLocalizations, matching the .code-switch pattern already used for GoogleSignInException elsewhere in the codebase.
- **Done when:** No throw StateError('<english sentence>') remains in firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart; a typed exception without a baked-in human sentence is thrown instead. · Existing 'throws when no user is signed in' tests updated to assert the new exception type. · A grep/test confirms no caller of deleteAccount/changePassword/reauthenticateWithEmail/sendEmailVerification renders the exception's raw message/toString() in a widget.

#### AUD-core-auth-04 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Add inline // keepAlive: justification comments to auth_providers.dart's two singleton providers
- **Rule:** SM-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** SM-6 requires every keepAlive: true to carry an inline `// keepAlive:` justification comment, specifically because the planned [Pending] audit grep keys off that literal tag beside the annotation (docs/coding-standards.md:156). Both providers here only have an ordinary doc comment above the function ('Provides the singleton ... used app-wide'), not the tagged comment the future checker looks for — when that grep ships, these two will false-positive as unjustified even though the reasoning is already documented in prose. (The same gap recurs at other keepAlive sites repo-wide, e.g. content_index.dart, registry_provider.dart, preference_providers.dart — those are outside this batch, noted here only for the orchestrator's dedup.)
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/auth/auth_providers.dart:13` — “@Riverpod(keepAlive: true)”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/auth/auth_providers.dart:22` — “@Riverpod(keepAlive: true)”
- **Fix:** Add a one-line `// keepAlive: <reason>` comment immediately above each @Riverpod(keepAlive: true), e.g. '// keepAlive: stateless singleton facade, cheap to keep for app lifetime'.

A future change (filtering a synthetic provider id, normalizing case) has to be remembered in two places, and the two are already one accidental edit away from disagreeing about what 'linked providers' means for the same user.

            .map((info) => info.providerId)”

#### AUD-core-auth-06 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Guard the force-unwrapped credential.user in FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl.createUserWithEmailAndPassword
- **Rule:** EH-2 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Every other credential.user access in this same file tolerates a null user (signInAndGetUser:74 and signInWithEmailLink:141 both route through _toAppUserOrNull). Here the `!` will throw a raw TypeError ('Null check operator used on a null value') instead of a typed, catchable error if Firebase ever returns a credential without a user — a TypeError carries no stable code (EH-5) and isn't a deliberately-thrown, meaningful exception, so it degrades straight to an opaque crash instead of a handleable condition, inconsistent with how the rest of the file treats the identical precondition.

- **Fix:** Mirror the null-check-and-throw pattern used elsewhere in the file (or the typed exception recommended in the EH-5 finding) instead of force-unwrapping credential.user.
- **Done when:** No bare `!` on credential.user in this file. · A regression test exercises the null-user branch of createUserWithEmailAndPassword.
- **Labels:** auth, defensive-coding

#### AUD-core-content-01 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Convert HierarchySelection and AdjacentItems to @freezed instead of hand-rolled/missing equality
- **Rule:** coding-standards.md:584 — never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** coding-standards.md is explicit: 'hand-rolled equality drifts from the fields and silently breaks rebuild-skipping.' HierarchySelection is stored in `Set<HierarchySelection>` in production code (bulk_mark_screen.dart:68, hierarchy_selection_panel.dart:88) — Set.add/remove/contains rely directly on ==/hashCode. All 4 fields are covered today, but the next field added to the class (a plausible edit given it already models a 4-level hierarchy with headroom) will silently break selection dedup in the bulk-mark/lifetime-marking flows unless the two overrides are manually kept in sync. AdjacentItems has no equality at all (identity-only), so two structurally-equal instances never compare equal — currently harmless since it's only null-checked, but not an @freezed value type either.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/content/hierarchy_selection.dart:19` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>
      identical(this, other) ||”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/content/content_index.dart:9` — “class AdjacentItems {
  const AdjacentItems({this.prev, this.next});”
- **Fix:** Annotate both as @freezed (or add copyWith by hand and a comment justifying why not, matching the project's stated carve-out pattern) so equality/hashCode/copyWith stay generated and in sync with the fields.
- **Done when:** HierarchySelection and AdjacentItems are @freezed classes; all existing == /hashCode assertions in hierarchy_selection_test.dart and epic_25_schema_core_test.dart still pass unchanged. · Set<HierarchySelection> usage in bulk_mark_screen.dart and hierarchy_selection_panel.dart compiles and behaves identically.
- **Labels:** core/content, freezed, equality, hygiene

#### AUD-core-content-02 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Fix ContentTree.parent()'s off-by-one when a leaf precedes its container in source order
- **Rule:** Correctness bug (Fowler duplicated-but-inconsistent logic between pass 1 and pass 2) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Empirically verified: constructed a 4-level Bavli fixture where the leaf item ('Berakhot 2a:1') appears before its own container ('Berakhot 2a') in the input list, called ContentTree.fromCurricula(...).parent('Berakhot 2a:1'), and got 'Berakhot 2' (the grandparent/daf-level container) instead of the correct immediate parent 'Berakhot 2a'. Root cause: for a leaf, `_ancestorLevels(item)` already returns the PARENT container's own key (that's its documented purpose, and pass 1 at lines 110-121 uses it directly with no further truncation). Pass 2 treats `levels` uniformly as if it were the item's own key and applies a second `.sublist(0, length - 1)` 'walk up one level' step — which, for leaves, walks up an extra level past the true parent. Pass 1 resolves leaves correctly when their container is registered first; pass 2's fallback only fires — with the wrong answer — when a leaf is encountered before its container. ContentTree.parent() currently has zero callers in lib/ (content_hierarchy_screen.dart uses only .children()/.containerFor()), so this is not live-user-visible today, but it is a public, documented, keepAlive-cached API on the exact class whose stated purpose is 'O(1) parent/child/adjacent traversal' — the first feature that calls .parent() for breadcrumb 'up' navigation inherits a silently-wrong result whenever source ordering isn't strictly parent-before-child.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/content/content_tree.dart:138` — “final levels = item.isLeaf ? _ancestorLevels(item) : _levelsOf(item);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/content/content_tree.dart:142` — “final parentLevels = levels.sublist(0, levels.length - 1);”
- **Fix:** In pass 2's leaf branch, use `ancestorLevels` (the value already returned by _ancestorLevels) directly as the parent container key, the same way pass 1 does — do not apply an additional sublist(0, length-1) truncation for leaves.
- **Done when:** A regression test at test/core/content/content_tree_test.dart builds a curriculum with a leaf listed before its own container and asserts ContentTree.parent(leafRef) returns the immediate parent, not the grandparent. · Existing epic_25_schema_core_test.dart ContentTree assertions continue to pass.
- **Labels:** core/content, correctness-bug, confirmed-by-repro

#### AUD-core-content-03 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Hoist the child-list sort out of the per-curriculum loop in ContentTree.fromCurricula
- **Rule:** Fowler — hoist loop-invariant code · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The sort block at lines 126-129 iterates `childrenByContainerKey.values` — the map accumulated across ALL curricula processed so far — but it sits inside the outer `for (final entry in byCurriculum.entries)` loop (opens line 93, the sort closes at line 130 still inside it). For 9 curricula this re-sorts every earlier curriculum's already-sorted child lists up to 9 times each instead of once. contentTree is a keepAlive provider built synchronously (no isolate offload) the first time any screen reads it, so this redundant O(9x) work sits directly on that first-access latency, not merely a style nit.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/content/content_tree.dart:93` — “for (final entry in byCurriculum.entries) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/content/content_tree.dart:126` — “// Sort each child list by sortOrder so display is stable.
      for (final list in childrenByContainerKey.values) {”
- **Fix:** Move the sort block outside the curriculum loop (one dedent) so each child list is sorted exactly once after all curricula are indexed.
- **Done when:** The sort loop executes once, after the curriculum loop, in content_tree.dart. · Existing children()-ordering assertions in epic_25_schema_core_test.dart continue to pass.
- **Labels:** core/content, performance, startup-latency

### core/database  (16 findings — 2 P0 / 3 P1 / 3 P2 / 8 P3)

#### AUD-core-database-01 · **P0** · CONFIRMED · Add profileId FK+CASCADE to 6 tables — tutored-mirror wipe currently orphans a mirrored child's data
- **Rule:** profileId-in-PK Invariant / DB-6 (sync-able entity integrity, FK-cascade discipline) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 6 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** None of these 6 tables declare `.references(LearnerProfiles, #id, onDelete: KeyAction.cascade)` on their profileId column (every sibling table that IS correctly protected does). `ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile()` compensates by explicitly deleting from all 6 before removing the profile row — the team clearly knows about this gap. But `TutoredMirrorWipeService.wipeMirrorForGrant/wipeAllMirrors/wipeRevokedMirrors` (used on tutor grant revoke/resign, tutor sign-out, and the D18 revoke-reconcile path) does NOT replicate that compensation — it only calls `ProfileDao.deleteTutoredMirrorByGrantId`, a bare delete of the `learner_profiles` row, while its own top-of-file comment incorrectly asserts universal FK cascade covering `curriculum_tracks, etc.`. `tutored_pull_service.dart` (line 99, 'a point_configs FK violation') confirms these tables are actually populated for a live mirror. Net effect: when a tutoring relationship ends, the tutored child's mirrored curriculum_tracks/daily_plans/point_configs/profile_programs/study_day_configs rows silently persist on the tutor's device forever — a child-privacy data-retention failure that contradicts the code's own stated invariant, with no error or log to reveal it.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/tables/curriculum_tracks.dart:16` — “IntColumn get profileId => integer()();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/tables/daily_plans.dart:11` — “IntColumn get profileId => integer()();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/tables/outbox_table.dart:16` — “IntColumn get profileId => integer()();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/tables/point_configs.dart:10` — “IntColumn get profileId => integer()();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/tables/profile_programs.dart:8` — “IntColumn get profileId => integer()();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/tables/study_day_configs.dart:5` — “IntColumn get profileId => integer()();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/tutored_mirror_wipe_service.dart:12` — “the learner_profiles row cascades to all mirrored rows in completions, ... curriculum_tracks, etc. No explicit child-row deletion is needed.”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/profile_dao.dart:174` — “The FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` on every child table (completions, streak_events, learning_ledger, bookmarks, goals, etc.)” _(+1 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Either (a) add `.references(LearnerProfiles, #id, onDelete: KeyAction.cascade)` to profileId on all 6 tables (schema migration + schema export per DB-4), or (b) make `TutoredMirrorWipeService` explicitly delete from all 6 tables before removing the `learner_profiles` row, mirroring `ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile`'s existing pattern (no migration needed, lower risk, matches established precedent). Fix the false comment either way.
- **Done when:** New regression test: after wipeMirrorForGrant/wipeAllMirrors, querying curriculum_tracks/daily_plans/outbox/point_configs/profile_programs/study_day_configs WHERE profileId = <wiped id> returns 0 rows. · tutored_mirror_wipe_service.dart's header comment no longer claims universal FK cascade for tables that don't have it. · tool/schema_check.dart (or a new companion checker) flags any core/database/tables profileId column lacking a `.references(LearnerProfiles, ...)` FK, so a future new table can't silently reintroduce the gap.
- **Labels:** child-privacy, data-integrity, sync, tutoring, P0 · verifier corrections: The "rule" field's mapping is imprecise: I searched coding-standards.md in full and neither DB-6 nor the profileId-in-PK Invariant actually mentions FK cascade/onDelete behavior anywhere (grep for "cascade|onDelete|forei

#### AUD-core-database-02 · **P0** · CONFIRMED · Filter LearningOrderDao.getLearningOrderByCurriculum/deleteAllForCurriculum by profileId to stop cross-sibling data leak and silent deletion
- **Rule:** profileId-in-PK (Naming/placement/invariants) + TQ-8 (test pins wrong behavior) · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 21 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** docs/architecture.md:105 confirms UserDatabase is per-ACCOUNT (user_acc_<id>.db), holding ALL sibling profiles' rows in the same tables — profileId is the only thing separating Child A's data from Child B's. LearningOrderDao.getLearningOrderByCurriculum() and .deleteAllForCurriculum() query only by curriculumId with no profileId predicate, even though the table's own uniqueKeys and every write path (upsertLearningOrder) correctly key on (profileId, curriculumId, sefariaRef). I wrote and ran a throwaway probe test (deleted after, not committed): seeded profile 1 with a custom Mishnayos row, then exercised profile 0's LearningOrderRepositoryImpl — profile 0's getOrder() returned profile 1's row (cross-sibling read leak) and profile 0's resetToDefault() then deleted profile 1's row (cross-sibling silent data loss), both runtime-confirmed. This fires whenever two children under one account share a curriculum — a mainstream scenario for a family Torah-study app (e.g. two kids both on Mishnah Yomi). The same unscoped call also feeds BookmarkRepositoryImpl._getNextItemId (bookmark 'next item' can jump per a sibling's order) and SchedulerLearningOrderRepositoryImpl.getOrder (the scheduler can sequence a child's next task using a sibling's custom order). Worse: this batch's own learning_order_repository_impl_test.dart doesn't just fail to catch this — its 'custom order' test and its 'resetToDefault' test both seed fixture rows under profileId:1 while exercising a repo instance defaulted to profileId:0, and both pass today only because the DAO ignores profileId; a correct fix would turn these two tests red until their fixtures are corrected.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/learning_order_dao.dart:34` — “..where((t) => t.curriculumId.equals(curriculumId))”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/learning_order_dao.dart:110` — “)..where((t) => t.curriculumId.equals(curriculumId))).go();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/whole_curriculum_order/data/repositories/learning_order_repository_impl.dart:17` — “int profileId = 0,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/whole_curriculum_order/data/repositories/learning_order_repository_impl.dart:57` — “final rows = await _database.learningOrderDao.getLearningOrderByCurriculum(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/whole_curriculum_order/data/repositories/learning_order_repository_impl.dart:163` — “await _database.learningOrderDao.deleteAllForCurriculum(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/learning/data/repositories/bookmark_repository_impl.dart:234` — “final customOrder = await _database.learningOrderDao
        .getLearningOrderByCurriculum(curriculumId.storageKey);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/data/repositories/scheduler_learning_order_repository_impl.dart:16` — “final rows = await _learningOrderDao.getLearningOrderByCurriculum(”; `learning_tracker/test/features/learning_order/data/repositories/learning_order_repository_impl_test.dart:103` — “profileId: 1,
            curriculumId: 'mishnayos',” _(+13 more sites in findings.json)_

#### AUD-core-database-03 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Add UNIQUE(profileId, ulid) to PointsLedger and RewardRedemptions — sync merge can double-credit a child's points
- **Rule:** DB-6 (sync-able entity integrity) / profileId-in-PK's composite-index companion requirement · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** PointsLedger and RewardRedemptions both carry a `ulid` column documented as "cross-device id for append-only cloud sync" — the exact same purpose LearningLedger's `ulid` serves, where it is protected by a real `UNIQUE(profileId, ulid)` @TableIndex. Neither PointsLedger nor RewardRedemptions has any uniqueKeys/@TableIndex at all. PointsLedgerMerger's own comment says entries are "deduplicated on ulid via INSERT-OR-IGNORE," but points_balance_dao.dart's insertRemoteLedgerEntryIfAbsent actually does a manual SELECT-then-INSERT with no DB constraint backing it — a classic TOCTOU race. If two merge calls for the same ulid ever interleave (concurrent pulls, a retried tutored pull, a future refactor that parallelizes merges), a duplicate row lands; reDeriveBalanceFromLedger sums ALL ledger deltas, so the child's points balance silently becomes wrong — violating the table's own documented invariant that balance is "the authoritative denormalised sum of all ledger entries."
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/tables/points_balance.dart:63` — “TextColumn get ulid => text().nullable()();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/tables/points_balance.dart:113` — “TextColumn get ulid => text().nullable()();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/tables/learning_ledger.dart:20` — “name: 'learning_ledger_profile_ulid', columns: {#profileId, #ulid}, unique: true,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/points_balance_dao.dart:308` — “await (select(pointsLedger)..where((t) => t.ulid.equals(ulid))..limit(1)).getSingleOrNull();”
- **Fix:** Add `@TableIndex(name: 'points_ledger_profile_ulid', columns: {#profileId, #ulid}, unique: true)` to PointsLedger and an equivalent unique index to RewardRedemptions (mirroring learning_ledger.dart), ship as a schema migration, and switch insertRemoteLedgerEntryIfAbsent to rely on that constraint (insertOnConflictDoNothing) instead of a separate SELECT.
- **Done when:** Schema migration adds the unique index to points_ledger and reward_redemptions, with committed schema export + generated migration test (DB-4). · Regression test: calling the merge path twice concurrently (Future.wait) with the same ulid results in exactly one row and exactly one balance credit.
- **Labels:** data-integrity, sync, gamification, race-condition · verifier corrections: The "rule" field's sub-clause "profileId-in-PK's composite-index companion requirement" is the finding author's own paraphrase/inference, not verbatim text from DB-6 in coding-standards.md (DB-6 literally only mandates l

#### AUD-core-database-04 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Make SacredWindowDao's cache replace atomic — clearAll()+insertAll() must be one transaction, not the caller's fire-and-forget chain
- **Rule:** DB-1 / DB-2 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** The DAO's own doc comment says '[clearAll] + [insertAll] are called together... Expects the caller to have called [clearAll] first so the table stays coherent' — but the DAO exposes no atomic way to do that, and the only caller (SacredWindowRepository._persistToDb) chains them with `.then(...).ignore()`: unawaited, no transaction, errors silently discarded. If the process dies (routine on mobile backgrounding) between clearAll() completing and insertAll() completing, sacred_window_entries is left empty. That table is the documented source of truth for 'background notification-fire-time checks... without the Flutter engine' (DNI-367) — an empty table means Sacred Time notification suppression silently fails open on next cold-start check, with no error anywhere (`.ignore()` explicitly suppresses it). invalidate() → _persistToDb runs on every location/timezone change and app resume, so the window isn't rare.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/sacred_window_dao.dart:19` — “Future<void> clearAll() => delete(sacredWindowEntries).go();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/sacred_window_dao.dart:23` — “Future<void> insertAll(List<SacredWindowEntriesCompanion> entries) =>
      batch((b) => b.insertAll(sacredWindowEntries, entries));”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/data/services/sacred_window_repository.dart:167` — “dao.clearAll().then((_) => dao.insertAll(companions)).ignore();”
- **Fix:** Add a single `SacredWindowDao.replaceAll(List<SacredWindowEntriesCompanion> entries)` that wraps clearAll+insertAll in one `db.transaction()`, and have sacred_window_repository.dart call that instead of the `.then().ignore()` chain. If fire-and-forget is intentional, at minimum log the failure via AppLogger instead of `.ignore()`.
- **Done when:** SacredWindowDao exposes an atomic replaceAll(); sacred_window_repository.dart no longer calls clearAll()/insertAll() separately. · A test makes insertAll throw mid-write inside replaceAll and asserts the table still holds the PREVIOUS rows (no empty-table window), not a partially-cleared state.
- **Labels:** DB-2, atomicity, notifications, silent-failure · verifier corrections: Downgrade P1 -> P2: the 'silent notification-suppression failure' consequence is aspirational, not live — grep confirms `sacredWindowDao.getAll()` is called nowhere in lib/ outside its own DAO/tests; isWindowActive() onl

#### AUD-core-database-05 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Wrap TrackLearningOrderDao.upsertOrder's per-row insert loop and its repository call sites in one transaction/batch
- **Rule:** DB-2, DB-3 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 7 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** upsertOrder writes N rows via an awaited for-loop with no db.transaction()/db.batch() wrapper, and its only callers (saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder/resetToDefault) then make a second, entirely separate write (stampReorderAt) with no shared transaction either. A user reordering a full masechta/seder (which can be dozens to hundreds of refs) who has the app killed mid-reorder (OS memory pressure, backgrounding kill — routine on mobile) is left with a partially-old/partially-new sortOrder sequence and no error anywhere. getByTrack() then feeds that corrupted order straight into the daily learning projection, producing skipped or repeated study segments with zero user-visible signal that anything went wrong. Even when upsertOrder itself completes, dying before the separate stampReorderAt call leaves a stale lastReorderAt, breaking the reorder-amnesty logic documented at architecture §10.1. This is discovered via track_learning_order_dao_test.dart (in this batch), which covers the happy path only and has no test for interrupted/partial writes.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/track_learning_order_dao.dart:18` — “Future<void> upsertOrder(int trackId, List<String> refs) async {
    for (var i = 0; i < refs.length; i++) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/track_order/data/repositories/track_learning_order_repository_impl.dart:124` — “await _database.trackLearningOrderDao.upsertOrder(trackId, refs);
    await _database.trackDao.stampReorderAt(trackId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/track_order/data/repositories/track_learning_order_repository_impl.dart:136` — “await _database.trackLearningOrderDao.upsertOrder(trackId, refs);
    await _database.trackDao.stampReorderAt(trackId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/track_order/data/repositories/track_learning_order_repository_impl.dart:144` — “await _database.trackLearningOrderDao.deleteByTrack(trackId);
    await _database.trackDao.stampReorderAt(trackId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/point_config_dao.dart:136` — “for (final d in fallbackDefaults) {
        await insertConfig(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/study_day_config_dao.dart:69` — “for (var day = 1; day <= 7; day++) {
      await into(studyDayConfigs).insertOnConflictUpdate(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/track_learning_order_dao.dart:19` — “for (var i = 0; i < refs.length; i++) {
      await into(trackLearningOrder).insert(”
- **Fix:** Replace the for-loop in upsertOrder with a single db.batch((b) { for (...) b.insert(trackLearningOrder, ..., onConflict: ...); }) — Drift batches are atomic, satisfying DB-2 and DB-3 in one change. In the repository, wrap the order-write + stampReorderAt call of saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder/resetToDefault in one _database.transaction(...) so the pair commits or rolls back together.
- **Done when:** TrackLearningOrderDao.upsertOrder issues one db.batch() instead of an awaited per-row loop. · saveSedarimOrder, saveMasechtosOrder, and resetToDefault each wrap their order-write + stampReorderAt call in a single db.transaction(). · New regression test asserts the reorder write is all-or-nothing (e.g. inject a failure partway through a multi-ref batch and assert zero rows changed / the pre-reorder order is intact). · No Rule-0 checker exists yet for this class of bug (DB-2/DB-3 are [P]ending) — note the gap; a grep for `for (` followed within a few lines by `await into(` or `await (db.update`/`await (db.delete` inside lib/core/database/daos/**/*.dart would catch this pattern cheaply.
- **Labels:** drift, atomicity, dao, data-integrity · merged 2 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 3 batches · verifier corrections: Note for orchestrator (not a reason to kill): a closely related/possibly overlapping finding exists elsewhere in the audit (grp-117 'Wrap saveOrder/resetToDefault's reorder-amnesty stamp in the same transaction as the or

#### AUD-core-database-06 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Replace awaited per-row insert/update loops with Drift batch() in curriculum_scope_dao, stage_dao, and track_dao.purgeHistory
- **Rule:** DB-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** These four loops are all already inside a db.transaction() (so DB-2 is satisfied — no partial-write risk), but each issues N sequential awaited statements where Drift's batch() would send one. track_dao.purgeHistory is the worst case: on 'delete and wipe history' for a track with hundreds of completions, it round-trips once per row to stamp purgedAt instead of one batched UPDATE. The three sites from the companion DB-2 finding (point_config_dao.seedDefaults, study_day_config_dao.seedDefaults, track_learning_order_dao.upsertOrder) share the identical pattern and compound this once they're wrapped in a transaction.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/curriculum_scope_dao.dart:63` — “for (final value in scopeValues) {
        await into(curriculumScopes).insert(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/stage_dao.dart:89` — “for (final stage in stages) {
        await insertStageDefinition(stage);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/stage_dao.dart:128` — “for (final stage in stages) {
        await insertStageDefinition(stage);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/track_dao.dart:417` — “for (final c in completionsForTrack) {
        await (db.update(db.completionEvents)..where(”
- **Fix:** Convert each loop to `batch((b) { for (...) { b.insert(...)/b.update(...); } })`, which Drift supports for both inserts and per-row updates with distinct WHERE clauses inside one batch call.
- **Done when:** curriculum_scope_dao.setScopes, stage_dao.replaceStagesForTrack/replaceStagesForCurriculum, and track_dao.purgeHistory's tombstone step use batch() instead of a per-row await loop. · Existing tests for these methods pass unchanged (behavior-preserving refactor).
- **Labels:** DB-3, batch, performance · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches

#### AUD-core-database-07 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Stop catching StateError (an Error subtype) in user_profile_dao.dart's AccountX.accountTier getter
- **Rule:** EH-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** `StateError` extends `Error` in dart:core, and `UserTierX.fromDb` throws it specifically for an unrecognized `tier` string — i.e. local DB corruption or a missed enum-value migration. Catching it here and silently returning `UserTier.localBorn` masks that bug: a `cloudBorn` account whose stored tier string ever drifts (bad migration, hand-edited row, future enum rename) silently behaves as local-born everywhere accountTier is read (sync gating, balance-row eligibility per 'Adults never have balance rows (Rule 3)', etc.), with nothing logged.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/user_profile_dao.dart:37` — “try {
      return UserTierX.fromDb(tier);
    } on StateError {
      return UserTier.localBorn;”
- **Fix:** Let the StateError propagate (or catch and rethrow after an AppLogger.error call) instead of returning a silent fallback — an unrecognized tier value is a bug that should be loud, not a normal control-flow case.
- **Done when:** AccountX.accountTier no longer has an `on StateError` handler that returns a default value. · A test asserts that an Account row with an unrecognized `tier` string causes accountTier to throw (or to log via AppLogger and rethrow), not silently return localBorn.
- **Labels:** EH-4, error-handling, silent-fallback

#### AUD-core-database-08 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Wrap DeviceRegistryDatabase.removeAccount's delete + state-clear in a transaction()
- **Rule:** DB-2 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3] · filed P1, revised
- **Why:** removeAccount's own docstring says it clears lastActiveAccountId 'so the next launch does NOT silently auto-activate an arbitrary fallback account against a dangling pointer (D10)' — but the delete and the pointer-clear are two separately-awaited statements with no db.transaction() around them. If the process dies between them (routine on Android when a backgrounded app is reclaimed, and account removal is exactly the kind of action a user triggers then backgrounds), the delete commits but the clear never runs, leaving deviceState.lastActiveAccountId pointing at a row that no longer exists — the exact D10 state device_registry_test.dart's 'removeAccount clears it when removing the ACTIVE account (D10)' test checks for, just reached through a crash path the in-memory test can't simulate. dedupeByEmail compounds this by calling removeAccount N times in an unwrapped loop, so a mid-run crash also leaves a partially-merged duplicate-account state. Every other multi-write DAO in this codebase (stage_dao.dart, curriculum_scope_dao.dart, user_profile_dao.dart, track_dao.dart, points_balance_dao.dart) wraps its writes in transaction() — this file is the outlier.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/registry/device_registry_database.dart:111` — “final deleted = await (delete(
      deviceAccounts,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/registry/device_registry_database.dart:114` — “if (await getLastActiveAccountId() == accountId) {
      await setLastActiveAccountId(null);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/registry/device_registry_database.dart:185` — “for (var i = 1; i < group.length; i++) {
        removed += await removeAccount(group[i].accountId);”
- **Fix:** Wrap removeAccount's body in `await transaction(() async { ... })`; wrap dedupeByEmail's per-group removal loop in one enclosing transaction (or a single batched delete) so a crash mid-merge can't leave a partially-deduped state.
- **Done when:** removeAccount and dedupeByEmail are wrapped in transaction()/batch(); a new test forces an exception between the delete and the state-clear and asserts neither write applied. · DB-2's Pending checker (audit grep for ≥2 awaited writes with no enclosing transaction() in a DAO method body) returns zero for this file.
- **Labels:** DB-2, transactions, D10 · verifier corrections: Third evidence line cites device_registry_database.dart:185 but the quoted two-line snippet actually starts at line 184 (`for (var i = 1; ...)`) with line 185 being the second line only — off-by-one, not load-bearing. |

#### AUD-core-database-15 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Replace track_dao.dart's stringly-typed TrackState class with a real Dart enum

Any code that branches on `.state` gets no exhaustiveness checking, and nothing stops a typo'd string reaching the column (mitigated today only by everyone remembering to use the TrackState.* constants rather than literals — a convention, not a guarantee).

  static const active = 'active';”
- **Fix:** Model TrackState as a real Dart `enum` (or use Drift's `.withConverter` to store it as text but expose an enum in Dart), so switches over track state are compiler-exhaustive and no non-member string can be constructed.

- **Labels:** modeling, type-safety, hotspot

#### AUD-core-database-16 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Type and log the swallowed catch blocks in content_database.dart, seed_manager.dart, and DeviceAccountX
- **Rule:** EH-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 6 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** content_database.dart's 4 migration catches use untyped `catch (_)` with only a comment, no AppLogger call — if an ALTER/CREATE fails for a real reason (disk full, corrupt file) rather than the anticipated 'already exists' case, the content DB silently proceeds on a half-migrated schema with zero diagnostic trail; contrast with ContentDbHealthChecker in this same batch, which does this correctly with typed `on SqliteException catch (e, st)` plus logger calls, but never gets a chance to react because no exception escapes here. seed_manager.dart's _rollback() catch(_) is a log-less outlier inside a file where every other catch (_extractSeedDb, _atomicReplace, _readSchemaVersion, _readInstalledVersion, _stampInstalledVersion) does call _logger?.error — a reader following this file's own dominant convention would log here too. DeviceAccountX.accountTier catches ArgumentError, an Error subtype EH-4 explicitly says never to catch (Errors are meant to crash loudly on programming bugs); here a malformed/legacy tier string in the DB silently downgrades to AccountTier.local with no signal that stored data is bad.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/content/content_database.dart:84` — “} catch (_) {
            // no-op: CREATE IF NOT EXISTS is defensive; failure here is non-fatal”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/content/content_database.dart:104` — “} catch (_) {
            // no-op: ALTER TABLE fails if column already exists (prior upgrade path); non-fatal”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/seed_manager.dart:336` — “} catch (_) {
        // Best effort”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/registry/device_registry_database.dart:22` — “} on ArgumentError {
      return AccountTier.local;”
- **Fix:** Give the content_database.dart and seed_manager.dart catches typed `on SqliteException`/`on Exception` clauses plus an AppLogger call (matching content_db_health_checker.dart's pattern). Change AccountTier.fromStorageKey to expose a non-throwing tryFromStorageKey returning null (or throw a non-Error type) so accountTier doesn't catch Error.
- **Done when:** No catch block in these 3 files is both untyped and log-less; EH-3's Pending tightened log-less-catch checker returns zero for them. · DeviceAccountX.accountTier no longer catches an Error subtype (EH-4's Pending avoid_catching_errors).
- **Labels:** EH-3, EH-4, logging · verifier corrections: Evidence array quotes only 4 of the 6 counted sites (misses content_database.dart:90,121); the sites:6 count and 'why' text are still numerically accurate per my independent grep.

#### AUD-core-domain-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Fix ScheduleSpec.weekly/.rolling to throw ArgumentError instead of assert() (silently unenforced in release builds)
- **Rule:** EH-4 / documented-contract (docstring promises `Throws ArgumentError`) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** WeeklySchedule and RollingSchedule enforce their invariants with Dart `assert()`, which the compiler strips out of release builds entirely (only active in debug/profile). Both factory doc comments explicitly promise 'Throws ArgumentError' — that promise is false in the exact build users run. `fromParts` (same file, line 63) feeds `daysOfWeek ?? const []` directly into `WeeklySchedule(...)` whenever the DB/JSON column is null, and the independent JSON codec path in stage_definition_repository_impl.dart:346-349 does the same for a missing `days_of_week`/`days` key, wrapped in a try/catch that only rescues the debug-mode AssertionError — in release it silently produces a `WeeklySchedule([])`. A stage with an empty day-list never matches any weekday, so its chazara review permanently stops being scheduled with no error, no log, and no user-facing signal.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart:40` — “Throws [ArgumentError] when [daysOfWeek] is empty or contains values”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart:123` — “assert(daysOfWeek.isNotEmpty, 'daysOfWeek must not be empty'),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart:153` — “assert(windowSize > 0, 'windowSize must be positive, got $windowSize');”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart:63` — “'weekly' => WeeklySchedule(daysOfWeek ?? const []),”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/stages/data/repositories/stage_definition_repository_impl.dart:347` — “((map['days_of_week'] ?? map['days']) as List<dynamic>? ?? [])”
- **Fix:** Replace both asserts with explicit `if (...) throw ArgumentError(...)` (matching the pattern already used correctly by ScopeLevel/StageOrder/Pin/DayKind/CalendarSystem in the same directory) so the invariant holds in release builds too.
- **Done when:** ScheduleSpec.weekly([]) and ScheduleSpec.rolling(0)/.rolling(-1) throw ArgumentError when run under `flutter test` compiled in release/profile mode (or any assert-disabled run), not just debug. · New test/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec_test.dart exists and is wired into the test suite, covering empty/out-of-range daysOfWeek, non-positive windowSize, and fromParts with a null daysOfWeek column. · AG-5 mirroring restored: lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart has a corresponding test file (currently missing).

#### AUD-core-domain-02 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Fix SefariaRef.titlePart/addressPart to match the documented chapter:verse split (or fix the docs)
- **Rule:** Evans (ubiquitous-language contract) / TQ-7-TQ-8 spirit (test encodes the bug instead of catching it) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** The class docstring's own worked example says titlePart of "Mishnah Berakhot 1:1" is "Mishnah Berakhot" (address "1:1"). The `_splitTail` regex only strips a single trailing digit run (optionally +1 letter), so it can never cross the ':' in a chapter:verse address — for that exact documented example it actually produces titlePart == "Mishnah Berakhot 1:" and addressPart == "1". The test file's own inline comment ('let's assert what we actually produce... The SefariaRef titlePart splits on the LAST pure-numeric token') shows the author noticed the mismatch and wrote the test to lock in the wrong output rather than fix the regex or the docs. Mishnah/Tanach chapter:verse is the single most common ref shape in this Torah-study app, so any future caller of titlePart/addressPart (currently unused in production) inherits silently wrong output for the primary case, with a green regression test giving false confidence.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/sefaria_ref.dart:66` — “/// For `"Mishnah Berakhot 1:1"` this is `"Mishnah Berakhot"`.”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/sefaria_ref.dart:133` — “r'^(.*?)(\d+[a-z]?)$',”; `learning_tracker/test/core/domain/value_objects/sefaria_ref_test.dart:67` — “expect(ref.titlePart, 'Mishnah Berakhot 1:');”
- **Fix:** Either extend `_splitTail` to also recognize a `\d+:\d+` chapter:verse tail as one address token, or correct the docstring to describe the actual single-digit-run behavior — then update the test to assert the corrected contract, not the current output.
- **Done when:** SefariaRef.parse('Mishnah Berakhot 1:1').titlePart equals whatever the corrected docstring promises (either 'Mishnah Berakhot' with the regex fixed, or the docstring rewritten to match current behavior). · sefaria_ref_test.dart's titlePart test for chapter:verse refs no longer contains a comment acknowledging the assertion doesn't match the documented contract.
- **Labels:** dead-code, contract-mismatch, test-quality

#### AUD-core-domain-03 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Make ScheduleSpec's delayDays/daysOfWeek/rollingWindowSize getters exhaustive instead of using a `_` catch-all
- **Rule:** EH-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** EH-6 requires sealed-type switches to be exhaustive with no `default:`/`_` arm, precisely so the compiler forces every call site to be revisited when a new subtype is added. All three convenience getters on the sealed ScheduleSpec base class use `_ =>` to cover 'the other two variants' instead of naming them. The file's own docstring says a W3.27 migration to a single JSON `schedule` column is coming and will touch this exact codec — when that (or any future) change adds a 4th ScheduleSpec variant, these three getters will compile cleanly and silently return 0/null/null for it instead of forcing a compile error, which is exactly the failure mode sealed classes exist to prevent.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart:75` — “DelaySchedule(:final delayDays) => delayDays,
    _ => 0,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart:81` — “WeeklySchedule(:final daysOfWeek) => daysOfWeek,
    _ => null,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart:87` — “RollingSchedule(:final windowSize) => windowSize,
    _ => null,”
- **Fix:** Rewrite each getter with an explicit arm per subtype (e.g. `WeeklySchedule() => 0, RollingSchedule() => 0` instead of `_ => 0`) so adding a new variant breaks the build until these getters are updated.
- **Done when:** delayDays/daysOfWeek/rollingWindowSize each list DelaySchedule/WeeklySchedule/RollingSchedule explicitly with no `_`/`default` arm. · Once dart run custom_lint is fixed (already tracked separately), no_hardcoded_domain_term-style exhaustiveness stays enforced; until then, `dart analyze` continues to flag any genuinely non-exhaustive switch if a variant is later added without updating these getters.
- **Labels:** EH-6, sealed-class, exhaustiveness

#### AUD-core-domain-06 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Give StartDateWindowException a stable error code instead of a raw pre-formatted English message (EH-5)
- **Rule:** EH-5 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** EH-5 requires domain/data errors to carry stable codes/enums rather than pre-formatted human messages, specifically because this is an EN+Hebrew app where a raw English string renders untranslated for Hebrew-locale users. '”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/program_starting_position.dart:182` — “class StartDateWindowException extends ValidationException {”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/exceptions/app_exception.dart:33` — “final String message;”
- **Fix:** Add a stable code/enum to StartDateWindowException (or to the AppException hierarchy generally) and have the presentation layer resolve it via AppLocalizations instead of displaying `message` directly.
- **Done when:** StartDateWindowException exposes a stable, locale-independent identifier (enum/const code) alongside or instead of the free-text message. · Any UI that surfaces this exception resolves the user-facing string via AppLocalizations/ARB, verified by an EN+HE widget test.

#### AUD-core-domain-07 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Migrate core/domain/value_objects/ hand-written ==/hashCode/toString classes to @freezed
- **Rule:** Naming/placement — "Domain/state models are immutable @freezed classes; never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes" · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 7 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Every non-enum class in this batch (Pin; ProgramStartingPosition; DelaySchedule/WeeklySchedule/RollingSchedule; ScopeLevel/ScopeValue/CurriculumScope; SefariaRef; StageOrder; StudyDayPattern — 10 classes across 7 files) hand-writes operator==/hashCode/toString rather than using @freezed, contrary to the stated codebase convention. All the ones I traced are currently correct, so this is not a live bug, but it is the exact pattern the standard calls out as risky: every future field addition to any of these classes requires manually keeping three methods in sync by hand with no compiler help, whereas @freezed generates all three from the field list and can't drift.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/pin.dart:58` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/program_starting_position.dart:163` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart:106` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/scope.dart:26` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/sefaria_ref.dart:113` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/stage_order.dart:77` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/domain/value_objects/study_day_pattern.dart:125` — “bool operator ==(Object other) {”
- **Fix:** Migrate these VOs to @freezed where the validating-factory pattern (private const constructor + public validating factory) fits, which all of these already structurally resemble; note any VO where freezed genuinely doesn't fit as a documented exception in coding-standards.md rather than leaving it a silent inconsistency.
- **Done when:** New or materially-changed value objects in core/domain/value_objects/ use @freezed, or coding-standards.md documents an explicit lightweight-VO exception. · No behavior change: existing equality/hashCode/toString tests for these 7 files continue passing unmodified after any migration.
- **Labels:** freezed, naming-placement, hygiene · verifier corrections: Finding's own enumerated list totals 11 classes, not 10 (Pin, ProgramStartingPosition, DelaySchedule, WeeklySchedule, RollingSchedule, ScopeLevel, ScopeValue, CurriculumScope, SefariaRef, StageOrder, StudyDayPattern).

### core/email  (2 findings — 1 P0 / 0 P1 / 0 P2 / 1 P3)

#### AUD-core-email-01 · **P0** · CONFIRMED · Redact TransactionalEmail.plaintextBody before logging in LoggingTransactionalEmailService.send()
- **Rule:** Child-privacy logging hygiene (PV-family principle) — breaks the PiiRedactor.sensitiveKeys contract in core/logging/logger.dart that the same function's sibling field already relies on · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** LoggingTransactionalEmailService.send() (the only bound TransactionalEmailService implementation today) logs the full plaintextBody under the key 'body' via AppLogger.instance.debug(). PiiRedactor.redactFields() only blanks values whose KEY is in the 49-entry sensitiveKeys allowlist (logger.dart:203-251) — 'body' is not in it, even though 'to'/'recipient'/'email_to' were deliberately added and regression-tested (test/core/logging/logger_extended_test.dart:271-304, tag V2-R5 C2) for the exact same call site two lines above. TutorDeclinedEmail, TutorResignedEmail and TutorGrantRevokedEmail are already constructed and sent today from tutor_notification_service.dart (decline/resign/revoke flows), so a child's name and a tutor's raw email address (embedded in TutorDeclinedEmail's prose body) land in the log buffer in cleartext on every one of those events. That buffer is exactly what features/settings/.../send_logs_service.dart uploads (unfiltered by level, last 10 minutes) to `users/{uid}/diagnostic_logs/` in Firestore, a collection its own docstring says a developer can view/query directly in the Firebase console. Once TutorInviteEmail (defined but not yet wired) goes live, the same gap will additionally leak the invite deep link. This directly contradicts the redaction guarantee the codebase already built and tested for the sibling 'to' field in the same function.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/email/transactional_email_service.dart:194` — “fields: {'body': email.plaintextBody},”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/email/transactional_email_service.dart:113` — “'$tutorEmail has declined your invitation to tutor $childName.\n\n'”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/logging/logger.dart:263` — “entry.key: sensitiveKeys.contains(entry.key)”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/utils/send_logs_service.dart:12` — “/// `users/{uid}/diagnostic_logs/{auto-id}` in Firestore via [FirestoreGateway].”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/domain/services/tutor_notification_service.dart:70` — “TutorDeclinedEmail(”
- **Fix:** Add 'body' (or a dedicated key such as 'email_body') to PiiRedactor.sensitiveKeys in core/logging/logger.dart, or stop passing plaintextBody to the logger entirely (log email.runtimeType/a template id instead of the rendered body). Extend the existing V2-R5 C2 test group in test/core/logging/logger_extended_test.dart to cover the debug() 'Payload' call the same way it already covers the warning() call.
- **Done when:** PiiRedactor.redactFields({'body': 'contains tutor@example.com and a child name'})['body'] == '[REDACTED]', or LoggingTransactionalEmailService.send() no longer logs the raw plaintextBody at all · A new/updated test in test/core/logging/logger_extended_test.dart fails against current logger.dart and passes after the fix · flutter analyze and make ci remain green
- **Labels:** privacy, child-data, logging, P0 · verifier corrections: The 'fields: {'body': email.plaintextBody},' quote is at transactional_email_service.dart:195, not line 194 (line 194 is the preceding AppLogger.instance.debug( call line). All other cited lines are exact.
