#### AUD-core-ids-01 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Adopt or delete 6 of 7 unused NaturalKey.forX factories — mergers duplicate the exact key-format logic inline
- **Rule:** Fowler duplication (DRY) / natural-key single-source-of-truth invariant · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 6 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The file's own doc comment claims these factories 'replac[e] ad-hoc `$a|$b` string concatenations that were scattered across the merger layer' — but a repo-wide grep of lib/ and test/ shows forTrackConfig, forStageDefinition, forSettings, forBookmark, forLearningOrder and fromSingle all have zero callers; only forCompletion is used (1 call site, in completion_event_merger.dart). The mergers still hand-roll the identical shapes instead: core/sync/merge/stage_definition_merger.dart:48 builds `'${decoded.curriculumId}|${decoded.trackId}|${decoded.stageOrder}'` by hand — the exact 3-column shape forStageDefinition exists for — and core/sync/merge/learning_order_merger.dart:35 does the same for the 2-column shape forLearningOrder exists for. Because DriftMergeStore decodes these keys by splitting on `|` (the documented invariant at line 13-14), the format is load-bearing for sync correctness but is maintained by convention across 8+ merger files instead of the one factory meant to own it — a future edit to one merger's key shape without updating the others would silently break natural-key matching (double-inserts or dropped LWW comparisons) with no compiler check to catch the drift.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/ids/natural_key.dart:13` — “/// [DriftMergeStore] splits on `|` to decode composite keys, so the”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/ids/natural_key.dart:57` — “factory NaturalKey.forTrackConfig({required String curriculumId}) =>”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/ids/natural_key.dart:63` — “factory NaturalKey.forStageDefinition({”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/ids/natural_key.dart:72` — “factory NaturalKey.forSettings({required String curriculumId}) =>”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/ids/natural_key.dart:79` — “factory NaturalKey.forBookmark({required String curriculumId}) =>”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/ids/natural_key.dart:97` — “factory NaturalKey.forLearningOrder({”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/ids/natural_key.dart:105` — “factory NaturalKey.fromSingle(String value) => NaturalKey(value);”
- **Fix:** Either route the unused-factory mergers (stage_definition, settings, track_config, bookmark, learning_order) through the matching NaturalKey.forX calls, or delete the unused factories and correct the misleading doc comment. Prefer adoption since it centralizes the `|`-separator invariant DriftMergeStore depends on.
- **Done when:** Every core/sync/merge/*_merger.dart natural-key construction calls a NaturalKey.forX factory, or the doc comment at natural_key.dart:9-11 is corrected to stop claiming repo-wide adoption · A regression test asserts NaturalKey.forStageDefinition/forLearningOrder produce the exact strings the mergers currently hand-build, so a future format change breaks loudly in one place instead of silently
- **Labels:** duplication, sync, natural-key, dead-code · verifier corrections: All 7 natural_key.dart quotes are exact and grep confirms only forCompletion has a caller; the other 6 are dead. Independently found 4 more mergers (bookmark/profile_program/settings/track_config_merger.dart) hand-rollin

#### AUD-core-ids-02 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Fix or delete NaturalKey.forLearnerProfile's fragile non-null-Object emptiness check — fallbackProfileId branch is effectively unreachable and untested
- **Rule:** Type-safety design flaw in dead code · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** profileIdOrRow is typed as non-nullable Object, so it can never be null, and Object.toString() is non-empty for every realistic value (an int, a non-empty String, or the default 'Instance of X') — the only way to hit the fallbackProfileId branch is to pass a literal empty string, which is nowhere documented as the sentinel. This reads like an attempt to model 'optional row value, else use this id' that should have used `Object?` with a null check instead of a string-emptiness check. It has zero callers repo-wide (confirmed via grep across lib/ and test/), so this has never been exercised and the bug would surface silently the moment someone starts using it expecting the fallback to work.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/ids/natural_key.dart:86` — “required Object profileIdOrRow,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/ids/natural_key.dart:89` — “profileIdOrRow.toString().isNotEmpty”
- **Fix:** If kept, change the signature to `Object? profileIdOrRow` and check `== null` instead of `.toString().isNotEmpty`. If truly unused going forward, delete it along with the other 5 unused factories (see companion finding).
- **Done when:** If kept: a unit test constructs NaturalKey.forLearnerProfile with profileIdOrRow omitted/null and asserts the fallbackProfileId branch actually executes · If deleted: covered by the companion 'unused factories' finding's acceptance criteria
- **Labels:** dead-code, type-safety, natural-key

#### AUD-core-learning-01 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Wire core/learning/completion_constants.dart's kBulkPriorSentinelMs into its would-be callers instead of leaving it dead and re-duplicated 3x
- **Rule:** Fowler-duplication / Evans (invariant re-derived instead of enforced in one place) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** completion_constants.dart's docstring claims kBulkPriorSentinelMs is 'used across domain services and providers,' but a repo-wide grep shows zero imports of this file anywhere in lib/ or test/ — it is dead code. Meanwhile SchedulerEngine, BulkPriorCompletionService, and StreakRestorer each independently hand-redefine the identical magic literal 946684800000 (DateTime.utc(2000,1,1)). Two of the three duplicate definitions explicitly self-describe as 'the single source of truth,' a direct contradiction between files. All copies currently agree, so there is no live bug today, but the sentinel governs whether a completion counts toward streak/daily-bar-chart 'live activity' — if any one of the 4 independent copies is ever edited (e.g. during the W3.27-style migrations already underway elsewhere in this codebase) without updating the others, gamification data would silently miscategorize bulk-imported completions as live activity or vice versa for affected users, with no compiler or test signal since nothing imports the canonical constant to compare against.

- **Fix:** Pick one true source (core/learning/completion_constants.dart is the natural core-layer home) and have SchedulerEngine, BulkPriorCompletionService, and StreakRestorer import and reuse it; if a core→features layering constraint genuinely blocks that, document why in coding-standards.md and delete the now-provably-false 'used across... providers' claim from whichever copy remains a local duplicate.
- **Done when:** grep for the literal 946684800000 (or DateTime.utc(2000, 1, 1) used as a sentinel) outside test/ resolves to exactly one definition plus its importers, not 4 independent literals. · core/learning/completion_constants.dart's docstring claim is verifiably true (has real importers) or the file is removed. · Existing bulk-prior/streak/scheduler regression tests continue passing after de-duplication (points_service_test.dart, chart_data_service tests, streak tests already reference the sentinel and act as the regression check).

### core/logging  (2 findings — 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 2 P2 / 0 P3)

#### AUD-core-logging-01 · **P2** · SUSPECTED · Guard CrashlyticsService's unawaited analytics calls with catchError — unguarded rejection can re-enter the runZonedGuarded fatal-error handler
- **Rule:** EH-2 / Nygard (I/O failure mid-flight) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** main.dart wraps the whole app in runZonedGuarded whose error callback (lines 26-31) calls _crashlytics.recordError(...) — which is FirebaseCrashlyticsService.recordError, firing `unawaited(_analytics.logCrashReported(...))` with no .catchError attached at either of the two sites cited. If the Firebase Analytics plugin call itself rejects (platform-channel failure, SDK not yet initialized, offline queue full), that unhandled Future error is delivered back into the very same Zone installed by runZonedGuarded, invoking the identical error callback again, which calls recordError again, firing another unawaited call — a self-feeding loop precisely at the moment (an active fatal-crash report) when the app's error-handling path most needs to be inert. Contrast with streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart in the same directory tree, which does guard its own fire-and-forget analytics call with `.catchError(...)` (line 63-70) — the inconsistency shows this omission wasn't a deliberate choice. Needs runtime confirmation: inject an AnalyticsService whose logCrashReported always rejects inside a runZonedGuarded harness and observe whether recordError re-enters.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/logging/crashlytics_service.dart:51` — “unawaited(_analytics.logCrashReported(fatal: true));”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/logging/crashlytics_service.dart:62` — “unawaited(_analytics.logCrashReported(fatal: fatal));”; `learning_tracker/lib/main.dart:27` — “_crashlytics.recordError(error, stack, fatal: true);”
- **Fix:** Add `.catchError((_, __) {})` (or route failures through AppLogger only) to both unawaited(_analytics.logCrashReported(...)) calls in crashlytics_service.dart, matching the guard pattern already used in streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart.
- **Done when:** Both fire-and-forget analytics calls in crashlytics_service.dart have an attached .catchError/try-catch so a rejected Future never re-enters the zone's onError · A regression test injects an AnalyticsService whose logCrashReported always throws, calls recordError once, and asserts it is not invoked a second time
- **Labels:** error-handling, crashlytics, P2, reliability · verifier corrections: main.dart citation line is off by 4: the quoted `_crashlytics.recordError(error, stack, fatal: true);` is actually at line 31 (comments above it push it down from the cited 27). Quote text itself is exact and uniquely lo

#### AUD-core-logging-02 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Remove or explicitly justify AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers — dead code duplicating crashlytics_bootstrap.dart's live handlers
- **Rule:** dead-code (Everything sweep) / Fowler duplication · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** Grepping every .dart file in the repo shows AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers is referenced nowhere except its own definition and its 3 unit tests in logger_test.dart. Production's bootstrap chain (bootstrap.dart:40) installs FlutterError.onError/PlatformDispatcher.onError exclusively via bootstrapCrashlyticsHandlers in app/bootstrap/crashlytics_bootstrap.dart — a completely independent implementation of the same responsibility that also forwards to Crashlytics (setupFlutterErrorHandlers only forwards to Talker). A maintainer reading logger_test.dart's 3 green tests would reasonably believe this is the production error-handling path; if some future refactor swaps main.dart's wiring back to this method for 'simplicity', fatal-crash reporting silently stops reaching Crashlytics while Talker logs keep looking healthy, and the existing green test suite would not catch it since it only ever exercises the unused copy.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/logging/logger.dart:85` — “static void setupFlutterErrorHandlers() {”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/bootstrap/crashlytics_bootstrap.dart:26` — “FlutterError.onError = (FlutterErrorDetails details) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/bootstrap/bootstrap.dart:40` — “crashlytics = bootstrapCrashlyticsHandlers(”; `learning_tracker/test/core/logging/logger_test.dart:54` — “AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers();”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/bootstrap/logger_bootstrap.dart:8` — “void bootstrapLogger() {
  AppLogger.init();”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/bootstrap/bootstrap.dart:37` — “final talker = AppLogger.init();
  final log = AppLogger(talker);”
- **Fix:** Delete AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers and its 3 tests, or — if it's meant as a documented fallback for contexts without Crashlytics wired — rename it and add a comment cross-referencing crashlytics_bootstrap.dart so the duplication is intentional and visible rather than accidental drift.
- **Done when:** grep -rn 'setupFlutterErrorHandlers' lib/ returns only its own definition, or a caller with a comment explaining the split from crashlytics_bootstrap.dart · No test exercises a code path unreachable from main.dart's actual bootstrap chain
- **Labels:** dead-code, hygiene, P2, logging · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · verifier corrections: None — all four cited file:line/quote pairs verified exact; grep confirms no other production callers.

#### AUD-core-network-01 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Convert ContentItem/CurriculumHierarchyConfig/FetchResult to @freezed instead of hand-rolled or absent equality
- **Rule:** Naming/placement/invariants — 'Domain/state models are immutable @freezed classes ... never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes — hand-rolled equality drifts from the fields and silently breaks rebuild-skipping.' · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** ContentItem's == compares only curriculumId+sefariaRef, silently ignoring level1-4/displayNameHe/displayNameEn/sortOrder/isLeaf — two items differing only in display text or sort order compare equal, so any future Set/Map-keyed-by-item or equality-based diff would silently drop a real change. CurriculumHierarchyConfig has no == at all (falls back to identity), so two field-identical instances are never equal, AND exposes a directly-mutable List<String> levelLabels with no defensive copy — content_repository_impl.dart caches these instances in _configCache and hands the same object to every reader, so one caller mutating the list would corrupt it for all subsequent readers. FetchResult (the public return type of fetchAllContent()) has the same gap.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/network/sefaria/models/content_item.dart:51` — “other is ContentItem &&
          runtimeType == other.runtimeType &&”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/network/sefaria/models/content_item.dart:55` — “curriculumId == other.curriculumId &&
          sefariaRef == other.sefariaRef;”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/network/sefaria/models/curriculum_hierarchy_config.dart:18` — “final List<String> levelLabels;”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/network/sefaria/curriculum_content_fetcher.dart:6` — “class FetchResult {”
- **Fix:** Make all three @freezed with generated ==/hashCode/copyWith; for CurriculumHierarchyConfig use an immutable list wrapper (e.g. List.unmodifiable or IList) for levelLabels.
- **Done when:** dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs regenerates these as @freezed with no manual ==/hashCode remaining · a regression test proves two ContentItems differing only in sortOrder/displayNameHe are NOT == · levelLabels cannot be mutated through the public CurriculumHierarchyConfig API
- **Labels:** freezed, equality, immutability

#### AUD-core-network-03 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Cancel or document the leaked DNS-lookup Future in ConnectivityGateway.isOnline on timeout
- **Rule:** Nygard lens — what happens when I/O fails halfway · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** Future.timeout() races a Timer against the lookup but cannot cancel the underlying OS-level DNS resolution — dart:io gives no cancellable primitive for InternetAddress.lookup. Under packet loss or a captive portal (exactly when this check matters most), the original lookup keeps running past the 2s timeout with no way to observe or cancel it; repeated calls (e.g. retrying a failed offline-account conversion in account_actions.dart) can accumulate abandoned lookups.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/network/connectivity_gateway.dart:14` — “final result = await InternetAddress.lookup(
        'dns.google',
      ).timeout(const Duration(seconds: 2));”
- **Fix:** Either document the accepted tradeoff inline (dart:io has no cancellable DNS API) with a bounded-impact justification, or switch to a primitive that supports cancellation (e.g. a raw socket connect with explicit close on timeout).
- **Done when:** Either an inline comment documents the accepted leak and its bound, or a test demonstrates no more than one lookup stays in flight after repeated rapid isOnline calls under a simulated timeout
- **Labels:** resource-leak, nygard-lens · verifier corrections: account_actions.dart:226's isOnline call is inside showDeleteAccountFlow (delete-account-requires-internet), not an offline-account-conversion retry path; the core evidence at connectivity_gateway.dart:14 is unaffected.

#### AUD-core-preferences-02 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Align readUseHebrewCalendar's stale '?? false' default with HebrewDatePreference.defaultValue=true
- **Rule:** Evans/DRY (invariant re-derived in two places) — no single rule ID; data-consistency correctness bug · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** outbox_sync_write_facade.dart:222 calls readUseHebrewCalendar() inside pushUiPreferencesSnapshot(), which _writeAndPushSnapshot() (preference_providers.dart) fires after every write to ANY sibling UI preference. A profile that never touches the calendar toggle but changes any other preference (font size, nikud, hebrew-terms script) pushes use_hebrew_calendar:false to the cloud snapshot, even though the local UI/HebrewDatePreference default is true — so a second device or a restore silently shows the Gregorian calendar instead of the Hebrew one the first device is displaying. This exact bug shape (a stale '?? false' default) was already found and fixed once for the sibling hebrewTermsScript field two methods below (comment: 'The old ?? false was stale') but the identical fix was never applied to readUseHebrewCalendar, and HebrewDatePreference.readFromPrefs duplicates rather than delegates to this helper (unlike TextDisplayPreference, which correctly delegates to readFontSizeIndex), so the two defaults can drift independently.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/preferences/profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart:51` — “return prefs.getBool(legacyUseHebrewCalendarKey) ?? false;”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/preferences/profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart:53` — “return false;”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/preferences/hebrew_date_preference.dart:12` — “bool get defaultValue => true;”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/preferences/hebrew_date_preference.dart:26` — “return defaultValue;”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/preferences/profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart:91` — “// (§9 of hebrew-terms.md). The old `?? false` was stale.”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/outbox_sync_write_facade.dart:222` — “'use_hebrew_calendar': ProfileScopedPreferenceKeys.readUseHebrewCalendar(”
- **Fix:** Change profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart:51/53 to default true, matching HebrewDatePreference.defaultValue. Better: delete the duplicated read logic in HebrewDatePreference.readFromPrefs and have it call ProfileScopedPreferenceKeys.readUseHebrewCalendar directly (the pattern TextDisplayPreference already uses), so there is exactly one place to get the default right.
- **Done when:** ProfileScopedPreferenceKeys.readUseHebrewCalendar(prefs, anyUnsetProfileId) returns true, matching HebrewDatePreference().defaultValue. · New regression test (test/core/preferences/hebrew_date_preference_test.dart, per AG-5) asserts HebrewDatePreference().read(profileId) and ProfileScopedPreferenceKeys.readUseHebrewCalendar(prefs, profileId) agree for a never-written profile. · pushUiPreferencesSnapshot()'s use_hebrew_calendar field for a fresh profile that only changed an unrelated preference equals what the UI displays.

#### AUD-core-preferences-04 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Wrap the unguarded SharedPreferences/service writes in 9 plain-value Notifier mutation methods across 6 files
- **Rule:** SM-5 · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 21 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The identical idiom repeats across 9 Notifier classes in 6 files: the class holds a plain-value (non-AsyncValue) state type, an async mutation method optimistically assigns `state` (or navigates state via copyWith), then `await`s a persistence/service call (SharedPreferences write, step.save(ref), jsonDecode of stored JSON) with NO enclosing try/catch anywhere in the call chain. Concretely: (1) preference_providers.dart's 5 `set()` methods and notification_providers.dart's 5 `toggle()`/`setTime()` methods write to SharedPreferences after already showing the new value — a write failure is an unhandled Future rejection and the change is silently lost, reverting on next launch with zero explanation to the user who believed they had already saved it; (2) sacred_location_provider.dart's detect()/setManualCity/setManualCoords/setInIsrael have the same gap, with the added wrinkle that a lost write means the in-Israel/location flag used for Sacred-Time window calculations silently reverts; (3) scheduler_providers.dart's SkippedTasks.skip/undoSkip repeat it despite the SAME file's _loadFromPrefs() correctly demonstrating the fix (full try/catch + AppLogger.error) two methods away; (4) add_track_controller.dart's _advance()/goBack() fire `_persist()` without await or unawaited(), and tryRestore() runs jsonDecode on stored JSON with no try/catch, so a corrupt or stale-schema persisted wizard state throws uncaught instead of falling back to a fresh wizard; (5) onboarding_controller.dart's init()/advance()/jumpTo() await arbitrary OnboardingStep.save/load(ref) implementations with no error channel at all, and the sole caller (learning_process_wizard_screen.dart) does not catch either, so a DB write failure inside any wizard step crashes the flow rather than showing a recoverable error.

    await _writeAndPushSnapshot(ref, pref, profileId, value);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:79` — “final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    await prefs.setBool(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/presentation/providers/sacred_location_provider.dart:89` — “final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();

      final list = jsonDecode(scopeJson) as List<dynamic>;”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/providers/onboarding_controller.dart:69` — “await current.save(ref);”
- **Fix:** Introduce a shared helper (e.g. `Future<void> guardedPersist(Ref ref, Future<void> Function() write, {required VoidCallback onFailure})`) that every listed mutation method routes its persistence call through, catching and logging via AppLogger and rolling back or surfacing the optimistic state change on failure; apply it at all 21 sites.

Add a `FirestoreCodec.parseDouble` helper mirroring parseInt and use it for GoalCodec's target_percent instead of the raw `as num?` cast.

#### AUD-core-sync-06 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Give OutboxProcessor's single-flight guard a generation token so stale-reclaim can't run concurrent drains
- **Rule:** Nygard-lens (offline-queue concurrency invariant) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** The single-flight guard is two plain fields (_draining/_drainingSince) with no per-invocation identity. In production, OutboxProcessor is built with unmodified defaults (outbox_providers.dart:98-105: pushTimeout/drainStaleAfter never overridden) and sync_orchestrator.dart fires a periodic drain every 60s forever (Timer.periodic(_periodicDrainInterval, ...)) while drainStaleAfter is 90s. Non-completion kinds are pushed one row at a time, individually awaited (up to 50 rows x ~18 kinds) — a real multi-kind backlog on a slow connection easily exceeds 90s. When that happens, the next periodic (or connectivity/lifecycle) trigger sees the guard as 'stale', resets it, and starts a second, genuinely concurrent `_doDrain()` while the first is still running — the code comment at line 206-211 only reasons about two *reclaimers* racing each other synchronously; it never accounts for the *original* stale-but-still-running drain's own `finally` unconditionally zeroing `_draining`/`_drainingSince` once it eventually completes, which can then let a THIRD trigger barge in on top of the second. This directly breaks the documented contract ('collapses them to one push round' / sync_orchestrator.dart:568 'the OutboxProcessor's single-flight guard collapses races with other triggers'), producing duplicate concurrent Firestore pushes and racy interleaved deleteRow/markAttempted calls that can double-count a row's attempts and dead-letter a recoverable failure roughly twice as fast as _maxAttempts=10 implies. The R6-13 regression test that targets exactly this code path never builds true overlap: every scenario releases and awaits the 'wedged' pipeline to full completion before the next drain runs (its own comment admits the limitation at line 1392/1396), so the actual race is untested.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/outbox/outbox_processor.dart:85` — “Duration drainStaleAfter = const Duration(seconds: 90),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/outbox/outbox_processor.dart:202` — “if (since != null &&
          _clock.nowUtc().difference(since) < _drainStaleAfter) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/outbox/outbox_processor.dart:219` — “} finally {
      _draining = false;”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/sync_orchestrator.dart:228` — “Duration periodicDrainInterval = const Duration(seconds: 60),”; `learning_tracker/test/core/sync/outbox/outbox_processor_test.dart:1392` — “// reclaim only inspects the *same instance's* private state we also”
- **Fix:** Replace the boolean+timestamp guard with a construct that can tell 'my invocation' apart from a later reclaimer — e.g. a monotonically increasing generation counter captured at acquire time, checked before `finally` clears state (`if (_generation == myGeneration) { _draining = false; ... }`), or switch to chaining onto the in-flight Future (a late caller awaits/joins the existing drain rather than racing a flag).
- **Done when:** New/updated unit test keeps the first drain's pipeline call parked on a Completer, advances the clock past drainStaleAfter, drives a second (reclaiming) drain to full completion, then completes the first — and asserts the pipeline was invoked exactly once for the outstanding rows, or that DAO state is never corrupted by true overlap. · Guard implementation carries a generation token (or equivalent) so a finally block from an earlier invocation cannot clear state established by a later one.
- **Labels:** sync, concurrency, reliability · verifier corrections: The finding's characterization of the R6-13 test as "never builds true overlap" is only partially accurate. Two of its three sub-scenarios (p and p2) do complete the wedged drain before proceeding. But the third sub-scen

#### AUD-core-sync-08 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Make MergeStore.upsert + persistUpdatedAt atomic to stop a stale LWW shadow-timestamp surviving a mid-merge crash
- **Rule:** DB-2 (>1 write runs inside a single transaction()) / Nygard: process death mid-write · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 8 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** Every natural-key LWW merger applies the remote row (_store.upsert, which writes the entity table including its own updatedAt column) and THEN separately persists the SyncKv shadow timestamp (_store.persistUpdatedAt) as two independent awaited Drift writes with no enclosing db.transaction(). If the process dies between the two — an OS kill or force-quit on mobile is routine, not exotic — the entity row is left holding the remote's updatedAt while SyncKv still holds the pre-merge value. Any local edit made before the next successful sync now races a STALE local timestamp: a re-pulled, unchanged remote row will look newer than the stale SyncKv record and DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer will silently let it overwrite the user's genuinely-newer local edit — no exception, no log, nothing to retry against. This is DB-2's 'crash mid-sequence leaves the DB half-written' failure applied to the LWW bookkeeping itself.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/bookmark_merger.dart:52` — “await _store.upsert(kind: kind, profileId: profileId, fields: row);
      await _store.persistUpdatedAt(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/track_config_merger.dart:57` — “await _store.upsert(kind: kind, profileId: profileId, fields: row);
      await _store.persistUpdatedAt(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/learner_profile_merger.dart:64` — “await _store.upsert(kind: kind, profileId: profileId, fields: row);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/stage_definition_merger.dart:68` — “await _store.upsert(kind: kind, profileId: profileId, fields: row);
      await _store.persistUpdatedAt(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/goal_merger.dart:86` — “await _db.goalDao.upsertGoalByTrack(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/learning_order_merger.dart:54` — “await _store.upsert(kind: kind, profileId: profileId, fields: row);
      await _store.persistUpdatedAt(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/profile_program_merger.dart:87` — “await _store.upsert(kind: kind, profileId: profileId, fields: row);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/settings_merger.dart:53` — “await _store.upsert(kind: kind, profileId: profileId, fields: row);
      await _store.persistUpdatedAt(”
- **Fix:** Add a MergeStore.applyRemote(...) that wraps the entity write and its SyncKv persistUpdatedAt in one db.transaction() (or expose a transaction-scoped variant), and switch all 8 callers to it.
- **Done when:** Fault-injection/unit test: call upsert() alone (simulating a crash before persistUpdatedAt commits), then perform a legitimately-newer local edit to the same row, then re-merge the identical stale remote row — assert the local edit survives. · New transaction-wrapped MergeStore method has a unit test asserting both writes roll back together when the second write is forced to fail.
- **Labels:** sync, merge, data-integrity, transactions, nygard · verifier corrections: 3 of the 8 sites (bookmark_merger.dart, goal_merger.dart, learning_order_merger.dart) have a redundant per-DAO LWW guard (e.g. BookmarkDao.upsertBookmarkByProfile checks `updatedAt.isAfter(existing.updatedAt)`) that part

#### AUD-core-sync-09 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Move _decodePayload() calls inside outbox_processor.dart's per-row try blocks so one bad payload can't abort the whole drain
- **Rule:** EH-2 / EH-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** _decodePayload throws FormatException when a row's payload isn't a JSON object (DB corruption, a future write bug, or jsonEncode(null)). A single malformed row therefore throws all the way out of _drainForProfile → _doDrain → drain()'s try/finally (the finally still clears the single-flight guard, but nothing catches or converts the error), skipping every other pending completion, every remaining non-completion kind, AND the profile-0 account sweep in _doDrain — on every one of the 5 wired drain triggers, forever, until the row is fixed out of band. This directly contradicts the code's own stated invariant quoted above.

        try {”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/outbox/outbox_processor.dart:404` — “// Continue draining other rows — don't abort the whole batch on
          // a single failure.”

#### AUD-core-sync-10 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Resolve profileId live, not by snapshot, when wiring OutboxSyncWriteFacade/LocalDataUploadService/PointsBalanceDao.syncSink in syncOrchestratorProvider
- **Rule:** sync push/pull invariant (docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md) / Nygard-lens: stale capture · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** syncOrchestratorProvider is a keepAlive singleton that (by explicit design, per its own comments and resolveProfileIdProvider's doc) survives a profile switch without rebuilding, reacting only via `ref.listen(activeProfileIdProvider, ...)` to restart listeners. But `profileId` at line 79 is a one-time ref.read snapshot baked into OutboxSyncWriteFacade/LocalDataUploadService and into pointsBalanceDao.syncSink — not the lazy `resolveProfileId` the same function already builds at line 68 for the orchestrator's own calls. OutboxSyncWriteFacade._enqueue (features/sync/data/outbox_sync_write_facade.dart) stamps every outbox row's `profileId` column from this captured field for every entity kind it handles except learner-profile-delete (bookmarks, settings, goals, learning order, curriculum tracks, notification/gamification/UI-preference snapshots, streak events, study-day configs, and — via PointsBalanceDao._pushRedemption calling sink.enqueueRewardRedemption — reward redemptions). OutboxProcessor._doDrain only sweeps the currently-active profileId plus account-level 0 (confirmed in outbox_processor.dart and explicitly documented for the analogous deleteLearnerProfile case: 'the drain only sweeps the ACTIVE profile + 0... orphans the row'). So after a household profile switch (Bug #1/R1 already proves this happens mid-session without an orchestrator rebuild), every write of the affected kinds for the newly-active profile gets tagged with the stale boot-time profileId and is never drained until — if ever — that exact stale profile becomes active again. Concretely: parent app open with childA active, orchestrator built (profileId=A); parent switches to childB; childB redeems a reward or a bookmark/goal/track change is made; the outbox row is stamped profileId=A; the orchestrator's periodic/lifecycle/connectivity drains all resolve the live profileId (=B) and never pick up the A-stamped row. That data silently never reaches Firestore / other devices.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/providers/sync_orchestrator_providers.dart:79` — “final profileId = ref.read(activeProfileIdProvider);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/providers/sync_orchestrator_providers.dart:91` — “database.pointsBalanceDao.syncSink = uploadFacade;”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/providers/sync_orchestrator_providers.dart:95` — “unawaited(database.pointsBalanceDao.reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows(profileId));”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/providers/sync_orchestrator_providers.dart:68` — “final resolveProfileId = ref.read(resolveProfileIdProvider);”
- **Fix:** Change OutboxSyncWriteFacade and LocalDataUploadService to take an `int Function() resolveProfileId` (reuse resolveProfileIdProvider) instead of a captured `int profileId`, reading it at each call instead of at construction. Re-wire pointsBalanceDao.syncSink and re-run reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows whenever the active profile changes, not just once at orchestrator build.
- **Done when:** OutboxSyncWriteFacade/LocalDataUploadService read the active profile id live at write time rather than at construction time. · Regression test: build a ProviderContainer, go cloud-born with profile A active, switch activeProfileIdProvider to B, perform a write that reaches OutboxSyncWriteFacade, and assert the resulting outbox row's profileId column equals B, not A. · Existing sync_orchestrator_providers.dart comments documenting the resolver-vs-snapshot distinction (Bug #1/R1) are updated to cover this fix.
- **Labels:** sync, offline-first, riverpod, data-loss-risk

#### AUD-core-sync-11 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Route LearningLedgerCodec.encode's completedAt through FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime instead of raw toIso8601String()
- **Rule:** Evans consistency (single documented UTC-safe conversion path) / data-integrity · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** Every other DateTime field in all 14 sibling codecs — and every other field in this very file (see decode() at line 84-86) — is pushed via FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime, which forces `.toUtc()` before serializing so the wire string always carries a 'Z' suffix. This one call skips it. entry.completedAt is read back from Drift's `dateTime()` column which, per the pinned drift-2.31.0 source (lib/src/runtime/types/mapping.dart:174, default storeDateTimesAsText=false, not overridden anywhere in this repo), decodes via `DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(unixSeconds*1000)` with no isUtc:true — producing a **local**, non-UTC-flagged DateTime even though the original value came from DateTimeFactory.nowUtc(). `.toIso8601String()` on a non-UTC DateTime omits the 'Z'/offset entirely. When a different device (a parent or tutor on a different device/timezone — an explicitly supported flow in this app, see tutor_grant_codec.dart in this same batch) pulls the row, FirestoreCodec.parseDateTime's `DateTime.tryParse(raw)?.toUtc()` (used by learning_ledger_merger.dart) reinterprets the offset-naive string using the READING device's local offset rather than the writer's, shifting completedAt by the delta between the two devices' UTC offsets — potentially moving a ledger entry onto the wrong calendar day on the syncing device.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/codec/learning_ledger_codec.dart:67` — “'completed_at': model.completedAt.toIso8601String(),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/codec/firestore_codec.dart:59` — “static String? encodeDateTime(DateTime? dt) => dt?.toUtc().toIso8601String();”
- **Fix:** Change line 67 to `'completed_at': FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime(model.completedAt),` to match every sibling codec.
- **Done when:** Regression test: encode a LearningLedgerRow with a non-UTC-flagged completedAt (isUtc:false, simulating the Drift round-trip) and assert the resulting 'completed_at' string ends in 'Z' and represents the correct UTC instant. · learning_ledger_roundtrip_test.dart extended so decode(encode(x)) is timezone-independent (passes under a non-UTC ambient TZ).
- **Labels:** sync, codec, timezone, data-integrity · verifier corrections: The reachable path is broader than cited: not only the bulk-backfill path in local_data_upload_service.dart:261, but also the default per-completion save path in learning_ledger_repository_impl.dart (recordCompletion re-

#### AUD-core-sync-12 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Wire onError (and a recovery-pull path) into TutoredListenerSupervisor's inner ListenerSupervisor
- **Rule:** EH-3 / observability parity · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** TutoredListenerSupervisor.attach() builds its ListenerSupervisor with only `source` and `onEvent` -- no `onError`, no `recoveryPullTriggers`. Inside ListenerSupervisor.start(), a stream error calls `_onError?.call(...)`, which is a silent no-op when `_onError` is null. Firestore terminates a `.snapshots()` stream on error (e.g. permission-denied when a parent revokes the grant while the tutor's 15 tutored channels are live, or any transient stream fault) -- so that one channel goes permanently dark for the rest of the session, with zero AppLogger entry, zero Crashlytics record, and no resubscription, while sibling channels keep working. The parallel own-profile path in sync_orchestrator.dart wires `onError: _onListenerError` (logs, forwards to Crashlytics, fires analytics) and `recoveryPullTriggers` (recovers from at-limit snapshots) -- the tutored path has neither, so it is both less observable and less self-healing than the path it was copied from.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/tutored_listener_supervisor.dart:97` — “_supervisor = ListenerSupervisor(
      source: source,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/tutored_listener_supervisor.dart:99` — “onEvent: (channel, payload) => _onEvent(localProfileId, channel, payload),
    );”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/sync_orchestrator.dart:478` — “onEvent: _onListenerEvent,
      onError: _onListenerError,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/listener_supervisor.dart:202` — “onError: (Object error, StackTrace stackTrace) {
          _onError?.call(channel, error, stackTrace);”
- **Fix:** Pass `onError` (log via AppLogger at minimum, consider triggering TutoredPullService.pull() on permission-denied) and `recoveryPullTriggers` into the ListenerSupervisor built in TutoredListenerSupervisor.attach(), mirroring SyncOrchestratorImpl.start().
- **Done when:** Unit test: a ListenerSource stub that emits a stream error during an attached tutored session asserts the error reaches a logger/callback, not silently dropped. · TutoredListenerSupervisor.attach() passes a non-null onError to ListenerSupervisor(...).
- **Labels:** EH-3, sync, tutored, observability · verifier corrections: Finding cites tutored_listener_supervisor.dart:97 for the 'source: source' line; actual file has '_supervisor = ListenerSupervisor(' at line 97 and 'source: source,' at line 98 -- one-line offset, immaterial to the claim

#### AUD-core-sync-13 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Write server timestamps for LWW ordering fields in FirestoreGatewayImpl's push* methods (FB-2)
- **Rule:** FB-2 · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 11 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md names `updatedAt` as the LWW comparison field for curriculum_tracks, goals, bookmarks and settings. pushTrack (line 337), pushSettings (316), pushBookmark (369) and pushGoal (562) all spread the caller's `data` -- which carries whatever client-clock `updated_at` the local write set -- straight through, and only add a separate `synced_at: FieldValue.serverTimestamp()` field that isn't the one the merger compares. pushLearnerProfile (line 417) shows the codebase already knows the right pattern: it explicitly overwrites `updated_at` itself with `FieldValue.serverTimestamp()` before sending. FB-2's own stated rationale is exact: 'two devices with skewed clocks writing client timestamps make last-write-wins non-deterministic -- the faster clock always wins and silently overwrites newer data.' A device with a fast or wrong clock editing a track/goal/bookmark/setting can have its stale edit incorrectly beat a genuinely later edit from another device, with the loss silent (no error, just the wrong value persisting until the next edit).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:337` — “..._stripInternalKeys(data),
      'synced_at': FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:316` — “..._stripInternalKeys(data),
      'synced_at': FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:369` — “..._stripInternalKeys(data),
      'synced_at': FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:562` — “..._stripInternalKeys(data),
      'synced_at': FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:417` — “..._stripInternalKeys(data),
      'updated_at': FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),”; `docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md:16` — “| `learner_profiles` | **LWW** | `updatedAt` | |
| `bookmarks` | **LWW** | `updatedAt` | |”; `docs/coding-standards.md:247` — “Every cross-device LWW ordering field is written as `FieldValue.serverTimestamp()`, never a client clock.”; `docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md:29` — “the device with the
strictly newer timestamp wins.” _(+3 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Apply the pushLearnerProfile pattern (server-side overwrite of the merger's LWW field) to pushTrack, pushSettings, pushBookmark, pushGoal and any other push* method whose entity is LWW-merged by a client-set timestamp field; confirm against core/sync/merge/*.dart which exact field each merger compares before changing it.
- **Done when:** Emulator test (per FB-2's own 'Enforce' note) asserts the persisted field each merger actually compares is a server Timestamp, not a client-supplied value, for tracks/goals/bookmarks/settings. · Audit grep: no client-clock value reaches a field a merger uses for cross-device LWW comparison, across firestore_gateway_impl.dart's push* methods.
- **Labels:** FB-2, clock-skew, sync, data-integrity · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches · verifier corrections: Two inaccuracies to correct, neither defeats the finding: (1) the docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md quote is real text but sits at lines 17-18, not line 16 (line 16 is the stage_definitions row). #### AUD-core-sync-14 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Add error handling and logging to resetFirestoreNetwork's disable/enable sequence in firestore_instance_provider.dart
- **Rule:** Nygard-lens: unguarded I/O fails halfway · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]

The connectivity-trigger caller in sync_orchestrator.dart (line ~611) does wrap this in try/catch+log, but the lifecycle/foreground-resume caller in lifecycle_observer.dart:147-148 does not — an exception there aborts the rest of the resume sequence (redetectTimezone, invalidateSacredCache, triggerPull) as an unhandled async error, silently skipping the resume pull.

      if (reset != null) await reset();”
- **Fix:** Wrap the disable/enable pair in try/catch inside resetFirestoreNetwork itself (so every caller gets the protection for free), log failures via AppLogger with a stable event code, and consider a bounded retry for enableNetwork() specifically so a mid-sequence failure doesn't leave the channel permanently disabled.
- **Done when:** resetFirestoreNetwork catches and logs failures from disableNetwork()/enableNetwork() instead of letting them propagate unhandled. · Unit test: stub FirebaseFirestore so enableNetwork() throws after disableNetwork() succeeds; assert the exception is caught/logged and does not abort the lifecycle-resume sequence (timezone redetect, sacred-cache invalidation, resume pull still run).

#### AUD-core-sync-17 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Batch OutboxProcessor's post-commit deleteRow/markAttempted cleanup instead of awaiting it per row
- **Rule:** DB-3 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]

- **Fix:** Add a bulk DAO method (e.g. deleteRows(List<int> ids) / markAttemptedBulk(List<int> ids, {required String error})) backed by a single batch()/DELETE...WHERE id IN(...) statement and call it once per commit/failure group instead of per row.

#### AUD-core-sync-20 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Extend FirestorePermissionDeniedException conversion beyond the 2 read call sites it currently covers
- **Rule:** Nygard lens (mandatory for this area) — permission-denied at every I/O point; EH-2 typed-exception boundary · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** _guardPermission (firestore_gateway_impl.dart:1197-1215) is the ONLY code in the app that ever throws FirestorePermissionDeniedException, and it wraps exactly 2 of this gateway's ~30 Firestore I/O methods — fetchPage (524) and fetchChildPage (1051), both reads, both with operation hardcoded to 'read'. None of the ~23 push* (write) methods route through it: pushStreak/pushSettings/pushTrack (288-337) issue raw .set() calls with no try/catch at all, and pushCompletionsBatch (246-285) wraps any commit failure — including permission-denied — as a generic SyncPushException instead. Traced end to end: OutboxProcessor absorbs every push failure internally (never rethrows to any AsyncValue/UI, so this is not a UI-facing bug), but the dedicated permission_denied analytics event in sync_orchestrator.dart (gated on `e is FirestorePermissionDeniedException`) therefore fires only from the pull path and never from an outbox push. The write path's only detector of this failure class is outbox_dao.dart's reviveIdentityDeadLetters, which pattern-matches raw persisted error text (`lastError.like('%permission-denied%')`) instead of a structured type — a duplicated, Firestore-SDK-wording-dependent re-derivation of the exact fact this exception exists to represent. This repo's own docs (on-device-preflight-cheatsheet.md, bug-hunt-findings-2026-05-31.md) call permission-denied on writes 'a known recurring failure mode in this project,' yet the typed signal for it covers roughly 1 in 15 of the gateway's I/O surface.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/exceptions/firestore_permission_denied_exception.dart:3` — “Thrown when a Firestore operation returns PERMISSION_DENIED.”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:1206` — “throw FirestorePermissionDeniedException(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:527` — “operation: 'read',”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:277` — “throw SyncPushException(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/outbox_dao.dart:149` — “(t.lastError.like('%permission-denied%') |”
- **Fix:** Route every push*/fetch* method in firestore_gateway_impl.dart through _guardPermission (or an equivalent shared wrapper) with an accurate operation value (read/write/delete) instead of only the 2 fetch methods, so FirestorePermissionDeniedException becomes the single source of truth for 'this failure was permission-denied' on both read and write paths. Then simplify outbox_dao.dart's reviveIdentityDeadLetters to check a structured signal instead of a LIKE-pattern on free text.
- **Done when:** count of _guardPermission( call sites in firestore_gateway_impl.dart increases beyond the current 2 to cover write (push*) methods · a new test asserts a push method (e.g. pushCompletionsBatch) surfaces FirestorePermissionDeniedException — not a generic SyncPushException/raw FirebaseException — when the underlying commit fails with code permission-denied · a test shows sync_orchestrator's permission_denied analytics event firing from a simulated outbox push failure, not only from pullOnLaunch
- **Labels:** sync, observability, nygard-lens, permission-denied

#### AUD-core-sync-21 · **P2** · SUSPECTED · Fix LearningLedgerMerger's fallback ULID generator to avoid a permanent same-millisecond collision loss
- **Rule:** Nygard: silent, non-self-healing data loss on a manufactured natural-key collision · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** This fallback (only used when a pulled row has no `ulid` — 'legacy data' pre-migration docs, per the file's own comment) is deterministic with zero entropy: two ledger rows completed in the same millisecond with no ulid produce the IDENTICAL synthetic id. LearningLedgerDao dedups on ulid via INSERT OR IGNORE, so the second row is silently dropped — permanently, since a retry regenerates the same colliding id every time (unlike the rest of this merge layer's failures, which self-heal on the next pull because the underlying condition changes). A bulk-mark flow (bulk_mark_screen.dart is a named churn hotspot) writing several legacy-shaped completions together is a plausible trigger.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/learning_ledger_merger.dart:112` — “String _makeUlid(DateTime ts) =>
      '${ts.millisecondsSinceEpoch.toRadixString(36).padLeft(10, '0').toUpperCase()}0000000000000000';”
- **Fix:** Add entropy to the fallback id (e.g. an index-within-batch or random suffix instead of a constant zero-padded tail), or skip rows with no ulid and no way to disambiguate instead of manufacturing a collidable one.
- **Done when:** Unit test: merge two distinct legacy (no-ulid) rows sharing the same completed_at millisecond — assert both are inserted, not deduplicated into one.
- **Labels:** sync, merge, data-loss, hygiene · verifier corrections: The bulk_mark_screen.dart trigger example is unsupported: local ledger writes always assign a real ULID via newUlid(now) (learning_ledger_repository_impl.dart:107,174), so bulk-marking today cannot produce a no-ulid row.

#### AUD-core-sync-23 · **P2** · SUSPECTED · Resolve outboxProcessor lazily in syncOrchestratorProvider instead of capturing it by value
- **Rule:** SM-6 lazy-resolver consistency / Nygard-lens: stale capture across DB swap · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** Every other volatile build-time dependency in this same constructor call (gateway, merge router, outbox DAO, identity status) is deliberately passed as a lazy `() => ref.read(...)` resolver specifically — per the inline comments at lines 136-137, 161-163 — 'so a DB swap (multi-account flow) is picked up without rebuilding the orchestrator singleton.' outboxProcessor is the one exception: it's read once (line 129) and stored as a plain value field. outboxProcessorProvider (outbox_providers.dart) watches userDatabaseProvider and rebuilds on a DB swap; database_provider.dart confirms userDatabaseProvider swaps via the independently-mutable accountDbFileNameProvider, decoupled from authStateProvider (the only thing syncOrchestratorProvider itself watches). If a DB swap can occur without authStateProvider's watched value also changing in the same tick, the orchestrator keeps draining through an OutboxProcessor bound to the pre-swap, superseded UserDatabase/outboxDao while its other lazily-resolved collaborators (gateway, merge router) may already be pointing at the new account — a split-identity state. Confirming this needs tracing whether the app's account-switch flow (account_actions.dart) can complete a DB swap before authStateProvider's emitted value settles to the new account.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/providers/sync_orchestrator_providers.dart:129` — “final outboxProcessor = ref.read(outboxProcessorProvider);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/providers/sync_orchestrator_providers.dart:160` — “outboxProcessor: outboxProcessor,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/providers/sync_orchestrator_providers.dart:164` — “resolveOutboxDao: () => ref.read(userDatabaseProvider).outboxDao,”
- **Fix:** Change the outboxProcessor parameter to a lazy `resolveOutboxProcessor: () => ref.read(outboxProcessorProvider)` resolver, matching resolveGateway/resolveMergeRouter/resolveOutboxDao, so it can't go stale relative to its siblings.
- **Done when:** syncOrchestratorProvider resolves outboxProcessor via a lazy resolver rather than a captured value. · Regression/integration test: trigger a userDatabaseProvider swap while syncOrchestratorProvider stays alive (authState unchanged) and assert the next drain operates against the new outboxDao's pending rows, not the pre-swap instance.
- **Labels:** sync, riverpod, multi-account, nygard · verifier corrections: 'gateway... may already be pointing at the new account' is wrong: firestoreGatewayProvider depends on authStateProvider, not userDatabaseProvider, so it stays old in lockstep with outboxProcessor during the window. The a

#### AUD-core-sync-24 · **P2** · SUSPECTED · Stop FirestoreGatewayImpl.pushGoal from using non-idempotent add() for id-less goals
- **Rule:** FB-4 / idempotent-write invariant · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x3] · filed P1, revised
- **Why:** Every other push* method here (pushCompletion, pushStreak, pushTrack, pushLedgerEntry...) derives a deterministic Firestore doc id so an outbox retry after a lost ack is a safe overwrite via set(merge:true). pushGoal is the one method that falls back to collection.add() -- a fresh random doc id -- whenever the payload carries no id/goal_id. outbox_sync_write_facade.dart's own _goalKey fallback (a composite curriculum_pct_timestamp key) proves this null case is real, not theoretical: it exists specifically to dedupe local enqueues of such goals. If the server commits the add() but the client never sees the ack (timeout, dropped connection -- exactly what the outbox's at-least-once retry exists to survive), the retry calls add() again and creates a second, permanent duplicate goal document in Firestore, which the pull path then merges back down as a duplicate goal locally.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:559` — “final docId = data['id']?.toString() ?? data['goal_id']?.toString();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:566` — “} else {

    if (id != null) return id;”
- **Fix:** Assign every goal a stable id before it is ever enqueued (mirror the ULID pattern already used for streak/ledger/points-ledger entries) and have pushGoal always do doc(id).set(merge:true); delete the add() branch.
- **Done when:** Regression test: call pushGoal twice with an id-less payload against a fake/emulator Firestore; assert exactly one document exists afterward. · pushGoal's add() branch is removed or provably unreachable.
- **Labels:** FB-4, idempotency, sync, data-integrity · verifier corrections: Downgrade to P2/SUSPECTED design-debt, not a live P1 defect: the add() branch and the docId-null path are dead code under every existing caller (goal_repository_impl.dart, local_data_upload_service.dart both always set a

#### AUD-core-sync-25 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Type the bare catch clauses in the merge layer so they stop swallowing Error subtypes
- **Rule:** EH-4 (typed `on X catch`; never catch Error subtypes) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Neither catch has an `on <Type>` clause, so both trap Error subtypes (TypeError, RangeError, AssertionError) alongside genuine Exceptions. Per EH-4's stated rationale, that masks real programming bugs introduced by a future edit to these exact files: instead of crashing loudly with a stack trace in dev/QA, a regression degrades silently to a 'sync_learner_profile_merge_row_failed' warning log (site 1) or a silently-emptied schedule days-of-week list inside _encodeSchedule (site 2).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/learner_profile_merger.dart:74` — “} catch (e, stackTrace) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/drift_merge_store.dart:701` — “} catch (_) {”
- **Fix:** Narrow both to `on Exception catch` (or the specific expected types, e.g. FormatException/SqliteException) and let genuine Error subtypes propagate and crash loudly.
- **Done when:** avoid_catches_without_on_clauses + avoid_catching_errors lints (EH-4's stated Pending checkers in coding-standards.md) pass for these two files. · Existing mergers_test.dart / learning_ledger_merger_test.dart suites still pass after narrowing.
- **Labels:** sync, error-handling, EH-4

#### AUD-core-sync-26 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Type the catch/catchError clauses across sync_orchestrator.dart, pull_pipeline.dart and tutored_listener_supervisor.dart (EH-4)
- **Rule:** EH-4 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 16 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** All 16 sites catch without an `on <Type>` clause, so each also catches Error subtypes (TypeError, StateError, RangeError, NoSuchMethodError) as if they were the transient I/O failures the surrounding code is designed to shrug off. Every one of these swallows-and-logs (the pull_pipeline.dart and tutored_listener_supervisor.dart sites don't rethrow at all; most of the sync_orchestrator.dart sites log a warning and return/fall through). Concrete cost: if a future change introduces a null-dereference or bad cast inside a merger reached from the 60s periodic drain, a recovery-pull trigger, or a listener dispatch, it gets caught here, logged once per occurrence as an ordinary 'drain failed'/'listener error' warning, and never crashes or reaches Crashlytics as a fatal -- masking a real regression indefinitely instead of surfacing it. (Two other sites -- sync_orchestrator.dart:768 and :939 -- were deliberately excluded from this list: :768 delegates to a typed `_isLocalDatabaseError` classifier before deciding to swallow, and :939 rethrows after converting to a status; both already behave like the fix this finding asks for elsewhere.)

- **Fix:** Narrow each listed catch to `on Exception catch` (Exception still covers FirebaseException/TimeoutException/SocketException etc.) so Error subtypes propagate to the zone's uncaught-error handler instead of being absorbed; use sync_orchestrator.dart:768's classifier-based pattern as the template for guards that need to stay broad on purpose.
- **Done when:** Enable avoid_catches_without_on_clauses + avoid_catching_errors once dart run custom_lint is unblocked; all 16 sites pass. · A test that injects a StateError into a merger/dispatch call reached from one of these paths shows the error propagating (not silently logged-and-continued).
- **Labels:** EH-4, error-handling, sync

#### AUD-core-sync-33 · **P3** · SUSPECTED · Defensively copy SyncPushException.committed so the partial-commit invariant can't be violated by a future caller
- **Rule:** Evans lens — invariant enforced in one place, not by caller convention · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** SyncPushException.committed exists specifically so OutboxProcessor can tell which outbox rows genuinely landed before a batch failed, so committed rows are 'never re-pushed or dead-lettered' (per this file's own docstring, H3). That invariant currently holds only because the single production call site remembers to wrap the list in List.unmodifiable(pushed) before throwing — the exception class itself accepts any List<String>, including a live mutable reference, with no internal defensive copy. A future call site (or a test double standing in for one) that passes a growable list it keeps appending to after constructing the exception would silently corrupt the partial-commit accounting this type exists to protect, with no compiler or runtime signal that anything went wrong.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/exceptions/sync_push_exception.dart:21` — “final List<String> committed;”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:278` — “committed: List.unmodifiable(pushed),”
- **Fix:** Copy defensively inside the constructor (e.g. an initializer that wraps committed in List.unmodifiable(committed)) so the guarantee doesn't depend on every future caller remembering to do it themselves.
- **Done when:** a new unit test constructs SyncPushException with a growable list, mutates the original list after construction, and asserts .committed is unaffected
- **Labels:** defensive-programming, sync, data-integrity

#### AUD-core-time-01 · **P3** · SUSPECTED · core/time/local_day_clock.dart's currentLocalDayClock global has no compiler-enforced set/reset pairing for tests
- **Rule:** SM-7 spirit (no global/static mutable singletons) / TQ-6 hermetic tests · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** This mutable top-level variable backs DateTimeFactory, which is called from 15+ production sites across DAOs/repositories/mergers (e.g. track_dao.dart, a churn hotspot, calls it 8 times). Test isolation relies entirely on every caller of useLocalDayClock() remembering to pair it with `tearDown(resetLocalDayClock)` per the doc comment's 'MUST' — nothing in the type system enforces this. A test file that calls useLocalDayClock() without the tearDown pairing would silently freeze time for every later test in that file/isolate, producing flaky failures unrelated to the code under test. I checked the two actual test files that use it (only outbox_processor_test.dart and one other) and both correctly pair set/reset via `tearDown(resetLocalDayClock)`, so this is a latent, convention-enforced risk rather than a demonstrated failure today.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/time/local_day_clock.dart:73` — “LocalDayClock currentLocalDayClock = const SystemLocalDayClock();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/time/local_day_clock.dart:77` — “/// reset to the default in `tearDown`.”
- **Fix:** Add a shared test helper (e.g. `withFakeClock(seed, body)`) that calls `addTearDown(resetLocalDayClock)` itself so individual tests can't forget the reset, and migrate the existing 2 call sites to it.
- **Done when:** A shared test helper pairs useLocalDayClock with an auto-registered tearDown reset · Existing call sites in outbox_processor_test.dart (and any sibling) migrated to the helper
- **Labels:** sm-7, test-hygiene, global-state

#### AUD-core-widgets-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Route AppErrorView/ErrorDisplay/PinEntryWidget user-facing strings through AppLocalizations instead of hardcoded English
- **Rule:** AX-2 / EH-5 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 18 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** This is a Hebrew-first RTL app (docs/hebrew-terms.md, device-locale Hebrew testing in project memory), yet these 3 core widgets never call AppLocalizations — 18 literal English occurrences across the 3 files. AppErrorView is the documented canonical replacement for ad-hoc error UI and is used from 16+ screens (dashboard, learning, bulk-mark, profile-picker among them); ErrorDisplay is live in 4 progress screens; PinEntryWidget gates every parent-mode entry. Any Hebrew-locale user who goes offline, hits a permission error, or mistypes the parent PIN 3 times sees raw English text ("Too many failed attempts", "Retry", "Something went wrong") embedded in an otherwise-Hebrew UI. This isn't a missing-infrastructure gap: app_en.arb already has `actionRetry: "Retry"` (line 1122) and an ICU-ready `tutorPinLockedOut: "Too many attempts. Locked for {minutes} minute(s)."` (line 2765) for the exact lockout-countdown case — the existing keys are simply not called. Line 163's `subtitle: error.message` additionally pipes a raw `AppException.message` (declared as "Human-readable description" in app_exception.dart) straight to the UI, which is exactly what EH-5 forbids.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/core/widgets/app_error_view.dart:112` — “label: const Text('Retry'),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/widgets/app_error_view.dart:163` — “subtitle: error.message,”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/widgets/app_error_view.dart:193` — “title: 'Something went wrong',”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/widgets/app_error_view.dart:171` — “title: 'Access denied',”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/widgets/app_error_view.dart:139` — “child: const Text('Report this issue'),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/widgets/error_display.dart:52` — “label: const Text('Retry'),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/widgets/pin_entry_widget.dart:14` — “this.title = 'Enter PIN',”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/widgets/pin_entry_widget.dart:146` — “'Too many failed attempts',” _(+5 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Thread AppLocalizations into AppErrorView._configFor (pass context/l10n in), replace error_display.dart's literal 'Retry' with l10n.actionRetry, and replace pin_entry_widget.dart's 4 literals with new/existing ARB keys (reuse the tutorPinLockedOut ICU pattern for the minute(s) string). ### features/account  (24 findings — 1 P0 / 4 P1 / 14 P2 / 5 P3)

#### AUD-account-01 · **P0** · CONFIRMED · account_lifecycle_service.dart removeCloudFromDevice() must verify the outbox is drained before deleting the local DB file
- **Rule:** AU-3 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** The outbox (tier-gated to cloud-born accounts, features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart) queues Firestore writes locally until drained; those rows are the only copy of a mutation until push succeeds. removeCloudFromDevice() is reachable mid-session via swipe-to-dismiss in the Account Picker with zero connectivity check and zero OutboxDao.depth() check, then unconditionally deletes the account's entire local Drift file (which holds the outbox table) and the registry row. A child completing offline study sessions, then swiping 'Remove from device' while those completions are still queued, permanently loses that specific progress even though the confirmation dialog explicitly promises 'Your cloud data is safe — you can sign back in anytime,' and the method's own doc comment claims the same. This is exactly the credential-less/offline-account data-loss territory the standard calls out, just triggered by an explicit destructive action rather than a bare signOut().
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/domain/services/account_lifecycle_service.dart:32` — “/// Firestore data and Firebase Auth are NOT touched — user can
  /// sign back in on any device and recover everything.”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/domain/services/account_lifecycle_service.dart:59` — “_deleteDbFile(account.dbFileName);
    await _registry.removeAccount(accountId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_picker_screen.dart:829` — “await service.removeCloudFromDevice(account.accountId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/l10n/app_en.arb:1100` — “"accountRemoveFromDeviceBody": "Your cloud data is safe — you can sign back in anytime.",”
- **Fix:** Before _deleteDbFile in removeCloudFromDevice, sum OutboxDao.depth(profileId) across every profile under the account (the outbox is per-profile, the account can have multiple learner profiles) and block or force a bounded drain-and-wait when depth > 0, surfacing a clear 'N changes not backed up yet' warning instead of silently proceeding. Stop promising unconditional safety in the ARB copy until this is true.
- **Done when:** Regression test: seed a cloud-born account with ≥1 undrained outbox row on any of its profiles, call AccountLifecycleService.removeCloudFromDevice, and assert it refuses/blocks rather than deleting the DB file. · Regression test: with outbox depth 0 for every profile under the account, removeCloudFromDevice still succeeds (no happy-path regression). · account_picker_screen.dart's swipe-to-remove flow surfaces the pending-outbox count (or blocks) before invoking removeCloudFromDevice for a cloud tile.
- **Labels:** auth, AU-3, data-loss, outbox, offline-account · verifier corrections: Rule AU-3's exact text ('Never signOut() an anonymous (unlinked) user that still has unsynced outbox entries') does not literally cover this case: the account here is cloud-born/linked (account.accountTier.isCloud, has f

#### AUD-account-02 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Add ref.mounted guards and Timer disposal to SignInController's autoDispose async flows
- **Rule:** SM-4 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** This 1016-line Notifier<SignInState> is registered autoDispose and performs 84 awaited operations per file (multi-second retries, 8s Firestore timeouts, 350ms polling loops) yet contains zero occurrences of 'mounted' anywhere in the file — every method touches `state`/`_ref` after an await with no disposal guard. If the user backs out of the sign-in screen mid-request (a completely ordinary action while a 'signing in...' spinner shows), autoDispose tears the notifier down; when the pending await resolves and the code does `state = SignInError(...)` or `_ref.read(...)`, Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException. The watchdog Timer compounds this: it is only cancelled in signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle's own `finally` block, never via ref.onDispose, so if the notifier is disposed mid-flight the Timer keeps running and fires `state = ...` against an already-disposed notifier up to 45s later. The codebase already has an established ref.mounted convention elsewhere (dashboard_providers.dart, notification_providers.dart, sacred_location_provider.dart all use it), so this file's total omission is an inconsistency, not a repo-wide non-issue.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/notifiers/sign_in_controller.dart:1013` — “final signInControllerProvider =
    NotifierProvider.autoDispose<SignInController, SignInState>(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/notifiers/sign_in_controller.dart:706` — “final watchdog = Timer(const Duration(seconds: 15), () {
      if (state is SignInSubmitting) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/notifiers/sign_in_controller.dart:878` — “} finally {
      watchdog.cancel();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/notifiers/sign_in_controller.dart:754` — “await _navigateAfterSignIn(router);
        state = const SignInIdle();”; `learning_tracker/test/features/account/presentation/notifiers/sign_in_controller_test.dart:207` — “final container = _makeContainer(authRepo: mockAuth);
        addTearDown(container.dispose);”
- **Fix:** After every await that precedes a `state =` or `_ref.read(...)` write, add `if (!ref.mounted) return;`. Register `ref.onDispose(watchdog.cancel)` immediately after each Timer is created (both the 15s and 45s watchdogs).
- **Done when:** A notifier test that disposes the ProviderContainer (or pops the route) while signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle is mid-await asserts no exception escapes and no post-dispose state write occurs · Watchdog Timers are cancelled by ref.onDispose in addition to the existing finally-block cancel
- **Labels:** sm-4, riverpod, crash-risk, autodispose · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches

#### AUD-account-03 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · AuthStateNotifier._init() must guard reloadCurrentUser() so an offline cold start cannot hang the session state forever
- **Rule:** AU-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl.reloadCurrentUser() calls User.reload(), a network round-trip that throws FirebaseAuthException(network-request-failed) when offline — an entirely ordinary cold-start condition for an offline-first app (this exact file set otherwise engineers carefully around it, e.g. sign_in_controller.dart wraps every Firestore/Firebase call in try/catch and timeouts). Nothing in AuthStateNotifier._init() catches this; the exception escapes the fire-and-forget call from build(), so `state` never advances past AuthState.initializing(). AuthGuard never touches Firebase and lets onboarded users straight through to the app shell, which reads authStateProvider downstream — so a returning cloud-born user opening the app with no connectivity can be stuck on an unresolved session state indefinitely, directly violating the SessionStatus.initializing doc comment's own 'must not hang' contract (a lesson the codebase already learned once for the router guard per the '19.6 startup hardening' reference, but that didn't carry over to this newer Notifier-based path).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/providers/auth_state_provider.dart:32` — “if (firebaseUser != null) {
      final refreshed = await authRepo.reloadCurrentUser();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/domain/models/auth_state.dart:9` — “/// App has not yet resolved the initial session (splash window).
  /// Must not hang — see 19.6 startup hardening.”
- **Fix:** Wrap the Firebase-touching logic in _init() (at minimum the reloadCurrentUser() call) in try/catch; on failure, fall back to trusting the cached bare currentUser or the local-born row rather than leaving state unset, mirroring the defensive timeout/try-catch pattern already used elsewhere in sign_in_controller.dart.
- **Done when:** Regression test: mock AuthRepository.reloadCurrentUser() to throw (simulating an offline reload()), build AuthStateNotifier, and assert state resolves to a terminal SessionStatus within a bounded time instead of remaining initializing indefinitely. · On-device check: cold-start the app in airplane mode with a previously-active cloud-born session and confirm no indefinite splash/loading hang.
- **Labels:** auth, AU-4, availability, offline-first · verifier corrections: The cited rule AU-4 is misapplied. AU-4's actual text/Why ("Gate startup/session routing on authStateChanges()/idTokenChanges() streams, never a bare currentUser read... currentUser can be null before auth finishes initi

#### AUD-account-04 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Extract the duplicated _extractFirebaseCode regex parser out of MagicLinkService and UpgradeToCloudService
- **Rule:** Fowler: duplicated code; layering tension with Rule 3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [2x2] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** Both files independently reimplement 'parse a Firebase error code out of an exception's toString()' via the identical regex, because Rule 3 blocks these features/account/{domain,data} files from importing FirebaseAuthException directly and matching its typed .code field. The fallback is fragile: if a Firebase Auth SDK bump changes the exception's string format so it no longer wraps the code in literal brackets, _extractFirebaseCode silently returns null everywhere at once — in upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart this means the 'email-already-in-use' retry-merge branch falls through to rethrow, and the guided merge flow silently stops firing, surfacing a raw exception to the user instead. The same helper is also duplicated at 3 more sites repo-wide (signup_screen.dart, sign_in_controller.dart, upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart), confirming this is a systemic gap rather than a one-off.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/data/services/magic_link_service.dart:238` — “final match = RegExp(r'\[([a-z-]+)\]').firstMatch(str);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/domain/services/upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart:374` — “final match = RegExp(r'\[([a-z-]+)\]').firstMatch(str);”
- **Fix:** Factor the regex parser into one shared, unit-tested helper (e.g. core/utils/firebase_error_code.dart, which only touches strings so it doesn't trip Rule 3) that all current call sites import.
- **Done when:** one shared, unit-tested extractFirebaseCode(Object e) utility exists · magic_link_service.dart and upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart delegate to it instead of each defining their own regex copy
- **Labels:** duplication, fowler, layering · verifier corrections: Traced firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart:78-87 (raw FirebaseAuthException propagates unwrapped) and upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart:193-274 (its own duplicate of the same buggy regex also gates the EmailCollisionException cat
