#### AUD-account-06 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Add try/catch around onSendAgain/onVerified in EmailVerificationConfirmPanel and un-skip the C6/E5 regression tests
- **Rule:** EH-2/EH-3 (typed exceptions handled at the boundary; no log-less catch) discovered via disclosed-but-unfixed test skips · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** `_wrapSendAgain`/`_wrapVerified` use try/finally with no catch, so any exception from the injected callback propagates as an unhandled async error instead of a graceful error state. The onVerified callback built in sign_in_controller.dart's buildVerificationCallback calls _refreshAndCheckVerified -> authRepo.reloadCurrentUser() with no surrounding try/catch, so a transient network error while the user is mid email-verification is a real, reachable path to this unhandled exception -- not just a theoretical one. Both regression tests that would catch this (C6, E5) are disclosed but left skip:true with no Linear id, so the gap is invisible to anyone not reading test source.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/widgets/email_verification_confirm_panel.dart:165` — “Future<void> _wrapSendAgain() async {
    setState(() => _sendingAgain = true);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/widgets/email_verification_confirm_panel.dart:167` — “try {
      await widget.onSendAgain();”; `learning_tracker/test/features/account/presentation/widgets/email_verification_confirm_panel_test.dart:520` — “// BUG: _wrapSendAgain uses try/finally but not try/catch, so exceptions
      // from onSendAgain propagate as unhandled async errors, cras”; `learning_tracker/test/features/account/presentation/widgets/email_verification_confirm_panel_test.dart:525` — “skip: true,”
- **Fix:** Add a catch clause to both wrapper methods that resets the loading flag and surfaces the failure (e.g. via a callback/snackbar, matching the pattern already used for signOut() failures elsewhere in this feature), then remove skip: true from C6 and E5.
- **Done when:** _wrapSendAgain and _wrapVerified catch and handle exceptions from the injected callbacks (no bare try/finally). · C6 and E5 in email_verification_confirm_panel_test.dart run (skip: true removed) and pass.
- **Labels:** error-handling, unhandled-exception, untracked-bug · verifier corrections: EH-2/EH-3 rule-fit is a bit loose (no catch clause exists to call 'empty/log-less'; EH-2 is about layer-boundary conversion) but the underlying defect and reachability are independently confirmed.

#### AUD-account-07 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Cache the account list Future instead of constructing it fresh inside AccountPickerScreen.build()
- **Rule:** PF-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** registry.getAllAccounts() is called directly inside `Widget build()`, which returns a brand-new Future object on every rebuild. FutureBuilder tracks futures by identity, so any unrelated rebuild of this ConsumerWidget (a ref.watch(accountDbFileNameProvider) change from switching accounts, a locale/theme change, or any ancestor rebuild) restarts the FutureBuilder into ConnectionState.waiting — flashing the loading spinner over the already-rendered account list and re-querying the device registry — the textbook 'Future-in-build' Flutter anti-pattern.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_picker_screen.dart:59` — “child: FutureBuilder<List<DeviceAccount>>(
          future: registry.getAllAccounts(),”
- **Fix:** Hoist the fetch behind a FutureProvider/AsyncNotifier (e.g. deviceAccountsProvider watched via ref.watch), or convert to ConsumerStatefulWidget and cache the Future in State so its identity is stable across rebuilds.
- **Done when:** A widget test triggers an unrelated provider rebuild while AccountPickerScreen is mounted and asserts the list does not revert to the loading spinner and getAllAccounts() is not invoked a second time
- **Labels:** pf-3, performance, futurebuilder

#### AUD-account-11 · **P2** · SUSPECTED · Guard AuthStateNotifier._init() against I/O exceptions so auth state never hangs at AuthState.initializing() forever
- **Rule:** SM-5 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3] · filed P1, revised
- **Why:** build() kicks _init() fire-and-forget and returns AuthState.initializing() immediately; _init() then awaits 4+ Firebase/DAO calls (reloadCurrentUser, findCloudBornByFirebaseUid, getUserProfileByFirebaseUid, upgradeLocalToCloud, findByTier) with zero try/catch anywhere in the method. AuthState has exactly 3 statuses (initializing/signedOut/signedIn) — there is no error state — so any exception during _init() (a DB read failure, a Firebase reload throwing) is an unhandled Future rejection that leaves sessionStatus permanently stuck at `initializing`. This directly contradicts the domain model's own doc comment: 'Must not hang — see 19.6 startup hardening.' Every screen gating on authStateProvider (router, app_shell, sign-in flows) would show a permanent splash/loading state with no retry path, recoverable only by force-killing the app. EH-1's global PlatformDispatcher.onError would log the exception, but nothing resets `state`, so the hang persists regardless of logging.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/providers/auth_state_provider.dart:21` — “_init();
    return const AuthState.initializing();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/providers/auth_state_provider.dart:32` — “if (firebaseUser != null) {
      final refreshed = await authRepo.reloadCurrentUser();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/domain/models/auth_state.dart:9` — “/// App has not yet resolved the initial session (splash window).
  /// Must not hang — see 19.6 startup hardening.”
- **Fix:** Wrap _init()'s body in try/catch (or convert the class to a plain function-style Future<AuthState> build via AsyncNotifier<AuthState> + AsyncValue.guard); on any caught exception, log via AppLogger and fall back to `state = const AuthState.signedOut()` rather than leaving `initializing` unresolved.
- **Done when:** _init() cannot leave sessionStatus at initializing on any exception path — it resolves to signedIn or signedOut every time, with the failure logged via AppLogger. · Regression test: override authRepositoryProvider/userDatabaseProvider with a fake that throws from reloadCurrentUser() (and separately from the DAO) during _init(); assert authStateProvider settles to a terminal state within the test, not stuck at initializing. · Rule-0 checker: none exists yet; add a heuristic grep/custom_lint (once custom_lint is unbroken) flagging a Notifier's build() that calls an unawaited private async method with zero try/catch in that method's body.
- **Labels:** sm-5, riverpod, error-handling, auth, startup-hang · verifier corrections: Cited rule SM-5 governs AsyncValue<T>-typed provider state (AsyncLoading/AsyncValue.guard) and explicitly bans manual try/catch state assignment; AuthStateNotifier's state is a custom AuthState (not AsyncValue), confirme

#### AUD-account-13 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Log the swallowed deleteAccountData Cloud Function failure in AccountManagementService._deleteFirestoreUserData (EH-3 log-less catch)

If the deleteAccountData Cloud Function fails during account deletion -- network error, quota, not-yet-deployed, permission-denied -- nothing is recorded anywhere (no Crashlytics, no Talker/AppLogger), so there is zero telemetry on failures of the primary Firestore-deletion path for a 'delete my account and my data' request. Verified account_management_service_test.dart has no test that stubs this call to throw and asserts on logging. - **Fix:** Add an AppLogger.error(...) call (uid only, no other PII) inside the catch block; add a test that stubs a throwing httpsCallable and asserts the log call fired.

#### AUD-account-14 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Migrate SignInController's hand-rolled Idle/Submitting/Error state to AsyncNotifier + AsyncValue.guard
- **Rule:** SM-5 · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** SignInController extends plain `Notifier<SignInState>` (a hand-written sealed union: SignInIdle/SignInSubmitting/SignInError) instead of `AsyncNotifier<void>`, then hand-manages the loading/error lifecycle with ~15 manual `state = ...` assignments spread across try/catch/finally blocks in signInWithEmail and signInWithGoogle — duplicating exactly what AsyncValue.guard provides for free. This maps cleanly onto AsyncValue<void> (AsyncLoading=Submitting, AsyncData(null)=Idle, AsyncError=Error) but the team hand-rolled it instead. The class's own DG-GAUTH-01 comment documents a previously-shipped bug caused by exactly this pattern: a code path where signInWithGoogle() completed without throwing but left currentUser null previously fell through with 'zero feedback' (state silently stayed at whatever it was rather than transitioning to Error) — proof this hand-rolled machinery has already let a state-transition gap through undetected by the type system. Any new branch added to this 1017-line method carries the same risk; AsyncValue.guard would make 'forgot to set error state' structurally much harder.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/notifiers/sign_in_controller.dart:704` — “state = const SignInSubmitting();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/notifiers/sign_in_controller.dart:906` — “// DG-GAUTH-01: signInWithGoogle() returned without throwing (no
        // user-cancel / interrupt) but left currentUser null — a silent JW”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/notifiers/sign_in_controller.dart:1013` — “final signInControllerProvider =
    NotifierProvider.autoDispose<SignInController, SignInState>(”
- **Fix:** Migrate to `class SignInController extends AsyncNotifier<void>` (or keep the SignInIdle/Submitting/Error shape but derive it FROM an underlying AsyncValue via a getter) so state transitions on the unhappy path are guaranteed by the framework rather than manually tracked across ~15 call sites.
- **Done when:** No code path in signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle can leave `state` at SignInSubmitting after the method's Future completes (success or failure) — verified structurally by the AsyncNotifier/AsyncValue.guard migration rather than by manual review. · Regression test: extend the existing ensureCloudEmailVerifiedForTest-style coverage with a case asserting that EVERY awaited external call, if it throws, ends in `state is SignInError`/`AsyncError` — not silently at Idle/Submitting. · Rule-0 checker: once custom_lint is unbroken, add a rule flagging hand-rolled sealed `*State` classes with Idle/Submitting/Error (or Loading/Success/Failure)-shaped variants used as Notifier state as SM-5 AsyncNotifier-migration candidates.
- **Labels:** sm-5, riverpod, auth, sign-in, tech-debt · verifier corrections: DG-GAUTH-01 comment (L906-910) actually describes a missed postcondition check (googleUser == null after a successful call), not a case where state 'silently stayed' un-transitioned — the prior bug explicitly returned Si

#### AUD-account-15 · **P2** · SUSPECTED · Remove the fixed height:32 on OfflineTopBanner's Container so large text-scale doesn't clip it
- **Rule:** AX-4 (no fixed heights on text wrappers) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** The banner's Container is given a tight height:32 which forces the same tight cross-axis height onto the Row wrapping the cloud-off Icon and the offline-message Text. The app sets no textScaler clamp anywhere (grep-confirmed repo-wide), so under a standard OS large-text accessibility setting the Text needs more than 32 logical pixels; because Container does not clip by default, the text would paint outside the 32px band, visually overlapping the AppBar/content around it rather than wrapping or growing the banner.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/widgets/offline_top_banner.dart:30` — “width: double.infinity,
                height: 32,”
- **Fix:** Let the banner size to its child's intrinsic height (drop the fixed height, or express it as a minHeight), and add a widget test that pumps OfflineTopBanner under a scaled MediaQuery (TextScaler.linear(1.6)+) and asserts no overflow/clip.
- **Done when:** a widget/golden test pumps OfflineTopBanner at textScaler >= 1.6x and asserts the rendered content fits within its layout bounds · the banner Container no longer hard-codes height:32
- **Labels:** accessibility, ax-4

#### AUD-account-17 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Stop leaking raw English InvalidInputException.reason to users; unify the diverged 6-vs-8 password-length rule
- **Rule:** EH-5 (stable codes, never pre-formatted human messages) + Evans invariant-in-one-place · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** InvalidInputException.reason is a hardcoded English string ('invalid format', 'must be at least 8 characters') and signup_screen.dart's `on InvalidInputException catch (e) { _showError(e.reason); }` (used by both _signUpCloud and _signUpLocal) renders it straight to the UI with no AppLocalizations pass — proven by this batch's own test asserting the literal English substring appears. For a bilingual EN/HE app, a Hebrew-locale user hitting this path sees untranslated English. The bug is latent today only because the sole live caller of LocalAuthService.signUp (_createOfflineAccount) always supplies a synthetic, always-valid UUID email/password — but the underlying invariant has already drifted: the form-level validator (auth_validators.validatePassword) accepts 6+ characters while LocalAuthService._minPasswordLength requires 8, so a form-valid 6-7 character password fed through any future real caller of LocalAuthService.signUp would throw this untranslated exception.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/domain/services/local_auth_service.dart:129` — “throw const InvalidInputException('email', 'invalid format');”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/onboarding/domain/validators/auth_validators.dart:24` — “if (value.length < 6) {
    return 'Password must be at least 6 characters';”; `learning_tracker/test/features/account/onboarding/presentation/screens/signup_screen_l1_test.dart:805` — “expect(find.textContaining('invalid format'), findsOneWidget);”
- **Fix:** Give InvalidInputException (and siblings) a stable code/enum instead of a free-text reason, and have signup_screen.dart resolve it via AppLocalizations the same way _mapAuthError already does for Firebase codes; extract one shared minimum-password-length constant used by both auth_validators.dart and local_auth_service.dart.
- **Done when:** InvalidInputException exposes a typed code instead of (or alongside) a raw English reason string · signup_screen.dart resolves the code via AppLocalizations before showing it · auth_validators.dart and local_auth_service.dart reference one shared minimum-password-length constant · regression test: a 6-7 character password does not throw InvalidInputException through any LocalAuthService.signUp caller
- **Labels:** i18n, eh-5, duplication

#### AUD-account-18 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Watch reactive auth state instead of ref.read-ing currentUser inside _AccountTileState.build()
- **Rule:** SM-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** SM-3 requires ref.watch in build and ref.read only in callbacks, precisely because a ref.read snapshot of a mutable getter (`.currentUser`, which changes on sign-in/out/re-auth without the authRepositoryProvider instance itself changing) is only re-evaluated when something else this widget DOES watch happens to force a rebuild — not when the underlying session actually changes. The tile's 'valid session' vs 'sign in again' pill/warning-icon can go stale after an auth event (e.g. a sibling tile's re-auth flow) that doesn't independently invalidate this tile.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_picker_screen.dart:274` — “final fbUser = ref.read(authRepositoryProvider).currentUser;”
- **Fix:** Replace with a watched, narrow selector, e.g. `ref.watch(authStateProvider.select((s) => s.currentUser?.firebaseUid))`, so the tile is reactive to session changes.
- **Done when:** A widget test changes the live Firebase session via a provider override while the picker is mounted and asserts the affected tile's badge updates without an unrelated rebuild trigger
- **Labels:** sm-3, riverpod, stale-ui

#### AUD-account-19 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Wire AuthStateNotifier to authStateChanges() instead of leaving a shadowed, unused stream-based authStateProvider
- **Rule:** AU-4 · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** auth_providers.dart defines a genuinely stream-backed authStateProvider (Stream<AppUser?> authState(ref) => ref.watch(authRepositoryProvider).onAuthStateChanged()) — exactly the AU-4-compliant primitive. But the provider that actually drives session routing everywhere (AuthGuard, AppShell, this screen) is the differently-implemented, identically-named authStateProvider generated from AuthStateNotifier, which never watches or listens to that stream — forcing every screen needing both to hide/alias one of them (see the 'hide authStateProvider' import here and the 'as auth_state' alias in sign_in_controller.dart/signup_screen.dart). If Firebase invalidates a session server-side (disabled account, revoked refresh token, forced sign-out elsewhere) while the app is running, nothing re-derives AuthStateNotifier's state from that change — the app keeps believing the user is signed in until an unrelated explicit action happens to call reload/signOut. account_picker_screen.dart:274 shows the same non-reactive pattern at tile-badge granularity: hasValidSession is a one-shot ref.read(...).currentUser snapshot, not derived from the stream.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_picker_screen.dart:19` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/account/presentation/providers/auth_providers.dart'
    hide authStateProvider;”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_picker_screen.dart:274` — “final fbUser = ref.read(authRepositoryProvider).currentUser;”
- **Fix:** Either delete the dead stream-based authState/authStateProvider if genuinely unused, or have AuthStateNotifier subscribe to it in build() so live Firebase-side session changes propagate into routing state, removing the need for every consumer to route around the name collision.
- **Done when:** authStateProvider resolves to exactly one declaration reachable without hide/as workarounds across the codebase. · Regression test: emit a value on the mocked authStateChanges() stream after AuthStateNotifier has already resolved to signedIn, and assert the notifier's state updates without requiring an explicit signOut()/mutation call.
- **Labels:** auth, AU-4, dead-code, riverpod · verifier corrections: Minor: AuthGuard (app/router/guards/auth_guard.dart) does not itself read authStateProvider — its own comment says session status is 'owned by AuthStateNotifier, read downstream by individual screens'; AuthGuard only gat

#### AUD-account-20 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Centralize the minimum-password-length constant shared by the UI validator and LocalAuthService
- **Rule:** Evans ubiquitous-language / invariant re-derivation · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]

Today the two never collide end-to-end — the offline-signup path that reaches LocalAuthService.signUp always passes a synthetic UUID password, never the user-typed one gated by the 6-char validator — but the values being a single conceptual invariant with two different numbers is a landmine for the next call site that wires a real user-typed password through both layers (client says valid at 6-7 chars, domain then throws InvalidInputException).

#### AUD-account-21 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Give SignInActions' TapGestureRecognizer a disposal owner instead of rebuilding it every build()
- **Rule:** Flutter widget lifecycle hygiene · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** SignInActions is a StatelessWidget, so every build() (e.g. each time isLoading flips) allocates a brand-new TapGestureRecognizer that nothing ever calls .dispose() on. - **Labels:** hygiene, flutter-lifecycle

  const AuthState({”

#### AUD-account-23 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Reconcile AccountManagementService.signOut()'s documented 'soft sign-out' with its always-hard-sign-out callers
- **Rule:** AU-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** AccountManagementService.signOut()'s doc comment claims it deliberately keeps the Firebase token cached specifically so Epic 21.9 AC2 (tap an account tile → dashboard in <200ms) keeps working. Its only two callers (showSignOutConfirmation, showDeleteLocalAccountFlow, both in account_actions.dart) immediately follow it with a genuinely hard authRepositoryProvider.signOut()/authStateProvider.notifier.signOut(), so the fast-resume behavior the comment describes is unreachable from Settings > Sign Out today. This is a stale/misleading comment rather than a functional bug (the actual hard sign-out is arguably the safer choice for an explicit Sign Out action), but it risks a future edit assuming the token survives this call, and no sign-out path anywhere in this batch tells the user whether unsynced changes are pending before ending the session.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/domain/services/account_management_service.dart:29` — “/// Soft sign-out — clears the in-app session so the user sees the
  /// account picker on next launch, but leaves Firebase's cached”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/utils/account_actions.dart:188` — “// Hard sign-out: clear Firebase session so the user must re-authenticate
    // on next launch rather than being silently resumed via cache”
- **Fix:** Update the doc comment to reflect that Settings > Sign Out is always hard, and note where (if anywhere) the soft path is actually exercised — or restore the soft path for the scenario it was designed for.
- **Done when:** Doc comment on AccountManagementService.signOut() matches an actual, tested call path, or the soft/hard distinction is removed from the comment.
- **Labels:** auth, AU-4, hygiene, doc-drift · verifier corrections: AU-4 tag is a loose fit — this is a stale-comment/doc-accuracy issue, not stream-vs-bare-currentUser session routing; no AU-1..5 rule precisely covers 'keep doc comments in sync with behavior.' Doesn't undermine the find

#### AUD-account-24 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Stop interpolating raw exception text into the sign-up failure l10n message
- **Rule:** custom_lint no_e_to_string_in_ui (currently non-enforcing) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]

- **Done when:** signUpFailed(...) or its replacement no longer receives e.toString() · Once custom_lint is repaired (tracked separately), no_e_to_string_in_ui passes clean on this file
- **Labels:** custom-lint, no_e_to_string_in_ui, i18n

#### AUD-content_browsing-04 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Move TextContent/TextSegment out of text_cache_repository.dart (data layer) into domain/entities/ so presentation and its tests stop importing the data layer
- **Rule:** Presentation→data import ban [P]; naming/placement (domain models belong in domain/); Evans lens (bounded-context leak) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** TextContent/TextSegment are plain immutable data holders — exactly what domain/entities/ is for (that directory exists, scaffolded with a lone .gitkeep, but was never populated) — yet they are defined at the top of text_cache_repository.dart, the DATA-layer repository implementation. That forces text_display_screen.dart (presentation, and a churn HOTSPOT at 1028 lines) to import the data layer just to type its own widget fields (_TextContentView.textContent, _NumberedSegmentColumn.segments). It then forces every test that builds fixture content — 3 of this batch's files (text_display_screen_test.dart, _l1_test.dart, _deep_l1_test.dart) — to do the same, so the test suite faithfully pins the wrong layering instead of catching it. Concrete cost: a presentation test can't get a TextContent value without also pulling in TextCacheRepository's own Drift-DAO-typed constructor surface (the seam Feathers-style testability depends on is gone); a different feature that wanted to render cached text would have to import a repository class to get the model type; and this is a same-feature leak, so it isn't caught by make audit's Rule 1/2 greps (which are scoped to cross-feature imports).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/content_browsing/presentation/screens/text_display_screen.dart:21` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/content_browsing/data/repositories/text_cache_repository.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/content_browsing/data/repositories/text_cache_repository.dart:10` — “class TextSegment {”; `learning_tracker/test/features/content_browsing/presentation/screens/text_display_screen_l1_test.dart:39` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/content_browsing/data/repositories/text_cache_repository.dart';”; `learning_tracker/test/features/content_browsing/presentation/screens/text_display_screen_deep_l1_test.dart:73` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/content_browsing/data/repositories/text_cache_repository.dart';”; `learning_tracker/test/features/content_browsing/presentation/screens/text_display_screen_test.dart:9` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/content_browsing/data/repositories/text_cache_repository.dart';”
- **Fix:** Create lib/features/content_browsing/domain/entities/text_content.dart holding TextContent/TextSegment (mechanical move, no behavior change). Update text_cache_repository.dart and text_display_screen.dart (+ its tests) to import the new domain file instead of the repository file.
- **Done when:** `grep -rn "features/content_browsing/data/" lib/features/content_browsing/presentation/` returns no hits. · text_display_screen_l1_test.dart, _deep_l1_test.dart, and text_display_screen_test.dart import domain/entities/text_content.dart, not data/repositories/text_cache_repository.dart, and still pass.
- **Labels:** layering, content_browsing, presentation-data-import, domain-model-placement

- **Rule:** lens:theme-consistency (beyond no_color_literal_outside_theme's Color(0x..) scope; extend lint or document statics-allowed) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x2] · chair-adjudicated

#### AUD-content_browsing-09 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Type the catch clauses in content_browsing instead of bare catch(e)
- **Rule:** EH-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 6 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** None of these restrict the caught type, so each also catches Error subtypes (a TypeError from a bad cast, a StateError from a logic bug) and handles them as an ordinary recoverable failure. The sharpest case is cloud_content_service.dart:317 (currently dead per the separate dead-code finding, but worth fixing if kept): if gzip.decode throws for a reason other than 'not gzipped' (e.g. a truncated download), the function returns the still-compressed bytes as valid data, turning a clear decompression failure into a confusing downstream JSON-parse error. text_display_screen.dart:755's bare catch(e, st) around _handleComplete will show 'Could not save' for a genuine programming bug exactly the same way it shows it for an expected write failure.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/content_browsing/presentation/screens/content_search_screen.dart:43` — “} catch (_) {
      return null;”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/content_browsing/data/repositories/content_repository_impl.dart:87` — “} catch (e) {
      throw ContentLoadException(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/content_browsing/presentation/screens/text_display_screen.dart:755` — “} catch (e, st) {
      AppLogger.instance.error(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/content_browsing/data/services/cloud_content_service.dart:317` — “} catch (_) {
      // Not gzipped, return as-is
      return data;”
- **Fix:** Narrow each to on FormatException/on Exception catch as appropriate; for the gzip fallback specifically, check the gzip magic number (0x1f 0x8b) instead of try/catch.
- **Done when:** a grep-based Rule-0 check for '} catch (' without a preceding 'on ' returns zero hits in these 4 files (or dart run custom_lint once its analyzer-9.0 incompatibility, already baselined, is fixed)
- **Labels:** eh-4, error-handling, hygiene

#### AUD-dashboard-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Add semantic labels to the icon-only ArrowButton carousel controls (AX-3)
- **Rule:** AX-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** The prev/next chevrons that page the active-tracks carousel are pure Icon-in-InkWell controls with no Semantics/tooltip/semanticLabel anywhere in the widget or its two call sites (prev at line 79, next at line 94 of active_tracks_carousel_section.dart). A TalkBack/VoiceOver user hears at best an unlabeled 'button' for each — no indication of direction or purpose — for the only pointer-driven way to move between active tracks. dashboard_body.dart:304-311 shows the team applying this exact fix elsewhere ('F-11: wrap the streak chip in a Semantics node so TalkBack/VoiceOver announces a descriptive label'), so the omission here is an inconsistency, not a policy gap.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/arrow_button.dart:18` — “return InkWell(
      onTap: onTap,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/active_tracks_carousel_section.dart:79` — “ArrowButton(
              icon: Directionality.of(context) == TextDirection.rtl”
- **Fix:** Wrap each ArrowButton instance (or give the widget a required semanticLabel) in Semantics(label: l10n.previousTrack / l10n.nextTrack, button: true, excludeSemantics: true, ...), mirroring the streak-chip pattern in dashboard_body.dart.
- **Done when:** A widget test using tester.getSemantics on ActiveTracksCarouselSection confirms both arrow controls expose a non-empty, direction-specific label. · Manual TalkBack/VoiceOver pass announces 'Previous track'/'Next track' (EN) and their Hebrew ARB equivalents.
- **Labels:** AX-3, accessibility, dashboard

#### AUD-dashboard-02 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Guard ref.invalidate with a mounted check in SkippedOnboardingCtaBanner's dismiss handler
- **Rule:** SM-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** clearOnboardingSkipState() performs two awaited SharedPreferences.remove() platform-channel calls. If the widget is disposed during that window — e.g. the user taps Dismiss then immediately navigates away, a plausible fast-tap-and-swipe sequence — the following ref.invalidate() fires on an unmounted ref. Riverpod 3.3.1 (pinned in pubspec.yaml) throws UnmountedRefException in that case. The same file already demonstrates the correct guard two callbacks earlier (line 146), and the identical operation is guarded correctly in add_profile_dialog.dart:241, so this is a one-line omission, not a missing pattern.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/skipped_onboarding_cta_banner.dart:164` — “await clearOnboardingSkipState();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/skipped_onboarding_cta_banner.dart:165` — “ref.invalidate(onboardingSkipStateProvider);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/skipped_onboarding_cta_banner.dart:146` — “if (!context.mounted) return;”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/add_profile_dialog.dart:241` — “if (context.mounted) ref.invalidate(profileListProvider);”
- **Fix:** Guard the invalidate call: await clearOnboardingSkipState(); if (!context.mounted) return; ref.invalidate(onboardingSkipStateProvider); — matching the pattern already used at line 146 and in add_profile_dialog.dart.
- **Done when:** widget test: pump SkippedOnboardingCtaBanner, tap Dismiss, dispose the widget tree before the SharedPreferences future resolves, assert tester.takeException() is null / no UnmountedRefException
- **Labels:** riverpod, sm-4, crash-risk, dashboard · verifier corrections: The finding's 'why' claims Riverpod throws UnmountedRefException; that class is specific to Notifier-context Ref (riverpod core package). The WidgetRef used here (via ConsumerWidget) actually throws a plain StateError fr

#### AUD-dashboard-06 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Guard ref.watch/ref.read after in-flight awaits in dashboard_providers.dart (SM-4)
- **Rule:** SM-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** dashboardTrackCompletionPercentage, dashboardCompletionPercentage, stripStockMilestonesEffect, and dashboardPaceStatus each call ref.watch/ref.read after an earlier await (a Drift DB read) with no ref.mounted check in between. If any of these autoDispose family providers loses its last listener while that DB read is still in flight — e.g. the user swipes the active-tracks carousel past a card or leaves the dashboard mid-load — the later ref call throws UnmountedRefException, an uncaught exception inside the async provider body. The same file's dashboardChildNextReward provider (line 343) already guards this exact hazard with `if (!ref.mounted) return null;`, proving the team knows the failure mode; it just isn't applied consistently.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/providers/dashboard_providers.dart:142` — “final track = await db.trackDao.getTrackById(trackId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/providers/dashboard_providers.dart:155` — “final totalItems = await ref.watch(
    scopedItemCountProvider(curriculum).future,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/providers/dashboard_providers.dart:323` — “await ref.read(syncWriteFacadeProvider)?.pushGamificationSettingsSnapshot();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/providers/dashboard_providers.dart:439` — “final totalItems = await ref.watch(
    scopedItemCountProvider(curriculum).future,”
- **Fix:** Add `if (!ref.mounted) return <default>;` immediately after the await that precedes the later ref access in each of the four functions, mirroring the existing guard in dashboardChildNextReward.
- **Done when:** A targeted test that disposes the ProviderContainer (or drops the last listener) mid-await for each of the four providers confirms no UnmountedRefException escapes. · A grep/lint check for 'ref.watch|ref.read after await without a preceding ref.mounted guard' is added to make audit or riverpod_lint config.
- **Labels:** riverpod, SM-4, dashboard, crash-risk · verifier corrections: Evidence array cites lines 142,155,323,439 (covering 3 of the 4 named functions) — dashboardCompletionPercentage's identical unguarded ref.watch after await at lines 189-190 is the 4th named site but has no matching evid

#### AUD-dashboard-07 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Inject LocalDayClock into ParentDashboardAggregator instead of hardcoding SystemLocalDayClock
- **Rule:** TQ-6 / SM-7 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** compute({DateTime? now}) documents now as 'pass explicitly for testability', and every other metric (pace, engagement, recent-completions window) honors it — but the streak sub-computation always builds StreakStateProvider with a hardcoded SystemLocalDayClock(), which reads real DateTime.now() regardless of the now argument. The accompanying test cannot control this and is forced to call real DateTime.now() to seed matching streak_events (quoted comment at lines 119-121 explains exactly why), making that test a genuine wall-clock dependency and leaving a live day-boundary race: if the wall clock ticks past local midnight between the caller choosing now and StreakStateProvider's internal clock read, currentStreak/maxStreak reflect a different 'today' than the rest of the ParentDashboardData snapshot.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/domain/services/parent_dashboard_aggregator.dart:94` — “clock: const SystemLocalDayClock(),”; `learning_tracker/test/features/parent_mode/domain/services/parent_dashboard_aggregator_compute_test.dart:122` — “final today = DateTime.now().toUtc();”
- **Fix:** Accept an optional LocalDayClock clock constructor parameter (default const SystemLocalDayClock()), pass it into StreakStateProvider, and derive it from the aggregator's own now so compute(now: ...) fully determines the snapshot including streak.
- **Done when:** A new unit test overrides the injected clock (not real DateTime.now()) and asserts currentStreak/maxStreak for a fixed 'today', replacing the wall-clock seeding at parent_dashboard_aggregator_compute_test.dart:118-122. · The TQ-6 hermetic-test grep (no DateTime.now() outside core/time) passes for this test file.
- **Labels:** TQ-6, clock-injection, dashboard, streak · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches

### features/gamification  (24 findings — 0 P0 / 3 P1 / 9 P2 / 12 P3)

#### AUD-gamification-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Add ref.mounted/context.mounted guards after awaits in RewardConfigController and the pending-redemptions fulfil/decline handlers
- **Rule:** SM-4 (after any await in a Notifier method/async callback, check ref.mounted before touching ref/state) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 6 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** RewardConfigController is an autoDispose Notifier (confirmed via reward_config_controller.g.dart: isAutoDispose: true) whose saveReward/toggleEnabled/deleteMilestone/_persistAndSync methods each await one or more DB/network calls and then read `state` or call `ref.invalidate`/`ref.read` afterward -- with zero ref.mounted checks anywhere in the file (grep confirms). If the user saves/toggles/deletes and the screen is popped (e.g. the success dialog's own navigation, or a fast back-gesture) before the await resolves, Riverpod 3 throws when a disposed Ref is touched. The same shape recurs in parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart's _fulfil/_decline: `ref.invalidate` runs BEFORE the `context.mounted` check that appears one statement later in the same function -- the check exists, it's just ordered too late. By contrast, every other async flow in this exact feature (child_redemption_screen.dart, achievement_unlock_celebration.dart, reward_configuration_screen.dart) consistently checks mounted immediately after every await, so this is a real, demonstrated-known-pattern that these two files skip. No test in reward_config_controller_test.dart exercises container/widget disposal mid-await (grep for 'Unmounted'/dispose-mid-call found nothing).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/providers/reward_config_controller.dart:179` — “final currentMilestones = state.usesGlobalLadder
        ? await svc.getGlobalMilestones()”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/providers/reward_config_controller.dart:137` — “await ref.read(syncWriteFacadeProvider)?.pushGamificationSettingsSnapshot();
    ref.invalidate(achievementsOverviewProvider);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart:145` — “await db.pointsBalanceDao.fulfilRedemption(redemption.id);
    ref.invalidate(pendingRedemptionsProvider);”
- **Fix:** Add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` immediately after every await in RewardConfigController's mutation methods before touching state/ref again; in parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart move `ref.invalidate(...)` after the `context.mounted` check, not before it.
- **Done when:** Every await in RewardConfigController's saveReward/toggleEnabled/deleteMilestone/_persistAndSync is followed by a ref.mounted check before further ref/state use · parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart's _fulfil/_decline check context.mounted before ref.invalidate, not after · A widget/provider test disposes the container or pops the screen mid-await and asserts no uncaught disposed-ref exception
- **Labels:** SM-4, riverpod, crash-risk, lifecycle

#### AUD-gamification-02 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Fix physical Positioned(right:) badge on AchievementTierCard so it doesn't overlap the title in Hebrew RTL
- **Rule:** AX-1 (EdgeInsetsDirectional/AlignmentDirectional required in this RTL app; no physical left/right) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** The title is positioned with AlignmentDirectional.topStart and padded with EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(end: 96) -- both direction-aware, so in Hebrew (RTL) the title anchors to the physical right and reserves 96px on the physical left. The TrackTagChip badge, however, is pinned with plain Positioned(top:0, right:0) -- direction-UNAWARE, so it stays on the physical right in both locales. In LTR this is correct (title occupies the left zone, badge sits in the reserved right zone). In RTL the title now ALSO occupies the right zone (topStart flips), so the badge renders directly on top of the milestone title text on every achievement card for every Hebrew-locale user. This exact bug class was already found and fixed once in this feature (progress_summary_card.dart's PositionedDirectional comment explicitly describes the identical failure mode), and a dedicated regression test already exists for this widget under Hebrew locale (gamification_screen_l1_test.dart, 'R6-16: AchievementTierCard under RTL has no Directionality(ltr) wrapper') but it only asserts the absence of a forced-LTR Directionality wrapper -- it never checks rendered geometry, so it passes today despite the overlap. point_config_screen.dart:428,445 have the same Positioned(right:) pattern but on purely decorative, content-free background circles (IgnorePointer, low opacity) -- same root cause, cosmetic-only impact.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/achievement_tier_card.dart:92` — “padding: const EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(end: 96),”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/achievement_tier_card.dart:94` — “alignment: AlignmentDirectional.topStart,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/achievement_tier_card.dart:110` — “top: 0,
                      right: 0,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/point_config_screen.dart:428` — “right: -36,
              bottom: -40,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/point_config_screen.dart:445` — “right: 40,
              bottom: -56,”
- **Fix:** Replace Positioned(right: 0) with PositionedDirectional(end: 0) at achievement_tier_card.dart:108-112 (and the two decorative sites in point_config_screen.dart for consistency). Extend the existing R6-16 test to pump under Locale('he') and assert the TrackTagChip's rendered Rect does not intersect the title Text's Rect.
- **Done when:** achievement_tier_card.dart uses PositionedDirectional(end:) instead of Positioned(right:) for the TrackTagChip badge · gamification_screen_l1_test.dart's R6-16 test (or a new sibling test) asserts non-overlapping geometry between the badge and title under Locale('he'), not just absence of a forced Directionality
- **Labels:** AX-1, RTL, hebrew, regression

#### AUD-gamification-03 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Stop achievementsOverviewProvider and _pointConfigDataProvider writing to Drift/SharedPreferences and pushing to Firestore from inside FutureProvider build
- **Rule:** SM-2 (provider build is pure: no writes/requests/side effects) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** Both providers exist to compute a read-only view model (achievements list / per-track point config rows), but their build functions mutate persisted state (SharedPreferences milestone config, Drift PointConfigs rows) and push a network sync write as an unguarded side effect of simply being watched. Riverpod rebuilds these providers on every dependency change (achievementsOverviewProvider re-runs on every completionCommittedProvider tick; _pointConfigDataProvider re-runs whenever activeTracksProvider emits) -- so opening the achievements screen or the point-settings screen can silently trigger writes and a Firestore push purely from reading state, with no user action and no guard against concurrent/duplicate invocation. This also makes both providers impossible to unit test as pure read logic without a working sync facade and DB write path.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/providers/achievements_overview_provider.dart:88` — “if (await service.stripStockTemplateMilestones()) {
        await ref.read(syncWriteFacadeProvider)?.pushGamificationSettingsSnapshot();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/point_config_screen.dart:122` — “await db.pointConfigDao.upsertConfig(
            PointConfigsCompanion.insert(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/point_config_screen.dart:154` — “if (wroteConfigs) {
      await sync?.pushGamificationSettingsSnapshot();”
- **Fix:** Move the strip-stock-templates / seed-default-configs mutations out of the read providers into an explicit one-shot action (invoked once from a screen lifecycle hook or a dedicated Notifier method with SM-4-safe mounted checks), leaving the FutureProviders as pure reads.
- **Done when:** achievementsOverviewProvider's build function performs no writes; a separate, explicitly-invoked action performs stripStockTemplateMilestones + push · _pointConfigDataProvider's build function performs no writes; seeding defaults happens in a separate action · A ProviderContainer.test() test watches each read provider twice and asserts the mutation/sync-push call count is 0 (or exactly 1, deliberately) rather than growing with rebuilds
- **Labels:** SM-2, riverpod, side-effects, sync

#### AUD-gamification-05 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Fix mergeCloudPayload treating a non-empty remote payload with a missing/unparseable updated_at as unconditionally newer than local
- **Rule:** EH-2 / Nygard lens (LWW ordering must not silently clobber on ambiguous input; mirrors FB-3's null-timestamp guard even though this path is SharedPreferences-based, not core/sync) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The short-circuit `remoteUpdatedAt != null && ...` means: when the remote payload is non-empty but its 'updated_at' fails to parse (missing key, malformed string, cross-version format drift), the early-return guard never fires, so the method falls through and unconditionally overwrites local milestones/unlocks with the remote payload -- treating 'timestamp unknown' as 'always newer' instead of the safer 'cannot prove newer, keep local'. This is the exact malformed-timestamp branch never exercised by either reward_milestone_service_test.dart's mergeCloudPayload group (only null/empty/older/newer-with-valid-ISO-dates are tested) or test/sync/merge/gamification_reward_merge_test.dart (same gap, confirmed by grep -- only valid ISO8601 updated_at values appear in that file too).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/domain/services/reward_milestone_service.dart:315` — “final remoteUpdatedAt = DateTime.tryParse(
      (remote['updated_at'] ?? '').toString(),
    );”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/domain/services/reward_milestone_service.dart:319` — “if (remoteUpdatedAt != null && !remoteUpdatedAt.isAfter(localUpdatedAt)) {
      return;”
- **Fix:** Change the guard so a null/unparseable remoteUpdatedAt is treated as NOT provably newer (skip the merge, same as the older-timestamp branch) rather than falling through to an unconditional overwrite.
- **Done when:** mergeCloudPayload with a non-empty milestones/unlocks payload and a missing or garbage 'updated_at' leaves existing local data untouched · A new test in the mergeCloudPayload group covers this exact case and fails against the current code
- **Labels:** EH-2, sync, LWW, data-loss · verifier corrections: Minor: claim that gamification_reward_merge_test.dart has 'only valid ISO8601 updated_at values' is imprecise -- that file never exercises mergeCloudPayload at all (uses a fake callback stub), so reward_settings.updated_

#### AUD-gamification-06 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Log RewardMilestoneService.getAllMilestones/getAllUnlocks JSON-decode failures instead of silently returning an empty list that can later overwrite cloud data
- **Rule:** EH-3 (log-less catch is a pending violation; every catch rethrows, converts, or logs via AppLogger) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** If the SharedPreferences-stored reward config JSON is unreadable (process death mid-write, storage corruption, cross-version format mismatch), getAllMilestones/getAllUnlocks silently treat 'corrupt' the same as 'genuinely empty', with zero AppLogger call. That empty result then flows straight into exportCloudPayload(), which is what pushGamificationSettingsSnapshot() uploads as the authoritative reward_settings snapshot on the next sync -- silently overwriting the family's real, previously-configured reward list on every other synced device, with no diagnostic trail to explain why rewards 'disappeared'. The existing test suite (reward_milestone_service_test.dart 'getAllMilestones edge cases', lines 536-574) exercises invalid/blank/non-list JSON but only ever asserts the method returns empty -- it pins the silent-swallow as the specified behavior rather than testing that the failure is surfaced or logged.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/domain/services/reward_milestone_service.dart:89` — “} catch (_) {
      return const [];”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/domain/services/reward_milestone_service.dart:112` — “} catch (_) {
      return const [];”
- **Fix:** Log via AppLogger.error (or similar) inside both catch blocks before returning the fallback list, including enough context (profileId, key) to diagnose; consider whether a corrupt-vs-genuinely-empty distinction should block the next cloud push instead of silently exporting empty.
- **Done when:** Both catch(_) blocks in getAllMilestones/getAllUnlocks call AppLogger before returning the empty fallback · A test seeds corrupted JSON, calls the method, and asserts the logger recorded the failure (fake/spy AppLogger sink)
- **Labels:** EH-3, data-loss, sync, logging

#### AUD-gamification-08 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Route child_redemption_screen.dart and parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart error states through AppLocalizations instead of raw e.toString()
- **Rule:** EH-5 / AX-2 (no raw exception reaches presentation; everything user-facing via AppLocalizations/ARB) -- matches the currently-non-functional custom_lint rule no_e_to_string_in_ui · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Both screens render the raw exception's toString() as the entire error-state UI, completely bypassing localization -- in an EN/Hebrew app, a Hebrew-locale user sees untranslated (and potentially technical/internal) English text if the balance or pending-redemptions stream errors. This is not a missing capability: the very same feature already has a sanctioned pattern for this (point_config_screen.dart:222,267 use `AppLocalizations.of(context)!.errorGeneric(e.toString())`, and gamification_screen.dart uses `l10n.errorLoadingCalendar` for its own error states) -- these two sites simply don't use it, an inconsistency within one feature slice.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/child_redemption_screen.dart:107` — “error: (e, _) => Center(child: Text(e.toString())),”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart:84` — “error: (e, _) => Center(child: Text(e.toString())),”
- **Fix:** Replace `Text(e.toString())` with `Text(AppLocalizations.of(context)!.errorGeneric(e.toString()))` (or a more specific localized string) in both files, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the same feature.
- **Done when:** Neither file renders a bare e.toString() as UI text; both route through an AppLocalizations-resolved string · A widget test pumps each screen in an error AsyncValue state under Locale('he') and asserts the rendered text is not raw English exception text
- **Labels:** EH-5, AX-2, i18n, hebrew

#### AUD-gamification-09 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Use directional layout APIs instead of EdgeInsets.only(left/right) and Positioned(right:) in gamification widgets
- **Rule:** AX-1 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** tier_icon_box.dart's lock badge is pinned to the visual right/bottom corner with plain Positioned, which does not mirror under RTL — in Hebrew locale the badge renders on the leading (left) corner instead of the trailing corner. This is not hypothetical: the sibling file progress_summary_card.dart (same presentation/widgets/ directory) carries an explicit comment describing this exact bug ('With a plain Positioned(right:) it stayed on the visual right — the LEADING edge in Hebrew RTL — and collided with the right-aligned header text') that was fixed there with PositionedDirectional but never applied to tier_icon_box.dart. reward_config_header.dart's EdgeInsets.only(left:4, right:4) is currently symmetric so it renders identically in both directions today, but is one one-sided edit away from the same class of bug and still fails the AX-1 grep/lint intent.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/tier_icon_box.dart:49` — “Positioned(
              right: 3,
              bottom: 3,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/reward_config_header.dart:29` — “padding: EdgeInsets.only(
          top: topInset + 4,
          left: 4,”
- **Fix:** Replace Positioned(right:, bottom:) with PositionedDirectional(end:, bottom:) in tier_icon_box.dart; replace EdgeInsets.only(left:, right:) with EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start:, end:) in reward_config_header.dart.
- **Done when:** grep -rn 'Positioned(' lib/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/tier_icon_box.dart shows PositionedDirectional, not Positioned with right:/left:. · A widget test pumped under Locale('he')/TextDirection.rtl asserts the lock badge sits on the trailing (left-in-RTL) corner.

#### AUD-gamification-10 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Wire RewardConfigController's async mutations to the RewardForm.loading/.error fields the screen already renders
- **Rule:** SM-5 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [2x3] · filed P1, revised
- **Why:** RewardForm carries loading/error fields and reward_configuration_screen.dart fully renders them (full-screen CircularProgressIndicator for form.loading, a dedicated error Scaffold for form.error) — but grep-confirmed, the controller's 4 async mutation methods (saveReward, toggleEnabled, deleteMilestone, milestonesForCurrentLadder) never set either field to a non-default value anywhere in the file; only bootstrap() touches them, always resetting to false/null. The screen's own try/catch only catches TutorWriteException per call site (for the tutor-permission-denied case). Any OTHER DB failure during a save/toggle/delete (constraint violation, disk error) is an unhandled Future rejection: the user taps Save, sees no spinner (loading never flips true) and no error (error never gets set) — the operation silently fails with zero feedback, while the fully-built error UI remains permanently dead code.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/reward_form.dart:16` — “this.loading = false,
    this.error,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/providers/reward_config_controller.dart:74` — “loading: false,
      error: null,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/providers/reward_config_controller.dart:189` — “await svc.upsertMilestone(
      trackId: trackId,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/reward_configuration_screen.dart:280` — “if (form.loading) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/reward_configuration_screen.dart:287` — “if (form.error != null) {”
- **Fix:** In each of the 4 mutation methods, set `state = state.copyWith(loading: true)` before the DB call and wrap it in try/catch: on success `loading:false`; on any exception (not just TutorWriteException) `state.copyWith(loading:false, error: <mapped message>)`, or migrate the class to expose `AsyncValue<RewardForm>`-style guard semantics.
- **Done when:** saveReward/toggleEnabled/deleteMilestone/milestonesForCurrentLadder each leave state.error non-null (not an unhandled Future rejection) when the underlying DB call throws anything other than TutorWriteException. · Widget test: a fake RewardMilestoneService/DB that throws a generic exception from upsertMilestone; assert the screen renders the form.error branch instead of hanging or throwing past the test. · Rule-0 checker: a grep/lint that flags a state class with loading/error-shaped fields where the owning @riverpod class file contains zero `state.copyWith(error:` (or equivalent) assignment with a non-null literal — i.e., a 'declared-but-dead error field' detector.
- **Labels:** sm-5, riverpod, error-handling, rewards, dead-code · verifier corrections: No factual error in the cited evidence — form.loading/form.error are confirmed dead (only bootstrap() touches them) and the 4 async mutations are confirmed to lack try/catch beyond the screen's TutorWriteException-only w

#### AUD-gamification-11 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Wrap RewardMilestoneService/StreakService/StreakStateProvider in @riverpod providers instead of constructing them ad-hoc at every call site
- **Rule:** SM-7 (repositories/services/DAOs constructed only inside their @riverpod provider; no ad-hoc construction/service-locator lookups) · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 9 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** No @riverpod/Provider wraps RewardMilestoneService, StreakService, or StreakStateProvider anywhere in the codebase (grep confirms zero matches for 'Provider<RewardMilestoneService>' etc.); instead `RewardMilestoneService(db, profileId: profileId)` is repeated at 12 call sites repo-wide (7 inside this batch alone across 4 files, plus reward_config_controller.dart has 4 separate occurrences of the identical two-line construction), and StreakService/StreakStateProvider follow the same pattern. Every call site must independently obtain a UserDatabase and profileId and re-derive the same object graph. A constructor signature change, a swap of the SharedPreferences-backed store, or a test override all require touching every call site instead of one provider. It also means these classes can only be faked in tests by injecting a fake UserDatabase all the way through, not by a single ProviderScope override.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/domain/services/points_service.dart:139` — “final reward = RewardMilestoneService(_database, profileId: profileId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/providers/reward_config_controller.dart:129` — “final svc = RewardMilestoneService(db, profileId: profileId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/providers/achievements_overview_provider.dart:86` — “final service = RewardMilestoneService(db, profileId: profileId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/child_redemption_screen.dart:53` — “final svc = RewardMilestoneService(db, profileId: profileId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/screens/gamification_screen.dart:35` — “final streakService = StreakService(db, profileId: profileId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/domain/services/streak_service.dart:17` — “_provider = StreakStateProvider(
        db: db,
        clock: const SystemLocalDayClock(),”
- **Fix:** Introduce rewardMilestoneServiceProvider / streakServiceProvider @riverpod providers (mirroring the existing, correct pointsServiceProvider pattern in points_providers.dart) and have every listed call site use ref.watch/ref.read of the provider instead of constructing directly.
- **Done when:** A single @riverpod provider exists for each of RewardMilestoneService, StreakService, and StreakStateProvider · All 9 in-batch construction sites (and the additional sites in dashboard/learning/sync features) are replaced with ref.watch/ref.read of the provider · Existing service unit tests continue to pass by overriding the provider rather than constructing the service directly
- **Labels:** SM-7, riverpod, DI, testability

#### AUD-gamification-12 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · streak_restorer.dart redefines kBulkPriorSentinelMs as a local magic number instead of importing the existing core constant
- **Rule:** Evans (invariant enforced in one place) / Fowler (duplicated code, magic number) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The comment's stated reason is wrong: SchedulerEngine.kBulkPriorSentinelMs (the thing it says it's avoiding importing) lives in features/scheduler, not core, so importing it would be a cross-feature import (Rule 2), not a core→features violation (Rule 1) — and the correct fix was available anyway: lib/core/learning/completion_constants.dart already exports this exact constant from core, which features/ may freely import, and its own doc comment explicitly says it 'MUST be excluded from... streak calculations.' The sentinel (2000-01-01 UTC ms) now has three independent definitions (core/learning/completion_constants.dart, features/scheduler/domain/services/scheduler_engine.dart, and this file) that can silently diverge if any one is edited, corrupting bulk-prior filtering in exactly one of streak restore, points history, or scheduler completion detection without any test catching the mismatch.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/streak/streak_restorer.dart:41` — “// kBulkPriorSentinelMs (DateTime.utc(2000, 1, 1)); we define it locally to
    // avoid a core→features layering violation.”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/streak/streak_restorer.dart:44` — “const bulkPriorSentinelMs = 946684800000; // DateTime.utc(2000,1,1) ms”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/learning/completion_constants.dart:18` — “const int kBulkPriorSentinelMs =
    946684800000; // DateTime.utc(2000, 1, 1).millisecondsSinceEpoch”
- **Fix:** Delete the local bulkPriorSentinelMs const and import kBulkPriorSentinelMs from core/learning/completion_constants.dart (a legal features→core import); fix the misleading comment.
- **Done when:** streak_restorer.dart imports and uses core's kBulkPriorSentinelMs; the local const is removed. · grep -rn '946684800000' lib/ returns exactly one hit (completion_constants.dart).
- **Labels:** duplication, layering, streak · verifier corrections: A 4th independent definition of this sentinel exists at features/onboarding/domain/services/bulk_prior_completion_service.dart:31-34 (with the identical flawed 'avoid core→features violation' comment) — not mentioned by

- **Fix:** Add `.autoDispose` to both curriculumPointsProvider and pointsHistoryProvider.

- **Labels:** SM-6, riverpod, P3 · verifier corrections: Line 61 citation for pointsHistoryProvider is off by one (quoted factory text is on line 62; 61 is the var name). Also achievementsOverviewProvider/_pointConfigDataProvider/pendingRedemptionsProvider are plain zero-arg a

#### AUD-gamification-14 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Convert RewardMilestone/RewardUnlockRecord to @freezed data classes
- **Rule:** Naming/placement (domain/state models are immutable @freezed classes; never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Both classes are hand-written data holders with a hand-rolled copyWith/toJson/fromJson but no == / hashCode override at all, so they fall back to identity equality -- two RewardMilestones with identical field values are not `==`. Current call sites happen to compare by `.id` field rather than object equality (so no live bug was found), but this is fragile: any future code that puts RewardMilestone in a Set, uses List.contains, or relies on Riverpod .select()-style equality skipping would silently misbehave. The sibling model in the same feature (StreakRecoveryInfo) already follows the correct @freezed convention, showing the pattern is known and used elsewhere in this exact directory.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/domain/models/reward_milestone.dart:3` — “class RewardMilestone {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/domain/models/reward_milestone.dart:107` — “class RewardUnlockRecord {”
- **Fix:** Convert RewardMilestone and RewardUnlockRecord to @freezed classes (keeping the existing toJson/fromJson as named factory/method overrides if the generated ones don't match the custom snake_case JSON shape).
- **Done when:** RewardMilestone and RewardUnlockRecord are @freezed with generated equality · Existing reward_milestone_test.dart suite passes unchanged (or updated only for the freezed toString/copyWith surface)
- **Labels:** freezed, naming-placement, P3

#### AUD-gamification-15 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Correct streak_event_log.dart's doc comment — the real unique index is (profileId, dayUtc, eventType), not eventTimestamp
- **Rule:** Evans (ubiquitous language consistency) / AG-8-adjacent (docs must match reality) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** The actual Drift table declares the UNIQUE composite as (profileId, dayUtc, eventType) — eventTimestamp is not part of it, and the table's own doc comment says so explicitly ('two devices writing the same logical day-event collapse to one row'). streak_event_log.dart's code is actually correct (it computes dayUtc from eventTimestamp before inserting), but its doc comment describes a different, wrong key. This class is the write path used by core/sync/merge/streak_event_merger.dart for cross-device streak-event merge — a maintainer who trusts this comment and 'optimizes' the dedup logic around eventTimestamp instead of dayUtc would break cross-device dedup and silently duplicate streak_events rows on sync, corrupting streak counts.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/streak/streak_event_log.dart:3` — “/// The single mutation method is [append]. Idempotency is enforced by
/// the UNIQUE `(profileId, eventTimestamp, eventType)` index on”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/tables/streak_events.dart:12` — “@TableIndex(
  name: 'streak_events_natural_key',
  columns: {#profileId, #dayUtc, #eventType},”
- **Fix:** Fix the doc comment to say (profileId, dayUtc, eventType), matching core/database/tables/streak_events.dart.
- **Done when:** streak_event_log.dart's doc comment states the same 3 columns as the @TableIndex on StreakEvents.
- **Labels:** docs-drift, sync, streak · verifier corrections: Quote for streak_events.dart cited at line 12; the @TableIndex block actually starts at line 13 (line 12 is the doc comment's last line). Quote text is verbatim correct, just off by one line.

#### AUD-gamification-22 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · RewardForm is a hand-written state class with no @freezed/== override, so Riverpod can never skip a rebuild on it
- **Rule:** naming/placement — 'Domain/state models are immutable @freezed classes... never hand-write ==/hashCode' · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** RewardForm is held directly as RewardConfigController's Notifier state (per its own doc comment) but has no @freezed codegen and no == /hashCode override anywhere in the file, so it falls back to identity equality. Every copyWith() call — including a no-op one — produces a referentially distinct instance that Riverpod's default identity-based updateShouldNotify always treats as changed, so any widget watching this provider rebuilds on every field mutation regardless of whether the visible state actually changed. This is exactly the failure mode coding-standards.md cites as the reason for the @freezed rule.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/reward_form.dart:7` — “class RewardForm {
  const RewardForm({”; `docs/coding-standards.md:584` — “hand-rolled equality drifts from the fields and silently breaks rebuild-skipping.”
- **Fix:** Convert RewardForm to @freezed, or at minimum hand-write a field-wise == / hashCode.
- **Done when:** RewardForm(...) == RewardForm(...) with identical field values returns true in a new unit test. · dart analyze / build_runner clean after the freezed conversion (if chosen).
- **Labels:** riverpod, equality, performance

#### AUD-learning-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Harden or test the failure path of the unawaited CompletionDetectionService call in CompletionRepositoryImpl.markComplete
- **Rule:** EH-2/EH-3 (errors converted/logged, no log-less catch) + Nygard (partial I/O failure) -- surfaced via this batch's tests · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** completion_detection_service.dart and learning_ledger_repository_impl.dart contain zero try/catch blocks (grep-confirmed), and the call site wraps them in unawaited(...) with no .catchError, so any exception during siyum detection (closed DB mid profile-switch, disk-full write, a malformed content lookup) becomes an unhandled Future error with no retry and no user-facing signal -- the completion itself still records, but the documented B1 policy ('a learner who bulk-marks a complete masechta still earns the siyum') silently fails to hold for that unit, permanently, with no reconciliation job anywhere in lib/ to catch the gap. No test anywhere in this batch makes checkAndRecordCompletions throw and asserts the outcome; the two tests that exercise this path can only prove the happy case, and both need a Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero) synchronization hack just to observe that -- itself a symptom that the design has no seam for verifying failure behavior deterministically.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/learning/data/repositories/completion_repository_impl.dart:190` — “if (_completionDetectionService != null && creditsAchievement) {
        unawaited(”; `learning_tracker/test/features/learning/domain/use_cases/mark_completion_use_case_siyum_routing_test.dart:210` — “await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);
        await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);”; `learning_tracker/test/features/learning/data/repositories/h4_lifetime_only_detection_test.dart:194` — “// Wait for any fire-and-forget unawaited futures to settle.
        await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero);”
- **Fix:** Wrap the unawaited call in a .catchError (or add an internal try/catch inside checkAndRecordCompletions) that logs via AppLogger per EH-3; add a test that forces the detection service to throw (e.g. a ContentRepository stub that throws) and assert markComplete still returns successfully while the failure is logged.
- **Done when:** A test drives CompletionDetectionService.checkAndRecordCompletions to throw and asserts (a) markComplete still returns successfully and (b) AppLogger records the failure · The unawaited call site in completion_repository_impl.dart has a catch path instead of relying on the global zone error handler
- **Labels:** error-handling, gamification, reliability, nygard · verifier corrections: The finding's "unhandled Future error" framing slightly overstates the silence: main.dart's runZonedGuarded + PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError DO catch this and route it through AppLogger.instance.handle() and Crashly

#### AUD-learning-02 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Reconcile the Rule 2 barrel filename (providers.dart vs Y.dart) and fix the dead cross-feature-import checker
- **Rule:** Rule 2 (cross-feature deep-import ban) + Rule 0 (deterministic checker requirement) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 28 · **Verified:** [3x3]

A rename inside tutoring/dashboard/profiles/scheduler internals will silently break learning_screen.dart with zero warning at review or CI time.

- **Fix:** Pick one barrel filename convention and update the other doc to match (or state a formal migration plan); fix the Makefile awk to compare the SECOND features/.../ match in the grep line (the import target), not the source path against itself; route learning_screen.dart's tutoring import through features/tutoring/tutoring.dart; either populate dashboard.dart/profiles.dart/scheduler.dart/learning.dart or apply coding-standards.md's documented fallback (route through a core provider/service).

#### AUD-learning-03 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Wrap LearningLedgerRepositoryImpl's ledger insert and outbox enqueue in one transaction
- **Rule:** DB-2 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** recordCompletion inserts the learning_ledger row (line 104) and then enqueues its outbox row (line 127) as two separate, unwrapped statements; recordCompletionsBatch commits all N ledger rows inside one _database.transaction() (closes at line 195) but then loops the outbox enqueue afterward, outside that transaction, one row at a time. A process death or crash between these steps leaves a ledger entry (e.g. a manual siyum mark from the Lifetime Marking screen) permanently local-only — nothing re-derives a missing outbox row from an existing ledger row, so it never reaches Firestore or a second device. The sibling CompletionWriter (completion_writer.dart) explicitly wraps its analogous completion_events + outbox insert in one Drift transaction for exactly this reason (its docs call this 'Both rows commit or both roll back' — the FR15/RC1 fix); LearningLedgerRepositoryImpl doesn't follow the same discipline for the same class of append-only sync-critical data.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/learning/data/repositories/learning_ledger_repository_impl.dart:104` — “final id = await _database.learningLedgerDao.insertEntry(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/learning/data/repositories/learning_ledger_repository_impl.dart:127` — “await _syncLedgerEntry(entry);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/learning/data/repositories/learning_ledger_repository_impl.dart:205` — “await facade.enqueueLedgerEntry(_ledgerDataToSyncMap(entry));”
- **Fix:** Move the outbox enqueue for recordCompletion inside the same transaction as the ledger insert (or into one atomic Drift batch, as CompletionWriter does); for recordCompletionsBatch, move the per-item enqueueLedgerEntry calls inside the existing transaction block instead of running them afterward in a separate loop.
- **Done when:** Both recordCompletion and recordCompletionsBatch write the ledger row(s) and their outbox row(s) inside one transaction; a regression test that fails mid-batch (e.g. a Fake outbox facade that throws after N/2 calls) asserts no ledger row survives without a matching outbox row.
- **Labels:** db-2, sync, nygard, data-integrity · verifier corrections: New evidence beyond the finding: lib/core/database/daos/outbox_dao.dart:11-12/19-20 states insertOutboxRow 'must be called inside the same transaction as the triggering write' — a directly-named invariant, stronger groun

                Icons.chevron_right_rounded,”

#### AUD-learning-06 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Narrow and log the catch-all in CompletionRepositoryImpl._appendStreakEvent
- **Rule:** EH-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** catch (_) swallows every exception from BOTH the streak_events Drift insert and the outbox enqueue (facade.enqueueStreakPayload) with no AppLogger call anywhere in this file — a codec bug, closed-DB race, or genuine corruption is indistinguishable from the expected benign duplicate-key case this comment is defending against. This is also EH-4-adjacent (catches Error subtypes, not just typed Exceptions) and evades the Rule-0 'no empty catch blocks' Makefile grep (`catch\s*(_\?\w*)\s*{}`), which only matches a literal same-line `{}` — this multi-line comment-only body is functionally empty but textually invisible to that checker. Per the file's own header comment, the outbox enqueue here is what 'closes the gap' where a second device sees a frozen streak; if enqueueStreakPayload throws, that gap silently reopens with zero diagnostic trail and no retry.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/learning/data/repositories/completion_repository_impl.dart:767` — “} catch (_) {
      // Defensive: never let a telemetry tee block the primary write.”
- **Fix:** Catch a specific expected type (e.g. the Drift unique-constraint exception) for the benign-duplicate case and let everything else propagate or be logged via AppLogger.instance.warning/error before swallowing, so a genuine failure is at least visible in Crashlytics/Talker.
- **Done when:** The catch narrows to the specific expected exception type; every other path logs via AppLogger before returning; a regression test that makes enqueueStreakPayload throw asserts the failure is logged, not silently dropped.
- **Labels:** eh-3, eh-4, error-handling, sync · verifier corrections: The cited 'closes the gap' comment is the doc-comment immediately above _appendStreakEvent (~line 727), not the file's top header — minor mislabel, doesn't affect the claim's substance since it's in the same file and dir
