#### AUD-notifications-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Guard ref access after await in notification_providers.dart effect providers (SM-4)
- **Rule:** SM-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** allProfilesReminderBootstrap, reminderSyncEffect and streakAlertSyncEffect all touch ref (read/watch) immediately after an await with no ref.mounted guard. If any of these keepAlive FutureProviders is invalidated or disposed while suspended past its first await (profile switch, container teardown during navigation/tests, hot-reload), the next ref access throws UnmountedRefException uncaught, leaving the provider's AsyncValue stuck in .error and silently freezing that profile's notification (re)scheduling until something else forces a rebuild.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:589` — “final profiles = await ref.watch(profileListStreamProvider.future);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:590` — “final gateway = ref.read(notificationServiceProvider);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:468` — “final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:499` — “final tasks = await ref.watch(allDailyTasksProvider.future);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:523` — “final location = ref.read(sacredLocationProvider);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:736` — “await service.cancelAlert();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:737` — “final analytics = ref.read(analyticsServiceProvider);”
- **Fix:** Add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` immediately after each await, before any further ref access, in all three functions.
- **Done when:** A test that invalidates a watched dependency mid-flight (e.g. activeProfileIdProvider while profileListStreamProvider.future is pending) asserts the effect settles instead of throwing UnmountedRefException. · A Rule-0 grep/lint flags ref.read(/ref.watch( on a line whose nearest preceding statement in the same async function contains await with no intervening ref.mounted check.
- **Labels:** riverpod, sm-4, notifications, hotspot

#### AUD-notifications-02 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Stop returning a hardcoded default from build() in the 5 notification preference providers (SM-2)
- **Rule:** SM-2 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 7 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** ReminderEnabled, ReminderTime, StreakAlertEnabled, StreakAlertTime and RewardNotificationEnabled all fire an async SharedPreferences load from build() and return a hardcoded default first. reminder_sync_sacred_time_test.dart's own comment documents the real consequence: this oscillation 'invalidates this effect mid-flight, disposing the first in-flight future (Riverpod throws "disposed during loading")' for any dependent FutureProvider whenever the persisted value differs from the default -- the test only passes by retrying up to 10 times. The M3 fix (lines 463-467) patches only reminderSyncEffect's symptom by re-reading SharedPreferences directly; the root defect reaches every other consumer (UI switches, streakAlertSyncEffect, future code) unmitigated.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:62` — “_loadFromPrefs(profileId);
    return true; // synchronous default; overwritten once prefs load completes”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:150` — “_loadFromPrefs(profileId);
    return true; // synchronous default; overwritten once prefs load completes”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:238` — “_loadFromPrefs(profileId);
    return true; // synchronous default; overwritten once prefs load completes”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/providers/reminder_sync_sacred_time_test.dart:260` — “// reminderEnabledProvider returns the default `true` synchronously and
      // then async-loads the persisted `false`. That state change i”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/providers/reminder_sync_sacred_time_test.dart:267` — “for (var i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
        try {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:463` — “// M3 fix: the pref notifiers return defaults (enabled=true, 19:00)
  // synchronously, then async-load the real values.”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:725` — “final enabled = ref.watch(streakAlertEnabledProvider);
  final time = ref.watch(streakAlertTimeProvider);”
- **Fix:** Convert these 5 providers to AsyncNotifier<T> (or an equivalent that actually awaits SharedPreferences before emitting) so there is no synchronous-default race; then delete the M3 workaround in reminderSyncEffect.
- **Done when:** A unit test asserts reminderEnabledProvider (and siblings) never emits the hardcoded default when a differing persisted value exists for the resolved profile. · reminder_sync_sacred_time_test.dart's retry-loop workaround (lines 265-274) is deleted once the fix lands and the test still passes on the first attempt.
- **Labels:** riverpod, sm-2, notifications, hotspot · merged 1 duplicate report(s)

#### AUD-notifications-05 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Log-less catch blocks in notifications swallow exceptions with no AppLogger trail (EH-3)
- **Rule:** EH-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** None of the three call AppLogger, so a real production failure is indistinguishable from the expected/benign case. The outbox-facade catch is the most consequential: it catches ANY exception from the whole outboxSyncWriteFacadeProvider dependency chain -- not just the 'test doesn't override this provider' case its comment describes -- and silently disables cloud sync of notification settings for that session with zero diagnostic trail.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:279` — “} catch (_) {
      // Some tests build notification providers without full sync dependencies.”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/widgets/timezone_lifecycle_observer.dart:62` — “} catch (_) {
      // Timezone re-detection failed — keep existing tz.local.”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/domain/services/notification_initializer.dart:47` — “} catch (_) {
      // Platform query failed — leave tz.local as UTC rather than crash.”
- **Fix:** Log via AppLogger in all three; for the outbox-facade catch, narrow the caught condition so only the intended test-scaffolding case is swallowed and real errors are logged/propagated distinctly.
- **Done when:** Each catch gains a corresponding AppLogger call. · A grep for catch (_) { or catch (e) { in lib/features/notifications without a following AppLogger call in the same block fails CI.
- **Labels:** eh-3, error-handling, notifications

#### AUD-notifications-06 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Route sacred_window_repository.dart through the sacred_time barrel instead of deep cross-feature imports (Rule 2)
- **Rule:** Rule 2 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** features/notifications reaches directly into features/sacred_time's domain internals instead of features/sacred_time/sacred_time.dart (itself an empty stub barrel with no exports), so a refactor inside sacred_time's domain layer can silently break notification scheduling with no barrel-boundary warning. Separately, make audit check 15's awk pattern always compares a feature name against itself: it runs match() against $0 (the whole grep -rn line, which starts with the FILE PATH), so the first 'features/X/' match in $0 is always the same X captured from $1 -- a[1] and b[1] can never differ, so check 15 can never print a warning for ANY file. This is confirmed empirically: check 15 produced zero WARN output in the clean-tree baseline despite this real cross-feature import existing.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/data/services/sacred_window_repository.dart:4` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/sacred_time/domain/models/sacred_location.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/data/services/sacred_window_repository.dart:6` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/sacred_time/domain/services/zmanim_window_service.dart';”; `learning_tracker/learning_tracker/Makefile:380` — “match($1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print”
- **Fix:** Populate features/sacred_time/sacred_time.dart with the needed exports (SacredLocation, SacredWindow, ZmanimWindowService) and import through it; separately fix the Makefile check 15 awk pattern to extract the import path (not the full grep line) before comparing feature names.
- **Done when:** make audit check 15, once its awk bug is fixed, flags this file today and reports clean after the barrel fix is applied.
- **Labels:** layering, rule-2, notifications, make-audit-bug · verifier corrections: Third evidence item cites 'learning_tracker/learning_tracker/Makefile:380' -- that path doesn't exist (double-nested). Real file is learning_tracker/Makefile; the quoted awk pattern appears verbatim at lines 378 and 384,

#### AUD-notifications-07 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Use a clock-skew-safe timestamp, not client clock, for notification_settings updated_at LWW field
- **Rule:** FB-2 (pattern) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** This client-computed timestamp becomes the payload's updated_at field pushed via enqueueNotificationSettings; core/sync/merge/notification_settings_merger.dart (outside this batch) parses remote['updated_at'] to arbitrate LWW. If two devices' clocks disagree, the device with the faster/wrong clock can push a stale settings change that looks 'newer' and wins over a genuinely newer change made on a correctly-clocked device, silently reverting the user's real edit with no error surfaced anywhere. Confirming the full blast radius requires reading the outbox-drain write path (outside this batch) to see whether it overwrites this field with FieldValue.serverTimestamp() before commit.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:341` — “final updatedAtMs = DateTimeFactory.nowUtc().millisecondsSinceEpoch;”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:366` — “'updated_at': DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(
      updatedAtMs,”
- **Fix:** Confirm whether the write path already substitutes a server timestamp before commit; if not, do so, or route the push side through the same clock-skew arbitration MergeStore.remoteIsNewer already implements for the pull side.
- **Done when:** A sync test with an artificially-skewed local clock demonstrates the genuinely later settings write wins regardless of which device has the faster clock.
- **Labels:** sync, fb-2, notifications, clock-skew · verifier corrections: DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() confirmed to be raw SystemLocalDayClock (core/utils/date_utils.dart:15-19) — genuinely uncorrected client clock, strengthening the claim.

#### AUD-notifications-09 · **P2** · SUSPECTED · Wrap SacredWindowEntries clear+insert in one transaction (DB-2)
- **Rule:** DB-2 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The table is briefly empty between clearAll() completing and insertAll() starting; neither call is awaited by any caller and neither is wrapped in a transaction. invalidate()'s own separate unawaited clearAll() (line 50) can also interleave with _persistToDb()'s clear-then-insert pair (line 167) in either order. The class's own doc says this cache exists so 'background notification-fire-time checks can read them on cold-start without the Flutter engine' -- a background read landing in the empty gap, or after invalidate() wins a race against a slower insertAll(), sees no Sacred Time windows and could fail to suppress a notification during Shabbos/Yom Tov, the entire point of DNI-367. Confirming the full consequence requires reading the background notification-fire-time isolate handler, which is outside this batch.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/data/services/sacred_window_repository.dart:50` — “_dao?.clearAll();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/data/services/sacred_window_repository.dart:167` — “dao.clearAll().then((_) => dao.insertAll(companions)).ignore();”
- **Fix:** Wrap clear+insert in one db.transaction(...) and await it from both invalidate() and _persistToDb(), or add an explicit generation-counter guard so a stale clear can't stomp a newer insert.
- **Done when:** A DAO-level test that races invalidate() against a concurrent _persistToDb() cycle never observes SacredWindowEntries transition through an empty state once a non-empty write has committed.
- **Labels:** drift, db-2, notifications, race-condition

#### AUD-notifications-11 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Convert ReminderPreferences to @freezed instead of hand-rolled ==/hashCode/copyWith
- **Rule:** naming/placement — data classes must be @freezed · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Matches the coding standard's explicit rule to never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes. The 7 fields are consistent between == and hashCode today, but every future field addition is a manual 3-way sync across the constructor, ==, hashCode and copyWith -- an easy place to introduce a silent equality bug (a field present in the constructor but missed in == makes two logically-different instances compare equal).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/domain/models/reminder_preferences.dart:75` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>
      identical(this, other) ||”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/domain/models/reminder_preferences.dart:88` — “int get hashCode => Object.hash(
    reminderEnabled,”
- **Fix:** Convert to @freezed class ReminderPreferences with _$ReminderPreferences.
- **Done when:** dart run build_runner build generates the freezed file and existing tests (e.g. notification_providers_deep_test.dart groups H/A-E) keep passing unmodified.
- **Labels:** hygiene, freezed, notifications

### features/onboarding  (17 findings — 0 P0 / 6 P1 / 5 P2 / 6 P3)

#### AUD-onboarding-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Check ref.mounted/State.mounted before touching state after await in onboarding async flows
- **Rule:** SM-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException when a disposed Notifier's ref/state is touched, and Flutter throws on setState() after dispose(). OnboardingController is @riverpod (autoDispose); if the wizard screen holding it is popped while current.save(ref) (a DB-touching step save) is in flight, advance() resumes and unconditionally reads/writes state, crashing. bulk_mark_screen.dart demonstrably knows the correct pattern -- _loadPreExistingCompletions checks mounted twice -- yet _proceedToConfirmation and both branches of _executeBulkMark omit it after their own awaits, so backgrounding the app or hitting back during a multi-hundred-item bulk-mark write reproduces the same crash class.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/providers/onboarding_controller.dart:69` — “await current.save(ref);
    if (!state.hasNext) return null;”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/bulk_mark_screen.dart:358` — “setState(() {
      _resolvedItems = resolved;”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/bulk_mark_screen.dart:381` — “final result = await service.execute(...);

      setState(() {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/bulk_mark_screen.dart:406` — “} catch (e) {
      setState(() {
        _error = e.toString();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/steps/onboarding_profile_creation_step.dart:133` — “ref.read(selectedProfileIdProvider.notifier).select(profile.id);
    await PendingLocalSignupStore.finalizeAfterFirstProfile(ref);”
- **Fix:** Add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` / `if (!mounted) return;` immediately after every await that is followed by a state=/setState/provider touch, matching the pattern already used correctly elsewhere in the same files.
- **Done when:** a notifier/widget test that disposes the provider/widget mid-await (pump then pop before the fake repository's Future completes) passes without throwing · a grep-based Rule-0 checker (or the fixed custom_lint) flags `state =`/`setState(` appearing after an `await` in a Notifier/State method without an intervening mounted guard
- **Labels:** riverpod, lifecycle, crash, onboarding · verifier corrections: Line 381/406 quotes in bulk_mark_screen.dart span across a small gap (e.g. cited line 381 quote actually starts at source line 375 and the setState opening brace itself is at 381/406 respectively) -- an elided-quote conv

#### AUD-onboarding-02 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Fix WizardCustomStep2 Slider crash when a 5th custom review round defaults delayDays to 90 (slider max is 60)
- **Rule:** TQ-8 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** CustomRoundState.withDefault(4) seeds the 5th review round's delayDays at 90, but _RoundTimingCard's delay Slider is capped at max:60. WizardCustomStep1's own slider allows chazarahRounds up to 5; advancing to WizardCustomStep2 renders all 5 timing cards immediately (ListView.builder over the full list), so the 5th Slider is constructed with value:90 outside [1,60]. Verified empirically with a throwaway flutter-test render: 'Failed assertion: ... `value >= min && value <= max`: Value 90.0 is not between minimum 1.0 and maximum 60.0' (package:flutter/src/material/slider.dart) — this fires in every debug/profile build and in `flutter test`, making the custom-review-builder path unusable for anyone who picks 5 rounds. No test anywhere sets chazarahRounds above 3 (line 683 is the batch's own highest), so nothing catches it.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/steps/wizard_steps.dart:31` — “const defaults = [1, 7, 30, 60, 90];”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/steps/wizard_steps.dart:763` — “max: 60,”; `learning_tracker/test/features/onboarding/presentation/steps/wizard_steps_l1_test.dart:683` — “stepData.chazarahRounds = 3;”
- **Fix:** Clamp the Slider's max to 90 (adjust divisions accordingly) or clamp state.delayDays when building the Slider's value; add a WizardCustomStep2 test that renders all 5 rounds (chazarahRounds=5) and asserts tester.takeException() is null.
- **Done when:** Slider value stays within [min,max] for every roundIndex 0..4 CustomRoundState.withDefault can produce · a regression test renders WizardCustomStep2 with 5 rounds and asserts no exception is thrown
- **Labels:** crash, boundary-condition, onboarding-wizard, slider · verifier corrections: Minor, non-fatal quibbles only: (1) the cited rule TQ-8 ('every bug fix lands with a regression test... every audit finding states its repro') is a process/meta-rule about the audit and fix workflow, not a rule the code 

#### AUD-onboarding-03 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Localize auth_validators.dart's hardcoded English error messages via AppLocalizations
- **Rule:** EH-5, AX-2 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** signup_screen.dart and sign_in_screen.dart call these validators directly on the account-creation form. A Hebrew-locale user sees raw English 'Email is required' / 'Password must be at least 6 characters' on one of the very first screens of the app instead of a translated message. auth_validators_test.dart and account_creation_validation_test.dart both assert these exact English literals as the correct return value, so a future ARB-based fix must touch both test files in the same change or they go red for the right reason.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/domain/validators/auth_validators.dart:10` — “return 'Email is required';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/domain/validators/auth_validators.dart:14` — “return 'Please enter a valid email address';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/domain/validators/auth_validators.dart:25` — “return 'Password must be at least 6 characters';”; `learning_tracker/test/features/onboarding/domain/validators/auth_validators_test.dart:18` — “expect(validateEmail(null), 'Email is required');”
- **Fix:** Add ARB keys (authEmailRequired, authEmailInvalid, authPasswordRequired, authPasswordTooShort, authDisplayNameRequired) to app_en.arb/app_he.arb; change the validators to resolve through AppLocalizations (or return a stable error-code enum resolved to text at the call site); update auth_validators_test.dart and account_creation_validation_test.dart to assert localized output per locale.
- **Done when:** A regression test pumps the sign-up/sign-in form in Locale('he') and asserts the Hebrew validation string renders (mirroring bulk_mark_screen_test.dart's 'title and heading are localized in Hebrew locale' pattern) · No literal English message string is returned directly from validateEmail/validatePassword/validateDisplayName
- **Labels:** i18n, onboarding, auth

#### AUD-onboarding-04 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Replace raw English string literals with AppLocalizations across onboarding screens, steps, and validators
- **Rule:** AX-2 / EH-5 · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 47 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** Hebrew-locale users (this app's RTL-supported primary non-English audience) hit untranslated English text through nearly every screen of the core onboarding flow: all 6 onboarding_screen.dart AppBar titles, the entire Parent-PIN setup screen (6 strings, file has no AppLocalizations import at all), 4 of 5 strings on the child hand-off screen, both add-another-track strings, 5 strings in the bulk-mark confirmation/search/done flow, ~19 strings across the learning-process wizard (wizard_steps.dart) including a literal mixed-language bug where Mon/Tue/Wed/Thu/Fri/Sun render in English but Shabbos correctly renders via terms.shabbos in the same label, the duplicated profile-name-exists error, and 3 signup/sign-in form validators whose return values render directly as TextFormField errorText. test/features/onboarding/presentation/steps/wizard_steps_l1_test.dart pins several of these literal strings directly (find.text('Follow a program'), find.text('How do you review?')), so the existing test suite locks in the bug instead of catching it.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/bulk_mark_screen.dart:351` — “'You must leave at least some content unmarked to continue learning.',”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/bulk_mark_screen.dart:539` — “'${_selections.length} selection(s)',”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/onboarding_screen.dart:323` — “_ScreenPhase.parentPinSetup => const AppBarTitle(text: 'Set Parent PIN'),”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/onboarding_screen.dart:330` — “_ScreenPhase.done => const AppBarTitle(text: 'All Set!'),”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/steps/onboarding_handoff_step.dart:45` — “"$name's learning is all set up",”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/steps/onboarding_handoff_step.dart:59` — “'You can set up rewards later in Parent Mode',”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/steps/onboarding_parent_pin_step.dart:55` — “_pinError = 'PINs do not match';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/steps/onboarding_parent_pin_step.dart:93` — “'Set a 4-digit PIN to access parent controls for $childName. '” _(+14 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Extract every literal into ARB keys mirroring the correct usages already present in the same files (e.g. l10n.startLearning), add ICU plurals for count-driven strings (trackCount, delayDays, _selections.length), replace the hardcoded day-abbreviation maps with a helper backed by AppLocalizations/DateFormat.EEEE so all 7 days localize uniformly, and update wizard_steps_l1_test.dart/related tests to assert on localized output instead of literal English text.
- **Done when:** make arb-parity stays green after new keys are added · a Rule-0 grep/lint added under lib/features/onboarding/presentation/** fails when a raw string literal (not an AppLocalizations getter) is passed to Text()/errorText/hintText/label — the AX-2 [P] literals checker this backlog needs · wizard_steps_l1_test.dart assertions changed from find.text('Follow a program') to locale-driven lookups so a regression re-breaks the test · manual/e2e pass with Locale('he') through onboarding shows no Latin-script UI copy and no mixed-language day labels
- **Labels:** i18n, AX-2, onboarding, hebrew · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches · verifier corrections: None needed — all quotes and line numbers matched exactly on inspection. Minor note: the finding's evidence file paths omit the `learning_tracker/` prefix used for the test file (learning_tracker/test/...) versus lib pat

#### AUD-onboarding-05 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Stop surfacing e.toString() as user-facing error text in BulkMarkScreen; route through AppErrorView/l10n
- **Rule:** EH-2, EH-5, no_e_to_string_in_ui · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** When BulkPriorCompletionService.execute() throws for any reason, the raw Dart exception's toString() renders directly in the confirmation-phase error banner shown mid-onboarding — untranslated, implementation-detail text like 'Exception: Network error'. onboarding_bulk_l1_test.dart's 'error in execute stays on confirmation with error text' test asserts this raw string as correct, so the anti-pattern is regression-protected instead of caught. bulk_mark_screen.dart already imports AppErrorView (line 11) but doesn't use it here — this is exactly the pattern the (currently non-functional) no_e_to_string_in_ui custom lint targets.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/bulk_mark_screen.dart:407` — “_error = e.toString();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/bulk_mark_screen.dart:650` — “_error!,”; `learning_tracker/test/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/onboarding_bulk_l1_test.dart:1080` — “expect(find.textContaining('Exception: Network error'), findsOneWidget);”
- **Fix:** Catch the specific exception types execute() can throw, map them to AppLocalizations-resolved messages (or AppErrorView), and update the test to assert the localized string instead of the exception's toString().
- **Done when:** onboarding_bulk_l1_test.dart's error-path test asserts an AppLocalizations-sourced string, verified in both Locale('en') and Locale('he'), not a literal 'Exception: ...' substring · Once custom_lint's analyzer version pin is fixed, dart run custom_lint reports no no_e_to_string_in_ui violations in bulk_mark_screen.dart
- **Labels:** error-handling, i18n, onboarding

#### AUD-onboarding-06 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Wrap multi-statement Drift writes in transaction() in the wizard stage-apply and prior-completion expunge paths
- **Rule:** DB-2 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** A process death (OOM kill, backgrounding) between the delete and the insert loop in applyWizardResult leaves a track with zero or partial review stages, breaking the B6 'every configured stage needs a completion row' invariant documented in bulk_prior_completion_service.dart's own docstring -- for both first-run onboarding and the edit-track flow. StageDao already ships a transactional `replaceStagesForTrack` (stage_dao.dart:83-93, wraps the identical delete+insert in db.transaction()) and a generic `runTransaction` helper, but applyWizardResult calls the raw untransacted DAO methods instead. Separately, expungePriorCompletions tombstones completion_events, deletes prior_completion_imports, then loops outbox inserts as three independently-awaited steps with no enclosing transaction; a crash after the tombstone UPDATE but before the outbox inserts land leaves the local device showing an item as unmarked while every other synced device still shows it complete, because the tombstone never reaches Firestore.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/domain/services/learning_process_wizard_service.dart:92` — “await _stageDao.deleteStagesForTrack(trackId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/domain/services/learning_process_wizard_service.dart:144` — “await _stageDao.insertStageDefinition(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/domain/services/bulk_prior_completion_service.dart:361` — “await (_database.update(_database.completionEvents)..where(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/domain/services/bulk_prior_completion_service.dart:412` — “await _outboxDao.insertOutboxRow(”
- **Fix:** Call the existing StageDao.replaceStagesForTrack/runTransaction helper from applyWizardResult instead of raw delete+insert; wrap expungePriorCompletions's update+delete+insert sequence in _database.transaction().
- **Done when:** a test that throws inside the stage-insert loop (fake DAO) asserts zero stages remain afterward (rollback), not a partial set · a test that throws after the tombstone UPDATE in expungePriorCompletions asserts the prior_completion_imports row still exists (rollback) instead of a half-tombstoned state · a DB-2 Rule-0 grep checker flags >1 awaited mutation in a service method with no enclosing db.transaction()
- **Labels:** drift, transactions, data-integrity, onboarding · verifier corrections: None needed; all cited file:line evidence is accurate.

#### AUD-onboarding-07 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Await BulkMarkScreen._expungeRefs's expunge writes before invalidating dependent providers
- **Rule:** Nygard-lens (unordered I/O) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The loop fires expungePriorCompletions (which internally does multiple awaited DB writes) without awaiting it, then immediately calls ref.invalidate on the dashboard/progress providers. Because those providers are manually invalidated rather than backed by a reactive .watch() stream, the invalidated providers can refetch before the un-awaited expunge write lands, showing the user a stale (pre-expunge) completion count right after unticking a previously-marked item. Confirming this needs a widget test with a deliberately delayed fake CompletionRepository asserting the provider's value immediately after _toggleItem completes.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/bulk_mark_screen.dart:303` — “service
          .expungePriorCompletions(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/bulk_mark_screen.dart:319` — “ref.invalidate(dashboardCompletionPercentageProvider(widget.curriculumId));”
- **Fix:** await Future.wait(refs.map((r) => service.expungePriorCompletions(...))) before the ref.invalidate calls, or move invalidation into a .whenComplete() continuation.
- **Done when:** a test with an artificially delayed expunge write asserts the dashboard provider reflects the post-expunge count immediately after the awaited toggle completes, not the pre-expunge count
- **Labels:** race-condition, riverpod, onboarding

#### AUD-onboarding-08 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · BulkPriorCompletionService.execute()'s profileId branch bypasses DI and its bookmark write is never asserted
- **Rule:** SM-7, TQ-8 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** When execute() runs with a non-null profileId — the live path add_track_flow_screen.dart uses when a parent adds a track for a specific child — the service `new`s up a BookmarkRepositoryImpl directly instead of using the injected _bookmarkRepository, so no test double can intercept it (no seam). bulk_prior_completion_service_test.dart's execute() tests never pass profileId, so that branch never runs there at all. bulk_prior_completion_siyum_detection_test.dart does pass profileId (lines 333, 372) so the branch does run against a real in-memory DB, but neither test reads back the bookmarks table afterward — the branch's correctness (right profileId, right track resolved) is completely unverified. A bug here would silently point a child's bookmark at the wrong profile/track with no test failure.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/domain/services/bulk_prior_completion_service.dart:282` — “? BookmarkRepositoryImpl(”; `learning_tracker/test/features/onboarding/domain/services/bulk_prior_completion_service_test.dart:234` — “final result = await service.execute(”; `learning_tracker/test/features/onboarding/domain/services/bulk_prior_completion_siyum_detection_test.dart:333` — “profileId: profileId,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/domain/services/bulk_prior_completion_service.dart:281` — “final bookmarkRepo = profileId != null
          ? BookmarkRepositoryImpl(”
- **Fix:** Parameterize bookmarkRepositoryProvider as a .family(profileId) (or inject a BookmarkRepository factory into BulkPriorCompletionService) so the profileId path goes through the same injectable seam as the rest of the class; add an assertion in bulk_prior_completion_siyum_detection_test.dart that reads back the bookmark row for the target profile and checks it points at the expected sefariaRef.
- **Done when:** A test calls execute(profileId: X) and then asserts (via a real or fake repository read) that the bookmark was written under profile X · bulk_prior_completion_service.dart contains no direct `BookmarkRepositoryImpl(` construction outside a provider
- **Labels:** di, testing, onboarding · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches

#### AUD-onboarding-09 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Hoist EmptyLoginScreen's getAllAccounts() future out of build()
- **Rule:** PF-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** future: is evaluated fresh on every rebuild of EmptyLoginScreen (theme change, locale change, any ancestor rebuild), so FutureBuilder restarts from its loading/no-data state each time, re-querying the device registry and making the account-switch icon flicker/disappear-and-reappear on unrelated rebuilds instead of staying stable.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/empty_login_screen.dart:40` — “future: ref.read(deviceRegistryProvider).getAllAccounts(),”
- **Fix:** Move the Future into a @riverpod FutureProvider (e.g. allDeviceAccountsProvider) and ref.watch it, or cache it in a late final in a stateful wrapper.
- **Done when:** a widget test that triggers an unrelated rebuild of EmptyLoginScreen asserts getAllAccounts() is called exactly once, not once per rebuild
- **Labels:** performance, PF-3, onboarding

#### AUD-onboarding-10 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Localize the hardcoded '…yos' decorative chip text in IntroMishnaIllustration
- **Rule:** AX-2 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The sibling chip on the same illustration correctly resolves via AppLocalizations (introMishnaReviewChip: 'Review…' EN / 'חזרה…' HE), but this second floating chip is a literal, unlocalized Latin-script fragment rendered unconditionally regardless of locale. In Hebrew locale a user sees a stray Latin '…yos' fragment floating over an otherwise fully-Hebrew first-run screen. No test in app_intro_screen_l1_test.dart's dedicated l10n-leak regression group — whose stated purpose is guarding this exact screen against exactly this class of bug — catches it, because that group checks a different text element on the same page.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/widgets/intro_mishna_page.dart:71` — “'…yos',”
- **Fix:** Add an ARB key for the fragment with a real Hebrew value (or drop it for HE if the design intent doesn't survive translation), and extend app_intro_screen_l1_test.dart's Hebrew l10n group to assert on it.
- **Done when:** make arb-parity and flutter analyze stay clean after adding the key · app_intro_screen_l1_test.dart's 'l10n — Hebrew locale renders Hebrew, not English literals' group gains an assertion that the English fragment does not appear in Locale('he')
- **Labels:** i18n, onboarding

#### AUD-onboarding-11 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Log the swallowed exception in BulkMarkScreen._loadPreExistingCompletions's catch block
- **Rule:** EH-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The B7 pre-tick feature (pre-checking previously-completed items when the bulk-mark screen opens) fails completely silently on any exception -- DB error, malformed hierarchy data -- with zero telemetry. If pre-ticking breaks in production (e.g. after a schema change), nobody will know; users will see every item as unticked and may re-mark (and re-earn siyum credit for) content already completed, with no log line to diagnose why.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/bulk_mark_screen.dart:149` — “} catch (_) {
      // Non-fatal: if pre-tick loading fails just open with unticked state.”
- **Fix:** Log via AppLogger.instance.warning(event: ..., exception: e, stackTrace: st) before falling through to the unticked-state fallback, matching the pattern already used in _expungeRefs's .catchError a few lines below in the same file.
- **Done when:** a test that forces getContentForCurriculum/getCompletionsByCurriculum to throw asserts AppLogger.instance received a warning/error call · the log-less-catch half of the Rule-0 empty-catch checker (once shipped) flags any catch block in lib/ with no AppLogger call and no rethrow
- **Labels:** error-handling, EH-3, observability, onboarding

#### AUD-onboarding-12 · **P3** · SUSPECTED · Confirm whether Positioned(left:/right:) illustration badges in intro pages need PositionedDirectional for RTL
- **Rule:** AX-1 (spirit) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 6 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** AX-1's RTL rule is written against EdgeInsets.only(left/right) and Alignment.centerLeft/Right, but Positioned(left:/right:) has the identical non-mirroring failure mode under RTL that PositionedDirectional(start:/end:) avoids. app_intro_screen_l1_test.dart's RTL smoke test only checks the screen mounts without throwing, not badge placement, so a mirroring regression on these floating badges in Hebrew locale would not be caught. This may be an intentional 'decorative collage doesn't need to mirror' choice rather than a bug — needs a visual check to confirm either way.

- **Fix:** Take a Locale('he') screenshot of AppIntroScreen pages 2-3 (reusing the app_intro_rewards_cta_overlap_test.dart rig) and confirm badge placement reads correctly; switch to PositionedDirectional(start:/end:) if not.
- **Done when:** A golden or screenshot test of pages 2-3 in Locale('he') exists and has been reviewed for correct badge placement
- **Labels:** rtl, onboarding, accessibility

#### AUD-onboarding-14 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Extract the hardcoded 'לימוד' stage-name sentinel to a shared constant
- **Rule:** Evans ubiquitous language, Fowler duplication · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** DomainTermLabels.resolveStoredStageName documents this literal as the canonical sentinel matched via HebrewTerms.stageNameMap to resolve the correct localized stage name at render time — it is load-bearing, not decorative. It's independently hand-typed in 3 separate files (2 sites in this batch's paired lib file) with no shared constant tying them together; a typo in one copy would silently break resolveStoredStageName's lookup for stages created by that one code path only, and nothing would catch it since the value is a plain string, not a shared symbol.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/domain/services/learning_process_wizard_service.dart:170` — “stageName: 'לימוד',”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/domain/services/learning_process_wizard_service.dart:216` — “stageName: 'לימוד',”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/constants/curriculum_defaults.dart:14` — “stageName: 'לימוד',”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/stages/data/repositories/stage_definition_repository_impl.dart:23` — “(stageOrder: 1, stageName: 'לימוד', delayDays: 0),”

#### AUD-onboarding-16 · **P3** · SUSPECTED · Stop surfacing PinService's raw ArgumentError.message as OnboardingParentPinStep's error text
- **Rule:** EH-2 / EH-5 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1] · filed P2, revised

#### AUD-profiles-01 · **P0** · CONFIRMED · Fix ParentTrackManagementScreen 'Archive (keep history)' — it wipes stage/goal/point config via deleteTrackAndData exactly like 'Delete and wipe history', and ts3_parent_track_archive_test.dart doesn't catch it
- **Rule:** TQ-8 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 13 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** A parent long-presses a track and taps 'Archive (keep history)'; the dialog literally asks 'What should happen to your child's completion history?' implying preservation. The real handler calls curriculumActivationServiceProvider.deactivate() -> ActiveCurriculumDao.deactivateByProfile() -> TrackDao.deleteTrackAndData(), whose own doc-comment says it 'clears config' by hard-deleting goals, stage_definitions, daily_plan rows, point_config, curriculum_scope, study_day_config, track_learning_order and the program-enrolment row, then sets state='deleted' — functionally identical to the 'Delete and wipe history' option (purgeHistory), which only additionally hard-deletes the track row and tombstones completions. `grep -rn TrackState.archived lib/` finds zero writers anywhere in production code — the 'archived' state the TS-3 fix was supposed to introduce is dead. None of the tests that claim to guard this catch it: ts3's 'DB unit' test hand-writes state=archived directly instead of calling deactivate()/deactivateByProfile(); its 'widget' test discards the real screen and shows a hand-built AlertDialog with hardcoded 'Archive (keep history)' text, so it always passes regardless of what the production dialog does; and the l1 suite's archive test only checks the track is absent from the *active* list, which is equally true whether state is 'archived' or 'deleted'. Repo-wide search found no other test (active_curriculum_dao_test.dart, track_dao_last_curriculum_guard_test.dart, epic_26_story_26_22_track_management_body_test.dart) asserting config survives a real deactivate() call — one of those files even names deleteTrackAndData's soft-delete '(archive)' in its own test description, i.e. the codebase's own test suite has internalised 'archive = wipe config' as normal, contradicting the UI copy and the TS-3 docstring's stated intent.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/screens/parent_track_management_screen.dart:293` — “.read(curriculumActivationServiceProvider)
.deactivate(curriculum);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/domain/services/curriculum_activation_service.dart:125` — “await _database.activeCurriculumDao.deactivateByProfile(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/active_curriculum_dao.dart:101` — “/// Delegates to [TrackDao.deleteTrackAndData] for each track belonging to”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/active_curriculum_dao.dart:124` — “await attachedDatabase.trackDao.deleteTrackAndData(track.id);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/track_dao.dart:208` — “/// Soft-delete a track by setting state = 'deleted' and clearing config.”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/track_dao.dart:245` — “state: const Value(TrackState.deleted),”; `learning_tracker/lib/l10n/app_en.arb:1935` — “"deleteTrackArchive": "Archive (keep history)",”; `learning_tracker/test/features/profiles/presentation/screens/ts3_parent_track_archive_test.dart:179` — “// Simulate exactly what the fixed archive path does:
// set state='archived' without deleting config rows.” _(+5 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Product decision required: (a) implement genuine archive semantics — set state=TrackState.archived and skip the config-table deletes in the code path 'archive' actually calls, or (b) if wiping config on archive is intentional, fix the misleading 'Archive (keep history)' / 'your child's completion history' copy to say what really happens and delete the dead TrackState.archived constant. Either way, rewrite ts3_parent_track_archive_test.dart's widget test to drive the real ParentTrackManagementScreen (longPress + tap on the actual widget tree, as parent_track_management_screen_l1_test.dart already does) and assert on stage_definitions/goal/point_config row survival, not a hand-rolled dialog.
- **Done when:** A widget test that longPresses a track on the real ParentTrackManagementScreen, taps the real 'Archive (keep history)' action, and asserts stage_definitions/goals/point_config rows for that track still exist afterward — this test fails on current main and passes only after the fix. · `grep -rn 'TrackState.archived' learning_tracker/lib/` finds at least one write site (currently zero). · ts3_parent_track_archive_test.dart's widget test pumps ParentTrackManagementScreen and interacts with its actual dialog, not a hand-built AlertDialog.

#### AUD-profiles-02 · **P0** · CONFIRMED · Stop ProfileRepositoryImpl.updateProfile silently swallowing tutor Cloud-Function write failures
- **Rule:** EH-2/EH-3 (typed errors must reach a boundary as values, no log-less catch) + Nygard lens (retry-assumption mismatch across facade implementations) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 8 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** ProfileRepositoryImpl wraps every _syncEngine?.pushLearnerProfile(...) call in a blanket catch(_) {} (createProfile:104-109, updateProfile:157-161, self-heal:321-336), on the premise that 'local write already succeeded (offline-first)' and the push will retry later. That premise only holds when _syncEngine is the durable OutboxSyncWriteFacade. Per sync_providers.dart:75-78, when a tutor session is active, _syncEngine is instead a TutoredWriteRouter that turns pushLearnerProfile into a one-shot, non-retryable Cloud Function RPC (tutorEditProfile). When that RPC fails (network drop, CF timeout, or the tutor's grant expiring mid-session), the failure is discarded: updateProfile still returns its local model as if the push succeeded, so the tutor's own local mirror shows the rename/mode/avatar change permanently while the owner's actual Firestore profile was never touched — a silent, non-retryable divergence between what the tutor sees and what actually persisted, with zero error surfaced. This also makes editProfileFlow's dedicated 'on TutorWriteException catch' (profile_edit_delete_actions.dart:46) dead code: repo.updateProfile can only ever let StateError or DuplicateProfileNameException (line 134) escape to its caller, and editProfileFlow doesn't catch the latter at all, so even a same-account name collision on the Edit flow throws unhandled — unlike ProfilePickerScreen's own separate rename dialog, which does catch DuplicateProfileNameException. profile_edit_delete_actions_test.dart exercises neither path (zero references to TutorWriteException or DuplicateProfileNameException in the whole file).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/data/repositories/profile_repository_impl.dart:159` — “} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded (offline-first)”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart:75` — “/// When a tutor session is active ([activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider] !=
/// null) the outbox facade is wrapped by a [TutoredWriteRout”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/profile_edit_delete_actions.dart:46` — “} on TutorWriteException catch (e) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/data/repositories/profile_repository_impl.dart:134` — “throw DuplicateProfileNameException(trimmedName);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/data/repositories/profile_repository_impl.dart:107` — “} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded (offline-first)”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/data/repositories/profile_repository_impl.dart:335` — “} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded.”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/data/repositories/profile_repository_impl.dart:250` — “await _syncEngine?.deleteLearnerProfile(id);
    _log.info(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/data/repositories/profile_repository_impl.dart:105` — “try {
      await _syncEngine?.pushLearnerProfile(_toFirestorePayload(model));”
- **Fix:** Only swallow pushLearnerProfile failures when the underlying facade is genuinely durable/retryable (OutboxSyncWriteFacade); let a TutorWriteException-shaped failure propagate (or convert it to a typed Result the caller must handle) so editProfileFlow's existing catch becomes reachable and can tell the tutor the edit didn't save. Add a catch for DuplicateProfileNameException in editProfileFlow mirroring profile_picker_screen.dart's _showRenameDialog.
- **Done when:** ProfileRepositoryImpl no longer unconditionally swallows pushLearnerProfile failures when the sync facade is the tutor-routed (non-durable) path · editProfileFlow catches DuplicateProfileNameException and shows the existing profileNameTaken feedback, matching profile_picker_screen.dart's rename dialog · New regression test: a failed tutor-routed pushLearnerProfile surfaces a user-visible error from editProfileFlow (currently unreachable code path) · New regression test: updateProfile throwing DuplicateProfileNameException from the Edit dialog shows an error instead of throwing unhandled
- **Labels:** profiles, tutoring, sync, silent-data-loss, error-handling · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches

#### AUD-profiles-05 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Add ref.mounted guards after awaits in PinFlowController before touching state
- **Rule:** SM-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Per SM-4 (and the digest's own note that Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException), every `await` in a Notifier method must be followed by a `ref.mounted` check before touching `state`. None of the four PIN-transition handlers in this @Riverpod(keepAlive:true) notifier do this — `_handleSetup`, `_handleChange` (twice), and `_handleVerify` all assign `state = state.copyWith(...)` immediately after an `await pinService.*Pin(...)` with no guard. The confirm-step of `_handleChange` (line 350-351) is worse: it has no try/catch at all around `setProfilePin`, unlike its own sibling handlers. If the provider is invalidated/torn down while a bcrypt hash/secure-storage write is in flight (e.g. rapid navigation away, container disposal), the resulting exception is unguarded and, for the confirm-step case, has no catch clause to even convert it to a value.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/pin_flow_controller.dart:274` — “try {
      await pinService.setProfilePin(profileId, pin);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/pin_flow_controller.dart:310` — “try {
          final ok = await pinService.verifyProfilePin(profileId, pin);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/pin_flow_controller.dart:350` — “state = state.copyWith(busy: true, errorMessage: null);
        await pinService.setProfilePin(profileId, pin);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/pin_flow_controller.dart:379` — “try {
      final ok = await pinService.verifyProfilePin(profileId, pin);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/pin_flow_controller.dart:380` — “final ok = await pinService.verifyProfilePin(profileId, pin);”
- **Fix:** After each await in _handleSetup/_handleChange/_handleVerify, add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` before assigning state; wrap the confirm-step setProfilePin call in the same try/catch pattern used by _handleSetup.
- **Done when:** Every await in pin_flow_controller.dart's four handlers is followed by a ref.mounted check before state is touched · A regression test disposes the ProviderContainer mid-await and asserts no UnmountedRefException escapes · _handleChange's confirm step catches the same exception types as _handleSetup
- **Labels:** riverpod, sm-4, pin-flow · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches · verifier corrections: keepAlive:true (per the file's own doc comment) defeats the 'rapid navigation away' trigger cited in the why-text; only container disposal (app teardown/tests) remains a realistic trigger. Doesn't kill the finding — rule

#### AUD-profiles-06 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Consolidate the PIN entry/verify/change/setup state machine duplicated across 3 live implementations in features/profiles
- **Rule:** SM-1/Fowler duplication, AG-4 duplicate top-level names · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The 4-digit-entry + busy-lock + lockout state machine is hand-rolled independently in PinFlowController (setup mode), _ParentPinSetupDialog (parent_pin_setup_dialog.dart), and _ParentPinVerificationDialog/_ParentPinChangeDialog (parent_pin_keypad_dialog.dart) — four near-identical but textually distinct copies of the same transitions (mismatch → reset to enterNew, lockout → freeze keypad, 4th digit → async verify/save). Worse, PinFlowController ALSO fully implements change/verify modes (and pin_flow_machine.dart even duplicates the enum names PinFlowMode/PinFlowStep as public top-level symbols, AG-4), but grepping every `.push(` call site in lib/ shows PinFlowVerifyRoute and PinFlowChangeRoute are registered in app_router.dart and never pushed anywhere — the app's real verify/change UX goes through the dialog-based _ParentPin*Dialog classes via router_provider.dart's promptForPin and settings_screen.dart. A confirmed device bug (PP-1: rapid 5th-digit tap racing the confirm-step reset) was fixed in _ParentPinSetupDialog's specific busy-before-reset ordering; because the other three copies re-derive the same logic independently, a fix like this has no guarantee of applying to the others.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/pin_flow_controller.dart:130` — “@Riverpod(keepAlive: true)
class PinFlowController extends _$PinFlowController {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/parent_pin_setup_dialog.dart:35` — “class _ParentPinSetupDialog extends ConsumerStatefulWidget {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/parent_pin_keypad_dialog.dart:71` — “class _ParentPinVerificationDialog extends StatefulWidget {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/parent_pin_keypad_dialog.dart:178` — “class _ParentPinChangeDialog extends StatefulWidget {”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/router/app_router.dart:254` — “path: '/parent-mode/pin-entry',
      page: PinFlowVerifyRoute.page,”
- **Fix:** Extract one shared PIN-entry state-machine class/notifier (digits, busy, lockedOut, lockoutMinutes, transitions) and have setup/verify/change dialogs and PinFlowScreen all delegate to it; delete PinFlowController's unreachable change/verify branches and their dead routes, or wire a real navigation call site to them.
- **Done when:** Only one implementation owns the digit-buffer/busy/lockout transition logic; setup, verify, and change UIs all call into it · Either PinFlowVerifyRoute/PinFlowChangeRoute get a real .push call site, or they and PinFlowController's change/verify modes are deleted · pin_flow_controller_test.dart and parent_pin_keypad_dialog_test.dart continue to pass against the consolidated implementation
- **Labels:** duplication, pin-flow, riverpod, dead-code

#### AUD-profiles-08 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Populate features/profiles/profiles.dart barrel exports so Rule 2 is satisfiable for the whole feature
- **Rule:** Rule 2 (barrel-only cross-feature imports) / Rule 0 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Every other actually-used feature barrel re-exports its public API (account.dart 21 exports, tracks.dart 26, tutoring.dart 22, progress.dart 1); profiles.dart has zero `export` statements, so its own header comment ('Import this barrel... Do NOT import deep paths directly') is impossible to follow. Grepping lib/features/**/*.dart for `features/profiles/` outside the profiles feature itself finds 65 files across 10+ other features deep-importing active_profile_provider.dart, profile_providers.dart, profile_model.dart, pin_service.dart etc. directly (plus lib/app/router/app_shell.dart, which can't even use the barrel since it exports nothing). Rule 2 is therefore 100% unenforceable for the single most cross-cut feature in the app: any future rename/move inside features/profiles/ breaks an unpredictable subset of 65+ files with no compiler-visible contract boundary.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/profiles.dart:7` — “library profiles;”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/router/app_shell.dart:16` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/profile_switcher_sheet.dart';”
- **Fix:** Populate profiles.dart with export statements for the feature's actual public surface (profile_model.dart, profile_repository.dart, pin_service.dart, active_profile_provider.dart, profile_providers.dart, profile_switcher_sheet.dart, etc.), mirroring the structure already used in tutoring.dart, then migrate consumers off deep imports incrementally.
- **Done when:** features/profiles/profiles.dart exports every symbol currently deep-imported by 2+ other features · learning_tracker/Makefile check 15/15 (once its self-comparison bug is fixed, see the tutored_children_section.dart finding) shows a declining, tracked count of profiles/ deep imports outside the feature · New cross-feature consumers of profiles/ import only features/profiles/profiles.dart
- **Labels:** layering, rule-2, barrel, architecture

#### AUD-profiles-09 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Replace string-matched PIN error localization with typed error codes (EH-5/AX-2)
- **Rule:** EH-5 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** PinFlowController.errorMessage carries raw English sentinel text (EH-5: domain/data errors must carry codes/enums, never pre-formatted messages), and PinFlowScreen._resolveError maps it back to ARB strings by exact string match, with a silent `_ => raw` fallback that renders raw English verbatim on any miss. The coupling has already drifted once undetected: the switch's 'Failed to save PIN' case matches nothing PinFlowController ever produces (only the dead pin_flow_machine.dart emitted that string — see companion dead-code finding). No test in the 628-line pin_flow_controller_test.dart or the screen test exercises _resolveError, so the next wording tweak to one file without the other silently regresses Hebrew (or English) users to wrong/raw text in a security-sensitive PIN-entry flow, undetected by CI.

Try again in $remainingMinutes minute(s).',”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/screens/pin_flow_screen.dart:198` — “_ => raw,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/screens/pin_flow_screen.dart:194` — “'Incorrect PIN' => l10n.incorrectPin,
    'PINs do not match' => l10n.pinsDoNotMatch,”
- **Fix:** Replace the free-text errorMessage field with a sealed PinFlowError enum/code on PinFlowState; have the screen switch on the enum (exhaustive switch expression, compiler-enforced) instead of string-matching English sentinels. Give PinLockoutException a stable code alongside its message. Add a widget test asserting the Locale('he') text renders for each error code.
- **Done when:** PinFlowState's error field is a closed enum/sealed type, not a String; pin_flow_screen.dart's switch has no fallback arm. · A test drives each PinFlowController error path and asserts the Locale('he') rendered text, not just non-null errorMessage.

#### AUD-profiles-11 · **P2** · SUSPECTED · Widen PinFlowController's catch scopes and add a finally so busy never sticks true on an untyped PinService exception
- **Rule:** SM-5 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [2x3] · filed P1, revised
- **Why:** PinFlowState hand-rolls AsyncValue's job via a `busy`/`errorMessage` pair instead of AsyncNotifier+AsyncValue.guard, and the hand-rolled error handling is incomplete: _handleSetup catches only ArgumentError, _handleChange's verifyCurrent and _handleVerify catch only PinLockoutException, and _handleChange's confirm step (line 350-351, the PIN-CHANGE save call) has no catch at all. appendDigit/backspace both early-return while `state.busy` is true, so any OTHER exception from PinService.setProfilePin/verifyProfilePin (a bcrypt hashing error, a DB write failure, disk full) leaves busy stuck true forever, permanently freezing the parent-PIN keypad with no error shown and no way to recover short of an app restart. This is the load-bearing PIN gate for parent/settings access.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/pin_flow_controller.dart:283` — “} on ArgumentError catch (e) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/pin_flow_controller.dart:350` — “state = state.copyWith(busy: true, errorMessage: null);
        await pinService.setProfilePin(profileId, pin);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/pin_flow_controller.dart:397` — “} on PinLockoutException catch (e) {”
- **Fix:** Wrap each of the 4 call sites in a catch-all (or a `finally { if (state.busy) state = state.copyWith(busy: false); }`) in addition to the existing typed catches, and route the generic-exception case to `state.copyWith(busy:false, errorMessage: <generic error>)` instead of leaving busy uncleared.
- **Done when:** Every code path through _handleSetup, _handleChange (all 3 async steps), and _handleVerify guarantees state.busy is false after the method returns, on both success and any exception type. · Regression test: a fake PinService that throws a generic StateError (not ArgumentError/PinLockoutException) from setProfilePin/verifyProfilePin in each of the 4 sites; assert state.busy == false and state.errorMessage != null afterward, and that appendDigit still accepts input. · Rule-0 checker: extend tool/ audit greps to flag a `busy: true`/`loading: true` state assignment in a Notifier method that is not followed by an unconditional reset before the method's closing brace (heuristic grep for `copyWith(busy: true` without a paired `finally`).
- **Labels:** sm-5, riverpod, error-handling, parent-pin, frozen-ui · verifier corrections: The claim 'no way to recover short of an app restart' is false and overstates severity. parent_pin_keypad_dialog.dart's PinKeypadDialogFrame wires PopScope(canPop:false) and the X close button's onPressed to `onClose` UN

#### AUD-profiles-12 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Convert ProfileSession to @freezed instead of hand-written ==/hashCode
- **Rule:** naming/placement — domain/state models are @freezed, never hand-written ==/hashCode · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** ProfileSession is a domain/state model living under domain/models/ (the same directory as the correctly-@freezed ProfileModel), but hand-writes operator== and hashCode instead of using @freezed as the coding standard requires. Today's implementation looks correct, but hand-rolled equality is exactly the class of bug (forgotten field, inconsistent hashCode) the @freezed rule exists to prevent, and it's inconsistent with its own sibling file in the same directory.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/domain/models/profile_session.dart:22` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>
      identical(this, other) ||”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/domain/models/profile_session.dart:30` — “int get hashCode => profileId.hashCode;”
- **Fix:** Convert ProfileSession to an abstract @freezed class with a private const constructor for the isActive getter, matching ProfileModel's pattern.
- **Done when:** ProfileSession is declared @freezed; dart run build_runner build generates profile_session.freezed.dart · Existing call sites (ProfileSession(profileId:), .none(), .isActive) keep compiling unchanged
- **Labels:** freezed, hygiene, naming · verifier corrections: First evidence line should read 23, not 22 — minor citation offset, doesn't affect substance.

#### AUD-profiles-14 · **P3** · SUSPECTED · Guard ref.read calls after the cached-profile await in TutoredChildrenSection._fireEntryPullAndNavigate
- **Rule:** SM-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** showProfileSwitcherSheet (profile_switcher_sheet.dart:43-50) calls showModalBottomSheet with neither isDismissible nor enableDrag overridden, so the sheet stays swipe/backdrop-dismissible for the whole window between the user's tap and the loading dialog appearing. The cached-mirror check at line 503 is a local DB read awaited BEFORE any dialog/barrier goes up; if the user swipes the sheet away during that window, _TutoredChildRow (a ConsumerWidget) unmounts, and the very next lines (514-516) call ref.read on a WidgetRef whose element is gone, outside any try/catch, so the exception would be unhandled. The same risk exists after the second await (svc.pull(...), up to 15s) at ~595. The author was clearly aware of this exact class of bug elsewhere in the same method (router is captured eagerly at line 487 specifically to survive unmounting; context.mounted is checked before every Navigator/ScaffoldMessenger call afterward) but the same treatment wasn't applied to these ref.read calls.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/tutored_children_section.dart:503` — “final cachedProfile = await ref”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/widgets/tutored_children_section.dart:515` — “.read(resolvedTutoredLocalProfileIdProvider.notifier)”
- **Fix:** Check context.mounted (or capture the needed notifiers before the await) before touching ref post-await, matching the pattern already used for `router` in the same method.
- **Done when:** A widget test drives _enterTalmidView, dismisses the switcher sheet while the getTutoredProfile future is pending, completes the future, and asserts no uncaught exception is thrown · ref is not touched after an await without a liveness check anywhere in _fireEntryPullAndNavigate
- **Labels:** riverpod, sm-4, lifecycle, tutoring · verifier corrections: Evidence line 515 quote '.read(resolvedTutoredLocalProfileIdProvider.notifier)' is actually on line 516; line 515 is the bare 'ref' token.

#### AUD-profiles-15 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Log TutoredChildrenSection's AsyncValue error branch instead of swallowing it silently
- **Rule:** EH-3 (no log-less catch) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** AppLogger is already imported in this file (line 6) but the error branch of incomingTutorGrantsProvider's AsyncValue.when discards both the error and stack trace with no log call. Hiding the section on a load failure is a defensible UX call (the batch's own test even labels it 'silent fail' intentionally), but the total absence of a log means a persistently failing grants query — e.g. a Firestore rule regression on the tutoring collection — leaves zero trace in AppLogger/Crashlytics breadcrumbs for anyone to diagnose.

- **Fix:** Add an AppLogger.instance.warning(event: ..., exception: error, stackTrace: stack) call in the error branch before returning SizedBox.shrink().

- **Labels:** profiles, error-handling, logging, hygiene · verifier corrections: Rule EH-3 literally targets try/catch; applying it to an AsyncValue.when error callback is a reasonable but non-literal extension worth flagging for the orchestrator.

- **Fix:** Use `e.message?.toString() ?? <fallback>` instead of the unchecked cast in both places.
- **Done when:** Both sites read e.message without an unchecked String cast · A test constructing ArgumentError.value(42, 'pin') and feeding it through does not crash

#### AUD-profiles-21 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Stop autoSelectedProfileId's build() from writing to the DB and mutating sibling providers

    ref.read(selectedProfileIdProvider.notifier).clear();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/profile_providers.dart:109` — “id = await repo.ensureDefaultProfile(
      accountId: accountId,”
- **Fix:** Move the self-heal side effect out of build() into an explicit ref.listen-driven effect (e.g. in app_shell.dart, which already watches auth state) or a widget-triggered callback, keeping build() a pure read.
- **Done when:** autoSelectedProfileId's build() (or its replacement) contains no writes to other providers or the database; existing BUG D1 self-heal tests keep passing

#### AUD-progress-01 · **P0** · CONFIRMED · Fix missing synthetic-container guard in items_learned_providers.dart:computeLifetimeViewSummary (composite-curriculum over-credit regression)
- **Rule:** Fowler duplicated-code / previously-fixed P0 composite-over-credit guard · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** A stray level1 ledger row targeting a composite curriculum's synthetic container (e.g. tanach/level1/'Torah' — created by a since-fixed bug and, per the code's own comment, never cleaned up on already-upgraded devices because the v32 migration only runs once) makes every leaf under that curriculum register as learned. lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart's lifetimeDataProvider defends against this by dropping synthetic-container level1 rows before building the tree (comment there explicitly calls it a 'P0 (composite over-credit) READ-TIME guard'). items_learned_providers.dart's computeLifetimeViewSummary reimplements the identical ledger-to-learned-refs algorithm from scratch in a private _learnedLeafRefs function, but never applies the guard. Since the Lifetime Knowledge screen's default tab is 'All sources' (_filter = allSources), which routes to computeLifetimeViewSummary via lifetimeViewSummariesProvider, a user with exactly one Chumash book bulk/lifetime-marked can open the app and see 'Tanach 100% learned' by default — a silent, high-visibility corruption of the app's core progress-tracking claim. The one regression test written for this exact invariant (lifetime_tree_builder_composite_test.dart) only calls LifetimeTreeBuilder directly, so it gives zero protection against this duplicate path.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/presentation/providers/lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart:189` — “return !CompositeCurriculumStrategy.isSyntheticContainerLevel1(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/presentation/providers/items_learned_providers.dart:126` — “final ledger = await db.learningLedgerDao.getEntriesByCurriculum(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/presentation/providers/items_learned_providers.dart:336` — “learnedRefs.add(leaf.sefariaRef);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/presentation/screens/lifetime_knowledge_screen.dart:49` — “_LifetimeSourceFilter _filter = _LifetimeSourceFilter.allSources;”
- **Fix:** Delete the duplicate _learnedLeafRefs/_buildCompletionTree/_levelKey/_hebrewForLeafGroup functions in items_learned_providers.dart and have computeItemsLearnedSummary/computeLifetimeViewSummary call LifetimeTreeBuilder (computeLearnedLeafRefs/buildTree) directly, exactly as lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart already does, so the guard and any future fix apply to both surfaces from one implementation.
- **Done when:** A test mirroring lifetime_tree_builder_composite_test.dart's single-book scenario, but driven through computeLifetimeViewSummary/lifetimeViewSummariesProvider, asserts the composite curriculum's learned count equals the single book's leaf count, not the whole curriculum's. · items_learned_providers.dart contains no second implementation of the ledger-scope-to-learned-refs algorithm; grep for '_learnedLeafRefs' in that file returns nothing after the fix.
- **Labels:** data-correctness, duplication, progress · verifier corrections: The recommendation's phrasing ('call LifetimeTreeBuilder directly... exactly as lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart already does') slightly understates that the synthetic-container guard is actually a ledger pre-filter ste

#### AUD-progress-03 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Batch trackDualProgressMetricsProvider's per-track sequential DB reads (N+1 left un-fixed by sibling F13)
- **Rule:** DB-5 / Fowler N+1 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Each loop iteration awaits _safeLoadLeavesForTrack (itself up to 4 sequential DAO calls: getScopesByTrack, getScopes x1-2, getActiveTracksForProfile, lines 618-648), then completionPercent (397), getCompletionsByTrackAndProfile (406), getEntriesByTrack (408), getProgramForProfileAndCurriculum (421), and conditionally programCalendarPositionProvider (430-431) — up to 9 sequential DB round-trips per track, none parallelized via Future.wait. A profile with 5 active tracks does ~40-45 sequential awaits to render the Progress-hub/Dashboard per-track section, and this provider re-runs on every completionCommittedProvider tick (line 357, i.e. after every single completion mark). The very same file already fixed this exact N+1 shape for the sibling lifetimeDataProvider under the F13 label (completionsByProfileForLifetimeProvider / priorImportsByProfileProvider, lines 78-138) but the batching was never extended here. Actual latency impact is unmeasured (SUSPECTED) — the un-batched pattern itself is CONFIRMED by static reading.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/presentation/providers/lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart:370` — “for (final track in tracks) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/presentation/providers/lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart:618` — “var scopes = await db.curriculumScopeDao.getScopesByTrack(trackId);”
- **Fix:** Batch the per-track queries the way F13 batched lifetimeDataProvider's — one profile-wide query per DAO partitioned in memory by trackId — or parallelize the independent per-track work with Future.wait.
- **Done when:** trackDualProgressMetricsProvider issues O(1) queries per DAO (or explicitly parallelizes per-track work), not O(tracks) sequential awaits · A ProviderObserver-based test mirroring lifetime_knowledge_screen_test.dart's F13 test asserts each batched provider builds once across N tracks
- **Labels:** performance, progress, riverpod

- **Rule:** EH-3 (log-less catch) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [2x2]

    return null;”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/presentation/providers/items_learned_providers.dart:272` — “} catch (_) {

- **Fix:** Log both catches via AppLogger.warning(event:, exception:, stackTrace:) before falling back, matching the F20 pattern used elsewhere in the same file.

#### AUD-progress-08 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Stop interpolating raw error.toString() into localized error messages across progress screens
- **Rule:** EH-5 / custom_lint no_e_to_string_in_ui (currently enforcing nothing repo-wide) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 6 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** error.toString() on a Dart/Firebase/Drift exception is always in English (e.g. 'Bad state: ...', 'SqliteException: ...') and not ICU-pluralizable; interpolating it into an otherwise-Hebrew ARB string means a Hebrew-locale, RTL user who hits any of these error states sees a sentence that switches to raw untranslated English mid-string. recent_activity_screen.dart in the same directory shows the correct pattern (l10n.chartFailedToLoad with no error interpolation, 4 uses) — the other 4 screens in this same feature diverge from it.

- **Fix:** Replace error.toString() interpolation with the generic localized failure string (as recent_activity_screen.dart already does) and, if diagnostic detail is genuinely needed, log error.toString() via AppLogger instead of rendering it to the user.
- **Done when:** None of the 4 screens' AsyncValue.error branches call .toString() on the error object inside a Text/l10n call. · Once dart run custom_lint is repaired, no_e_to_string_in_ui reports zero hits in lib/features/progress/.
- **Labels:** i18n, error-handling · verifier corrections: Narrative says recent_activity_screen.dart uses the correct pattern '4 uses' — actual grep shows 5 uses of l10n.chartFailedToLoad; trivial miscount, doesn't affect the finding's validity. | The corroborating claim 'recen
