#### AUD-progress-14 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Replace hand-rolled ==/hashCode on PaceCalculator, LifetimeLeafProvenance and RecentActivityWindow with @freezed or a record
- **Rule:** naming/placement — domain/state models are @freezed; never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Three separate hand-written equality implementations exist in this one feature slice alongside a fourth model file (journey_view_model.dart) that correctly uses @freezed for the same kind of value object, and alongside sibling family-key records elsewhere in this same batch (e.g. lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart's ({int profileId, CurriculumId curriculumId})) that get structural equality for free. Hand-rolled equality is exactly the boilerplate freezed exists to generate and keep in sync; PaceCalculator's == only compares 6 of its 13 fields (the derived ones are excluded) which is easy to get wrong silently the next time a field is added, since nothing forces == and hashCode to be touched together.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/domain/services/pace_calculator.dart:209` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/domain/models/lifetime_knowledge.dart:67` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/presentation/providers/recent_activity_providers.dart:46` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>”
- **Fix:** Convert PaceCalculator and LifetimeLeafProvenance to @freezed classes (both fit the private-const-factory-plus-named-computing-factory pattern already used elsewhere for derived-field value objects); convert RecentActivityWindow to a named-field record (({DateTime startDate, DateTime endDate, String? curriculumId})) to match the record-based family keys already used in this same feature.
- **Done when:** grep -rn 'bool operator ==' lib/features/progress/ (excluding .freezed.dart/.g.dart) returns no hits.
- **Labels:** consistency, freezed

#### AUD-progress-15 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Replace hand-rolled ==/hashCode on RecentActivityWindow with @freezed or a record
- **Rule:** naming/placement (no hand-written ==/hashCode on data classes) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Standards mandate immutable @freezed classes with generated equality, never hand-written ==/hashCode. RecentActivityWindow hand-writes both. Its sibling family-key type in the very same feature, lifetimeDataProvider's `({int profileId, CurriculumId curriculumId})` record (lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart:148-151), gets structural equality for free and cannot drift out of sync — RecentActivityWindow's hand-rolled version would silently under-compare (stale FutureProvider.family cache hits) if a field were ever added to the class but forgotten in operator==.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/presentation/providers/recent_activity_providers.dart:46` — “bool operator ==(Object other) =>
      other is RecentActivityWindow &&”
- **Fix:** Convert RecentActivityWindow to @freezed, or to a record matching the lifetimeDataProvider sibling's pattern.
- **Done when:** RecentActivityWindow has no hand-written operator==/hashCode · Adding a field to the type cannot silently break FutureProvider.family memoization
- **Labels:** riverpod, hygiene, progress

### features/sacred_time  (9 findings — 0 P0 / 3 P1 / 3 P2 / 3 P3)

#### AUD-sacred_time-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Guard ref.mounted after await in SacredLocationNotifier/InIsraelNotifier mutator methods
- **Rule:** SM-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** detect() awaits a GPS fix with a 15-second timeout then unconditionally writes state/invalidates ref on success; setManualCity, setManualCoords and InIsraelNotifier.setInIsrael likewise touch state/ref after an await with no ref.mounted check. This file's own _load() methods DO guard (comment: 'an account switch rebuilds it. Never write state on a disposed notifier'), and the paired test file carries a regression test titled 'was a race' proving the team already hit a real race in this exact provider once. If the notifier is disposed while one of these four unguarded methods is mid-await (profile/account switch during a slow GPS fetch is the obvious trigger), Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException, which nothing in the call chain catches (the caller's try/finally in sacred_time_settings_card.dart has no catch clause).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/presentation/providers/sacred_location_provider.dart:41` — “final result = await ref.read(locationServiceProvider).detectCurrent();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/presentation/providers/sacred_location_provider.dart:54` — “state = result.location;
        ref.invalidate(inIsraelProvider);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/presentation/providers/sacred_location_provider.dart:153` — “await ref.read(syncWriteFacadeProvider)?.pushUiPreferencesSnapshot();”
- **Fix:** Add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` immediately after every await in detect(), setManualCity(), setManualCoords(), setInIsrael(), and _pushSnapshot() before the next ref/state touch, mirroring the guard already used in _load().
- **Done when:** Every async Notifier method in sacred_location_provider.dart checks ref.mounted after each await before touching ref/state · A new test disposes/invalidates the ProviderContainer while detect()/setManualCity() is mid-await (e.g. a Completer-backed fake LocationService) and asserts no UnmountedRefException propagates
- **Labels:** riverpod, race-condition, crash-risk · verifier corrections: Minor nuance only: in setManualCoords() and setInIsrael(), the `state =` assignment itself happens synchronously before the method's first await (not "after an await" as the finding's prose implies for all four sites) —

The file's own RTL smoke test ('idle hint renders without overflow under he locale') only asserts no overflow/ErrorWidget, never the text itself, so the defect has zero regression coverage despite the rest of the screen being fully localized.

#### AUD-sacred_time-03 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Stop surfacing raw exception .toString() text to Sacred Time users
- **Rule:** EH-5 (no_e_to_string_in_ui) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** LocationFetchResult already models the common failure modes (service disabled, permission denied) as clean typed variants with their own l10n strings, but the catch-all LocationFetchError carries e.toString() verbatim — including a TimeoutException after the 15s GPS timeout, a common indoor/poor-signal scenario — rendered directly via sacredTimeLocationDetectError(message). Separately, CitiesRepository never converts its SQLite/IO exceptions, so citySearchProvider's raw AsyncError is shown via e.toString() in the error branch. Both put untranslated, technical English text inside an otherwise fully-Hebrew screen. coding-standards.md names this exact defect class as recurring, citing prior fixes (ST-4, SY-3).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/data/services/location_service.dart:74` — “return LocationFetchError(e.toString());”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/presentation/screens/city_picker_screen.dart:69` — “AppLocalizations.of(context)!.errorSearchFailed(e.toString()),”
- **Fix:** Give LocationFetchError (and CitiesRepository's failure paths) a stable enum/code instead of a free-text message, resolved to a localized string in presentation; reserve e.toString() for AppLogger only, never for display.
- **Done when:** LocationFetchError carries a typed reason code, not a raw String message · CitiesRepository exposes a typed Result/sealed failure for I/O errors instead of letting exceptions reach citySearchProvider raw · A widget test under Locale('he') asserts no raw exception text (e.g. 'Exception:', 'TimeoutException') ever renders

#### AUD-sacred_time-04 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Fix ZmanimWindowService polar-fallback candle-lighting/tzais to use the target location's time, not the device's
- **Rule:** Nygard failure-mode / domain-logic correctness · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** DateTime(y, m, d, 17) (no .utc) constructs a device-local wall-clock time; .toUtc() then converts using the DEVICE's current timezone offset, not the offset of latitude/longitude — an arbitrary location the user picked, which the feature explicitly lets differ from the device's own timezone (manual city/coords). The doc comment above promises 'a wide local-time window' at the target, but the fallback is local to whichever timezone the device (or test runner) happens to be in. It only fires at extreme (polar) latitudes when getCandleLighting()/getTzais() return null, and zmanim_window_service_test.dart has no test forcing that branch, so it has never been exercised.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/domain/services/zmanim_window_service.dart:163` — “return DateTime(forDate.year, forDate.month, forDate.day, 17).toUtc();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/domain/services/zmanim_window_service.dart:182` — “return DateTime(forDate.year, forDate.month, forDate.day, 21).toUtc();”
- **Fix:** Compute the fallback from a fixed offset derived from longitude (or explicitly switch to UTC and correct the 'local-time' claim in the comment) instead of relying on DateTime's device-local constructor.
- **Done when:** Fallback candle-lighting/tzais no longer depends on the executing device's timezone · A unit test at an extreme-latitude fixture forces getCandleLighting()/getTzais() to return null and asserts the returned UTC instant is stable regardless of the test machine's TZ
- **Labels:** domain-logic, timezone, edge-case

Every other cross-layer type this feature exposes to presentation (City, SacredLocation, SacredWindow) correctly lives in domain/models/ — LocationFetchResult is the one outcome type stranded in data/, forcing presentation to reach past domain into data, breaking the layering the rest of the feature follows consistently.

#### AUD-sacred_time-06 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Narrow LocationService's `on Object catch` clauses so programming errors aren't swallowed
- **Rule:** EH-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** `on Object` catches everything Dart can throw, including Error subtypes (TypeError, NoSuchMethodError, StateError, ...) that only_throw_errors-compliant code elsewhere in the app throws for genuine programming bugs. A plugin-level type mismatch or null-safety violation inside geolocator/geocoding would silently become 'location fetch failed' (or a silently-null country code) forever, with no crash report and no log line — exactly the bug-masking EH-4 exists to prevent.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/data/services/location_service.dart:73` — “} on Object catch (e) {
      return LocationFetchError(e.toString());”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sacred_time/data/services/location_service.dart:86` — “} on Object {
      return null;”
- **Fix:** Change both clauses to `on Exception catch (e)` (or the specific exception types geolocator/geocoding document), letting Error subtypes propagate and reach Crashlytics/crash loudly.
- **Done when:** Both catch clauses in location_service.dart are typed to Exception (or narrower), not Object · A test asserts a thrown Error from the fake platform is NOT converted to LocationFetchError/null but propagates
- **Labels:** error-handling, hygiene

### features/scheduler  (25 findings — 0 P0 / 2 P1 / 15 P2 / 8 P3)

#### AUD-scheduler-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Lazy-load GroupedDailyView's per-curriculum task list instead of List.generate-ing every DailyTaskCard
- **Rule:** PF-2 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** SchedulerScreen's grouped view (one tap on the view-toggle button next to the task count) renders every task for every curriculum synchronously: GroupedDailyView maps curricula (bounded, <=9) into always-expanded ExpansionTiles, and inside each tile calls `List.generate(tasks.length, ...)` to build one DailyTaskCard per task with zero windowing, inside a non-builder `ListView(children:...)`. The daily-task backlog is explicitly unbounded by design — a lapsed user (the app's own core scenario: a child who stops opening the app for weeks) accumulates overdue new-learning/chazara items across every active track. The Learn tab already anticipates exactly this by hard-capping its own preview to `tasks.take(5)` (learning_screen.dart:346) and linking its 'View all' button straight into this screen (SchedulerRoute). Opening the grouped view after a multi-week gap forces dozens of DailyTaskCard widgets (icons, badges, InkWell, Riverpod watches) to build on the main isolate in a single frame — visible jank or a frozen scroll, worst on the older/budget Android devices this app targets for children. The file's own sibling `_TaskList` in scheduler_screen.dart:210 (the default, non-grouped view of the SAME data) already solves the identical problem correctly with `ListView.builder(itemCount: tasks.length, ...)`, so this is a local inconsistency/regression, not an unknown gap.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/presentation/widgets/grouped_daily_view.dart:39` — “children: curricula.map((curriculum) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/presentation/widgets/grouped_daily_view.dart:45` — “initiallyExpanded: true,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/presentation/widgets/grouped_daily_view.dart:51` — “children: List.generate(tasks.length, (i) {
            final task = tasks[i];”
- **Fix:** Rebuild GroupedDailyView on a CustomScrollView: one SliverToBoxAdapter per curriculum for the expand/collapse header, followed by a SliverList(delegate: SliverChildBuilderDelegate(...)) (or a lazily-built ListView per expanded section) so only on-screen DailyTaskCards are realized — mirroring the SliverList/SliverChildBuilderDelegate pattern gamification_screen.dart already uses for its own (also unbounded) achievements list.
- **Done when:** Rule-0: PF-2 checker flags `List.generate(` / `.map(...).toList()` feeding a `children:` list under lib/features/**/presentation/** where the source count is a ref.watch'd/provider-derived collection, excluding verified-bounded enums (e.g. CurriculumId.values). · Regression test: pump SchedulerScreen with a fixture of ~200 synthetic overdue DailyTasks spread across 3 curricula, switch to grouped view, and assert via find.byType(DailyTaskCard) that only the initial viewport's worth of cards are realized (matching the count already asserted for the compliant _TaskList path) rather than all ~200.
- **Labels:** performance, PF-2, scheduler · verifier corrections: None needed — all cited file:line quotes match the source exactly. | Severity corrected from P1 to P2; all cited evidence (grouped_daily_view.dart lines, sibling _TaskList pattern, learning_screen.dart:346 take(5), produ

#### AUD-scheduler-03 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Add a profileId ownership check to GoalRepositoryImpl.updateGoal/deleteGoal and unify its profileId source
- **Rule:** profileId-in-PK / multi-profile isolation invariant (repository as last line of defense); naming/placement (single source of truth) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** getGoals() filters by the constructor-injected _profileId field, but createGoal takes its own explicit profileId parameter that is never cross-checked against _profileId — the interface lets a caller create a goal 'for' a different profile than the repository instance represents, which would then be invisible to that same instance's getGoals(). Independently, updateGoal and deleteGoal load the existing row by bare goalId and mutate/delete it with no ownership check at all — updateGoal even copies existing.profileId straight back into the write (line-133, not separately confirmed) without ever comparing it to _profileId. None of this is proven to be hit by today's UI (all current call sites happen to pass matching profileIds), but the repository adds zero defense-in-depth on top of the DAO layer (which itself does not scope goalDao.updateGoal/deleteGoal/getGoalById by profile) — the next screen or bug that supplies a mismatched id/profileId pair silently edits or deletes another profile's goal.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/data/repositories/goal_repository_impl.dart:19` — “int profileId = 0,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/data/repositories/goal_repository_impl.dart:74` — “final goals = await _database.goalDao.getGoalsByCurriculumAndProfile(
      curriculumId.storageKey,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/domain/repositories/goal_repository.dart:16` — “required int profileId,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/data/repositories/goal_repository_impl.dart:92` — “final existing = await _database.goalDao.getGoalById(goalId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/data/repositories/goal_repository_impl.dart:163` — “final existing = await _database.goalDao.getGoalById(goalId);”
- **Fix:** Pick one source of truth for 'which profile owns this repository instance' and have updateGoal/deleteGoal verify existing.profileId against it before mutating, throwing a typed error on mismatch.
- **Done when:** createGoal derives profileId from the same single source as the rest of the class (drop the redundant parameter or validate it against _profileId). · updateGoal and deleteGoal verify existing.profileId == _profileId before mutating/deleting, throwing a typed error otherwise. · New regression test: construct two GoalRepositoryImpl instances (one per profile) sharing one DB; assert profile B's repository cannot update or delete a goalId belonging to profile A.
- **Labels:** multi-profile-isolation, authorization, goal-repository

#### AUD-scheduler-04 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Add regression tests for GoalRepositoryImpl's not-found and delete-sync payload paths
- **Rule:** EH-2 (typed exceptions surfaced correctly) / TQ-8 (every reachable error branch needs a red-first test) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 8 · **Verified:** [2x2]

(b) The file's own 'sync payload completeness (R4-6)' group exists specifically because create/update once shipped without profile_id/id in the outbox payload — but that hardening was never extended to deleteGoal: _RecordingGoalSyncFacade.deleteGoal is a blind no-op with no payload recorder (unlike goalPayloads for pushGoal), and the sole 'deleteGoal removes the goal' test uses the sync-less `repo` instance, so _syncDeleteGoal's {firestore_id, curriculum_id} payload is completely unverified. #### AUD-scheduler-10 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Guard SkippedTasks.build()'s fire-and-forget prefs load with ref.mounted
- **Rule:** SM-2 / SM-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** build() kicks off an un-awaited async side effect (SM-2 forbids side effects in build). _loadFromPrefs() then does `await SharedPreferences.getInstance()` and further awaits before writing `state = ...` twice, with no `ref.mounted` check (SM-4) anywhere in the method. If the provider is disposed (e.g. the user navigates off the Scheduler screen quickly) before the load resolves, the post-await `state = ...` throws Riverpod 3's UnmountedRefException — which the surrounding try/catch swallows and logs via `AppLogger.instance.error(event: 'Failed to load skipped tasks', ...)`, i.e. a routine dispose race gets misreported as a genuine load failure in production logs/Crashlytics breadcrumbs, obscuring real failures of the same code path.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/scheduler_providers.dart:184` — “Set<String> build() {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/scheduler_providers.dart:185` — “unawaited(_loadFromPrefs());”
- **Fix:** Check `ref.mounted` immediately before each `state = ...` assignment in _loadFromPrefs, and return early (without logging) when unmounted, matching Riverpod 3's documented SM-4 pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.
- **Done when:** _loadFromPrefs checks ref.mounted before both `state = refs.toSet()` and `state = {}`. · A widget test that disposes the ProviderContainer/screen mid-load does not produce an AppLogger error log.
- **Labels:** SM-2, SM-4, riverpod

#### AUD-scheduler-13 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Normalize config.currentDate before delay-stage due-date arithmetic in SchedulerEngine
- **Rule:** DB-6 / Nygard (clock skew) / date-arithmetic · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** config.currentDate flows in unnormalized: allDailyTasksProvider sets `now = ref.watch(clockProvider)` (a raw timestamp with time-of-day) and _buildFreshPlan passes it straight through generator.generateAll(activeCurricula, now, ...) -> ScheduleConfig(currentDate: date). previousCompletedAt also carries a real time-of-day (completion timestamps are never normalized — confirmed via completion_writer.dart). Duration.inDays truncates toward zero, so when the true calendar-day gap is exactly 1 day but the elapsed wall-clock time is <24h (e.g. item completed at 20:00 five days ago, now it's 02:00 the next calendar day — only 6h elapsed), daysUntilDue computes 0 instead of -1: a chazara item that is genuinely 1+ calendar days overdue is shown in 'due today' (scheduledTasks) instead of 'overdue' (overdueTasks), silently under-reporting overdue-ness by up to a day. This is the same class of bug (R4-1) this codebase has explicitly fixed elsewhere in the very same feature (local_calendar_engine.dart's UTC-midnight handling, goal_setup_screen.dart's daysRemaining guard, and _buildProjectionTasks's pervasive DateUtils.extractLocalDate use) — just missed in the delay-stage path.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/domain/services/scheduler_engine.dart:368` — “final dueDate = previousCompletedAt.add(Duration(days: stage.delayDays));”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/domain/services/scheduler_engine.dart:369` — “final daysUntilDue = dueDate.difference(config.currentDate).inDays;”
- **Fix:** Normalize both previousCompletedAt/currentCompletedAt and config.currentDate to calendar-date-only (e.g. via DateUtils.extractLocalDate) before computing daysUntilDue in _processDelayStage, matching the pattern already used in _buildProjectionTasks.
- **Done when:** New unit test: a delay-stage item whose previous-stage completedAt time-of-day is later than the current query's time-of-day, with a true 1-calendar-day gap, asserts the task lands in overdueTasks (not scheduledTasks). · scheduler_engine_schedule_types_test.dart / scheduler_engine_dni346_test.dart (sibling test files) continue to pass.
- **Labels:** date-arithmetic, chazara, scheduler-engine, P2-correctness · verifier corrections: Rule tag 'DB-6' doesn't match (DB-6 covers sync-able entity local-Drift-as-source-of-truth, unrelated to date arithmetic) — the real grounding is the general date-arithmetic/Nygard clock-skew lens, not a named DB rule. I

#### AUD-scheduler-15 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Resolve the ambiguous stageId/stageOrder dual-interpretation in SchedulerCompletionRepositoryImpl.resolveStageOrder
- **Rule:** Evans lens — a single field pattern-matched against two overlapping ID spaces with no way to tell them apart · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The comment says newer completion rows store a stage's stageOrder in c.stageId while older rows store the stage's DB id; resolveStageOrder tries to guess which format a given row used by checking 'does rawStageId match some CURRENT stage's stageOrder' first. Stage id (a table-wide autoincrement) and stageOrder (a small 1..N per-curriculum ordinal) share the same small-integer space, especially for the first curriculum/stages ever created in a fresh install or test DB (id and stageOrder can be identical by coincidence, e.g. 1,2,3). When they collide, an OLD-format row that really means 'stage id 3' gets misread as 'stageOrder 3' and silently resolves to the wrong stage — which would misreport a chazara/review stage as complete (or vice versa) with no error. I have not constructed a concrete seed scenario proving the collision fires against real data (id values grow globally across curricula, so the window narrows over an install's lifetime), so this is reported as SUSPECTED, not CONFIRMED — a runtime/unit test seeding a stage whose id equals a different stage's stageOrder plus an old-format completion would confirm or rule it out.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/data/repositories/scheduler_completion_repository_impl.dart:33` — “final stageOrderMap = {for (final s in stages) s.id: s.stageOrder};
    final knownStageOrders = {for (final s in stages) s.stageOrder};”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/data/repositories/scheduler_completion_repository_impl.dart:39` — “if (knownStageOrders.contains(rawStageId)) return rawStageId;”
- **Fix:** Give completion rows an explicit format marker (or normalize all stored stageId values to stageOrder in a one-time migration) instead of guessing per-row from an ambiguous value.

#### AUD-scheduler-16 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Stop keying GoalEntity.firestoreId on mutable targetPercent — every goal-percent edit orphans a Firestore document instead of updating it
- **Rule:** Evans invariant (aggregate identity must be stable across normal mutation); adjacent to the FB family's stable-natural-key principle · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** firestoreId = curriculumId + '_' + targetPercent.toStringAsFixed(1) + '_' + createdAt.millisecondsSinceEpoch. updateGoal preserves createdAt but allows targetPercent to change, so any 'adjust my goal target %' edit (a routine, expected user action) computes a DIFFERENT firestoreId and _syncGoal pushes a brand-new Firestore document instead of updating the original — the original document is never touched again and deleteGoal only ever removes the CURRENT firestoreId's doc, so the old one is orphaned forever. GoalMerger happens to key its LWW arbitration by track_id rather than firestoreId, so the local state pulled on other devices generally self-heals to the latest edit — but Firestore itself accumulates one permanent garbage document per percent-edit for the life of the account, silently inflating every future full pull of that profile's goals collection. The test suite tests firestoreId's format exhaustively (contains curriculumId / contains targetPercent / contains createdAt, in TWO separate near-duplicate files) and even exercises the exact repro (create at 50.0, update to 75.0) but never asserts the one invariant that matters: the id must stay the same across that edit.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/domain/models/goal_entity.dart:160` — “targetPercent.toStringAsFixed(1),
      createdAt.millisecondsSinceEpoch.toString(),”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/data/repositories/goal_repository_impl.dart:136` — “targetPercent: drift.Value(targetPercent ?? existing.targetPercent),”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/data/repositories/goal_repository_impl.dart:143` — “createdAt: drift.Value(existing.createdAt),”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/data/repositories/goal_repository_impl_test.dart:363` — “targetPercent: 50.0,”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/data/repositories/goal_repository_impl_test.dart:367` — “await repoWithSync.updateGoal(goalId: goal.id!, targetPercent: 75.0);”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/domain/models/goal_entity_extended_test.dart:129` — “test('two goals with different createdAt have different firestoreIds', () {”
- **Fix:** Derive firestoreId only from fields that cannot change through updateGoal (drop targetPercent from the id, or key on the DB row id / trackId+curriculumId+createdAt) so an update always resolves to the same document.
- **Done when:** GoalEntity.firestoreId no longer includes targetPercent (or any other field updateGoal can change). · New regression test: create a goal, call updateGoal changing only targetPercent, and assert the pushed sync payload's id/firestoreId is identical to the create call's.
- **Labels:** sync, firestore, goal, data-hygiene

#### AUD-scheduler-17 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Wrap the DB write in StudyDayConfigScreen._toggleDay with catch/log and a consistent mounted guard
- **Rule:** EH-2 / EH-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** _toggleDay runs its DB lookup + db.studyDayConfigDao.upsertDayConfig(...) inside a detached `.then()` async closure with no surrounding try/catch and no caller awaiting the result — if upsertDayConfig throws (constraint violation, disk error), the failure is silently swallowed by the Future machinery with no AppLogger call and no user feedback (unlike the sync-push call three lines later, which IS wrapped in `on TutorWriteException catch`). The same closure calls `ref.invalidate(allDailyTasksProvider)` at line 288 with no `context.mounted` check, yet the SAME method DOES check `context.mounted` before the SnackBar at line 299 just after — an inconsistent, incomplete guard that leaves the earlier call exposed to a disposed-widget race if the user navigates away quickly after tapping a day toggle.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/presentation/screens/study_day_config_screen.dart:288` — “ref.invalidate(allDailyTasksProvider);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/presentation/screens/study_day_config_screen.dart:299` — “if (context.mounted && e.code == 'permission-denied') {”
- **Fix:** Wrap the DB write in try/catch with an AppLogger.error call and user-facing feedback on failure; check `context.mounted` (or equivalent) before the `ref.invalidate` call, matching the guard already present for the SnackBar.
- **Done when:** A thrown exception from upsertDayConfig is logged via AppLogger and does not vanish silently. · ref.invalidate(allDailyTasksProvider) is only called when the widget is still mounted.
- **Labels:** EH-2, EH-3, error-handling · verifier corrections: The claim 'silently swallowed...no AppLogger call' is factually wrong: main.dart wraps runApp in runZonedGuarded, whose handler calls AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack) plus Crashlytics.recordError(fatal: true). The

#### AUD-scheduler-23 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Migrate scheduler-adjacent tests off the deprecated LearningProgramRepository.instance singleton
- **Rule:** SM-7 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** This static singleton is exactly the 'global/static mutable singleton' SM-7 prohibits, and it has zero production (lib/) call sites — but 30+ test files across the suite (test/core/services/*, test/story_acceptance/*, test/features/tracks/*, test/features/onboarding/*, etc.) construct their fixtures via `LearningProgramRepository.instance` instead of overriding `learningProgramRepositoryProvider`. Because `test/` and `lib/` share one Dart package, Dart's default `deprecated_member_use` lint does not fire for same-package usage (only `deprecated_member_use_from_same_package` would, and it isn't enabled) — which is exactly why `flutter analyze: No issues found` coexists with 30+ live uses of a member explicitly marked for removal. The singleton can never actually be deleted while this fan-out exists, and every test using it is verifying against a construction path the app itself no longer uses.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/domain/services/learning_program_service.dart:69` — “@Deprecated('Use learningProgramRepositoryProvider via Riverpod instead')”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/domain/services/learning_program_service.dart:70` — “static final instance = LearningProgramRepository._create();”
- **Fix:** Migrate test fixtures to override learningProgramRepositoryProvider via ProviderContainer overrides instead of reading the singleton directly; once the fan-out is gone, delete the singleton entirely.
- **Done when:** New test code does not introduce further LearningProgramRepository.instance call sites. · Existing call sites tracked for migration (e.g. a DNI ticket) with a path to eventual deletion of the singleton.
- **Labels:** SM-7, singleton, test-quality · verifier corrections: Actual scope is 12 test files with 34 real .instance construction call sites, not '30+ test files' as stated — the finding conflated call-site count with file count. Substance unaffected. | Lines 69-70 quotes are exact;

- **Fix:** Delete _localDateOnly and call DateUtils.extractLocalDate at its two call sites instead.

- **Labels:** duplication, hygiene

#### AUD-settings-03 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Scope DataExportImportService.importData()'s 16 bare table deletes to the imported profile, not every profile on the device
- **Rule:** Documented class invariant (data_export_import_service.dart:501-504) + Evans invariant-enforced-in-one-place · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 16 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** Every delete in importData() (lines 517-532, one per user-data table) calls Drift's `delete(table).go()` with no `.where()` clause, which executes an unconditional DELETE FROM on that table. On a device with more than one local account or learner profile (the app's own account-switcher/registry and sibling-profile model), importing ONE profile's exported JSON silently erases every OTHER profile's/account's rows in all 16 tables first -- directly contradicting the method's own doc comment. The multi-account round-trip test (epic_26_story_23_data_export_round_trip_test.dart) can't catch this because it manually wipes the ENTIRE database before calling importData(), so a scoped delete and this unscoped one are indistinguishable to that test. DataExportImportService has zero production callers today (grepped repo-wide across lib/), so no user is exposed yet, but it is fully implemented and covered by ~900 lines of tests across 8 test files -- clear signal a 'restore backup' UI hookup is imminent, at which point the first restore on a multi-child/multi-account device would silently erase a sibling's entire Torah-study history.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:502` — “/// Per-profile import: deletes all existing rows and re-inserts from the
  /// export payload. Does not hard-delete accounts not present in”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:517` — “await _database.delete(_database.streakEvents).go();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:532` — “await _database.delete(_database.accounts).go();”
- **Fix:** Thread profileId/accountId into importData() and scope every delete with `..where((tbl) => tbl.profileId.equals(profileId))` (account-level equivalent for accounts/learnerProfiles); extend the round-trip test to seed two profiles and import only one.
- **Done when:** New/updated test seeds profile A and profile B, exports+imports only A, and asserts profile B's rows in all 16 tables are byte-for-byte unchanged (not just non-empty). · Every _database.delete(...) call in importData() carries a matching .where(...) scoping clause -- checkable by a Rule-0 grep asserting no bare `delete(_database.` call lacks a following `..where(` in this file.
- **Labels:** data-loss, settings, drift, dormant-code

#### AUD-settings-04 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Batch DataExportImportService.importData()'s 16 per-row insert loops instead of awaiting each row individually
- **Rule:** DB-3 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 16 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Every one of the 16 imported tables is inserted row-by-row with an individual `await ...insert(...)` inside a for loop instead of Drift's batch()/insertAll for same-shape bulk writes (lines 538-901). The whole thing is correctly wrapped in one _database.transaction() (DB-2 satisfied), but each row still pays its own round-trip; a family with several years of daily completions (thousands of completionEvents/learningLedger rows) multiplies import wall-clock time by roughly the row count instead of running as a handful of batched statements. Same dormant-code caveat as the delete-scoping finding in this file: no production caller exists yet, so this is a design defect ready to bite the first real user of a to-be-built restore feature, not an active incident.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:538` — “for (final u in data['userProfiles'] as List) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:717` — “for (final e in (data['completionEvents'] as List? ?? [])) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:887` — “for (final e in (data['streakEvents'] as List? ?? [])) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:558` — “for (final p in (data['learnerProfiles'] as List? ?? [])) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:581` — “for (final t in data['curriculumTracks'] as List) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:621` — “for (final s in (data['curriculumScopes'] as List? ?? [])) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:638` — “for (final p in (data['profilePrograms'] as List? ?? [])) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:658` — “for (final s in data['stageDefinitions'] as List) {” _(+8 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Replace each per-table loop with _database.batch((b) => b.insertAll(_database.<table>, rows)) inside the existing transaction.
- **Done when:** Import of a large fixture (1,000+ completionEvents) uses batch()/insertAll, verifiable by code review confirming no remaining bare `for` + `await ...insert(` loop in importData(), or by an insert-call-count assertion in a test.
- **Labels:** performance, settings, drift, dormant-code · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches

- **Fix:** Add tests importing legacy-quartet payloads with scheduleType: 'weekly' (including a JSON-string-encoded daysOfWeek and a native-List one) and 'rolling', plus one with the new 'schedule' field pre-populated, asserting the resulting stage_definitions.schedule column.

#### AUD-settings-09 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Route UserProfileHeaderCard through feature barrels instead of 6 deep cross-feature imports; settings.dart barrel is dead (Rule 2)
- **Rule:** Rule 2 (cross-feature barrel) + Rule-0 checker defect · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 7 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Rule 2 requires cross-feature references go through a barrel; UserProfileHeaderCard instead reaches directly into 3 files under features/account and 3 under features/profiles. Meanwhile features/settings/settings.dart -- the feature's only declared public surface, per its own header comment -- exports nothing and a repo-wide grep shows zero files import it. This is invisible in the audit baseline because the Makefile's own Rule-2 checker (make audit check 15/15, learning_tracker/Makefile:374-386) is broken: its awk step compares the feature name parsed from the file-path column against the feature name parsed from the FIRST 'features/X/' match in the whole grep line, which is always the importing file's own path (it appears before the import statement in `grep -n` output) -- so a[1] always equals b[1] and the WARN branch can never fire, for any file, repo-wide. I confirmed this by running the exact Makefile pipeline against this file: it produced zero matches despite the 6 genuine cross-feature imports above. Concrete cost: renaming/restructuring AppUser, AuthState or ProfileModel inside account/profiles breaks this widget with no barrel boundary to absorb the change, and nothing in CI would warn about it even though Rule 2 is nominally 'enforced'.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/widgets/user_profile_header_card.dart:4` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/account/domain/models/app_user.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/widgets/user_profile_header_card.dart:5` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/account/domain/models/auth_state.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/widgets/user_profile_header_card.dart:6` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/account/presentation/providers/auth_state_provider.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/widgets/user_profile_header_card.dart:7` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/profiles/domain/models/profile_model.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/widgets/user_profile_header_card.dart:8` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/profiles/presentation/providers/active_profile_provider.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/widgets/user_profile_header_card.dart:9` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/profiles/presentation/providers/profile_providers.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/settings.dart:3` — “// Import this barrel (features/settings/settings.dart) from outside this”
- **Fix:** Either populate settings.dart (and account's/profiles' equivalents) with a real public surface and route UserProfileHeaderCard's imports through them, or delete the dead settings.dart if the barrel convention is being abandoned. Separately, fix the awk field-comparison in Makefile check 15/15 so it diffs the importing file's own feature (from the path column) against the feature parsed specifically from the `package:learning_tracker/features/...` import string, not the first match in the whole line.
- **Done when:** make audit check 15/15 flags a deliberately-reintroduced cross-feature deep import in a scratch file (proves the checker actually fires) · user_profile_header_card.dart imports account/profiles symbols only via their barrels, or settings.dart is removed if the barrel convention is dropped
- **Labels:** layering, rule-2, tooling-defect · verifier corrections: coding-standards.md's actual Rule 2 text names `providers.dart` as the sole sanctioned barrel, not `<feature>.dart` — settings.dart is not really 'the' correct target either. Also verified account.dart (populated, real e

#### AUD-settings-13 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Throw a typed ValidationException, not dart:core FormatException, from DataExportImportService.validateAndPreview
- **Rule:** EH-2 / Evans ubiquitous-language consistency · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Every other domain exception in this batch (e.g. LastActiveCurriculumException) extends the project's AppException/ValidationException hierarchy in core/exceptions/app_exception.dart, letting callers catch by stable project type and letting presentation map to a localized message by type. validateAndPreview instead throws bare dart:core FormatException at 4 sites (463, 468, 474, 477), indistinguishable from the FormatException json.decode itself can throw two lines above -- a caller can't tell 'malformed JSON' from 'well-formed JSON missing a required section' without string-matching the message, and can't localize it the way the rest of the domain layer does.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:463` — “throw const FormatException('Invalid JSON format');”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/domain/services/data_export_import_service.dart:474` — “throw FormatException('Missing required section: $section');”
- **Fix:** Introduce a typed exception (e.g. ImportValidationException extends ValidationException) and throw it in place of FormatException at all 4 sites; update the tests currently asserting throwsA(isA<FormatException>()).
- **Done when:** validateAndPreview/importData throw the new typed exception, not FormatException; existing malformed-import tests updated to assert the new type.
- **Labels:** error-handling, settings, consistency · verifier corrections: DataExportImportService (validateAndPreview/importData) has zero callers anywhere in lib/ outside itself — confirmed via repo-wide grep. The 'propagates to presentation, can't localize' framing is currently hypothetical 

### features/sync  (8 findings — 0 P0 / 1 P1 / 3 P2 / 4 P3)

#### AUD-sync-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · SyncStatus.error and RestoreStatus.error carry a free-text message instead of a stable code, inviting raw/untranslated text downstream
- **Rule:** EH-5 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [2x2] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** EH-5 requires domain/data errors to carry stable codes/enums, never pre-formatted human messages, because this is an EN+Hebrew app where presentation must resolve text via AppLocalizations. Both status models instead expose a raw String message, and sync_providers.dart populates SyncStatus.error.message straight from error.toString() -- an unbounded, unlocalized, potentially technical string. This is not hypothetical: features/settings/presentation/widgets/backup_sync_section.dart already had to add an explicit guard (its own comment: 'never pass a raw exception string into the user-facing subtitle') to avoid rendering SyncStatusError.message directly, and lib/app/restore/device_restore_service.dart embeds RestoreStatus.error's message straight into a rethrown Exception's text. Any future consumer that pattern-matches .message without knowing about that workaround ships raw/English text to Hebrew-locale users.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/domain/models/sync_status.dart:41` — “required String message,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/domain/models/restore_status.dart:26` — “const factory RestoreStatus.error({required String message}) =”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart:60` — “message: error.toString(),”
- **Fix:** Replace the free-text message field on both SyncStatus.error and RestoreStatus.error with a stable enum/code (e.g. SyncErrorCode) plus optional non-user-facing debug detail, and have presentation resolve the code via AppLocalizations, per EH-5.
- **Done when:** EH-5 Rule-0 checker (grep for `required String message` on sealed status/result types, or raw error.toString() flowing into a domain model) passes. · backup_sync_section.dart's existing raw-string guard becomes structurally unnecessary because the type no longer exposes text to short-circuit around.
- **Labels:** EH-5, i18n, error-handling, sync · verifier corrections: Finding's claim that device_restore_service.dart 'embeds RestoreStatus.error's message into a rethrown Exception' has causality reversed -- line 175 embeds SyncStatus.error's message into a thrown Exception, whose toStri

#### AUD-sync-02 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · LocalDataUploadService.pushAllLocalData enqueues every entity kind via a per-row awaited loop instead of a batched outbox write
- **Rule:** DB-3 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 7 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** pushAllLocalData is explicitly a one-time bulk operation ('Called once after a local-born account is upgraded to cloud... so the user's offline learning history is immediately available') yet writes to the single Drift outbox table one row at a time across 7 loops, each await-ing OutboxSyncWriteFacade._enqueue -> OutboxDao.insertOutboxRow individually. Per outbox_sync_write_facade.dart:289-292, each insert also fires its own unawaited network drain-kick. A learner with a full year of history could have hundreds of completions/streak events/ledger entries; the one-time account-conversion flow does hundreds of sequential single-row DB writes plus hundreds of concurrent drain-kick Futures where a handful of batch inserts would do, extending how long this migration keeps the DB busy and widening the exposure window for the SM-4 race described in the companion finding.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/local_data_upload_service.dart:84` — “for (final p in ownProfiles) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/local_data_upload_service.dart:135` — “for (final b in bookmarks) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/local_data_upload_service.dart:162` — “for (final g in goals) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/local_data_upload_service.dart:196` — “for (final p in profilePrograms) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/local_data_upload_service.dart:229` — “for (final e in streakEvents) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/local_data_upload_service.dart:258` — “for (final e in ledgerEntries) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/local_data_upload_service.dart:287` — “for (final t in tracks) {”
- **Fix:** Batch each entity kind's outbox rows via db.batch()/insertAll (build the list of OutboxCompanions first, one transaction per kind) instead of looping individually-awaited _enqueue calls; fire at most one drain-kick per pushAllLocalData call rather than one per row.
- **Done when:** DB-3 Rule-0 checker (audit grep for awaited per-row insert loops against the same table) reports zero hits in local_data_upload_service.dart. · Test asserting pushAllLocalData with N seeded rows of a given kind performs O(1) outbox-table statements via a batch/insertAll spy, not O(N).
- **Labels:** DB-3, performance, sync, drift

#### AUD-sync-03 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · OutboxSyncWriteFacade._enqueue swallows every drain-tee failure with no log and no AppLogger field in the class
- **Rule:** EH-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** OutboxSyncWriteFacade never declares an AppLogger field, so this catchError has no way to log even if it wanted to. Any exception from the drain tee -- including the UnmountedRefException from the companion SM-4 finding, or a genuine permission-denied/network failure -- is discarded with zero trace. Every push*/enqueue* method in this class, used for every sync write in the app, funnels through this one _enqueue, making it the single choke point where all fire-and-forget drain failures currently vanish silently. No test in this batch (including the 1184-line local_data_upload_service_test.dart, which never wires onEnqueueDrain) exercises this path either.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/outbox_sync_write_facade.dart:291` — “unawaited(tee().catchError((Object _) {}));”
- **Fix:** Inject an AppLogger into OutboxSyncWriteFacade (mirroring LocalDataUploadService's existing nullable _logger field) and log the swallowed exception at warn/error level inside catchError before discarding it.
- **Done when:** EH-3 Rule-0 checker (log-less catch grep) reports no hits in outbox_sync_write_facade.dart. · Unit test that stubs onEnqueueDrain to throw and asserts the logger receives the error.
- **Labels:** EH-3, error-handling, observability, sync

#### AUD-sync-04 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · onEnqueueDrain closures in sync_providers.dart read ref after an await with no ref.mounted guard
- **Rule:** SM-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Both onEnqueueDrain closures (in syncWriteFacadeProvider and outboxSyncWriteFacadeProvider) do a ref.read after an await with no ref.mounted check, violating SM-4. Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException if ref is used after its provider has rebuilt. Both providers watch activeProfileIdProvider/authStateProvider, which change on every profile switch or sign-out -- realistic during the network round-trip a drain takes. If that happens between the two awaits, the second ref.read(syncOrchestratorProvider)?.recordDrainAttempt() throws on a stale ref. The surrounding comment (sync_providers.dart:100-104) spells out the user-visible cost of skipping recordDrainAttempt: 'the badge stays at its old value (e.g. a stale Synced) ... a false-Synced when the push failed.' Because this closure runs inside unawaited(tee().catchError((Object _) {})) in outbox_sync_write_facade.dart, the resulting exception is silently swallowed (see the companion EH-3 finding), so this failure currently has zero observability.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart:105` — “onEnqueueDrain: () async {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart:108` — “await ref.read(syncOrchestratorProvider)?.recordDrainAttempt();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart:165` — “await ref.read(syncOrchestratorProvider)?.recordDrainAttempt();”
- **Fix:** Check ref.mounted after the first await in both closures before the second ref.read call, per SM-4; extract the duplicated closure body into one shared helper to fix both sites at once.
- **Done when:** custom_lint/riverpod_lint rule flagging ref use after an await without a mounted check (SM-4 Enforce backstop). · Provider test that rebuilds/switches the active profile mid-drain and asserts no UnmountedRefException reaches the caller and recordDrainAttempt either completes or is safely skipped.
- **Labels:** SM-4, riverpod, race-condition, sync

#### AUD-sync-05 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Repositories/services constructed inline instead of injected via a provider at three sync-path call sites
- **Rule:** SM-7 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** SM-7 requires repositories/services/DAOs to be constructed only inside their @riverpod provider or a test override, so they stay swappable in tests without also having to fake the DB the constructor pulls in. All three sites construct a repository/service directly inside a plain method body, given only the already-available UserDatabase. A unit test of pushAllLocalData, buildGamificationSnapshot, or the reward-merge delegate cannot substitute a fake ParentAnalyticsRepositoryImpl/RewardMilestoneService without also faking the whole Drift database those classes read. This is a repo-wide pattern (23 similar sites exist outside this batch too, e.g. lib/core/navigation/guards/restore_guard.dart), not unique to these three, so the cost here is real but modest.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/local_data_upload_service.dart:106` — “final analytics = ParentAnalyticsRepositoryImpl(_database);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/outbox_sync_write_facade.dart:141` — “final rewardService = RewardMilestoneService(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/data/reward_settings_merge_delegate.dart:35` — “final service = RewardMilestoneService(db, profileId: profileId);”
- **Fix:** Where these services need independent test substitution, accept them as constructor parameters (defaulting to the real implementation) instead of instantiating inline; lower priority given the pattern is pervasive repo-wide and each site is already exercisable via a real in-memory DB, as this batch's own tests demonstrate.
- **Done when:** SM-7 Rule-0 checker (audit grep for direct Repository/Service/Dao construction outside provider/test files) either passes for these three sites or the finding is explicitly filed as backlog alongside the wider repo-wide pattern.
- **Labels:** SM-7, testability, sync

#### AUD-sync-06 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Six leftover migration re-export shims in features/sync/ are unused by production code and violate Rule 2's 'only providers.dart barrel' clause
- **Rule:** Rule-2 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 6 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** Rule 2 states the providers.dart barrel is 'the only sanctioned re-export file. Do not add other barrel/re-export files.' These six are bare `export '...';` shims (or, for sync.dart, an empty library-only file with zero exports) left over from moves labelled W1.4/W1.7/W1.8 in their own comments. Grepping every .dart file in the repo: restore_providers.dart, device_restore_screen.dart, and sync.dart have zero importers anywhere, even in tests. merge_rules.dart, profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart, and device_restore_service.dart are imported only by test files, never by lib/ production code, which already uses the canonical core/app paths directly. sync.dart's comment additionally claims 'the legacy sync stack is being deleted in Wave 2... After deletion, sync infrastructure lives in lib/core/sync/', which is stale -- OutboxSyncWriteFacade and LocalDataUploadService are the live, current replacement and were never meant to be deleted. A developer trusting this comment or grepping 'where is merge_rules defined' gets actively misleading signal.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/domain/merge_rules.dart:2` — “export 'package:learning_tracker/core/sync/merge/merge_rules.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/domain/profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart:2` — “export 'package:learning_tracker/core/preferences/profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/domain/services/device_restore_service.dart:2` — “export 'package:learning_tracker/app/restore/device_restore_service.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/presentation/providers/restore_providers.dart:2` — “export 'package:learning_tracker/app/restore/restore_providers.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/presentation/screens/device_restore_screen.dart:2` — “export 'package:learning_tracker/app/restore/device_restore_screen.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/sync.dart:8` — “library sync;”
- **Fix:** Delete all six files; repoint the test files that still import the deprecated paths (merge_rules_test.dart, profile_scoped_preference_keys_test.dart, device_restore_service's story-acceptance tests) at their canonical locations, moving them to the AG-5-mirrored test path in the process.
- **Done when:** grep confirms zero remaining files under lib/features/sync/ that are bare export re-directs to core/ or app/. · merge_rules_test.dart and profile_scoped_preference_keys_test.dart import from lib/core/sync/merge/merge_rules.dart and lib/core/preferences/profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart respectively, at the AG-5-mirrored test path.
- **Labels:** Rule-2, dead-code, AG-5, migration-debris

#### AUD-sync-08 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · outboxSyncWriteFacadeProvider mutates DAO state and fires a network re-enqueue from inside its Provider build function
- **Rule:** SM-2 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** The code directly inside `Provider<OutboxSyncWriteFacade?>((ref) {...})` mutates pointsBalanceDao.syncSink and unawaited-fires reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows(profileId) unconditionally on every build. This provider watches authStateProvider, activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider, userDatabaseProvider, activeProfileIdProvider, and localDayClockProvider -- any of which changing (e.g. every profile switch in this multi-child app) reruns build and refires the recovery scan, which its own D14 comment says is meant to run once. SM-2 exists precisely because 'side effects in build race and get skipped or duplicated on rebuild' -- here they duplicate on every rebuild instead of running once.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart:147` — “ref.read(userDatabaseProvider).pointsBalanceDao.syncSink = null;”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart:172` — “database.pointsBalanceDao.syncSink = facade;”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart:176` — “unawaited(database.pointsBalanceDao.reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows(profileId));”
- **Fix:** Move syncSink wiring and the one-time ledger-recovery call out of build into a ref.listen/onDispose pairing or an explicit one-shot recovery triggered on cloud-conversion, leaving build to only construct and return the facade.
- **Done when:** riverpod_lint/custom_lint rule flagging DAO field mutation or unawaited async calls directly inside a Provider build body (SM-2 Enforce backstop). · Regression test with a spy DAO asserting reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows is invoked at most once per profile per session, not once per rebuild (simulate two profile switches).
- **Labels:** SM-2, riverpod, side-effects, sync · verifier corrections: The finding's 'why' misquotes sync_providers.dart:175's own comment (actual text: 'Idempotent + fire-and-forget so it never blocks the UI', not 'meant to run once'). points_balance_dao.dart:559-567's doc comment on reEnq

#### AUD-tracks-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Fix duplicate 'Track progress' label on TrackDetailScreen showing two differently-sourced percentages
- **Rule:** Evans (invariant re-derived, not enforced once) / user-visible defect · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 11 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** build() reads cycleFraction from dashboardTrackCompletionPercentageProvider (documented in dashboard_providers.dart:131-134 as 'all-time, multi-stage gate') and separately reads currentCyclePct from trackDualProgressMetricsProvider (documented as 'time-gated, single-ref check') — two admittedly different formulas. The header card then shows currentCyclePct combined with the label text 'Track progress' at line 397, and — whenever the track has no chazara stages — reuses the exact same `trackProgressLabel` variable for the second row at line 419, next to cycleFraction's value at line 427. Any track where the two formulas diverge (routine per their own doc comment) renders two different numbers under the identical label on the same card. The dedicated regression test for this exact section (track_detail_screen_test.dart `_overridesFor`) feeds the SAME `currentCycle` value into both provider overrides by construction, so it can never catch the two rows disagreeing — a textbook tautological fixture.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/screens/track_detail_screen.dart:152` — “dashboardTrackCompletionPercentageProvider(track.id),”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/screens/track_detail_screen.dart:162` — “trackDualProgressMetricsProvider(track.profileId),”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/screens/track_detail_screen.dart:397` — “'$trackProgressLabel: $trackProgressDisplay',”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/screens/track_detail_screen.dart:419` — “: trackProgressLabel,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/screens/track_detail_screen.dart:427` — “cyclePercentDisplay,”; `learning_tracker/test/features/tracks/setup/presentation/screens/track_detail_screen_test.dart:103` — “dashboardTrackCompletionPercentageProvider(”; `learning_tracker/test/features/tracks/setup/presentation/screens/track_detail_screen_test.dart:110` — “trackDualProgressMetricsProvider(track.profileId).overrideWith(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/screens/track_detail_screen.dart:896` — “if (activeCurricula.length <= 1) {
      if (!mounted) return;” _(+3 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Give the lower ('cyclePercentDisplay') row a distinct, non-reused label instead of falling back to trackProgressLabel, or drive both rows off the same provider/formula. Update the test fixture to pass different currentCycle-vs-dashboard values so a future re-divergence fails.
- **Done when:** A widget test overrides dashboardTrackCompletionPercentageProvider and trackDualProgressMetricsProvider with DIFFERENT values and asserts the screen never shows two different percentages under the same 'Track progress' label · track_detail_screen_test.dart's _overridesFor no longer derives both provider overrides from one shared currentCycle parameter
- **Labels:** ui-bug, progress-metrics, track-detail · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches

#### AUD-tracks-04 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Log and surface the swallowed exceptions in step_starting_position.dart._loadContent and step_starting_position_calendar.dart._refreshCalendarEntry instead of silently stranding the user
- **Rule:** EH-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** step_starting_position.dart._loadContent catches everything and only flips _loading to false — it never logs via AppLogger and never sets an error flag. Since _containers/_leaves default to [], build() falls straight through to `_buildContainerList` with an EMPTY list and no CircularProgressIndicator, no error text, and no retry action: the user lands on a blank, silently-broken 'starting position' step of the Add-Track wizard with the Continue button permanently disabled (onPressed requires _selectedLeaf != null, which can never become non-null from an empty list) and zero indication anything went wrong. step_starting_position_calendar.dart._refreshCalendarEntry has no catch at all (only `finally`) around two awaits, and every caller invokes it via `unawaited(...)`, so a thrown exception becomes an unhandled Future rejection with no AppLogger trail; the user instead sees the ALSO-hardcoded 'No local calendar entry found for this date.' fallback, which mislabels a real fetch/service failure as 'no data for this date'.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/steps/step_starting_position.dart:113` — “} catch (_) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/steps/step_starting_position.dart:114` — “if (mounted) setState(() => _loading = false);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/steps/step_starting_position_calendar.dart:95` — “final service = await ref.read(calendarProgramServiceProvider.future);”
- **Fix:** In both catches (or the missing one in the calendar file), log via AppLogger with context (curriculumId/programKey), and expose a distinct error state to the widget (e.g. an AppErrorView with retry, matching the pattern TrackManagementBody already uses via ref.watch(...).when(error: ...)) instead of silently falling through to an indistinguishable empty/fallback UI.
- **Done when:** Both catch paths call AppLogger.error/warning with the caught exception before updating state. · A widget test that makes the repository/service throw asserts a visible error affordance (not a blank list / not the generic 'no entry' text) appears. · EH-3's log-less-catch grep (once made a checker) passes on both files.
- **Labels:** error-handling, silent-failure, ux-dead-end · verifier corrections: Site 2's claim of 'no AppLogger trail' is not accurate: main.dart wraps runApp in runZonedGuarded(), whose handler calls AppLogger.instance.handle(error, stack) (and Crashlytics.recordError) for any uncaught zone error, 

#### AUD-tracks-05 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Rebuild TrackLearningOrderScreen's masechtos ReorderableListView with a lazy builder, not shrinkWrap+children
- **Rule:** PF-2 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** Track Detail's 'Reorder Learning Order' tile (track_detail_screen.dart:642-658, one tap: `onTap: () => Navigator.of(context).push(MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => TrackLearningOrderScreen(...)))`) opens a screen whose masechtos section renders one DraggableOrderItem (a ListTile wrapped in ReorderableDragStartListener, itself a ConsumerWidget with its own label-provider watch) per distinct level-2 hierarchy value of the track's curriculum, via the plain (non-.builder) ReorderableListView constructor with shrinkWrap:true nested inside a SingleChildScrollView. hasReorderableLevel2 enables this section for every curriculum except Chumash/Tanach. I counted distinct level-2 values directly from the bundled assets/content/hierarchy/*.json: Mishna Berurah=697 (Simanim), Mishneh Torah=85, Mussar=59, Mishnayos=63, Yerushalmi=39, Bavli=37. Any user with one of these active tracks — the majority of the app's curricula — who taps 'Reorder Learning Order' forces the screen to synchronously build and lay out every one of those rows in one frame: shrinkWrap:true requires the sliver to size itself before the outer SingleChildScrollView can lay out, so simply swapping to `.builder` without also removing shrinkWrap would not fix it. This is the most severe PF-2 site found in this pass: worst-case count (697) is the highest found, per-item cost is heavier than a bare ListTile, and it is reached by an ordinary, one-tap, documented user action on ordinary curricula (not an edge case).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/track_order/presentation/screens/track_learning_order_screen.dart:121` — “ReorderableListView(
                      shrinkWrap: true,”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/track_order/presentation/screens/track_learning_order_screen.dart:126` — “for (var i = 0; i < _localMasechtos!.length; i++)
                          DraggableOrderItem(”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/constants/curriculum_defaults.dart:1168` — “static bool hasReorderableLevel2(CurriculumId id) =>
      id != CurriculumId.chumash && id != CurriculumId.tanach;”
- **Fix:** Replace `ReorderableListView(children:...)` with `ReorderableListView.builder(itemCount: _localMasechtos!.length, itemBuilder: ...)`, and remove the shrinkWrap:true + SingleChildScrollView nesting — host the sedarim and masechtos sections in a single CustomScrollView with SliverReorderableList sections (or SliverList for read-only rows) instead, so the shrinkWrap-forced full eager layout is eliminated along with the eager builder.
- **Done when:** Rule-0: PF-2 checker (grep/custom_lint) flags `ReorderableListView(` (non-.builder) combined with `shrinkWrap: true` anywhere under lib/features/**. · Regression test: pump TrackLearningOrderScreen for a Mishna Berurah track backed by a 700-item trackMasechtosOrderProvider fixture; assert via find.byType(DraggableOrderItem) that only a viewport's worth of rows are realized (not all 700), and that tester.pumpAndSettle completes within a bounded frame budget instead of timing out.
- **Labels:** performance, PF-2, tracks, reorder

#### AUD-tracks-06 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Stop LearningOrderRepositoryImpl.getOrder from writing to the DB as a side effect of a FutureProvider build call
- **Rule:** SM-2 (provider build is pure — no writes/side effects) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** getOrder is invoked directly from learningOrderProvider's FutureProvider.family build callback, yet it performs a DB write (_stampReorderAt) whenever the stored learningOrderVersion is stale — and nothing else ever updates learningOrderVersion except an explicit user reorder/reset. So on every cold start or provider invalidation while the version mismatch persists, merely reading the curriculum's order silently re-stamps lastReorderAt = now, which is exactly the reorder-amnesty trigger — overdue-item detection for that curriculum stays silently suppressed after any content reseed until the user happens to manually reorder or reset, defeating a named product invariant via a function that looks like a pure read.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/whole_curriculum_order/data/repositories/learning_order_repository_impl.dart:69` — “if (savedVersion != _currentContentVersion) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/whole_curriculum_order/data/repositories/learning_order_repository_impl.dart:76` — “await _stampReorderAt(curriculumId, DateTimeFactory.nowUtc());”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/whole_curriculum_order/presentation/providers/learning_order_providers.dart:66` — “return repository.getOrder(curriculumId);”
- **Fix:** Move the version-mismatch re-amnesty write out of getOrder into an explicit, one-shot repair step (run once at app start or as part of the content-reseed pipeline) so provider build stays a pure read.
- **Done when:** Test: call getOrder() twice in a row with a stale learningOrderVersion and assert lastReorderAt is stamped at most once, not on every call · Provider build functions in learning_order_providers.dart contain no DB write calls
- **Labels:** riverpod, state-management, tracks

#### AUD-tracks-08 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Surface reorder/reset save failures to the user in the learning-order screens instead of silently swallowing them
- **Rule:** EH-2 (no raw exception reaches presentation without becoming a value) + Nygard I/O-failure-halfway lens · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** None of these 5 call paths (2 persist + 1 reset in track_learning_order_screen.dart; 1 reorder + 1 reset in learning_order_screen.dart) has a try/catch or .catchError. The UI has already applied the optimistic reorder to local widget state before the write lands, so if saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder/saveOrder/resetToDefault throws (DB busy, disk full, offline outbox push failure) the screen keeps showing the new order as saved with zero error affordance and no rollback — the user believes it persisted; it silently didn't, and it reverts on next app load. Sibling screens in the same feature (edit_track_screen.dart, add_track_flow_screen.dart, track_management_hub_screen.dart) all wrap the equivalent save call in try/catch + ScaffoldMessenger SnackBar; this pair is the outlier.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/track_order/presentation/screens/track_learning_order_screen.dart:187` — “unawaited(_persistSedarim(updated));”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/track_order/presentation/screens/track_learning_order_screen.dart:214` — “_persistMasechtos(updated);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/track_order/presentation/screens/track_learning_order_screen.dart:245` — “Future<void> _resetToDefault(BuildContext context) async {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/whole_curriculum_order/presentation/screens/learning_order_screen.dart:155` — “unawaited(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/whole_curriculum_order/presentation/screens/learning_order_screen.dart:163` — “Future<void> _resetToDefault(BuildContext context) async {”
- **Fix:** Wrap each persist/reset call in try/catch (or move the mutation into a proper AsyncNotifier using AsyncValue.guard), show a SnackBar/retry matching the add_track_flow_screen.dart pattern, and revert _local*/_localOrder to the pre-optimistic value on failure.
- **Done when:** Widget test: stub the repository/use-case to throw on saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder/saveOrder/resetToDefault and assert a visible error affordance appears and local state reverts · No unawaited(...persist...) or bare .then(...) without an adjacent catch remains in these two files
- **Labels:** error-handling, tracks, ux

#### AUD-tracks-13 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Fix AX-1's EdgeInsets.only(left:/right:) grep to match multi-line dart-format output, and fix the resulting hit in track_management_body.dart
- **Rule:** AX-1 / Rule 0 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 7 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** track_management_body.dart:102-107 uses EdgeInsets.only(left: 16, right: 16, top: 8, bottom: 96) — the exact pattern AX-1 bans. The root Makefile's check 10/12 grep is single-line only (`[^)]*` cannot span the newline dart format inserts after 4+ named args), so `grep -rn 'EdgeInsets\.only([^)]*\(left\|right\):' lib/` returns zero hits repo-wide even though this exact violation exists; a `-Pzo` multiline reproduction confirms the hit. Because left==right==16 here there's no live RTL rendering bug today, but the checker gives false confidence: a future edit that makes left != right (a real RTL mirror bug) would ship silently, and this is the only file in the batch with this shape so the blind spot is real, not hypothetical.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/widgets/track_management_body.dart:102` — “padding: const EdgeInsets.only(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/widgets/track_management_body.dart:103` — “left: 16,”; `Makefile:184` — “HITS=$$(grep -rn 'EdgeInsets\.only([^)]*\(left\|right\):' "$$LIB/" \”; `packages/custom_lints/lib/src/rules/no_hardcoded_text_direction.dart:38` — “'Alignment': {'centerLeft', 'centerRight'},
    'TextAlign': {'left', 'right'},”; `Makefile:183` — “echo "[10/12] EdgeInsets.only(left:|right:) — RTL violation (NFR16/UX-DR5)"; \”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/screens/track_management_hub_screen.dart:126` — “padding: const EdgeInsets.only(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/screens/track_management_hub_screen.dart:127` — “left: 16,”
- **Fix:** Rewrite the grep to be multiline-aware (e.g. `grep -Pzo` or a small Dart/Python AST-ish scan) so it catches EdgeInsets.only(...) regardless of formatting, then replace this instance with EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start:, end:, top:, bottom:).
- **Done when:** The root Makefile's AX-1 check flags a deliberately-added multi-line EdgeInsets.only(left:...) fixture. · track_management_body.dart's padding is EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start:, end:, top:, bottom:). · `make audit` (root) still exits 0 after the fix.
- **Labels:** accessibility, rtl, rule-0, false-negative · merged 2 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 3 batches

#### AUD-tracks-16 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Wrap saveOrder/resetToDefault's reorder-amnesty stamp in the same transaction as the order write

- **Fix:** Move the _stampReorderAt call inside the same _database.transaction(...) block in both saveOrder and resetToDefault.
- **Done when:** Test: throw inside a fake trackDao.stampReorderAt call and assert the learning_order upsert rows are also rolled back as one atomic unit
- **Labels:** data-integrity, drift, tracks

- **Why:** _saveStudyDaysLocal (track_creation_service.dart:348-368) and _saveStudyDays (track_edit_service.dart:95-115) are byte-for-byte identical except a parameter name — the exact 'delete then loop-await-upsert' method copy-pasted into two sibling services. A future fix (validation, batching, a new column) applied to one copy silently leaves the other stale. - **Fix:** Extract one shared DAO-level batched helper (e.g. StudyDayConfigDao.replaceAll using batch()) and call it from both services; do the same for _saveScopes.
- **Done when:** One shared helper implements the delete+insert study-day/scope replacement using batch()/insertAll · TrackCreationService and TrackEditService both call it; no duplicate method body remains
- **Labels:** duplication, drift, performance
