#### AUD-tutoring-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Check TutorGrantResult before treating revoke/resign/rescind as successful in manage_tutors_screen.dart and manage_grants_screen.dart
- **Rule:** EH-2 / EH-6 (exhaustive Result handling) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** All three handlers await the use case's Future<TutorGrantResult> and discard the return value, then unconditionally run the success branch (wipe local mirror, invalidate the grant list, send a lifecycle email) inside `if (mounted) { ... }`, with only a generic `catch` around thrown exceptions. FirestoreTutorGrantRepository.revokeGrant/resignGrant/rescindInvite never rethrow FirebaseFunctionsException — they always return TutorGrantFailure. So when the Cloud Function genuinely rejects the call (permission-denied, already-revoked race, offline), the UI still shows success, wipes the tutor's local mirror, and — worst case for _revoke — emails the tutor 'your access was revoked' while the grant is still active server-side, giving the parent false assurance that access was cut off. The sibling screens (invite/accept/decline) all correctly `switch` on the same result type, proving the pattern is known but was missed here.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/manage_grants_screen.dart:228` — “await ref.read(resignTutorGrantUseCaseProvider).call(grant: widget.grant);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/manage_tutors_screen.dart:368` — “await ref.read(revokeTutorGrantUseCaseProvider).call(grant: widget.grant);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/manage_tutors_screen.dart:427` — “.read(rescindTutorInviteUseCaseProvider)
          .call(grant: widget.grant);”
- **Fix:** Assign the awaited call to a `result` variable and exhaustively switch on TutorGrantSuccess/TutorGrantFailure/TutorGrantPreconditionError exactly as invite_tutor_screen.dart/accept_invite_screen.dart/decline_invite_screen.dart already do; only run the mirror-wipe/invalidate/notify side effects on Success, and surface a localized error (not e.toString()) otherwise.
- **Done when:** Add a widget test in manage_tutors_screen_l1_test.dart that stubs revokeTutorGrantUseCaseProvider/rescindTutorInviteUseCaseProvider to return TutorGrantFailure and asserts wipeMirrorForGrant/notifyTutorOfRevocation/ref.invalidate are NOT invoked and an error is shown. · Add the equivalent test in manage_grants_screen_l1_test.dart for resignTutorGrantUseCaseProvider returning TutorGrantFailure. · flutter analyze clean; existing Success-path tests continue to pass.
- **Labels:** error-handling, correctness, tutoring, security-adjacent

Update the two pinned test assertions to check the localized string.
- **Done when:** TutorGrantPreconditionError carries a code/enum, not a pre-formatted message; tutor_invite_use_cases.dart no longer interpolates grant id/state into user-facing text · accept_invite_screen.dart and decline_invite_screen.dart resolve the code via AppLocalizations/ARB with EN+HE parity · accept_invite_screen_l1_test.dart and decline_invite_screen_l1_test.dart assert the localized string, not literal English; a Locale('he') variant confirms the Hebrew string renders

#### AUD-tutoring-04 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Catch and log exceptions around TutorPinService calls in the PIN entry/setup async handlers
- **Rule:** EH-2 / EH-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** _onPinComplete (gate) and _onConfirmPinEntered (setup) wrap their await in try/finally with no catch clause. TutorPinService.verifyTutorPin/setTutorPin only converts PinLockoutException — an underlying secure-storage failure (a real class of Android keystore/PlatformException issue this environment has hit before per the App Check debug-token flakiness on wipes) propagates as a raw, uncaught exception. Because _onPinComplete is invoked fire-and-forget (not awaited) from _appendDigit, the failure is swallowed by whatever global handler exists, with zero AppLogger call from this site and zero user feedback: _isVerifying resets to false in the finally block but _errorMessage stays null and _digits stays at 4 filled dots, leaving the user staring at a stalled numpad with no explanation and no way to retype until they notice backspace still works.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/tutor_pin_entry_gate.dart:90` — “try {
      final service = ref.read(tutorPinServiceProvider);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/tutor_pin_entry_gate.dart:117` — “} finally {
      if (mounted) setState(() => _isVerifying = false);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/tutor_pin_setup_screen.dart:118` — “try {
      final service = ref.read(tutorPinServiceProvider);”
- **Fix:** Add a typed catch around the await that logs via AppLogger and sets a generic, localized _errorMessage (consistent with EH-2's 'no raw exception reaches presentation').
- **Done when:** _onPinComplete and _onConfirmPinEntered both have a catch block that calls AppLogger.instance.error and sets a localized _errorMessage · a test that makes the stubbed TutorPinService throw confirms the screen shows an error state instead of a silent stall
- **Labels:** EH-2, EH-3, P2 · verifier corrections: Minor: 'setTutorPin only converts PinLockoutException' overstates it — setTutorPin has zero exception handling (no lockout check exists for set), so it's worse than stated, not misleading in finder's favor. | EH-3's text

#### AUD-tutoring-05 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Convert TutorPermissions to @freezed instead of hand-writing ==/hashCode
- **Rule:** Naming/placement — "never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes" · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** coding-standards.md is explicit: domain value objects must be `@freezed` with generated `==`/`hashCode`/`copyWith`, specifically because hand-rolled equality drifts from the field list. TutorPermissions — its own doc-comment calls it 'Immutable value object' / 'VO' — hand-writes both operators across 9 fields, plus a separately hand-written constructor, copyWith, toFirestore, and fromFirestore: 5 places a future field addition must be updated by hand. The drift risk is already visible today: `canMarkLiveCompletion` is deliberately excluded from both `==` and `hashCode` (harmless only because it is hardcoded false for every instance) — exactly the kind of silent omission @freezed generation would make structurally impossible.

- **Fix:** Convert TutorPermissions to a @freezed class (keeping canMarkLiveCompletion as a computed getter rather than a constructor field, or a private default so it can't be set), and delete the hand-written ==/hashCode/copyWith.
- **Done when:** TutorPermissions.freezed.dart is generated; no hand-written operator == or hashCode remains in tutor_permissions.dart. · Existing TutorPermissions unit tests (defaults/readOnly/toFirestore round-trip) still pass unmodified.
- **Labels:** freezed, value-object, hygiene

#### AUD-tutoring-07 · **P2** · SUSPECTED · Handle mid-loop failure in TutoredWriteRouter.pushStageDefinitions (tutored_write_router.dart)
- **Rule:** Nygard (partial I/O failure) / DB-6 offline-first parity · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** pushStageDefinitions awaits one Cloud Function call per stage sequentially and _handleResult throws immediately on the first TutorWriteFailure. If a tutor edits several stages at once and the network drops partway through, the earlier stages are already committed server-side while the remaining ones are simply lost — the thrown TutorWriteException names only the failing stage, not which stages already succeeded. Unlike the normal (non-tutored) write path, tutored writes deliberately bypass the local outbox (per this file's own header comment), so there is no retry queue to pick the dropped stages back up on reconnect — the class's offline-first guarantee (DB-6, exercised everywhere else in this app) does not hold here. This is architectural/edge-case reasoning, not a reproduced runtime failure.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/data/routers/tutored_write_router.dart:141` — “for (final stage in stages) {”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/data/routers/tutored_write_router.dart:157` — “_handleResult(result, 'tutorUpsertStageDefinition[$stageId]');”
- **Fix:** Either batch the per-stage calls into a single CF invocation (atomic on the server) or collect per-stage results and surface a structured partial-failure summary (which stages succeeded/failed) so the caller can retry just the failed subset instead of losing silent state.
- **Done when:** A test that fails the 2nd of 3 stage upserts asserts the caller learns which stages succeeded (not just a single opaque exception). · Documented decision (in tutored_write_router.dart's header) on whether partial multi-stage failure is an accepted risk or gets a retry path.
- **Labels:** offline-first, nygard, partial-failure

#### AUD-tutoring-08 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Lazy-load the tutor-grants roster in ManageGrantsScreen and Settings' embedded pending-invites section
- **Rule:** PF-2 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Both screens map `incomingTutorGrantsProvider`/`pendingTutorInvitesProvider` (a tutor's full roster of children/parents who granted them access) into rows via a `for` loop feeding a non-lazy ListView/Column, in two independent places, and no cap on roster size exists anywhere in the codebase (grepped for maxTutor/tutorLimit/kMaxTutors and product-rules.md — none found). A dedicated tutor (e.g. a rebbi/melamed tracking many talmidim across seasons — the tutoring feature's own stated use case) accumulates one grant per student relationship over time with no visible archiving path; both the dedicated Manage Grants hub and the every-visit Settings screen's embedded pending-invites card rebuild every row on every open/rebuild. This is lower-urgency than the curriculum-hierarchy findings above (realistic roster sizes are more plausibly in the tens than the hundreds), but it is a genuine, duplicated PF-2 pattern on two commonly-visited screens — Settings in particular re-renders the full roster inline on its own top-level ListView every time any grant's state changes.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/manage_grants_screen.dart:83` — “return ListView(”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/manage_grants_screen.dart:91` — “for (final grant in activeGrants)
                    _GrantRow(grant: grant, canResign: true),”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/screens/settings_screen.dart:730` — “for (final grant in pendingGrants) ...[
          _TutorGrantTile(grant: grant, isPending: true),”
- **Fix:** Swap the `for`-loop expansion in ManageGrantsScreen (which already scrolls independently) for ListView.builder/ListView.separated. For Settings' embedded _PendingInvitesSection (which must stay non-scrolling inside the outer settings ListView), cap the inline preview (e.g. first 3-5 grants + a 'View all' link into Manage Grants) instead of rendering the full roster inline.
- **Done when:** Rule-0: PF-2 checker flags `for (final ... in ...)`/`.map(...)` expansions feeding ListView(/Column( children under lib/features/** where the source is a ref.watch'd stream/future provider rather than a literal bounded enum. · Regression test: seed 50 tutor grants in the fixture repo; pump ManageGrantsScreen and SettingsScreen and assert both build within a bounded frame budget, and (post-fix) that off-screen _GrantRow/_TutorGrantTile widgets are not realized via find.byType counts.
- **Labels:** performance, PF-2, tutoring, settings · verifier corrections: A third analogous site exists (manage_tutors_screen.dart:261-278, parent-side per-child tutor list) not counted in 'sites: 2' — an undercount, not an overclaim, so it doesn't weaken the finding.

#### AUD-tutoring-09 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Localize TutorPinValidationError.message instead of leaking raw English into tutor PIN screens
- **Rule:** EH-5 / AX-2 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]

- **Fix:** Replace the message field with a stable code/enum and resolve it via AppLocalizations in both screens, mirroring the TutorGrantFailure fix.
- **Done when:** TutorPinValidationError carries a code, not a literal English string · tutor_pin_setup_screen.dart and tutor_pin_entry_gate.dart resolve the code via AppLocalizations with EN+HE parity · a widget test forces the validation-error branch (e.g. directly invoking the service with a malformed pin) and asserts the localized string renders

#### AUD-tutoring-12 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Stop misreporting a failed local PIN clear as a failed reset email in TutorPinResetScreen
- **Rule:** Nygard-partial-failure · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** sendPasswordResetEmail and clearTutorPin are two sequential awaits inside one try block with one shared catch that always sets the l10n key tutorPinResetSendFailed ('Failed to send reset email...'). If the email send succeeds but the subsequent local-PIN-clear throws (a real possibility given documented secure-storage flakiness in this environment), the user is told the email failed when it actually sent — they will retry, triggering a second real password-reset email, while the actual failure (local PIN not cleared) goes unaddressed and unreported.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/tutor_pin_reset_screen.dart:76` — “await authRepo.sendPasswordResetEmail(email);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/tutor_pin_reset_screen.dart:80` — “await pinService.clearTutorPin(widget.profileId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/tutor_pin_reset_screen.dart:91` — “)!.tutorPinResetSendFailed,”
- **Fix:** Split the two operations into separate try/catch blocks (or at minimum track which step failed) so the error message and retry behavior match what actually happened.
- **Done when:** a failure in clearTutorPin after a successful sendPasswordResetEmail does not show the 'send failed' string · a regression test simulates clearTutorPin throwing after a successful email send and asserts the UI does not claim the email failed
- **Labels:** error-handling, P2

#### AUD-tutoring-13 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Type and log the catch block in TutorPinResetScreen._sendResetEmail
- **Rule:** EH-3 / EH-4 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The bare `catch (e)` has no `on X` type, so per Dart semantics it catches everything thrown — including Error subtypes (StateError, TypeError, NoSuchMethodError from a programmer bug) — and silently converts all of them into the same generic 'send failed' UI message with zero AppLogger call. A real programming defect elsewhere in the call chain would present identically to a normal network failure, with no trace to diagnose it.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/screens/tutor_pin_reset_screen.dart:86` — “} catch (e) {
      if (mounted) {”
- **Fix:** Catch a specific exception type (or at least log via AppLogger.instance.error before setting the UI message) so Error subtypes are not silently masked and failures are traceable.
- **Done when:** the catch block logs via AppLogger with the exception and stack trace before updating _errorMessage · the catch is narrowed to typed exceptions the send/clear operations can actually throw, not a bare catch(e)
- **Labels:** EH-3, EH-4, P2

#### AUD-tutoring-14 · **P3** · SUSPECTED · Add ref.mounted guards after awaits in manage_tutors_providers.dart's incomingTutorGrantsProvider
- **Rule:** SM-4 (ref.mounted after await) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** incomingTutorGrantsProvider watches `authStateProvider.select((s) => s.currentUser?.firebaseUid)` and then awaits two network/DB calls before touching `ref.read` three more times (lines 118, 124, 131). If the watched uid changes mid-flight (e.g. the tutor signs out while this fetch is in progress — the exact account-switch race this file's own comments say it must defend against), Riverpod 3 tears down this build invocation and a subsequent `ref.read` throws UnmountedRefException instead of the intended AsyncError/graceful outcome. No `ref.mounted` check guards any of the three post-await reads.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/providers/manage_tutors_providers.dart:106` — “final cfResult = await useCase.callWithStatus();”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/presentation/providers/manage_tutors_providers.dart:118` — “.read(activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider)
        ?.grantId;”
- **Fix:** Check `if (!ref.mounted) return const <TutorGrant>[];` (or equivalent) immediately after each await before touching ref again, mirroring the SM-4 pattern used elsewhere in Notifier methods.
- **Done when:** A test that invalidates authStateProvider's uid while incomingTutorGrantsProvider's future is pending does not throw UnmountedRefException.
- **Labels:** riverpod, SM-4, race-condition · verifier corrections: The 'why' text's line list (118, 124, 131) is slightly off — 131 is an await, not a ref.read; the second post-await ref-touch is actually line 121 (ref: ref, passed to buildTutoredMirrorWipeService).

#### AUD-tutoring-16 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Convert TutorPinResult switches in gate/setup screens from statements to switch expressions per EH-6
- **Rule:** EH-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** coding-standards.md EH-6 states closed variant sets must be modeled as sealed + 'switch over it with switch expressions; never add a default:/_ arm.' Both files use switch STATEMENTS (case Pattern: followed by statement blocks) over the sealed TutorPinResult, not the mandated expression form (contrast with tutor_pin_reset_screen.dart's `child: switch (_step) { ... => ..., }`, which does it correctly). Functionally harmless today — Dart's exhaustiveness checker covers statement-form switches too — but it's a textual violation of an explicitly documented, partially-enforced standard, and inconsistent with the sibling file in the same feature.

        case TutorPinSuccess():”
- **Fix:** Rewrite both switches as switch expressions (`TutorPinSuccess() => widget.onPinVerified(), ...`), matching tutor_pin_reset_screen.dart's style.

#### AUD-tutoring-17 · **P3** · SUSPECTED · Guard int.parse(sel.profileId) in tutored_write_router.dart
- **Rule:** EH-3/EH-4 (unhandled exception type breaks the class's stated contract) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 10 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The class doc says 'CF failures... are re-thrown as TutorWriteException so callers can surface a clear snackbar,' but int.parse(sel.profileId) is called unguarded at 10 sites before any CF call happens. If profileId is ever non-numeric (malformed TutoredProfileSelection, future ID-scheme change), a raw uncaught FormatException propagates instead of the documented TutorWriteException — no AppLogger context, and callers that specifically catch TutorWriteException per this class's contract won't catch it. - **Fix:** Parse once via a small helper (e.g. `_profileIdOrThrow(sel)`) that logs via AppLogger and throws a typed TutorWriteException on failure, matching the class's documented error contract; call it once instead of int.parse at each of the 10 sites.

#### AUD-app-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Fix app_shell.dart's fixed-height context banners — they truncate text under accessibility scaling and undersize the exit-button tap targets
- **Rule:** AX-4 (no fixed heights on text wrappers; 48dp targets) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** _ChildViewBanner (height: 28), TutorModeIndicatorBar (height: 24), and ProfileSwitcherBar (height: 44) are hardcoded-height Containers wrapping Text with maxLines:1/overflow:ellipsis and fontSize 11-14; none of them scale with MediaQuery.textScaler. At a larger accessibility text-scale setting, a real, present-day user segment sees the child/talmid name or role badge clipped tighter than intended, or the row overflowing the fixed bar. Independent of text scale, the Exit buttons in the first two banners are geometrically provable to be under the 48dp minimum: an icon(12)+padding(vertical:2x2)+text(11sp) inside a 24-28dp-tall parent caps the whole tap target at roughly 20-24dp — well short of 48dp — for a control (exiting parent/tutor mode) that a stressed or motor-impaired user needs to hit reliably.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/app/router/app_shell.dart:672` — “Container(
  height: 28,”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/router/app_shell.dart:769` — “Container(
  height: 24,”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/router/app_shell.dart:535` — “Container(
  key: const Key('appShellProfileSwitcherBarBackground'),
  height: 44,”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/router/app_shell.dart:704` — “padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 8, vertical: 2),”
- **Fix:** Let the banner Containers size to content (IntrinsicHeight or padding-driven, not a literal height:), and grow the Exit InkWell's hit area to kMinInteractiveDimension via padding/ConstrainedBox independent of the visual bar height.
- **Done when:** _ChildViewBanner, TutorModeIndicatorBar, and ProfileSwitcherBar no longer hardcode a literal `height:` that can clip scaled text. · A widget test pumped at TextScaler.linear(1.3)+ and Locale('he') asserts no RenderFlex overflow and no truncated semantics label on these three banners. · The Exit/tap affordance in each banner measures >=48dp in its tappable dimension (verified via a hitTestable finder or explicit SizedBox/ConstrainedBox in the widget tree).
- **Labels:** accessibility, hotspot, rtl · verifier corrections: The '20-24dp' tap-target estimate is slightly generous; closer computation gives ~18-20dp for the _ChildViewBanner/TutorModeIndicatorBar Exit buttons — still well short of 48dp, so the conclusion is unaffected.

#### AUD-app-02 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Stop showing raw e.toString() as the device-restore error message in RestoreStatus/DeviceRestoreService
- **Rule:** EH-5 / AX-2 (no pre-formatted human messages; ARB-only user text) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** RestoreStatus.error(message: String) is a raw String, not a code/enum, and DeviceRestoreService feeds it e.toString() directly — a raw exception message (e.g. 'Exception: Data pull failed: [firebase_firestore/unavailable] ...'). device_restore_screen.dart renders this string verbatim next to a properly-localized l10n.deviceRestoreFailed headline (lines 214-222), so any restore failure — plausible on flaky mobile networks, which this cloud-restore flow specifically targets — shows raw, untranslated, technical English text to Hebrew-locale users today, live, with no masking guard. Separately, RestoreStatus.restoring's `phase` field is a hardcoded English sentence matched by string equality in _localizePhase(); the two files' string literals must stay in lockstep by convention only — if either drifts, the fallback silently renders the raw English phase instead of erroring.

- **Rule:** no_color_literal_outside_theme (custom_lint, currently non-functional) / Fowler (duplicated knowledge) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 9 · **Verified:** [2x2]

Worse, the SAME hex value (0xFFF1F3FA, 'opaque pale blue') is hand-copied in both files as an unrelated local constant rather than a shared AppTheme token, and 0xFF0038A8 is a bespoke blue never defined in AppTheme at all (AppTheme.brandBlueDeep is a different value, 0xFF3F41AB). The file's own comments document this exact bar going through TWO rounds of contrast bugs ('Bug 7' and 'Bug 7 (re-fix)') — duplicated, untracked magic colors are precisely what makes a third recurrence likely, since a future contrast fix to one copy can silently miss the other.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/app/router/app_shell.dart:25` — “const _tutorAccentColor = Color(0xFFD97706); // Amber-600”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/router/app_shell.dart:367` — “color: selected ? const Color(0xFF0038A8) : Colors.transparent,”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/router/app_shell.dart:436` — “const barBackground = Color(0xFFF1F3FA); // opaque pale blue”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/router/app_shell.dart:437` — “const barBorder = Color(0xFFD7DEF0);”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/router/persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart:157` — “color: const Color(0xFFF1F3FA),”
- **Fix:** Move _tutorAccentColor, _childViewAccentColor, barBackground/barBorder, and the nav-item selected-color into AppTheme/AppColors named constants; have persistent_switcher_scaffold.dart reference the same constant app_shell.dart uses.

#### AUD-app-06 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Log the swallowed exceptions in firebase_bootstrap.dart's two comment-only catch blocks (lines 39-41, 50-52) — invisible to the Makefile's single-line-only empty-catch grep
- **Rule:** EH-3 (log-less catch) + Rule-0 checker gap · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Both catch blocks have a comment as their only content — no rethrow, no state conversion, no AppLogger call — so they satisfy none of EH-3's three disjuncts ('rethrows, converts, or logs'). This is not merely a Pending-tier gap: the project's own 'Enforced' check for exactly this class of bug (Makefile [9/12], NFR23, 'empty catch blocks catch (_) {}') only matches the single-line literal pattern `catch\s*(_)\s*{}`; running it against this file confirms zero hits despite two genuinely empty-bodied (comment-only) catches spanning multiple lines. The App Check catch (39-41) is the more consequential of the two: the surrounding comment documents a known real failure mode ('FirebearStorageCryptoHelper decryption failures... cause activate() to hang indefinitely') that the timeout specifically guards against, yet if it fires there is zero log trace — this is the same class of App-Check/permission-denied failure this team has separately had to debug via manual token inspection. The outer catch (50-52) swallows a bare (untyped) exception from Firebase.initializeApp() itself with equally zero trace, so a total Firebase-subsystem failure in the field (no sync, no crash reporting, no analytics) would leave no diagnostic breadcrumb anywhere.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/app/bootstrap/firebase_bootstrap.dart:39` — “} catch (_) {
      // App Check unavailable — continue; sync may be rejected if enforced.”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/bootstrap/firebase_bootstrap.dart:50` — “} catch (_) {
    // Firebase init failed — app continues in local-first mode.”; `Makefile:176` — “HITS=$$(grep -rn 'catch\s*(_)\s*{}' "$$LIB/" \”
- **Fix:** Change both `catch (_) { /* comment */ }` blocks to `catch (e, stack) { AppLogger.instance.warning(event: '...', exception: e, stackTrace: stack); }` (AppLogger.instance is safe to call here even though AppLogger.init() hasn't run yet — crashlytics_bootstrap.dart already relies on the same lazy-singleton behavior). Separately, broaden the Makefile NFR23 grep so it is not blind to multi-line comment-only catch bodies.
- **Done when:** Both catch blocks in firebase_bootstrap.dart (App Check activation, Firebase.initializeApp) capture the exception/stack and call AppLogger.instance.{warning|error} with a distinct event name. · Makefile check [9/12] (NFR23) is extended to also flag catch blocks whose body contains only comments/whitespace, not just literal `catch (_) {}`; re-running it against firebase_bootstrap.dart now reports the two sites instead of 0 hits. · A regression test forces FirebaseAppCheck.instance.activate (or Firebase.initializeApp) to throw and asserts an AppLogger/Talker history entry is recorded.
- **Labels:** error-handling, logging, rule-0-gap, bootstrap, app-check · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches · verifier corrections: The recommended fix (AppLogger.instance.warning inside the catch) runs before bootstrap()'s AppLogger.init() on the next line; init() replaces _talkerInstance, discarding pre-init history, so in release builds that logge

#### AUD-app-07 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Thread AppLogger into database_provider.dart's SeedManager construction — bootstrapSeedDb's logger wiring is dead code and SeedManager's diagnostics are silent in production
- **Rule:** Fowler-duplication (dead code) / EH-3 (diagnostic loss) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Repo-wide grep for `bootstrapSeedDb` finds only its own definition — bootstrap.dart no longer calls it (a prior commit, 6fff5af9, deliberately removed the awaited call to fix cold-start latency, deferring seeding into contentDbPathProvider). The provider that now does the real work (database_provider.dart:51-56) re-implements the SeedManager call but constructs it with `SeedManager(dbDirectory: docsDir.path)` — no `logger:` argument. SeedManager's `_logger` field is `AppLogger?` (nullable) and every one of its ~13 internal diagnostic calls is null-safe-guarded (`_logger?.info(...)`, `_logger?.warning(...)`, `_logger?.error(...)`) at lines covering interrupted-upgrade detection, first-launch extraction, extraction failures, upgrade failures, .bak rollback, and corruption recovery. Because `_logger` is null on the only construction path that runs in a real app, every one of those calls is a silent no-op today. SeedManager's own doc explicitly anticipates 'version-driven upgrades, .bak rollback, and corruption recovery' as real scenarios, and AppLogger's own doc states its ring buffer exists precisely so 'Send Diagnostic Logs' in Settings can capture failures like this — but if content-DB extraction or corruption-recovery ever misbehaves for a real user, there will be zero trace of it anywhere the team can retrieve.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/app/bootstrap/seed_bootstrap.dart:14` — “final seedManager = SeedManager(dbDirectory: dbDirectory, logger: log);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/providers/database_provider.dart:54` — “final seedManager = SeedManager(dbDirectory: docsDir.path);
  return seedManager.ensureContentDb();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/seed_manager.dart:69` — “final AppLogger? _logger;”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/seed_manager.dart:241` — “_logger?.error(event: 'seed_manager_extract_failed', exception: e);”
- **Fix:** Pass `logger: AppLogger.instance` in database_provider.dart's `SeedManager(dbDirectory: docsDir.path)` call — keep seeding lazily deferred inside the provider (do not reintroduce an awaited bootstrapSeedDb() call in bootstrap.dart; that would regress the cold-start fix in 6fff5af9). Then delete lib/app/bootstrap/seed_bootstrap.dart, since its only remaining purpose — threading a logger into SeedManager — is met at the real call site and the function itself is unreachable.
- **Done when:** database_provider.dart's contentDbPath provider constructs SeedManager with a non-null logger. · A regression test forces SeedManager.ensureContentDb() to throw inside contentDbPathProvider (e.g. corrupt/missing seed asset fixture) and asserts a Talker/AppLogger history entry with an event like 'seed_manager_extract_failed' is recorded — proving the logger is wired, not just constructed. · Rule-0: grep-based `make audit` check that every `SeedManager(` construction site outside test/ passes a `logger:` argument. · lib/app/bootstrap/seed_bootstrap.dart is removed once its logic is folded into the real call site.
- **Labels:** bootstrap, dead-code, logging, seed-db, observability

#### AUD-app-08 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Close the DeviceRegistryDatabase connection on account_bootstrap.dart's exception path
- **Rule:** Nygard (I/O failure handling) / resource cleanup · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** `registry.close()` sits at the end of the try block, not in a finally. If sessionService.resolveActiveAccountId() (line 30) or registry.findById() (line 33) throws, execution jumps straight to the outer catch (line 51), which logs and returns a fallback filename WITHOUT ever closing the Drift-backed device_registry connection — the exact 'I/O fails halfway' scenario the Nygard lens asks about. Impact is low in practice (this runs once per app process at startup), but a leaked native database handle held for the app's whole lifetime is still an avoidable defect, and it would compound if this code path were ever retried (e.g. a future hot-reattempt) or re-used in a longer-lived context.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/app/bootstrap/account_bootstrap.dart:23` — “final registry = DeviceRegistryDatabase(
  driftDatabase(name: 'device_registry'),
);”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/bootstrap/account_bootstrap.dart:49` — “await registry.close();”; `learning_tracker/lib/app/bootstrap/account_bootstrap.dart:51` — “} catch (e, stack) {”
- **Fix:** Move `final registry = ...` construction above a try/finally (or wrap the resolveActiveAccountId/findById calls in try{...}finally{ await registry.close(); }) so every exit path closes the connection.
- **Done when:** registry.close() executes on both the success path and any exception path out of bootstrapAccount. · A unit test makes sessionService.resolveActiveAccountId() throw and asserts the registry/executor was still closed.
- **Labels:** resource-leak, hygiene, bootstrap

#### AUD-t-account-02 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Replace sign_in_context_reset_test.dart's source-text-matching 'wiring' assertions with real call-chain verification
- **Rule:** TQ-1/TQ-8 methodology (Feathers seam) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [1x1]

This proves the token exists in the file — including inside a comment, a dead branch, or an `if (false)` — not that the reset actually runs during a real sign-in. A refactor that renames a local variable, extracts the same call into a helper, or reorders it outside the funnel would either false-fail (token literally moved) or false-pass (token still present but now unreachable) without any real Riverpod/router state ever being observed. The file's own 'runtime semantics' group shows the better pattern is available (it drives the real PinGuard/activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider primitives directly) — it just never chains them through an actual signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle call.

#### AUD-t-account-05 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Move sign-in/account-picker test cleanup into addTearDown so a failed assertion doesn't leak the ProviderContainer/Drift DB
- **Rule:** TQ-2 (fresh, reliably-torn-down ProviderContainer per test) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Both files call their cleanup helper (_tearDown / _tearDownContainer + registry.close()) as the last statement inside each test body, after several `expect()` calls. If any expect() throws (the exact moment a real regression would be caught), cleanup is skipped and the in-memory Drift registry/userDb connections and ProviderContainer leak for the rest of the suite run — the opposite of TQ-2's 'never share state between tests' guarantee, and the failure that most needs a clean teardown is the one that gets skipped. Sibling files in this exact batch (account_picker_local_data_missing_test.dart's tearDown(), and the notifier tests' addTearDown(container.dispose)) show the correct, already-established pattern.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_picker_screen_l1_test.dart:251` — “Future<void> _tearDown(WidgetTester tester, _Fixture fixture) async {”; `learning_tracker/test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_picker_screen_l1_test.dart:312` — “await _tearDown(tester, fixture);”; `learning_tracker/test/features/account/presentation/notifiers/sign_in_wrong_password_no_callback_test.dart:161` — “Future<void> _tearDownContainer(
  WidgetTester tester,”; `learning_tracker/test/features/account/presentation/notifiers/sign_in_wrong_password_no_callback_test.dart:272` — “await _tearDownContainer(tester, container);
        await registry.close();”
- **Fix:** Replace the manual end-of-test _tearDown/_tearDownContainer calls with addTearDown(...) registered immediately after the container/registry/userDb are created, matching account_picker_local_data_missing_test.dart's tearDown() in this same batch.
- **Done when:** Cleanup (container dispose, registry.close(), userDb.close()) is registered via addTearDown/tearDown() immediately after creation, not as the final statement of the test body. · A deliberately-failing expect() inserted mid-test still leaves the Drift databases closed.
- **Labels:** tq-2, test-hygiene, resource-leak

- **Fix:** Remove both `skip:` parameters. - **Rule:** FB-5 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 7 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** pushCompletionsBatch chunks at _writeBatchLimit=500 and, per the documented H3 fix, must report only the entityKeys of chunks that actually committed when a later chunk throws, so OutboxProcessor deletes exactly the landed rows and retries the rest. Group 5's largest test pushes only 10 items — never crosses a chunk boundary — and group 15's 'SyncPushException partial-commit reporting' test just constructs a SyncPushException object directly and checks its own constructor round-trips fields; it never calls pushCompletionsBatch at all. A regression in the chunk loop (e.g. moving pushed.addAll before batch.commit(), or an off-by-one in the start/end clamp) would re-push or silently drop already-committed outbox rows and this suite would not notice.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl_test.dart:954` — “items: List.generate(
            10,”; `learning_tracker/test/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl_test.dart:1978` — “final ex = SyncPushException(
        committed: ['key1', 'key2'],”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:273` — “// committed rows are never re-pushed or dead-lettered (H3).”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:461` — “final batch = _firestore.batch();

      throw Exception('Firestore supports at most 500 tasks in a batch');”
- **Fix:** Add a test that pushes >500 items where a wrapped/stubbed Firestore batch throws on the second chunk, and assert pushCompletionsBatch throws SyncPushException with committed containing exactly chunk 1's entityKeys and none of chunk 2's.
- **Done when:** New test drives >500 items through the real pushCompletionsBatch code path (not a hand-constructed exception) with an injected failure on chunk 2 and asserts SyncPushException.committed equals exactly chunk 1's keys · Test fails red if the chunk loop's addAll/commit ordering is swapped

#### AUD-t-cross-08 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Close or auto-close inMemoryDb() in profiles _buildApp test helpers — 3 files leak native Drift handles whenever db: is omitted
- **Rule:** TQ-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 15 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** drift_memory.dart's own contract says callers MUST close inMemoryDb(). In these 3 files, _buildApp (and _buildAppLoading/_buildAppError, which have no db: parameter at all) construct one via `db ?? inMemoryDb()` whenever the optional db: is omitted, and the large majority of testWidgets in parent_settings_screen_l1_test.dart and parent_track_management_screen_l1_test.dart (~30 of ~40 across the two files) do omit it, so each test run leaks a native sqlite3 in-memory connection nothing ever closes — the caller has no reference to the db, so it can't be closed even in a teardown. At the scale of this test suite (dozens of files following the same pattern), this is a plausible contributor to CI slowness or file-descriptor/memory pressure.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/helpers/drift_memory.dart:40` — “/// Callers MUST `await db.close()` in `tearDown` to free the native
/// resources.”; `learning_tracker/test/features/profiles/presentation/screens/parent_settings_screen_l1_test.dart:114` — “final resolvedDb = db ?? inMemoryDb();”; `learning_tracker/test/features/profiles/presentation/screens/parent_track_management_screen_l1_test.dart:129` — “final database = db ?? inMemoryDb();”; `learning_tracker/test/features/profiles/presentation/screens/parent_track_management_screen_l1_test.dart:167` — “final database = inMemoryDb();”; `learning_tracker/test/features/profiles/presentation/screens/ts14_parent_track_management_copy_test.dart:71` — “final database = db ?? inMemoryDb();”; `learning_tracker/test/features/tracks_studydays_and_content_hierarchy_l1_test.dart:142` — “userDatabaseProvider.overrideWith((ref) => inMemoryDb()),”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/providers/database_provider.dart:37` — “final database = UserDatabase(driftDatabase(name: dbName));
  ref.onDispose(database.close);”; `learning_tracker/test/helpers/drift_memory.dart:36` — “/// Callers MUST `await db.close()` in `tearDown` to free the native” _(+7 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Make db a required parameter (as ts3_parent_track_archive_test.dart already does correctly, forcing every call site to own+close it), or have _buildApp itself call addTearDown(() => resolvedDb.close()) so omitting db: is automatically safe.
- **Done when:** Every _buildApp/_buildAppLoading/_buildAppError variant in these 3 files either requires db: or internally registers addTearDown to close the database it created.
- **Labels:** resource-leak, test-quality, drift, profiles · merged 3 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 4 batches

#### AUD-t-cross-09 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Cover reminderSyncEffect's D1/D2 guards with a real ProviderContainer test instead of overdue_notifications_test.dart's hand-duplicated logic
- **Rule:** TQ-8 (tautological/re-derived test) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** None of O8-a..d builds a ProviderContainer or overrides allDailyTasksProvider to invoke the actual reminderSyncEffect provider, contradicting the file's own docstring claim. O8-b calls scheduler.cancel() directly rather than exercising the 'if (taskCount == 0)' guard in production; O8-d hand-retypes the today-only filter instead of calling it. #### AUD-t-cross-36 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Replace fixed-millisecond delay polling with emitsInOrder stream matchers in points_balance_dao_test.dart watchBalance tests
- **Rule:** TQ-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The two watchBalance tests collect stream emissions into a list via `.listen(emissions.add)` then assert on `emissions.last` after fixed 20ms/50ms sleeps. Under CI contention (parallel shards, a throttled runner) the reactive Drift query stream may not have emitted the post-write value before the sleep expires, producing an intermittent failure on `expect(emissions.last, 50)` that has nothing to do with a real regression — the classic flaky-test pattern that gets 'fixed' by rerunning rather than investigated. profile_dao_test.dart in this same batch (watchProfilesByAccount test) shows the deterministic alternative already in use elsewhere: `expect(stream, emitsInOrder([...]))`, which waits for the actual emission instead of racing a clock.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/core/database/daos/points_balance_dao_test.dart:90` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 20));”; `learning_tracker/test/core/database/daos/points_balance_dao_test.dart:100` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));”; `learning_tracker/test/core/database/daos/points_balance_dao_test.dart:113` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));”; `learning_tracker/test/core/database/daos/points_balance_dao_test.dart:140` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 20));”; `learning_tracker/test/core/database/daos/points_balance_dao_test.dart:146` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));”
- **Fix:** Rewrite both watchBalance tests to assert via `expect(db.pointsBalanceDao.watchBalance(1), emitsInOrder([0, 50, ...]))` (or expectLater) registered before the mutating calls, matching the pattern already used by profile_dao_test.dart's watchProfilesByAccount test, instead of manually collecting emissions behind a fixed sleep.
- **Done when:** Both watchBalance tests in points_balance_dao_test.dart use emitsInOrder/expectLater with no fixed-millisecond Future.delayed used purely to wait for a stream emission · Tests pass repeatedly under both default and constrained (--concurrency=1, or CI-like throttled) runs · Rule-0 checker: grep test/**/*_test.dart for `Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds` occurring in the same test body as a preceding `.listen(` call

#### AUD-t-cross-41 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Rewrite ConnectivityGateway's only test — it is tautologically true and hits the real network
- **Rule:** TQ-6 (hermetic tests: no network) + TQ-8 (assertion weaker than what the source can do wrong) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** isOffline is defined as the literal negation of isOnline, so expect(online, isNot(offline)) reduces to 'online == online' — true for every possible return value, including if isOnline were hardcoded to `return true;`. The test can never catch a regression in the actual DNS-lookup logic. Because ConnectivityGateway has no injectable seam for the lookup, the test cannot fake a response either way and instead performs a live DNS query to dns.google on every run — flaky/slow/blocked in network-restricted CI or sandboxes, and this is the class's only test.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/core/network/connectivity_service_test.dart:14` — “expect(online, isNot(offline));”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/network/connectivity_gateway.dart:26` — “Future<bool> get isOffline async => !(await isOnline);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/network/connectivity_gateway.dart:14` — “final result = await InternetAddress.lookup(
        'dns.google',”
- **Fix:** Add an injectable lookup function (e.g. `Future<List<InternetAddress>> Function(String)`, defaulting to InternetAddress.lookup) to ConnectivityGateway, then test both the true and false paths via a fake with zero real network access.
- **Done when:** test asserts isOnline == true for a faked successful lookup and == false for a faked SocketException/timeout · test suite passes with network access disabled · renamed to connectivity_gateway_test.dart (see naming finding)
- **Labels:** testing, hermeticity, tautological-test

#### AUD-t-cross-44 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Stop using app_localizations_coverage_test.dart's 1482 zero-assertion lines to pad the CI coverage floor over generated l10n code
- **Rule:** TQ-8 / Rule 0 (coverage floor's stated generated-file exclusion is unenforced) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** grep -c 'expect(' on the file returns 0 — in 1482 lines, nothing can ever fail except a compile error (e.g. a renamed getter), which would abort the whole file rather than flag the specific key. The file's own docstring admits its purpose is purely to drive line-execution through lib/l10n/app_localizations_en.dart and _he.dart (5100+ generated lines each) for the CI-enforced coverage floor. docs/coding-standards.md states the 60% line-coverage floor is measured with 'generated files excluded', but .github/workflows/ci.yml's coverage-floor step runs `lcov --summary` directly on the raw lcov.info with no `lcov --remove` step anywhere in the repo (verified: no lcov --remove/genhtml exclude pattern exists in Makefile or ci.yml) — so generated files are NOT excluded in practice, and this file's 725-getter roll call launders thousands of auto-generated, logic-free lines into the numerator that the doc claims shouldn't count. Concrete cost: every new l10n key needs a manual line added here (already 725, and easy to forget silently since forgetting produces no failure), for a test that cannot catch a wrong translation, a missing plural case, or the exact ARB duplicate-key bug found elsewhere in this batch.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/l10n/app_localizations_coverage_test.dart:3` — “return paths. No assertion is made on the text — the goal is line coverage of the generated translation strings.”; `learning_tracker/.github/workflows/ci.yml:256` — “SUMMARY=$(lcov --summary "$LCOV_FILE" 2>&1)”
- **Fix:** Either (a) wire the promised exclusion into the CI coverage step (lcov --remove coverage/lcov.info 'lib/l10n/app_localizations_*.dart' '*.g.dart' ... before lcov --summary) and delete this file, or (b) if kept for its doc-verification role, replace the per-getter roll call with a real check (e.g. that every ARB key has a corresponding generated getter) instead of 1482 lines that assert nothing.
- **Done when:** CI's coverage-floor step excludes generated files from the denominator (matching the doc's claim) OR this file is deleted/replaced with an assertive test. · docs/coding-standards.md's 'generated files excluded' claim matches what .github/workflows/ci.yml actually does.
- **Labels:** testing, coverage-gaming, ci · verifier corrections: Second evidence entry's file path 'learning_tracker/.github/workflows/ci.yml' is wrong — the file is at repo-root '.github/workflows/ci.yml' (no learning_tracker/ prefix). Content and line 256 quote are otherwise verifie

#### AUD-t-cross-47 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · infrastructure_test.dart's 'database is isolated between tests' only proves two objects aren't identical(), not that data is isolated
- **Rule:** TQ-8 (assertions weaker than what the source under test can actually do wrong) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** createTestDatabase() is a plain constructor call with no caching, so identical(db1, db2) is guaranteed false for any two invocations regardless of whether UserDatabase has any shared/static state that leaks data between instances — the assertion cannot fail even if isolation were genuinely broken. Running this test (`flutter test test/infrastructure_test.dart`) confirms it passes today, and also prints a real Drift runtime warning at exactly this test's stack frame: 'It looks like you've created the database class UserDatabase multiple times... race conditions will occur and might corrupt the database' (createTestDatabase at test_database.dart:13, called from infrastructure_test.dart:134). Twenty-plus other test files in this repo (app_shell_test.dart, e2e_harness.dart, the sync/merge/* roundtrip suite) already know about this and explicitly set `driftRuntimeOptions.dontWarnAboutMultipleDatabases = true` when intentionally creating multiple in-memory DBs — this test does not follow that established convention, so it emits unnecessary warning noise on every run on top of not checking the property its name promises. A real cross-instance state leak (e.g. an accidental static/singleton in UserDatabase) would sail through this test undetected.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/infrastructure_test.dart:132` — “test('database is isolated between tests', () async {”; `learning_tracker/test/infrastructure_test.dart:137` — “expect(identical(db1, db2), false);”; `learning_tracker/test/infrastructure_test.dart:22` — “final mockAuthRepo = MockAuthRepository();
        expect(mockAuthRepo, isNotNull);”; `learning_tracker/test/infrastructure_test.dart:44` — “expect(mishna.curriculumId, CurriculumId.mishnayos.storageKey);”; `learning_tracker/test/fixtures/content_fixtures.dart:24` — “curriculumId ?? CurriculumId.mishnayos.storageKey,”
- **Fix:** Replace the identical() check with a real isolation assertion: insert a row into db1 (e.g. via seedProfile) and assert it is absent when querying db2, or that db2's relevant table starts empty. Also set driftRuntimeOptions.dontWarnAboutMultipleDatabases = true here to match the repo's established pattern for intentional multi-instance in-memory DBs.
- **Done when:** The test inserts data into db1 and asserts it is not visible from db2 (or vice versa), not just that the two references are non-identical. · Running the test no longer prints the Drift multiple-database-instantiation warning.
- **Labels:** test-quality, tq-8, tautological-test, empirically-verified · merged 1 duplicate report(s)

#### AUD-t-cross-51 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · test/helpers/golden_runner.dart and flutter_test_config.dart produce no usable golden-regression coverage — no fonts loaded, and every caller skips the pixel assertion
- **Rule:** TQ-5 (goldens deterministic — fonts loaded in flutter_test_config.dart) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** flutter_test_config.dart runs before every test file but never calls FontLoader/loadAppFonts — it only disables GoogleFonts network fetching. I built a throwaway probe (`goldenTest('probe', builder: (l) => const Text('Probe'))`) and ran `flutter test ... --update-goldens`: the captured PNG was 100% blank white — no glyphs at all. A second probe (`Container(color: red, child: Text(...))`) rendered the red container at full size (proving layout/paint itself works) but the text area was a solid opaque black smear, never legible characters. For comparison, test/golden/goldens/phone_1_dashboard.png (built by the separate store_screenshots_test.dart, which does call FontLoader itself) renders crisp real glyphs in the same sandbox — proving the blankness is caused by golden_runner.dart's missing font load, not an environment limitation. Because of this (or in anticipation of it), every one of the 11 current goldenTest() call sites across test/story_acceptance/ passes skipGolden: true, so matchesGoldenFile never actually executes anywhere today. The RTL/LTR visual-regression protection this helper's own doc comment claims to provide ('UI bugs that only manifest in RTL Hebrew layouts... cost the team a release window in E18') is not happening — if anyone flips skipGolden to false today to 'baseline' goldens per the tracked follow-up (DNI-380), they will commit blank/illegible PNGs as the accepted baseline without any test failure to warn them.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/flutter_test_config.dart:13` — “GoogleFonts.config.allowRuntimeFetching = false;”; `learning_tracker/test/helpers/golden_runner.dart:53` — “matchesGoldenFile('goldens/$name.${locale.languageCode}.png'),”; `docs/coding-standards.md:472` — “Goldens are deterministic (fonts loaded in `flutter_test_config.dart`; pinned size/theme/locale; fixed clock; constant data)”
- **Fix:** Add explicit font loading to flutter_test_config.dart (FontLoader per family declared in pubspec's fonts: section, mirroring what store_screenshots_test.dart already does locally) before testMain() runs. Re-run the probe pattern above with skipGolden:false to confirm real glyphs render, then un-skip and baseline the goldens that are ready (per the DNI-380 tracked follow-up).
- **Done when:** A goldenTest() call with skipGolden:false and real text content produces a PNG with legible (non-blank, non-tofu-smear) glyphs, verified by re-running the probe pattern used in this audit. · flutter_test_config.dart contains a font-loading step covering every family declared in pubspec.yaml's fonts: section. · At least one of the 11 currently-skipped call sites is un-skipped and baselined, or a tracked ticket documents why it remains skipped beyond DNI-380's original scope.
- **Labels:** test-infra, golden-tests, tq-5, empirically-verified · verifier corrections: 10 goldenTest() call sites exist today, not 11 as claimed (3+1+6across three files) — minor miscount, doesn't affect the 'every site skips' claim, which holds for all 10.

- **Fix:** Override the clock with a FakeLocalDayClock in setUp/tearDown (matching the pattern already used in learner_profile_delete_enqueue_profile0_test.dart) and advance it between the two at-limit snapshots to assert both 'inside window → coalesced' and 'past window → retriggers'.

- **Labels:** testing, hygiene, clock-seam · verifier corrections: Minor: recommendation's 'matching the pattern in learner_profile_delete_enqueue_profile0_test.dart' is imprecise — that test injects a clock via constructor param, not the global useLocalDayClock seam ListenerSupervisor

#### AUD-t-cross-68 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Fix hand-rolled test _FakeMergeStore.remoteIsNewer implementations to match DriftMergeStore's clock-skew/D15 semantics

Neither test currently uses timestamps close enough to trigger the divergent branch, so the suite passes today, but any future near-tie/clock-skew test added against these fakes would silently validate the WRONG (pre-D15) behavior, hiding exactly the bug class DriftMergeStoreTest exists to pin down.

- **Fix:** Replace both hand-rolled remoteIsNewer bodies with a delegate to the real DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer (construct a throwaway DriftMergeStore over an in-memory DB inside the fake, or extract the pure comparison so both share one implementation) instead of re-deriving the algorithm by hand.
- **Done when:** A within-skew-window / no-syncedAt / older-remote test case added to either file fails before the fix and passes after, or the fake is proven identical to DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer by delegation (making such drift structurally impossible).
- **Labels:** testing, test-fidelity, TQ-4

- **Rule:** TQ-6 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 6 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** read()/watch() call StreakReducer.reduce() without pinning the injectable `dayOf` seam that streak_reducer.dart's own doc comment says exists precisely 'so tests can pin a fixed UTC offset deterministically without depending on the host machine's timezone.' - **Fix:** Either give StreakStateProvider.read/watch an explicit dayOf override (mirroring the reducer's own seam) or have the test suite pin TZ=UTC explicitly (Makefile/CI env var) so pass/fail can't depend on the runner's locale.
- **Done when:** `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati flutter test test/core/streak/streak_state_provider_test.dart` and the default-TZ run both stay green by construction (pinned dayOf or pinned TZ), not by coincidence of current fixture values.

#### AUD-t-cross-81 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Remove flutter_test_config.dart's FlutterError.onError GoogleFonts filter — TestWidgetsFlutterBinding never lets it run during a test
- **Rule:** Test-infra correctness (no direct coding-standards rule ID) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The comment above this block claims it suppresses 'residual font not found errors... cosmetic rendering issues, not test logic failures' during test execution. I traced the installed Flutter SDK (3.44.1, matching this repo's `flutter --version`): TestWidgetsFlutterBinding._runTest() (binding.dart:1770) saves whatever handler is currently installed into _oldExceptionHandler, then unconditionally overwrites FlutterError.onError with its own handler that just does `_pendingExceptionDetails = details` — it never calls the previously-installed handler. postTest() (binding.dart:2131-2134) restores _oldExceptionHandler only after the test body has finished. Since _runTest() wraps every individual test()/testWidgets() body, the custom GoogleFonts-substring filter installed in flutter_test_config.dart is captured as 'the old handler' before the first test and is never invoked while any test is actually running — exactly the window in which a font-not-found FlutterError would fire. If such an error does occur during a pump, it is captured into _pendingExceptionDetails and fails the test outright, contradicting the file's own comment about what it does.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/flutter_test_config.dart:18` — “FlutterError.onError = (details) {”; `/home/daniel/flutter/packages/flutter_test/lib/src/binding.dart:1773` — “FlutterError.onError = (FlutterErrorDetails details) {”
- **Fix:** Delete the dead FlutterError.onError override (lines 17-22), or replace it with a mechanism proven to run mid-test (e.g. wrap only the specific pump inside affected tests, or fix the font-loading gap in finding 'golden_runner.dart never renders real glyphs' so the underlying error stops occurring). Do not rely on a global onError swap in this file for anything that needs to suppress errors during pumpWidget/pumpAndSettle.
- **Done when:** A widget test that deliberately throws/renders a FlutterError whose message contains 'GoogleFonts' mid-pump either fails (proving the current filter does nothing) or is demonstrated to pass only via a mechanism that actually executes during _runTest's window. · The doc comment above the handler is removed or corrected to match what the code can actually do.
- **Labels:** test-infra, dead-code, misleading-comment, sdk-traced

#### AUD-t-cross-97 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Use `is TalkerDioLogger` instead of a runtimeType.toString() string match in dio_client_test.dart
- **Rule:** Feathers/hygiene — type-safe test assertions · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** Comparing runtimeType.toString() to a string literal bypasses the type system: a rename or a subclass would silently break or falsely pass this check with a confusing failure message, where `is TalkerDioLogger` (talker_dio_logger is already a transitive dependency of tool/lib/dio_client.dart) is both safer and clearer.

- **Done when:** Test uses an `is` type check, no runtimeType.toString() comparison remains, test still passes
- **Labels:** test-quality, hygiene · verifier corrections: talker_dio_logger is a direct (non-dev) pubspec dependency, not merely transitive as the finding states — makes the fix even easier, doesn't weaken the finding. | Finding calls talker_dio_logger a 'transitive dependency'

#### AUD-t-cross-99 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Use the existing useLocalDayClock seam instead of DateTime.now() in sync_orchestrator_test.dart resume-throttle tests
- **Rule:** TQ-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]

#### AUD-t-dashboard-02 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · dashboard_todays_missions_heading_test.dart: override trackHasChazaraProvider so ActiveTrackCard stops opening a real UserDatabase
- **Rule:** TQ-6 (hermetic tests: no real DB/network) / TQ-2 (fresh, controlled container) / Feathers seam lens · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]

Confirmed by execution: running this file prints drift's own runtime warning 'WARNING (drift): It looks like you've created the database class UserDatabase multiple times... race conditions will occur and might corrupt the database' twice (once per extra testWidgets in the file), with a stack trace tracing straight through ActiveTrackCard.build -> trackHasChazaraProvider -> userDatabase -> UserDatabase(driftDatabase(...)). The 'widget' test is therefore not hermetic: it opens 3 real native Drift databases per run, the chazara-badge branch in ActiveTrackCard is exercised against whatever that ambient real DB happens to return for stageDao.countStagesForTrack(1) rather than the _track() fixture (so this test asserts nothing about, and cannot regress-guard, that branch), and it is measurably slower and flakier than the fake/in-memory pattern (test/helpers/test_database.dart) used elsewhere in the suite.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/dashboard_todays_missions_heading_test.dart:116` — “anyActiveTrackHasChazaraProvider.overrideWith(

),”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/active_track_card.dart:322` — “.watch(trackHasChazaraProvider(track.id))”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/providers/dashboard_providers.dart:521` — “final db = ref.watch(userDatabaseProvider);
  final count = await db.stageDao.countStagesForTrack(trackId);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/providers/database_provider.dart:36` — “final database = UserDatabase(driftDatabase(name: dbName));”
- **Fix:** Add `trackHasChazaraProvider(1).overrideWith((ref) => Future.value(false))` (mirroring the existing anyActiveTrackHasChazaraProvider override) to _buildApp's overrides list, or override userDatabaseProvider directly with the shared in-memory test database helper.
- **Done when:** trackHasChazaraProvider(1) (or userDatabaseProvider) is overridden in _buildApp's overrides list. · `flutter test test/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/dashboard_todays_missions_heading_test.dart` produces zero 'WARNING (drift): ... created the database class UserDatabase multiple times' output.

#### AUD-t-dashboard-03 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · dashboard_todays_missions_heading_test.dart: remove the blind exception-drain loop in pumpAt (proven dead, masks any real regression in the pumped tree)
- **Rule:** TQ-7 (never weaken/bypass assertions without a stated, scoped justification) / Fowler stale-comment smell · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The loop unconditionally drains and discards ANY exception raised anywhere in the pumped DashboardBody tree, not just the specific MainFocusMissionCard overflow the adjoining comment names -- there is no type/message check. Verified by direct execution: (1) with the code as shipped, a print-probe substituted for the loop shows the pending exception is null for all 3 testWidgets in this file at its own matrix (412x915, en/he, scale 1.0/1.3) -- there is nothing to drain today; (2) after temporarily reverting main_focus_mission_card.dart's FittedBox fix back to the exact pre-fix plain Row (commit 2c62ff2c, reverted then git-restored), rerunning this file UNMODIFIED still reports 'All tests passed' with zero exceptions surfacing -- so the comment's stated justification does not reproduce under this test's own conditions either. The loop is therefore proven, executable dead code whose only live effect is to silently swallow any *actual future* exception (a provider throwing, a genuine new overflow) raised by any widget in this subtree during these three pumps, without ever failing the test.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/dashboard_todays_missions_heading_test.dart:198` — “// an unrelated sibling card (MainFocusMissionCard's "Start learning"

    while (pending != null) {”
- **Fix:** Delete the unconditional while-loop. If some exception genuinely needs tolerating, capture it once via a single tester.takeException() and assert its type/message matches a specifically named, filed issue (with a // weaken-ok:-style comment and Linear id) instead of draining blind.

### tests/gamification  (9 findings — 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 3 P2 / 6 P3)

#### AUD-t-gamification-01 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Replace wall-clock Future.delayed synchronization with deterministic waits in gamification staleness tests
- **Rule:** TQ-6 (hermetic tests: no wall-clock) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 7 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** 7 sites across 2 files (curriculum_breakdown_staleness_test.dart:66; points_providers_reactive_test.dart:61,68,100,111,154,164) synchronize on a Riverpod stream/FutureProvider re-emission by sleeping a fixed real-world duration instead of awaiting the actual event — the same feature area's achievements_overview_staleness_after_redemption_test.dart shows the deterministic alternative already in use (container.invalidate(...) + await container.read(provider.future)). A fixed delay is a flaky-under-CI-load bet: too short and a legitimately-fixed provider that happens to take longer intermittently fails the test; the tests exist specifically to pin reactive-update timing, so racing against the clock to verify timing is a contradiction in terms.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/gamification/presentation/providers/curriculum_breakdown_staleness_test.dart:66` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));”; `learning_tracker/test/features/gamification/presentation/providers/points_providers_reactive_test.dart:61` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 20));”; `learning_tracker/test/features/gamification/presentation/providers/points_providers_reactive_test.dart:68` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));”
- **Fix:** Await the stream's next matching emission via a Completer or StreamQueue keyed on the expected value (or pumpEventQueue() for Drift's microtask-driven watch streams) instead of a fixed delay.
- **Done when:** Zero `Future<void>.delayed` calls remain in curriculum_breakdown_staleness_test.dart and points_providers_reactive_test.dart. · Both files pass 20 consecutive runs under --test-randomize-ordering-seed=random without flake.
- **Labels:** flaky-test, hermeticity, riverpod

These 7 factory call sites (used by ~1041+709+9+3 individual test invocations respectively) never do, so every test run leaves a live FFI-backed sqlite3 in-memory connection open until the file's isolate exits. 6 other files in this same batch (child_redemption_balance_reactive_test.dart, child_redemption_rewards_staleness_test.dart, pending_redemptions_reactive_test.dart, parent_pending_redemptions_screen_l1_test.dart, r_ga2_...test.dart, and 7 of 9 sites in child_redemption_screen_l1_test.dart) follow the contract correctly, proving it's practical here and making the gap inconsistent rather than structural.

- **Fix:** Route each factory through addTearDown(db.close) (or the setUp/tearDown pattern parent_pending_redemptions_screen_l1_test.dart already uses correctly) so every inMemoryDb()/createTestUserDatabase() call in this feature is closed.
- **Done when:** grep-based Rule-0 checker: every `inMemoryDb()`/`createTestUserDatabase()` call site under test/ has a matching close() reachable from the same scope. · The 7 cited call sites each gain an addTearDown(..., .close) or equivalent.
- **Labels:** hygiene, test-quality, resource-leak

#### AUD-t-gamification-07 · **P3** · SUSPECTED · Replace fixed-duration Future.delayed sleeps with deterministic sync in gamification reactive-stream tests
- **Rule:** TQ-6 hermetic tests · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** These 3 files (10 occurrences total) use hard-coded 20/50/150ms real-time sleeps as the only synchronization before asserting a Drift Stream has propagated a new emission, with no retry/poll and no use of pumpEventQueue() (confirmed 0 usages repo-wide). On a loaded CI runner a slower-than-budgeted FFI round-trip would fail the assertion with no code regression involved — exactly the kind of flake that erodes trust in the 'staleness regression' suite meant to guard DG-RDMP-01/02 and DG-PND-05.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/gamification/presentation/screens/child_redemption_balance_reactive_test.dart:57` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 20));”; `learning_tracker/test/features/gamification/presentation/screens/child_redemption_rewards_staleness_test.dart:99` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 150));”; `learning_tracker/test/features/gamification/presentation/screens/pending_redemptions_reactive_test.dart:89` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 20));”
- **Fix:** Replace `Future.delayed(fixedDuration)` with `pumpEventQueue()` or a small poll-until-condition helper bounded by a generous timeout, so the wait tracks actual event-loop drain rather than a guessed duration.
- **Done when:** No test in these 3 files gates its only assertion on a bare Future.delayed(fixed duration); a poll/pumpEventQueue-based helper is used instead.
- **Labels:** flaky-test, test-quality

#### AUD-t-gamification-08 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Replace the wildcard `case _:` on the sealed AsyncValue switch in gamification_screen_l1_test.dart
- **Rule:** EH-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** AsyncValue is `sealed class AsyncValue<T>` with exactly 3 subtypes (AsyncData/AsyncLoading/AsyncError, verified in the riverpod package source). This switch handles AsyncData and AsyncError explicitly but falls back to a `case _:` wildcard for AsyncLoading instead of naming it. Per docs/coding-standards.md:197-199 (EH-6), a wildcard arm 'silently absorbs future variants and destroys' the compiler's exhaustiveness guarantee — here it also hides that the loading case is deliberately made to hang (Completer().future never completes) rather than being an oversight.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/gamification/presentation/screens/gamification_screen_l1_test.dart:143` — “case _:
            return Completer<AchievementsOverview>().future;”
- **Fix:** Change `case _:` to `case AsyncLoading():` so the switch is explicitly exhaustive.
- **Done when:** The switch in _buildApp's achievementsOverviewProvider override names AsyncLoading() explicitly instead of using a wildcard arm.
- **Labels:** hygiene, EH-6

#### AUD-t-notifications-01 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Override reminderSyncEffectProvider/streakAlertSyncEffectProvider in notifications_screen_test.dart and ws5_two_layers_test.dart to stop opening a real Drift database
- **Rule:** TQ-6 (hermetic tests, Pending) — novel violation · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** NotificationsScreen.build() unconditionally does `ref.watch(reminderSyncEffectProvider)` / `ref.watch(streakAlertSyncEffectProvider)` (both @Riverpod(keepAlive) FutureProviders that chain into notificationSchedulerProvider -> sacredWindowRepositoryProvider -> userDatabaseProvider, i.e. a real drift_flutter-backed UserDatabase opened via driftDatabase(name: 'learning_tracker')). Neither buildSubject() (notifications_screen_test.dart) nor _buildWithProviders() (ws5_two_layers_test.dart) overrides these two effects, unlike the newer notifications_screen_l1_test.dart which does so explicitly "to isolate the UI tests" (its own header comment). Actually running `flutter test test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_test.dart` reproduces Drift's own runtime warning verbatim: "It looks like you've created the database class UserDatabase multiple times. When these two databases use the same QueryExecutor, race conditions will occur and might corrupt the database" (fires because the file pumps a fresh ProviderScope 5 times against the same default DB name in one process). ws5_two_layers_test.dart pumps the same unguarded path once, so the warning doesn't fire there today, but the identical missing-override defect is present and would manifest the same way if a second pump were added.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_test.dart:29` — “return ProviderScope(
      overrides: [notificationServiceProvider.overrideWithValue(mockService)],”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/ws5_two_layers_test.dart:30` — “overrides: [
      if (gatewayOverride != null)”
- **Fix:** Add `reminderSyncEffectProvider.overrideWith((ref) async {})` and `streakAlertSyncEffectProvider.overrideWith((ref) async {})` to both builders, matching notifications_screen_l1_test.dart's pattern, so no real UserDatabase/scheduler chain is ever constructed in these widget tests.
- **Done when:** buildSubject() in notifications_screen_test.dart and _buildWithProviders() in ws5_two_layers_test.dart both override reminderSyncEffectProvider and streakAlertSyncEffectProvider with no-ops. · Re-running `flutter test test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_test.dart` prints no "WARNING (drift): It looks like you've created the database class UserDatabase multiple times" output. · (Rule-0, Pending) TQ-6 audit grep: any widget test file that pumps NotificationsScreen must also override both keepAlive sync-effect providers in the same overrides list.
- **Labels:** testing, hermeticity, riverpod, drift

It's non-fatal today, but a growing pile of unregistered-tag warnings trains developers/agents to ignore the warning stream, which is exactly where a genuine typo'd or newly-broken tag filter would also hide.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_test.dart:1` — “@Tags(['needs_flutter'])”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/ws5_two_layers_test.dart:9` — “@Tags(['needs_flutter'])”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_l1_test.dart:29` — “@Tags(['notifications', 'notifications_screen_l1'])”
- **Fix:** Add `needs_flutter:`, `notifications:`, and `notifications_screen_l1:` to dart_test.yaml's tags: block (and any other in-use-but-unregistered tags found elsewhere in the suite).
- **Done when:** dart_test.yaml lists needs_flutter, notifications, and notifications_screen_l1. · `flutter test test/features/notifications/` runs with no "A tag was used that wasn't specified in dart_test.yaml" warning.
- **Labels:** testing, config, dart_test.yaml

#### AUD-t-notifications-08 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Stop relying on find.byKey(...).last for time-row lookups in notifications_screen_l1_test.dart and notifications_screen_test.dart
- **Rule:** hygiene (fragile widget finder / Feathers seam) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 8 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** _SettingsTimeRow (learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen.dart:306, `return ListTile(key: key, ...)`) forwards its own key onto the inner ListTile it builds, so Key('reminder_time')/Key('streak_alert_time') each match 2 elements in the tree. All 8 sites paper over that with `.last`, trusting find.byKey's traversal order to put the ListTile after its wrapper -- an implementation detail, not a documented Flutter API contract -- while the very same file already uses a robust, order-independent alternative for the Switch rows (e.g. l1_test.dart:218-220, `find.descendant(of: reminderRow, matching: find.byType(Switch))`). If the match order ever flipped, `.last` would silently resolve to the wrapper widget and the ensuing `tester.widget<ListTile>(...)` cast would throw, breaking otherwise-unrelated tests with a confusing error.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_test.dart:86` — “await tester.tap(find.byKey(const Key('reminder_time')).last);”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_l1_test.dart:232` — “find.byKey(const Key('reminder_time')).last,”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_l1_test.dart:267` — “find.byKey(const Key('reminder_time')).last,”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_l1_test.dart:426` — “await tester.tap(find.byKey(const Key('reminder_time')).last);”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_l1_test.dart:446` — “find.byKey(const Key('reminder_time')).last,”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_l1_test.dart:494` — “find.byKey(const Key('streak_alert_time')).last,”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_l1_test.dart:509` — “find.byKey(const Key('streak_alert_time')).last,”; `learning_tracker/test/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen_l1_test.dart:614` — “await tester.tap(find.byKey(const Key('streak_alert_time')).last);”
- **Fix:** Match the ListTile the same way the Switch rows already do -- e.g. `find.widgetWithText(ListTile, l10n.notifReminderTime)` or, on the production side, stop forwarding `key` to the inner ListTile in _SettingsTimeRow and instead expose a distinct key for it -- so the finder resolves to exactly one widget without depending on registration order.
- **Done when:** Time-row assertions no longer call `.last` on a byKey finder with 2 matches. · The 8 call sites are updated or, if `.last` is kept, each carries a comment justifying why the order is guaranteed.
- **Labels:** testing, widget-finder, fragility
