#### AUD-t-progress-02 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Complete B18 in siyumim_timeline_and_lifetime_providers_test.dart to actually exercise the unmark-after-mark ledger conflict it documents
- **Rule:** TQ-8 (tautological / weaker-than-claimed test) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** B18's name and inline comments describe adding a positive seder mark then an unmark entry for the same seder, asserting the 'first (positive) mark' wins per putIfAbsent. The actual ledgerEntries list (lines 1143-1156) contains only the single positive entry -- the unmark _fakeLedgerData call described in the comment was never written -- so B18 exercises nothing beyond a trivial single-entry seder expansion already covered by B17, under a misleading name. computeLearnedLeafRefs' putIfAbsent (builder) plus getEntriesByCurriculum/getEntriesByTrack's orderBy(desc(completedAt)) (DAO) together implement a real 'most-recent-ledger-action-wins' contract with no shared documentation and no runtime assertion tying the two together; only B18b tests the mirror direction (unmark first, mark second). A regression that flips either half of that contract (e.g. a new query path that forgets the desc ordering, or a putIfAbsent that becomes an overwrite) would silently make an old bulk-mark override a later intentional unmark, and nothing in this suite would catch the positive-first/unmark-second direction.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/progress/siyumim_timeline_and_lifetime_providers_test.dart:1151` — “// Then unmark the same seder — FIRST-WRITE WINS per putIfAbsent,
// so the positive mark placed first takes priority.”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/progress/domain/services/lifetime_tree_builder.dart:110` — “level1Actions.putIfAbsent(unitId, () => action);”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/learning_ledger_dao.dart:70` — “..orderBy([(t) => OrderingTerm.desc(t.completedAt)]))”
- **Fix:** Add the described second _fakeLedgerData(..., entryScope: 'unmark_seder') entry after the positive one in B18 and assert the leaf remains learned (mirroring B18b's assertion in the opposite order); add a doc comment on computeLearnedLeafRefs stating the newest-first ordering precondition it relies on from callers.
- **Done when:** B18's ledgerEntries list contains both a positive seder entry and a corresponding unmark_seder entry, and the test fails if putIfAbsent semantics regress · computeLearnedLeafRefs doc comment states its ledgerEntries-must-be-newest-first-by-completedAt precondition

#### AUD-t-scheduler-03 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Replace fixed Future.delayed sleeps with a deterministic await in scheduler provider tests
- **Rule:** TQ-6 (hermetic tests, no timing-based synchronization) / Fowler flaky-test smell · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 25 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Every one of these sites follows the same pattern: `c.listen(skippedTasksProvider, (_, __) {})` then a hardcoded 100-200ms sleep, hoping SkippedTasks._loadFromPrefs() (fired via `unawaited()` inside build()) finished first — instead of awaiting the load itself, because the notifier exposes no future to await. Under a loaded CI runner or slower SharedPreferences-mock resolution the guess can be wrong: assertions then run against the stale initial `{}` state, or (in the several tests that call `.skip()`/`.undoSkip()` immediately after the sleep) a late-resolving `_loadFromPrefs()` can overwrite `state` with old prefs data right after the test's own mutation, silently clobbering it. The result is an intermittent, hard-to-reproduce CI failure with no diagnostic pointing at the real cause, plus 3+ seconds of pure sleep time paid on every run across these 4 files.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart:309` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart:356` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart:441` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart:523` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart:583` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 150));”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart:622` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 150));”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart:688` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart:714` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));” _(+17 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Give SkippedTasks a way to be awaited deterministically (e.g. an internal `Future<void>` the notifier tracks that a test helper can await via `container.read(...notifier).debugReadyForTest`), or restructure as an AsyncNotifier so tests can `await container.read(skippedTasksProvider.future)`. Replace all fixed-delay call sites with that await.
- **Done when:** No `Future<void>.delayed` remains in test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/*.dart used purely to wait for provider initialization. · A test that artificially slows the fake SharedPreferences resolution (e.g. via a delayed Future in the mock) still passes, proving synchronization is no longer time-based.
- **Labels:** testing, flaky-test, scheduler, riverpod

#### AUD-t-scheduler-06 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Drop the hard-coded 500ms wall-clock assertion from scheduler_engine_performance_test.dart
- **Rule:** TQ-6 (hermetic tests) / Nygard erratic test · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** This test asserts a hard wall-clock budget (elapsedMilliseconds < 500) for a 5,000-item/10,000-completion synchronous computation, running inside the same hermetic unit suite as every other file in this batch (no @Tags/exclusion). It passed on this run, but pass/fail now depends on host CPU speed and contention from parallel test-runner isolates/CI-runner noise, not on SchedulerEngine's correctness — a classic Nygard/Fowler 'erratic test.' A spurious failure on a busy CI runner produces a false-negative unrelated to the diff under review, and the natural response ('just rerun it') erodes trust in the suite over time.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/domain/services/scheduler_engine_performance_test.dart:102` — “final stopwatch = Stopwatch()..start();
      final tasks = await engine.generateDailyTasks(config);”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/domain/services/scheduler_engine_performance_test.dart:107` — “stopwatch.elapsedMilliseconds,
        lessThan(500),”
- **Fix:** Tag it out of the default hermetic run (e.g. `@Tags(['perf'])`, matching how the repo already tags story-acceptance suites) so it runs in a dedicated, less contention-sensitive job, or replace the absolute threshold with a much wider safety margin / relative-regression check.
- **Done when:** Test is excluded from the default `flutter test` sweep, or its threshold is widened enough (e.g. 5-10x measured baseline) to tolerate CI contention while still catching a genuine algorithmic regression (e.g. an accidental O(n^2) reintroduction).
- **Labels:** tq-6, flaky-test, performance

#### AUD-t-scheduler-07 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Fix the sefaria_ref_matcher_test.dart sortOrder test that cannot verify its own claim
- **Rule:** TQ-8 (assertion must match what the source can actually do wrong) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** leafChildrenForContainer returns Set<String>, so any internal sort is erased before the caller sees it; the test's own comment admits this and falls back to containsAll (membership only, no order check), so the test cannot fail if the production sort() call were deleted entirely — its name promises an ordering guarantee the assertion never checks.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/domain/services/sefaria_ref_matcher_test.dart:568` — “test('sorts result by sortOrder ascending', () {”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/domain/services/sefaria_ref_matcher_test.dart:580` — “// Sets don't preserve insertion order, but the function sorts before”
- **Fix:** Rename the test to describe what it actually checks (all three leaves present), or — if callers genuinely depend on order (resolveIndexedUnitRefs re-sorts independently, suggesting they don't) — change the return type to an ordered List and assert order for real.
- **Done when:** Test name matches its assertion, or the assertion is strengthened to check real order via a List-returning API.

#### AUD-t-scheduler-08 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Replace DateTime.now() with a fixed clock value in scheduler test fixture seeding
- **Rule:** TQ-6 (hermetic tests, no wall-clock) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]

No current assertion reads these two columns, so it doesn't flip any test's pass/fail today, but it's an easy trap: the moment a future test (or the production code these tests exercise) starts reading track state-change recency, these three tests will intermittently disagree with their own fixed 'now' by however many days/years separate the two clocks.

              activatedAt: DateTime.now(),”
- **Fix:** Pass the file's existing fixed now/today constant for stateChangedAt/activatedAt instead of DateTime.now(), matching the pattern already used for every other timestamp in the same setUp blocks.
- **Done when:** `grep -n 'DateTime.now()'` across the three files returns nothing.
- **Labels:** tq-6, wall-clock, hygiene

#### AUD-t-scheduler-09 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Replace the hardcoded trackId:1 literal with the captured track id in two scheduler tests
- **Rule:** Feathers fragile-test / general test hygiene · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Both files insert a real curriculumTracks row and capture its autoincrement id into a `trackId` local specifically so downstream code can reference the real id — and both then ignore that variable and hardcode `trackId: 1` in the ScheduleConfig/generator.generate() calls that drive the assertions, while still correctly using the captured `trackId` variable a few lines away for the StageDefinitions/CompletionEvents inserts. It works today only because a fresh in-memory DB's first insert is always id 1 (verified: neither seedProfile nor seedProfileZero touch curriculumTracks). If either helper is ever extended to seed a track, or a second track is inserted earlier in a shared setUp, config.trackId/DailyTask.trackId would silently diverge from the row the stages/completions actually reference, and no assertion in either file would catch it since nothing currently checks task.trackId's value.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/domain/services/daily_task_generator_test.dart:52` — “trackId = trackRow.id;”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/domain/services/daily_task_generator_test.dart:108` — “trackId: 1,”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/domain/services/scheduler_engine_integration_test.dart:55` — “trackId = trackRow.id;”; `learning_tracker/test/features/scheduler/domain/services/scheduler_engine_integration_test.dart:105` — “trackId: 1,”
- **Fix:** Replace the `trackId: 1` literals with the captured `trackId` variable in both files; add one assertion per file that a produced DailyTask.trackId equals the seeded track's real id, so the variable is load-bearing rather than decorative.
- **Done when:** `grep -n 'trackId: 1,'` in both files returns nothing after the fix. · At least one test per file asserts DailyTask.trackId against the captured trackId variable.
- **Labels:** test-quality, fragile-test, magic-number

#### AUD-t-settings-10 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Override the injectable LocalDayClock in backup_sync_section_l1_test.dart's relative-time assertions
- **Rule:** TQ-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [2x2]

This file never overrides it: it seeds 'just now'/'Xm ago' assertions from real DateTime.now() at 5 call sites (lines 155, 179, 201, 227, 657), then the widget independently re-reads the clock a pump later. Today's margins (e.g. a 30s buffer under the 60s 'just now' cliff) make an actual flake unlikely, but the suite is non-deterministic by construction and the gap between test-now and widget-build-now is unbounded on a loaded/slow CI runner.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/settings/presentation/widgets/backup_sync_section_l1_test.dart:179` — “final now = DateTime.now(); / final lastSynced = now.subtract(const Duration(seconds: 30));”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/settings/presentation/widgets/backup_sync_section.dart:478` — “final diff = DateTimeFactory.nowLocal().difference(dateTime);”
- **Fix:** In _buildHarness, call useLocalDayClock(FakeLocalDayClock(fixedInstant)) (or override localDayClockProvider) and derive lastSynced from that same fixed instant, removing the wall-clock dependency entirely.
- **Done when:** backup_sync_section_l1_test.dart's relative-time tests construct lastSyncedAt from a fixed instant and override localDayClockProvider/useLocalDayClock to that same instant. · The suite still passes with no bare DateTime.now() feeding a time-relative text assertion.
- **Labels:** testing, settings, hermeticity, flake-risk · verifier corrections: Line 657's test ('cloud-born already synced on mount does NOT kick another pull') asserts only verifyNever(pullOnLaunch), not relative-time text, so 'sites:5' overcounts by one for the specific 'just now'/'Xm ago' assert

Advance bookmark (outside transaction — uses content repo cache)”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/learning/data/repositories/completion_repository_impl.dart:218` — “newMilestoneUnlocks = const <RewardUnlockRecord>[];”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/gamification/domain/services/reward_milestone_service.dart:292` — “return const [];”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/content_browsing/presentation/screens/text_display_screen.dart:704` — “if (userMode == ProfileMode.child && newUnlocks.isNotEmpty) {”; `learning_tracker/test/features/gamification/presentation/widgets/achievement_unlock_celebration_test.dart:197` — “await tester.pumpWidget(_buildHarness(unlocks: [_makeUnlock()]));”

#### AUD-t-story-acceptance-06 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Delete or replace compile-time-tautological assertions across Epic 1/2 acceptance tests
- **Rule:** TQ-8 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 46 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** In null-safe Dart, `expect(SomeClass, isNotNull)` on a Type literal, a non-nullable getter, or a non-nullable top-level provider constant is guaranteed true by the type system before the test ever runs — the same is true for a bare `expect(true, isTrue)`. None of these 42 assertions, spread across 6 of Epic 1's 12 stories (1.1, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.7, 1.9) and 3 of Epic 2's AC blocks, can fail for any runtime reason; they only prove the referenced symbol resolves at compile time, which flutter analyze / the test file's own import block already guarantees. Story 1.3, for example, consists of exactly these two assertions and nothing else, yet the file header claims 'All 12 stories are DONE and actively tested,' and CLAUDE.md frames `make test-story-X.Y` passing as the story's acceptance gate ('always validate it before marking it done'). A regression in AuthGuard's guard logic, AppRouter's routes, SyncOrchestrator's wiring, or any of the 11 DAOs' real behavior ships green through that gate.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_01_foundation_test.dart:74` — “expect(UserDatabase, isNotNull);”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_01_foundation_test.dart:81` — “expect(true, isTrue);”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_01_foundation_test.dart:102` — “expect(db, isNotNull);”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_01_foundation_test.dart:110` — “expect(db.activeCurriculumDao, isNotNull);”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_01_foundation_test.dart:111` — “expect(db.completionDao, isNotNull);”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_01_foundation_test.dart:112` — “expect(db.goalDao, isNotNull);”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_01_foundation_test.dart:113` — “expect(db.pointConfigDao, isNotNull);”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_01_foundation_test.dart:114` — “expect(db.stageDao, isNotNull);” _(+38 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** For each site, either delete the assertion (documenting that the import block is the only intended check) or replace it with a behavioral assertion that calls a representative method/route/guard and checks its actual return value — the pattern Stories 1.2, 1.6, 1.11, 1.12 and the rest of Epic 2 already use in the same files.
- **Done when:** No `expect(X, isNotNull)` remains where X's static type is non-nullable, and no standalone `expect(true, isTrue)` remains, in epic_01_foundation_test.dart / epic_02_content_test.dart · Each surviving test in the affected groups exercises at least one real method call or return value
- **Labels:** test-quality, tautological-test, false-safety-net · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · verifier corrections: Affected Epic 1 stories are actually 8 (adds 1.2 and 1.10), not the 6 listed in 'why'; the 42-site count and every individual quote are accurate. | The 'why' claims tautological assertions are 'spread across 6 of Epic 1'

#### AUD-t-story-acceptance-09 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Fix inverted guard in epic_26_story_15's 'isComposite returns false for leaf curricula' test — it cannot fail
- **Rule:** TQ-8 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The loop wraps the assertion in `if (!isComposite(id))`. When isComposite correctly returns false, the guard is true, entering the block to assert isFalse on a value already known false — tautological but harmless. When isComposite returns true for some non-tanach id — the exact regression this test's name claims to catch — the guard is false, the block (and its expect) is skipped entirely, and the test passes silently. The test cannot fail for any implementation of CompositeCurriculumStrategy.isComposite, including a buggy one that marks every curriculum composite.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_26_story_15_composite_strategy_test.dart:67` — “if (!CompositeCurriculumStrategy.isComposite(id.storageKey)) {
            expect(”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_26_story_15_composite_strategy_test.dart:214` — “'saveOrder writes all items atomically — all rows present after call',”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_26_story_15_composite_strategy_test.dart:260` — “contains('_database.transaction('),”
- **Fix:** Drop the inner if and assert directly: `expect(CompositeCurriculumStrategy.isComposite(id.storageKey), isFalse, reason: 'only tanach should be composite');` for every non-tanach id.

#### AUD-t-story-acceptance-15 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Move DB/temp-dir cleanup into addTearDown across epic_21_multi_account_test.dart so failed assertions don't leak resources
- **Rule:** TQ-6 / Nygard lens (cleanup on the failure path) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 20 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** 20 of this file's ~30 tests acquire a DeviceRegistryDatabase/UserDatabase/temp Directory and release it as the very last statement of the test body instead of via addTearDown/tearDown -- the correct pattern the SAME file already uses in Stories 21.1, 21.3, and 21.4 (`tearDown(() => registry.close())` at lines 32/208/257). When an earlier expect() in one of the 20 ad-hoc tests fails, execution stops before the cleanup line runs: the temp directory and its .db file are never deleted, and the Drift database handle is never closed. On a local edit-test-rerun loop this leaks a fresh systemTemp directory on every failed run; a leaked open DB handle mid-suite risks 'database is locked'-style failures bleeding into unrelated tests later in the same run, muddying CI triage of an unrelated failure.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_21_multi_account_test.dart:194` — “await aliceDb.close();”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_21_multi_account_test.dart:365` — “await db.close();”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_21_multi_account_test.dart:475` — “await registry.close();”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_21_multi_account_test.dart:636` — “await registry.close();”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_21_multi_account_test.dart:637` — “await tempDir.delete(recursive: true);”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_21_multi_account_test.dart:1002` — “await registry.close();”
- **Fix:** Replace every trailing `await registry.close()` / `await db.close()` / `await tempDir.delete(recursive: true)` with `addTearDown(() => ...)` registered immediately after the resource is created, mirroring the tearDown(() => registry.close()) pattern already used in this file's Stories 21.1/21.3/21.4 groups.
- **Done when:** No test body in this file calls .close()/.delete(recursive on a resource it created without a preceding addTearDown for that same resource · A deliberately-failing expect() inserted before the old cleanup line still results in the temp dir/DB being cleaned up (verified via addTearDown running)
- **Labels:** Nygard-lens, resource-leak, test-hygiene, TQ-6 · verifier corrections: The 'database is locked-style failures bleeding into unrelated tests' mechanism is overstated: all DBs cited use NativeDatabase.memory() and each tempDir has a unique generated name, so cross-test file-lock contention is

- **Rule:** TQ-4 / PV-2 (fake diverges from the class it stands in for) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]

If a future change to the real class's encoding diverges from the fake -- e.g. a prefix, or an email fallback on a null check gone wrong -- this acceptance test keeps passing green while the production Crashlytics identifier regresses into leaking PII, exactly the class of bug this story exists to prevent. '' : '$profileId');”
- **Fix:** Replace _CapturingCrashlyticsService for the identifier tests with a MockFirebaseCrashlytics (mocktail) wrapped in a real FirebaseCrashlyticsService, and verify(() => mock.setUserIdentifier('5')), matching the interaction-verification pattern already used in epic_24_stop_bleeding_test.dart.
- **Done when:** AC3/AC4 identifier tests exercise FirebaseCrashlyticsService.setUserIdentifier (via a mocked FirebaseCrashlytics), not a hand-duplicated encoding · Changing the ternary in FirebaseCrashlyticsService.setUserIdentifier without updating the test causes a test failure
- **Labels:** TQ-4, PV-2, fake-drift, child-privacy · verifier corrections: A third independent duplicate of the same ternary exists at test/core/logging/crashlytics_service_test.dart:93-95, strengthening (not weakening) the finding's core claim that the real class's logic is never exercised.

#### AUD-t-story-acceptance-37 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Fix the two-call wall-clock race in epic_25_schema_core_test.dart's SystemLocalDayClock.today() test
- **Rule:** TQ-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** clock.today() and DateTime.now() are two independent wall-clock reads compared for equal year/month/day; if local midnight falls between the two calls the assertions intermittently disagree — a hairline but real flake source, exactly the class TQ-6 exists to keep out of test/ (test/ is not yet covered by the DateTime.now() audit grep that already protects lib/).
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_25_schema_core_test.dart:1140` — “final today = clock.today();”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_25_schema_core_test.dart:1141` — “final sysNow = DateTime.now();”
- **Fix:** Capture one DateTime.now() first and derive both the expected y/m/d and the clock.today() call from it, or bracket clock.today() between a before/after DateTime.now() pair instead of comparing to a second independent read.
- **Done when:** test reads the wall clock once (or brackets before/after) instead of comparing two independent DateTime.now()-derived values
- **Labels:** TQ-6, wall-clock, flaky-test-risk

#### AUD-t-story-acceptance-38 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Import the shared MockContentRepository fake instead of redeclaring it in epic_24_stop_bleeding_test.dart

Harmless today since mocktail scoping is per-file/per-library, but it's 1 of 11 files repo-wide carrying the exact same fork (checked via repo-wide grep, the other 10 are outside this batch) -- if ContentRepository's interface grows, updates to the shared fake won't reach files that forked their own copy, and a future author has no signal a shared version already exists.

#### AUD-t-story-acceptance-39 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Inject a fake clock instead of comparing against real DateTime.now() in completion/restore timing assertions
- **Rule:** TQ-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [2x2]
- **Why:** Both assertions pin correctness to a 5-second window measured against the real wall clock at assertion time, rather than the FakeLocalDayClock/DateTimeFactory override the codebase already provides and uses correctly elsewhere (e.g. epic_08_gamification_test.dart Story 8.2). On a slow or contended CI runner, a stall of more than 5 seconds between the write and the assertion — plausible for a cold Drift/sqlite3 open — flakes the test for a reason unrelated to the code under test.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_03_learning_cycle_test.dart:118` — “DateTime.now().difference(completion.completedAt).abs().inSeconds,
          lessThan(5),”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/regression_invariants_test.dart:251` — “restored.activatedAt.isAfter(
              beforeRestore.subtract(const Duration(seconds: 5)),”
- **Fix:** Install a FakeLocalDayClock (or equivalent) before the write and assert equality/near-equality against the fake's fixed instant, matching the pattern already used in epic_08_gamification_test.dart Story 8.2.
- **Done when:** Both assertions compare against a fixed/fake clock value, not a DateTime.now()/DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() call made at assertion time
- **Labels:** test-quality, hermetic, flake-risk · verifier corrections: epic_03_learning_cycle_test.dart evidence line should be 119, not 118 — the quoted text begins one line after the cited line number.

#### AUD-t-story-acceptance-40 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Log the empty catch(_) blocks swallowing temp-dir cleanup failures in epic_19_offline_first_test.dart
- **Rule:** EH-3 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** EH-3 bans empty and log-less catches repo-wide. If Directory.delete(recursive: true) fails here — e.g. a held SQLite file handle on the just-closed content/read-only DB — the failure is silently discarded, leaving stray temp dirs with no breadcrumb that cleanup ever failed, exactly the swallowed-exception debugging dead-end EH-3 exists to prevent.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_19_offline_first_test.dart:274` — “} catch (_) {}”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_19_offline_first_test.dart:324` — “} catch (_) {}”
- **Fix:** At minimum print/log the caught error instead of a bare catch (_) {} in both addTearDown blocks.
- **Done when:** grep -n 'catch (_) {}' learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_19_offline_first_test.dart returns no match, or each site logs the caught error
- **Labels:** hygiene, error-handling, EH-3

#### AUD-t-story-acceptance-41 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Pin the LocalDayClock in epic_27_story_05_bulk_mark_prior_test.dart's second test instead of relying on real wall time
- **Rule:** TQ-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** No `useLocalDayClock(...)` call exists anywhere in this file, so `repo.markComplete(...)` writes `eventTimestamp` via `DateTimeFactory.nowUtc()` → the real `SystemLocalDayClock`, while `StreakStateProvider(..., clock: FakeLocalDayClock(today))` pins `today = DateTime.utc(2026, 5, 13, 9)` — violating TQ-6's no-wall-clock rule. The in-file comment claiming real 'now' is 'at most a few seconds before `today`' is already false (real time is ~7 weeks past 2026-05-13 as of this audit). The assertion (`state.maxStreak == 1`) only survives because streak_reducer.dart computes maxStreak from distinct-day count, independent of `today`, for a single-event list — confirmed by reading the reducer and by `flutter test` passing today. Any future addition of a currentStreak/lastCompletionDayLocal assertion here would go flaky depending on wall-clock date.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_27_story_05_bulk_mark_prior_test.dart:190` — “await repo.markComplete(
        const CompletionRequest(”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_27_story_05_bulk_mark_prior_test.dart:208` — “// The completion landed "today" (DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() at
      // test execution time) — which is at most a few seconds before”
- **Fix:** Call `useLocalDayClock(FakeLocalDayClock(today))` in setUp with `resetLocalDayClock()` in tearDown, matching the pattern already used in epic_27_integration_lockout_redaction_atomic_test.dart's AC1 group.
- **Done when:** Test pins the global LocalDayClock explicitly and passes independent of wall-clock date.
- **Labels:** testing, TQ-6, hermeticity

- **Rule:** TQ-8 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 14 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Each asserts isNotNull on a bare top-level class reference, a resolved provider identifier, or a non-nullable enum constant. None of these can ever be null if the file compiles — the import at the top of the same file already fails the build otherwise. The tests add zero information beyond 'this file compiles', which flutter analyze and every sibling test in the same group already guarantee; dashboard_model_provider_test.dart's AC1 group is 6 of 7 tests in this exact shape.

- **Fix:** Delete these 14 tests, or replace each with the structural/behavioral check its AC actually promises — e.g. TrackTaskCategory's 'has exactly 3 values' test (already present alongside 3 of these) is the real assertion; the 3 existence checks beside it add nothing.

#### AUD-t-story-acceptance-46 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Replace fixed 50ms Future.delayed polling with stream.first awaits in epic_15's curriculum-scope watch-stream test
- **Rule:** TQ-6 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** 'scope watch stream emits on every change for provider reactivity' uses a fixed 50ms sleep 4 times as a stand-in for 'the stream has emitted by now', when the same test group already shows the deterministic alternative 100 lines earlier ('watchScopes emits updates when scopes change', lines 3439-3462, uses `await stream.first`). A timed sleep is a generic flakiness anti-pattern (no upper bound is ever truly safe under load) even though the practical risk here is low since the stream is backed by an in-memory NativeDatabase.memory() with no real I/O latency.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_15_multi_profile_test.dart:3549` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_15_multi_profile_test.dart:3561` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_15_multi_profile_test.dart:3572` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));”; `learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_15_multi_profile_test.dart:3578` — “await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));”
- **Fix:** Replace the 4 Future.delayed calls with `await emissions stream.first` / a captured StreamQueue read, consistent with the pattern already used at lines 3446 and 3459 in the same test group.
- **Done when:** The test contains no Future.delayed/sleep-based synchronization; each emission is awaited directly from the stream. · Test still asserts the same 4 transitions (initial empty, set, change, clear).
- **Labels:** TQ-6, flaky-test-pattern

- **Fix:** Delete the runtime expect() calls and keep this as a documented compile-only shape check (a referenced-but-uncalled function is enough to prove the interface compiles), or point the docstring at auth_repository_impl_test.dart so reviewers don't mistake mock-echo assertions for behavioural coverage.

- **Why:** TQ-6 requires tests use a fixed DateTimeFactory rather than the wall clock. None of these 15 sites are currently asserted on, so there is no live flake today — but the codebase already has a working seam (DateTimeFactory.nowUtc(), used correctly by test/helpers/drift_memory.dart's seedProfile in the very same suite and throughout production DAOs) that these two files bypass with raw DateTime.now(). - **Fix:** Replace DateTime.now() with DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() (or a fixed literal) at all 15 sites, matching the pattern already used in test/helpers/drift_memory.dart.
- **Done when:** grep -n 'DateTime.now()' learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_18_track_overhaul_test.dart learning_tracker/test/story_acceptance/epic_19_offline_first_test.dart returns no match

#### AUD-t-track_setup-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Stop testing the stale copy of AddTrackFlowScreen._getSmartDefault in add_track_result_test.dart — it asserts pre-fix buggy behavior
- **Rule:** TQ-8 (regression-test integrity) / Feathers testability seam · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 7 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** Commit 1fead3de ("fix: resolve 14 defects from run-7 on-device E2E audit", the wave immediately preceding this one) fixed a real user-visible bug: the track-setup wizard's smart default name showed the last-selected scope value (e.g. 'Seder Zeraim') instead of the curriculum label, so the post-creation snackbar didn't match the Track Management hub card title. The fix rewrote the real `_getSmartDefault()` to always call `curriculumLabelText(ref, curriculum: c)`. add_track_result_test.dart never imports that method — a private test-local copy (comment: 'Extracted logic from AddTrackFlow for unit testing') still implements the PRE-fix logic (`return state.scopeSelections!.last.value;`), and the test 'uses scope value when scope narrowed' asserts exactly the behavior the fix removed, still expecting 'סדר זרעים'. #### AUD-t-tracks-04 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Inject FakeLocalDayClock into TrackCreationService's B3 back-date tests instead of reading the wall clock
- **Rule:** TQ-6 (hermetic tests: no wall-clock) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Neither B3 test overrides LocalDayClock, so DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() reads the real system clock both for the test's 'before' and again inside the SUT's _parseProgramStartingRef moments later. Duration.inDays truncates: (Duration(days:5) - Duration(microseconds:1)).inDays == 4, verified directly in this Dart VM; an empirical 200k-iteration back-to-back DateTime.now() sample in this same environment showed roughly 4% of pairs returning a non-zero gap (up to 70us), meaning daysBack can legitimately compute to 4 instead of 5 and fail expect(daysBack, 5, ...) for reasons unrelated to any real regression. This is exactly the flakiness class LocalDayClock/FakeLocalDayClock exists to eliminate, and the sibling provision_track_use_case_test.dart correctly uses FakeLocalDayClock for the equivalent B3 assertions — this file is the outlier.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/tracks/setup/domain/services/track_creation_service_atomicity_test.dart:131` — “final before = DateTimeFactory.nowUtc();”; `learning_tracker/test/features/tracks/setup/domain/services/track_creation_service_atomicity_test.dart:157` — “expect(daysBack, 5, reason: 'offset:5 must be exactly 5 days in the past');”
- **Fix:** Thread a FakeLocalDayClock(seed) into TrackCreationService/_parseProgramStartingRef so the test's 'before' and the SUT's 'now' are the identical fixed instant, making daysBack deterministic.
- **Done when:** Test passes across many repeated runs with an artificial delay inserted between test setup and SUT invocation · Test no longer depends on two independent real-clock reads landing in the same tick
- **Labels:** test-quality, flaky-test, clock

Neither test ever calls tester.pumpWidget — they only construct the widget object and assert the constructor stored the field verbatim, which Dart's own field assignment guarantees trivially. - **Fix:** Rewrite both as widget tests: for TS-10, pump SelfPacedGoalStep with initialGoal set to a deadline-type GoalEntity and assert the deadline card renders active (not blurred) and/or that tapping Continue immediately emits goalType=='deadline' with the restored targetDate. #### AUD-t-tracks-06 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Rewrite TrackLearningOrderScreen 'race-safety' test to actually verify the _sedarimSaveSeq guard
- **Rule:** TQ-8 (regression test weaker than what the source can do wrong) / Feathers seam lens · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Test '20. rapid successive reorders only persist the final order (seq guard)' claims to pin the _sedarimSaveSeq race guard, but its only assertions are that saveSedarimOrder was called twice and that some DraggableOrderItem still renders. Both saves are dispatched regardless of the guard (the guard only gates the *post-await* provider-invalidate/setState in _persistSedarim), so deleting the 'mySeq != _sedarimSaveSeq' checks entirely would not change either assertion's outcome — the test cannot fail if the guard regresses. Contrast with track_learning_order_reset_test.dart in the same batch, which correctly uses controlled Completers to prove which read 'wins'; that pattern is available and not applied here, so a future refactor could silently reintroduce the stale-continuation race (flicker/revert of the reordered list) with CI green.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/test/features/tracks/track_management_body_and_order_l1_test.dart:1059` — “repo.saveSedarimOrder(_kTrackId, any<List<LearningOrderItem>>()),
        ).called(2);”; `learning_tracker/test/features/tracks/track_management_body_and_order_l1_test.dart:1064` — “expect(find.byType(DraggableOrderItem), findsAtLeastNWidgets(1));”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/track_order/presentation/screens/track_learning_order_screen.dart:223` — “if (!mounted || mySeq != _sedarimSaveSeq) return;”
- **Fix:** Give the mocked repo.saveSedarimOrder two distinguishable outcomes (e.g. via Completers, as done in track_learning_order_reset_test.dart) so the first (slow) save's post-await continuation would visibly corrupt state if it ran; assert that only the second reorder's masechtos invalidation/refetch is reflected in the rendered order, and that the test fails when the mySeq guard is removed.
- **Done when:** Test fails (red) when the 'if (!mounted || mySeq != _sedarimSaveSeq) return;' guard is deleted from _persistSedarim in track_learning_order_screen.dart · Test distinguishes stale vs fresh masechtos-fetch results (e.g. per-call Completers) rather than only counting saveSedarimOrder invocations · Final rendered/persisted order is asserted to match the second (last) reorder, not merely 'a list renders without crashing'
- **Labels:** testing, TQ-8, race-condition, tracks

#### AUD-t-tutoring-10 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Replace tautological isNotNull(Type)/constructor-tearoff compile-checks with real interface/constructor assertions
- **Rule:** TQ-8 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 4 · **Verified:** [1x1] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** expect(SomeType, isNotNull) and expect(SomeClass.new, isNotNull) can never fail — a bare Type literal and a constructor tear-off are non-null by construction regardless of what the class implements or does. The docstrings explicitly claim these verify 'that FirestoreTutorGrantRepository satisfies the TutorGrantRepository interface' and that 'the class is constructible without error' — neither claim is actually checked: an accidental removal of `implements TutorGrantRepository`, or a constructor that throws on null functions, would leave these tests green.

- **Fix:** Replace with real assertions, e.g. `TutorGrantRepository Function({FirebaseFunctions? functions}) ctor = FirestoreTutorGrantRepository.new;` (fails to compile if the interface isn't satisfied) or actually instantiate and check `is`/`isA<>`.
- **Done when:** each of the 3 tests either performs a real assignability check (typed constructor-tearoff assignment) or instantiates the class and asserts isA<Interface>() · temporarily removing the `implements`/`extends` clause from the target class locally makes the corresponding test fail

#### AUD-guardrails-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Add Goals to tool/schema_check.dart's whitelist — the profileId-in-PK Rule-0 checker silently skips it
- **Rule:** profileId-in-PK [E] (Naming/placement/invariants) + Rule 0 checker coverage · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 10 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** schema_check.dart's own docstring says Goals is deliberately exempted from the profileId-composite-key invariant pending DNI-323/DNI-324 — but docs/planning/epics.md marks both Done, and the other 3 tables named in the same sentence (CompletionEvents, LearningLedger, StreakEvents) already HAVE their composite @TableIndex and are already in the whitelist — only Goals was never followed up. Concretely, goals.dart has a bare autoincrement id with profileId as a plain FK column (no composite key/index), and goal_dao.dart's getAllGoals() has zero profileId filter while deleteGoalsByCurriculum(curriculumId) filters only by curriculumId — which is NOT unique per profile (two child profiles can each have a track on the same curriculum, e.g. Mishnayos). `make ci` runs schema-check and reports green while this gap ships every build, giving false confidence exactly where Story 25.1 (the multi-profile-leak story that motivated this checker) says it matters most.
- **Evidence:** `tool/schema_check.dart:44` — “///   - Completions, Goals, LearningLedger, Streaks: profile-scoped but
///     lack a composite UNIQUE/index today. DNI-323 / DNI-324 will ”; `tool/schema_check.dart:55` — “const _defaultWhitelist = <String>{ 'Bookmarks', ... 'StudyDayConfigs' };  // 'Goals' is absent”; `docs/planning/epics.md:775` — “- **DNI-323** — 25.2: Append-only event tables with composite-natural-key UNIQUEs *(Done)*”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/tables/goals.dart:10` — “IntColumn get id => integer().autoIncrement()();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/goal_dao.dart:22` — “Future<List<Goal>> getAllGoals() => select(goals).get();”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/database/daos/goal_dao.dart:60` — “Future<int> deleteGoalsByCurriculum(String curriculumId) =>
      (delete(goals)..where((t) => t.curriculumId.equals(curriculumId))).go();”; `.github/workflows/ci.yml:98` — “run: dart analyze --fatal-infos”; `Makefile:228` — “ci: analyze format schema-check test-all” _(+2 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Add profileId to a composite uniqueKeys/@TableIndex on the Goals table (migration + schema export per DB-4), add 'Goals' to _defaultWhitelist, and correct the docstring to stop citing DNI-323/DNI-324 as pending. Separately, audit goal_dao.dart's curriculumId-only queries for cross-profile scoping (getAllGoals, deleteGoalsByCurriculum) and add profileId filters or justify their absence explicitly.
- **Done when:** `dart run tool/schema_check.dart` (wired into `make ci` via the `schema-check` target) fails red for Goals until it has profileId in a composite key/index, then passes green after the migration. · _defaultWhitelist includes 'Goals'; the docstring no longer references DNI-323/DNI-324 as pending work. · A regression test asserts getAllGoals()/deleteGoalsByCurriculum() cannot return/delete another profile's row when two profiles share a curriculumId.
- **Labels:** data-integrity, rule-0-gap, drift, multi-profile · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches · verifier corrections: First evidence quote (schema_check.dart) is cited at line 44 but actually begins at line 45 (line 44 is the header comment '/// Tables intentionally omitted from this list (and why):'); the quoted two lines are 45-46. #### AUD-guardrails-02 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Fix the cross-feature-deep-import checker (Makefile audit 15/15) — its awk logic can never fire
- **Rule:** Rule 0 / Rule 2 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 14 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** The awk derives BOTH the importing-file's feature name and the imported feature name from $0, which is the full grep -rn output line beginning with the FILE PATH — so match($0,...) always finds the importer's OWN feature name (from the path prefix) before ever reaching the import statement, making a[1]!=b[1] always false. Verified by feeding the exact grep -rn output line for pending_local_signup.dart through the isolated awk: it printed 'SUPPRESSED (bug present)'. Because of this, Rule 2 has zero real enforcement repo-wide despite 'make audit' reporting 15/15 clean, and two concrete violations sit undetected in this batch alone: pending_local_signup.dart (a domain/services file) reaches directly into a different feature's presentation/providers instead of a barrel — profiles' own barrel (features/profiles/profiles.dart) is an empty stub with nothing exported, so there was no barrel path available — and onboarding_screen.dart in a different feature deep-imports account's onboarding_intent_screen.dart because account.dart's barrel doesn't export it.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/Makefile:378` — “awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}'”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/domain/services/pending_local_signup.dart:11` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/profiles/presentation/providers/profile_providers.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/onboarding/presentation/screens/onboarding_screen.dart:10` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/account/onboarding/presentation/screens/onboarding_intent_screen.dart'; // W6.1”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/profiles/profiles.dart:6` — “library profiles;”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/track_stat_grid.dart:8` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/scheduler/domain/models/daily_task.dart';”; `learning_tracker/Makefile:377` — “| grep -P "features/([^/]+)/(?!\1\.dart)" \”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/screens/edit_track_screen.dart:20` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/dashboard/presentation/providers/dashboard_providers.dart';”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tracks/setup/presentation/providers/after_track_change_invalidation.dart:6` — “import 'package:learning_tracker/features/dashboard/presentation/providers/dashboard_providers.dart';” _(+7 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Fix the awk to extract the imported-feature name from the import-statement TEXT only (e.g. split the grep -rn line on the first ':' twice to isolate the content, or use grep -oP 'features/\K[^/]+' scoped to the substring after the import path's package: prefix) so it stops reading the file-path prefix. Then resolve the two concrete violations: export a currentAccountId-style accessor from features/profiles/profiles.dart and import through it, and export OnboardingIntentStep from features/account/account.dart. Add a tiny fixture-based regression so a bad cross-feature import always reproduces a checker failure.

#### AUD-guardrails-11 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Escape jq string interpolation in tool/linear-sync.sh before it corrupts YAML on titles/authors containing a quote
- **Rule:** Tier-2 AREA NOTE: correctness of tooling (silent corruption) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** All 5 sites build a quoted YAML scalar by raw string-concatenating a Linear-supplied value (issue title, or comment author name) between literal backslash-quotes, with no escaping of embedded `"` characters. Any Linear issue titled e.g. `Fix "broken" login` (or a comment author display name containing a quote) produces a line like `title: "Fix "broken" login"` in sprint-status.yaml, the per-story .yaml cache files, AND the generated epics.md — a malformed value with no error raised anywhere in the pipeline (set -e doesn't catch it, since jq itself succeeds). Downstream, docs/planning/epics.md's AUTO:EPIC-LIST block (also written by this script) silently carries the corrupted text into checked-in documentation.
- **Evidence:** `tool/linear-sync.sh:301` — “"    title: \"" + .title + "\"\n" +”; `tool/linear-sync.sh:323` — “"    title: \"" + .title + "\"\n" +”; `tool/linear-sync.sh:336` — “"title: \"" + .title + "\"",”; `tool/linear-sync.sh:381` — “"title: \"" + .title + "\"",”; `tool/linear-sync.sh:388` — “"  - author: \"" + .user.name + "\"\n    body: |\n" + ...”
- **Fix:** Replace the raw `"...\"" + .field + "\""` concatenation with jq's `(.field | tojson)` (or `@json`) at all 5 sites, which correctly escapes embedded quotes/backslashes/newlines and is still valid YAML flow-scalar syntax.
- **Done when:** Feed a synthetic Linear issue JSON with a `"` in .title (and .user.name for comments) through the jq filters; the emitted YAML parses cleanly via `python3 -c "import yaml,sys;yaml.safe_load(sys.stdin)"` or `yq`. · All 5 sites (lines 301, 323, 336, 381, 388) use tojson/@json instead of manual quote concatenation.
- **Labels:** correctness, silent-corruption, tooling

#### AUD-guardrails-13 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Fix root Makefile's audit/analyze/test-all targets so they stop reporting false passes
- **Rule:** Rule 0 (checker failures must exit non-zero) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The whole `audit` recipe is one shell invocation (backslash-continued); its final two statements are joined by `;`, not `&&`, so the recipe's exit status is that of the LAST command (`echo "audit PASSED."`), never custom_lint's. Empirically reproduced: a `false;`-then-`echo` recipe in a throwaway Makefile prints the trailing text and `make` still exits 0. Since custom_lint is currently broken (crashes, per baseline), running `make audit` from the repo root today prints the crash output and then unconditionally declares "audit PASSED." Separately, root `analyze` omits `--fatal-infos` and `test-all` omits `--coverage`, unlike learning_tracker/Makefile's equivalents (which say "matches CI --fatal-infos flag" and are correct) — so `make ci` from repo root can go green on issues the real CI gate (which always runs from learning_tracker/) would reject.
- **Evidence:** `Makefile:217` — “cd learning_tracker && dart run custom_lint; \
	echo "audit PASSED."”; `Makefile:86` — “@echo "Running all tests..."
	@cd learning_tracker && flutter test”; `Makefile:90` — “@echo "Running dart analyze..."
	@cd learning_tracker && dart analyze”
- **Fix:** Replace the trailing `;` with `&&` (or check `$?` explicitly) so a lint failure fails the recipe; add `--fatal-infos` to root `analyze` and `--coverage` to root `test-all`, or better, make the root Makefile's targets thin `cd learning_tracker && make $@` wrappers so there is exactly one place these flags can drift.
- **Done when:** `make audit` from the repo root exits non-zero when the underlying custom_lint invocation fails. · root `make analyze` uses --fatal-infos and root `make test-all`/`ci` produce coverage output, matching learning_tracker/Makefile.
- **Labels:** rule-0, makefile, guardrails, bypassable-gate

#### AUD-guardrails-14 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Gate deploy-play-store.yml on a passing CI run for the exact SHA being deployed
- **Rule:** Rule 0 / AG-11 (bypassable gates) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** deploy-play-store.yml has no `needs:`/`workflow_run:` dependency on ci.yml and no step that checks the target SHA's check-run status. Its only steps between checkout and Play Store upload are checkout, codegen, and `flutter build appbundle --release` — no `flutter test`, `dart analyze`, `make audit`, or firestore-rules check. A maintainer who tags a commit that never went through review/CI (an emergency hotfix, a stale local branch, the wrong SHA) or whose ci.yml run is still red/in-progress can ship straight to Google Play production with nothing in the committed config to stop it — the only backstop is human diligence, which is exactly the kind of implicit, non-deterministic gate Rule 0 says not to rely on.
- **Evidence:** `.github/workflows/deploy-play-store.yml:15` — “on:
  workflow_dispatch:”; `.github/workflows/deploy-play-store.yml:28` — “push:
    tags:”
- **Fix:** Add a job that queries the GitHub Checks API for the deploying SHA's required workflows before the build/upload steps run (or trigger deploys via a `workflow_call` from a successful ci.yml run instead of independent `push: tags`/`workflow_dispatch` triggers).
- **Done when:** deploy-play-store.yml fails fast if the deploying SHA has no green ci.yml run, before any build/signing steps execute. · A dry run against a SHA with a failing/missing CI run demonstrates the new gate blocking the deploy.
- **Labels:** ci, deploy, bypassable-gate, release

#### AUD-guardrails-15 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Reconcile the first AVD entry across avd-setup.ps1, emulators-start.ps1, and adb-connect-wsl.sh
- **Rule:** Tier-2 AREA NOTE: drift between duplicated configs · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 6 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** avd-setup.ps1's own $MATRIX creates the port-5554 device as API 24 on a 'Nexus 5' profile named `lt_api24_nexus5`. But emulators-start.ps1's $ALL_AVDS and adb-connect-wsl.sh's EXPECTED_NAMES/EXPECTED_APIS both expect an AVD literally named `lt_api28_pixel2` (API 28, Pixel 2) at that same port — and both agree with EACH OTHER, only avd-setup.ps1 disagrees. All 4 other matrix rows (29/31/34/36.1) match perfectly across all 3 scripts. Following avd-setup.ps1's own documented next step ('Start all 5: .\tool\emulators-start.ps1') on a fresh machine launches `emulator -avd lt_api28_pixel2`, which was never created — that emulator slot fails to boot, and adb-connect-wsl.sh's health check for it reports NOT FOUND.
- **Evidence:** `tool/avd-setup.ps1:70` — “name      = "lt_api24_nexus5"
        port      = 5554”; `tool/emulators-start.ps1:44` — “lt_api28_pixel2  = 5554”; `tool/adb-connect-wsl.sh:39` — “EXPECTED_NAMES=(lt_api28_pixel2 lt_api29_pixel3 lt_api31_pixel5 lt_api34_pixel7 lt_api36_tablet)”; `tool/device_e2e/driver.py:44` — “ADB = "/home/daniel/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb"”; `tool/adb-connect-wsl.sh:29` — “ADB="$ANDROID_SDK_WIN/platform-tools/adb.exe"”; `tool/vision_find_pass.js:7` — “const ADB = '/home/daniel/bin/adb'”
- **Fix:** Pick one name/API/device-profile for the port-5554 slot and make all 3 scripts agree — most likely revert avd-setup.ps1's first matrix row back to api=28/device='Pixel 2'/name='lt_api28_pixel2' to match the other two (already-agreeing) scripts, unless the API-24 floor change was intentional, in which case propagate it to emulators-start.ps1 and adb-connect-wsl.sh instead.
- **Done when:** The AVD name/API/port for the first device slot is identical across avd-setup.ps1, emulators-start.ps1, and adb-connect-wsl.sh. · Running avd-setup.ps1 followed by emulators-start.ps1 boots all 5 emulators, verified by adb-connect-wsl.sh reporting 5/5 ONLINE.
- **Labels:** drift, tooling, windows-wsl2 · merged 1 duplicate report(s)

#### AUD-guardrails-16 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Replace make audit's dead literal-phrase TODO/FIXME/XXX grep with a real AG-6 check
- **Rule:** AG-6 (every TODO/FIXME carries a Linear DNI-#### id) / Rule 0 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Audit check 10/15 ('No banned TODO/FIXME/XXX markers') matches only three exact, oddly-specific literal phrases. Verified: `grep -rn "TODO: refactor later\|FIXME: hardcoded for now\|XXX: temporary" learning_tracker/lib/` returns zero hits anywhere in the app, and always will — no developer writes that literal string. Meanwhile there are real, uncaught TODOs with no Linear id anywhere (`grep -c "DNI-[0-9]"` on all lib/ TODO/FIXME lines returns 0 of 4), and my own batch contains a live example the check silently misses: integration_test/app_test.dart:25. This grep gives the false impression that TODO/FIXME hygiene (AG-6) is enforced by `make audit`, when in fact it enforces nothing a real comment would ever trip.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/Makefile:350` — “if grep -rn "TODO: refactor later\|FIXME: hardcoded for now\|XXX: temporary" lib/ --include="*.dart" | grep -q .; then \”; `learning_tracker/integration_test/app_test.dart:25` — “// TODO: Add more integration tests as features are implemented:”
- **Fix:** Change the pattern to match any `// TODO`/`// FIXME`/`// XXX` NOT followed by `DNI-\d+` (e.g. `grep -rnE '//\s*(TODO|FIXME|XXX)' lib/ | grep -vE 'DNI-[0-9]+'`), which is what AG-6 actually requires.
- **Done when:** `make audit` fails on any TODO/FIXME/XXX comment in lib/ (or test/) lacking a DNI-#### id. · A regression fixture (one TODO with a DNI id, one without) proves the new grep distinguishes them.
- **Labels:** ag-6, dead-check, makefile, rule-0

#### AUD-guardrails-20 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Decode xz's stderr before interpolating it in seed_content_db.dart's failure message (currently prints a raw byte list)
- **Rule:** Nygard I/O-failure lens / general correctness · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Process.runSync is called at line 312-317 with `stderrEncoding: null`, so ProcessResult.stderr holds raw bytes (a Uint8List), not a decoded String. String-interpolating it at line 319 invokes List.toString(), producing something like 'xz failed: [120, 122, 58, 32, ...]' instead of xz's actual human-readable stderr text — exactly when a maintainer most needs a readable error, during a failing release build.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/tool/seed_content_db.dart:319` — “throw StateError('xz failed: ${xzResult.stderr}');”
- **Fix:** Pass `stderrEncoding: systemEncoding` (or explicit `utf8`) to this Process.runSync call, or explicitly `utf8.decode(xzResult.stderr as List<int>)` before interpolating it into the thrown StateError.
- **Done when:** Triggering an xz failure (e.g. temporarily pointing dbPath at a nonexistent file, or aliasing xz unavailable) prints a human-readable message, not a numeric byte-list · seed_content_db.dart's xz Process.runSync call sets stderrEncoding to a real Encoding, or decodes stderr before use
- **Labels:** correctness, tool, hygiene, error-handling

#### AUD-guardrails-31 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Hoist the triplicated screenshot names[] list in tool/upload_store_assets.py to one constant
- **Rule:** Fowler duplication (extract constant) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]

If a screenshot is ever added/renamed/reordered, all 3 copies must be updated in lockstep by hand; missing one silently mislabels an upload (the loop just indexes names[i-1] against whatever list is present) with no error since the script only checks os.path.exists implicitly via MediaFileUpload's own failure mode.
- **Evidence:** `tool/upload_store_assets.py:141` — “names = ["dashboard", "learning", "progress", "scheduler", "gamification"]”; `tool/upload_store_assets.py:150` — “names = ["dashboard", "learning", "progress", "scheduler", "gamification"]”; `tool/upload_store_assets.py:159` — “names = ["dashboard", "learning", "progress", "scheduler", "gamification"]”
- **Fix:** Define `SCREENSHOT_NAMES = ["dashboard", "learning", "progress", "scheduler", "gamification"]` once at module scope (near PACKAGE_NAME/LANGUAGE) and reference it in all 3 loops.

#### AUD-guardrails-32 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Log the caught exception at 7 silent/overbroad catch sites across tool/ fetch-and-resolve helpers
- **Rule:** EH-3 (log-less catch) / EH-4 (Error-subtype catch) — general lens applied to tool/ · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 7 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** None of these seven catch/except blocks log the caught error before discarding it — Dart sites return a generic error flag, Python sites `pass`/`continue`/`return None`. When a fetch or ref-resolution genuinely fails, the operator sees only an aggregate 'N errors'/'SKIP' count, never why (network error vs. malformed data vs. a real bug in the resolver itself), making failures expensive to diagnose. verify_seed_calendar.dart:202 additionally catches `Object` — broader than even `Error` — so it would also swallow a `TypeError`/`RangeError` from a bug in the tool's own JSON-parsing code and silently retry it up to 4 times before reporting the day as a generic 'live fetch failed', masking a real programming defect as a transient network blip.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/tool/seed_text_content.dart:141` — “} catch (_) {”; `learning_tracker/tool/seed_text_content.dart:146` — “} catch (_) {”; `learning_tracker/tool/verify_seed_calendar.dart:202` — “} on Object {”; `learning_tracker/tool/text_extract/extract_books.py:184` — “except Exception:”; `learning_tracker/tool/text_extract/extract_books.py:199` — “except Exception:”; `learning_tracker/tool/text_extract/extract_books.py:207` — “except Exception:”; `learning_tracker/tool/text_extract/main.py:78` — “except Exception:”
- **Fix:** Add a log line (print/stderr.writeln/sys.stderr.write) with the caught exception's message and ref/date context at each of the 7 sites before falling through to the existing error-flag return. Narrow verify_seed_calendar.dart:202's `on Object` to the specific exception types the HTTP client/JSON decoder can actually throw.
- **Done when:** Each of the 7 cited sites logs the caught exception before returning its existing failure value · verify_seed_calendar.dart:202 no longer catches bare Object
- **Labels:** EH-3, EH-4, tool, hygiene, log-less-catch

#### AUD-guardrails-33 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Mark tool/text_extract/ as retired in-repo and fix extract_books.py's footnote-stripping regression before any reuse
- **Rule:** dead-code + text-cleaning correctness (BUG-5 invariant) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** docs/seed-build.md:6,123 explicitly states the daily-content resolvers were 'ported from the retired tool/text_extract/main.py', and the live pipeline (make seed → tool/seed/build_text_cache.dart, tool/seed/build_daily_content.dart) never invokes anything under tool/text_extract/. Yet the directory's own README still reads as a live runbook (present-tense 'Builds…', full venv setup, a 'Failure modes' section) with no pointer to the replacement or the fact it's retired. Worse, extract_books.py's _clean() (which shares the exact same directory/README/venv and produces tool/data/curriculum_books.json — the very file build_text_cache.dart now treats as a static committed input) only strips HTML *tags* via a bare `<[^>]+>` regex; it does not remove footnote *bodies* the way its own sibling main.py's `_FOOTNOTE` regex does, or the way the runtime's HebrewUtils.cleanSefariaText does (documented as the 'BUG-5' fix in sefaria_mongo.dart:19 and seed_content_db.dart:583-591). A contributor trusting the README who re-runs extract_books.py to add a book would regenerate curriculum_books.json/book_text_cache.json with Sefaria footnote text merged back into the main body — reintroducing exactly the corruption the rest of the codebase guards against three times over.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/tool/text_extract/README.md:3` — “Builds `tool/data/daily_content_cache.json` — a pre-resolved bilingual”; `learning_tracker/tool/text_extract/extract_books.py:119` — “s = _HTML.sub("", s)”; `learning_tracker/tool/text_extract/main.py:46` — “_FOOTNOTE = re.compile(r" ?\(…\)|<i class=\"footnote\".*?</i>", re.S)”
- **Fix:** Add a retirement banner to tool/text_extract/README.md pointing at tool/seed/build_text_cache.dart and build_daily_content.dart as the current replacement. If the directory is kept for reference/history rather than deleted, fix extract_books.py's _clean() to strip footnote bodies the same way main.py's _FOOTNOTE regex does, so it can't silently corrupt data if someone runs it anyway.
- **Done when:** tool/text_extract/README.md states the retirement and names the current replacement tools, or the directory is removed entirely · A test asserts extract_books.py's _clean() removes an `<i class="footnote">…</i>` span wholesale (matching main.py's _FOOTNOTE behavior) — red before the fix, green after, or the file is deleted
- **Labels:** dead-code, data-quality, tool, regression-risk · verifier corrections: extract_books.py:262-283 shows BOOKS_OUT/curriculum_books.json is built from raw r.normal() ref strings, never routed through _clean(); only TEXT_OUT (gitignored book_text_cache.json) uses _clean(), and build_text_cache.

#### AUD-guardrails-36 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Stop hand-copying private lint-rule path helpers into test files; assert through the real rule only
- **Rule:** TQ-4 (lens: Feathers — fake seam) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 6 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Because each rule's `_isWhitelisted`/`_isGenerated`/`_isBarrel`/`_featureOf` helper is private and static, the test authors copy-pasted a second implementation into the test file rather than exposing a testable seam (e.g. @visibleForTesting) or relying solely on the full testAnalyzeAndRun assertions the same files already have. If a rule's real whitelist changes (as F1b's recommended fix would do), the hand-copied test function has to be remembered and updated separately, or the 'whitelist — file path checks' group keeps passing while asserting stale behavior that no longer matches the shipped rule — a false sense of unit coverage on top of the genuine end-to-end tests in the same file.
- **Evidence:** `packages/custom_lints/test/no_color_literal_outside_theme_test.dart:152` — “bool _invokeIsWhitelisted(String path) {
  final normalised = path.replaceAll(r'\', '/');”; `packages/custom_lints/test/no_curriculum_display_name_bypass_test.dart:31` — “bool _invokeIsWhitelisted(String path) {
  final normalised = path.replaceAll(r'\', '/');”; `packages/custom_lints/test/no_feature_cross_import_test.dart:28` — “bool _isBarrel(String importedFeature, String importedPath) {
  return importedPath == '$importedFeature.dart';”; `packages/custom_lints/test/no_firebase_outside_core_test.dart:157` — “bool _invokeIsWhitelisted(String path) {
  final normalised = path.replaceAll(r'\', '/');”; `packages/custom_lints/test/no_hardcoded_text_direction_test.dart:201` — “bool _invokeIsGenerated(String path) {
  final normalised = path.replaceAll(r'\', '/');”; `packages/custom_lints/test/no_raw_talker_test.dart:148` — “bool _invokeIsWhitelisted(String path) {
  final normalised = path.replaceAll(r'\', '/');”
- **Fix:** Delete the six _invoke*/_isBarrel/_featureOf copies and keep only the testAnalyzeAndRun-based violation/allowed groups (already present in every file and sufficient to exercise the same whitelist logic through the real code path).
- **Done when:** No custom_lints test file re-implements a rule's private path-matching logic; whitelist behavior is asserted only via rule.testAnalyzeAndRun. · dart test coverage of whitelist behavior is unchanged or improved after removal.
- **Labels:** testing, duplication, custom-lint

#### AUD-guardrails-39 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · tool/merge_arb.py silently no-ops because all 4 hardcoded source branches (r1-tracks2 etc.) no longer exist
- **Rule:** Nygard lens: silent failure on missing input · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** `git branch -a` confirms none of the 4 branches this script reads from still exist locally or on the remote — they were the ephemeral R1 fix-wave worktree branches, presumably merged and deleted. load_branch_arb() swallows a failing `git show <branch>:<path>` into an empty dict with no warning, so running this script today prints '<path>: no new keys' for both ARBs — which reads as 'already in sync' when the real reason is 'none of the source branches exist.' A future dev who reruns this expecting it to pick up some other branches' ARB changes gets silent, misleading success.
- **Evidence:** `tool/merge_arb.py:10` — “BRANCHES = ["r1-tracks2", "r1-content2", "r1-locale", "r1-gamif2"]”; `tool/merge_arb.py:18` — “if out.returncode != 0:
        return {}”
- **Fix:** Either delete this one-off script now that its job (the R1 merge) is done (git history preserves it), or make it fail loudly when a listed branch doesn't resolve via `git rev-parse --verify <branch>` before attempting `git show`.
- **Done when:** Running the script against a nonexistent branch either exits non-zero with a clear error, or the script (and its stale branch list) is removed.
- **Labels:** dead-code, silent-failure, tooling

### firebase  (15 findings — 1 P0 / 3 P1 / 7 P2 / 4 P3)

#### AUD-firebase-01 · **P0** · CONFIRMED · Verify emailVerified (or the invite_token) before granting tutor-invite acceptance by email match
- **Rule:** SR-5 (tutor cross-user access) / child-privacy · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** Firebase Auth lets anyone register an account with any unverified email string. acceptTutorInvite, declineTutorInvite, and listTutorGrants({mode:'pending_for_me'}) all authorize 'is this caller the invited tutor' purely by comparing the caller's Auth email to grant.tutor_email -- none of them checks callerRecord.emailVerified (or the token claim), despite comments at both call sites explicitly (and incorrectly) claiming this 'prevents anyone from claiming an invite not addressed to them' / matches the 'verified' email. An attacker who front-runs registration of the invited tutor's email address can call listTutorGrants(pending_for_me) to discover the grantId, then acceptTutorInvite to gain ongoing read access (and any write permissions the parent granted) to the child's full learning profile -- without ever proving ownership of that inbox. The invite_token generated specifically to prevent exactly this (comment: 'single-use, per NFR-3') is stored on the grant doc but is never read back or compared anywhere in the file, so it provides zero actual protection. cf_grant_invite.test.mjs's own header comment confirms this exact gate is never exercised by any test.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:691` — “// This prevents anyone from claiming an invite not addressed to them.”; `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:693` — “const callerEmail = (callerRecord.email ?? "").toLowerCase().trim();”; `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:1006` — “// without needing the emailed deep link. Match the caller's verified email.”; `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:657` — “const { grantId } = request.data ?? {};”; `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:597` — “const inviteToken = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString("hex");”
- **Fix:** Require callerRecord.emailVerified === true in acceptTutorInvite/declineTutorInvite before trusting the email match, and/or require the caller to supply invite_token and compare it against grant.invite_token (the mechanism already built for this). Apply the same emailVerified gate to listTutorGrants' pending_for_me query so an unverified account cannot even discover invites addressed to an email it doesn't own.
- **Done when:** A new Auth-emulator-backed test in cf_grant_invite.test.mjs seeds an unverified-email account and asserts acceptTutorInvite rejects it (e.g. permission-denied). · acceptTutorInvite/declineTutorInvite check emailVerified or invite_token before authorizing by email match. · make test-functions (or a new CI job per the companion finding) seeds Auth-emulator users so this path is actually exercised, not skipped.
- **Labels:** security, child-privacy, cloud-functions, P0 · verifier corrections: The finding's rule citation "SR-5 (tutor cross-user access)" is imprecise: SR-5's literal text (coding-standards.md:313) governs Firestore *security rules* (state/expiry checks in firestore.rules), not Cloud Functions ca

#### AUD-firebase-02 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Guard inviteTutor against silently resetting an already-active tutor grant
- **Rule:** functions correctness · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** grantId is deterministic ({encodedEmail}__{parentUid}__{childProfileId}), so a second inviteTutor call for the same tutor+child pair overwrites the same doc unconditionally, even when the existing grant is currently 'active'. That silently resets state back to 'pending', issues a fresh invite_token/expires_at, and replaces permissions with the request-supplied defaults (which include can_bulk_prior_completion: true) -- while the already-active tutor_active_access index doc is untouched, so the tutor keeps live read access even though tutor_grants.state now says 'pending'. Neither the Cloud Function nor the Dart InviteTutorUseCase (whose own docstring claims it validates against the local grant aggregate, but whose implementation only validates email format) guards against this, so a parent re-sending an invite, or a duplicate form submission, can silently re-grant a permission the parent had explicitly turned off.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:617` — “state: "pending",”; `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:627` — “await db.collection("tutor_grants").doc(grantId).set(grantData, { merge: false });”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/tutoring/domain/use_cases/tutor_invite_use_cases.dart:10` — “//   1. Validate preconditions against the local [TutorGrant] aggregate.”
- **Fix:** Before writing, read the existing grant (if any) and reject/short-circuit re-invites while state === 'active' (direct the caller to a permission-editing flow instead), or explicitly preserve prior permissions and keep tutor_active_access consistent with the resulting state.
- **Done when:** A new cf_grant_invite.test.mjs test: inviteTutor called twice for the same tutorEmail+childProfileId while the grant is 'active' does not silently reset state/permissions.
- **Labels:** cloud-functions, correctness, P2 · verifier corrections: manage_tutors_screen.dart:284-286: the 'Invite a tutor' button is always visible per child section, with an explicit comment 'so the parent can add a tutor even when one is already active,' and the screen has no check ag

#### AUD-firebase-03 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Refresh docs/firestore-collection-layout.md to match the current firestore.rules and firestore.indexes.json
- **Rule:** AG-8 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 9 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** The doc's header claims 'Status: current -- reconciled ... 2026-05-18 (Wave 2)', but firestore.rules has since gone through W3.32-W3.43 and the V2-R3 tutor-access rework, none of which are reflected: it says the indexes file declares zero composite indexes when it declares six; it describes a 3-part rules structure (default-deny, top-level compat blocks, live nested) when the compat blocks (accounts/completion_events/track_configs/etc.) no longer exist in the file at all; it documents a `streak` snapshot singleton that was replaced by `streak_events` (W3.37); it lists notification_settings/gamification_settings/ui_preferences as three separate collections when they were unified into `preferences/{scope}` (W3.33); and it never mentions tutor_grants/tutor_active_access/audit_log -- the highest-risk, cross-user part of the whole schema -- at all. A developer or AI agent trusting this 'canonical' doc would reason from a materially wrong model of the app's Firestore security surface.
- **Evidence:** `docs/firestore-collection-layout.md:152` — “`learning_tracker/firestore.indexes.json` declares **no composite indexes**.”; `learning_tracker/firestore.indexes.json:4` — “"collectionGroup": "tutor_grants",”; `docs/firestore-collection-layout.md:115` — “2. **Top-level compatibility blocks** for `accounts`, `learner_profiles`,”; `docs/firestore-collection-layout.md:81` — “| `streak` | `data` (single doc) | Current streak snapshot | `pushStreak` |”; `learning_tracker/firestore.rules:245` — “match /streak_events/{streakEventId} {”; `docs/firestore-collection-layout.md:86` — “| `notification_settings` | `preferences` (single doc) | Notification preferences | `pushNotificationSettings` |”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/codec/firestore_codec.dart:57` — “The Firestore SDK converts ISO-8601 strings into Timestamp objects on write, so this format is safe to use in push documents.”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl.dart:164` — “in Firestore Security Rules a `string <= timestamp` comparison is `false`, which would deny EVERY completion create.” _(+1 more sites in findings.json)_
- **Fix:** Regenerate the collection tables and 'Security rules' section from the current firestore.rules/firestore.indexes.json, and add the tutor_grants/tutor_active_access/audit_log subsystem.
- **Done when:** The doc's index-count claim, collection tables, and rules-structure description all match a fresh read of firestore.rules/firestore.indexes.json. · The doc documents tutor_grants, tutor_active_access, and audit_log.
- **Labels:** docs, firestore-rules, P1 · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches

#### AUD-firebase-04 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Wire functions/test/cf_*.test.mjs and a functions build step into CI
- **Rule:** TQ-9 · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** functions/src/index.ts is 2029 lines of Admin-SDK-privileged, rules-bypassing server code -- the highest-privilege code in the repo -- yet no CI job builds, type-checks, or tests it. `make ci` runs only `analyze validate-calendar test` (Flutter side); `test-functions` (which runs the 7 cf_*.test.mjs files, 3,236 lines) and `npm --prefix functions run build` are only reachable via a developer manually typing the make target. This is distinct from the already-known 'make ci doesn't run test-rules' gap (that's the separate firestore_rules.test.mjs suite, which does have a dedicated CI job) -- functions/ has no CI path of any kind. A PR that reintroduces the P0 auth gap above, or any other Cloud Function regression, or a plain TypeScript compile error, gets a green CI check.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/functions/package.json:6` — “"scripts": {
