#### AUD-firebase-08 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Make tutor audit-log writes idempotent and failure-visible instead of best-effort auto-ID writes
- **Rule:** functions error-handling (Nygard: I/O failure/retry) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 13 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The audit log is the parent's only visibility into what an invited tutor did to their child's data (12-month retention, W3.42), but every write to it is swallowed on failure (the primary mutation still returns success:true even if its audit entry silently failed) and keyed by Firestore auto-ID rather than a deterministic key, so a client-side retry of a timed-out-but-actually-succeeded Cloud Function call produces a duplicate entry for the same real action. A parent reviewing the trail can see gaps or phantom duplicates with no way to tell which from inside the app.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:1218` — “/** Write an audit log entry for a tutor mutation (best-effort — errors are logged but not thrown). */”; `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:1243` — “} catch (e) {
    logger.warn(`writeAuditLog: failed for grant=${grantId} action=${action}`, e);”; `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:1233` — “.collection("audit_log")
      .add({”
- **Fix:** Derive a deterministic audit_log doc ID from (grantId, action, target, an idempotency key) so retries coalesce, and consider writing the audit entry in the same batch/transaction as the primary mutation so both succeed or fail together.
- **Done when:** Calling the same tutor mutation twice with the same idempotency key produces exactly one audit_log entry, proven by a new test.
- **Labels:** cloud-functions, correctness, P2

#### AUD-firebase-11 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Wrap tutorEditProfile's read-then-overwrite in a transaction to stop the lost-update race
- **Rule:** functions correctness (Nygard: concurrent I/O) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** Every other stateful mutation needing read-then-write consistency in this file (acceptTutorInvite, revokeTutorGrant, resignTutorGrant, expirePendingInvites) wraps it in db.runTransaction. tutorEditProfile instead reads the profile doc, merges edit fields in application memory, then does a full-document `set(..., {merge:false})` with no transaction. If the owner's own device (or a second tutor) writes any other field to the same learner_profiles/{profileId} doc between the get() and the set(), that write is silently overwritten by tutorEditProfile's stale full-doc replace -- a lost-update race, undermining the very H2 fix comment that motivated reading the full doc first.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:2000` — “const beforeSnap = await profilePath.get();”; `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:2008` — “const fullDoc = beforeValue ? { ...beforeValue, ...updates } : updates;”; `learning_tracker/functions/src/index.ts:2009` — “await profilePath.set(fullDoc, { merge: false });”
- **Fix:** Wrap the read+write in db.runTransaction (txn.get + txn.set), consistent with the rest of the file, or switch to `profilePath.set(updates, {merge:true})` for the scalar fields being edited -- Firestore applies a merge write atomically server-side without a client-side read first.
- **Done when:** A concurrency test (a second writer updates an unrelated profile field between tutorEditProfile's get and set) shows that field survives.
- **Labels:** cloud-functions, correctness, P2

#### AUD-docs-01 · **P0** · CONFIRMED · Add SR-1 changed-value-denied test to firestore_rules.test.mjs for completions/streak_events/learning_ledger/points_ledger
- **Rule:** SR-1 · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 8 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** Confirmed by grep: no `resource.data == request.resource.data`-style identical-replay guard exists anywhere in firestore.rules (447 lines, zero hits). Every SR-1-named collection's update branch is just `isOwner(uid)` (plus unrelated format checks on completions only) — an owner-authenticated client (a modified build, a compromised device, or a bug in the sync engine's outbox-retry logic) can silently overwrite an EXISTING completion's points, a streak event, or a ledger/points-ledger entry with any new value, and the rule accepts it as an ordinary update. firestore_rules.test.mjs is this repo's only server-side gate test for owner writes and its own header claims it 'locks the LOAD-BEARING security boundaries' — yet none of its 4 SR-1 describe blocks (completions:306, streak_events:337, learning_ledger:347, points_ledger:357) ever attempt a changed-value update and assert it fails; each only proves identical-value re-writes and tutor-writes are handled. This is exactly the risk coding-standards.md itself names for SR-1: 'a child's study record is tamperable' — and since points/streak/ledger entries feed reward_redemptions (real-world reward fulfilment), undetected mutation directly undermines the rewards economy's integrity, with zero test coverage to catch a regression today or after any future fix.
- **Evidence:** `docs/coding-standards.md:293` — “SR-1 — Append-only collections (`completions`, `streak_events`, `learning_ledger`, `points_ledger`) deny value mutation on update: allow onl”; `docs/coding-standards.md:295` — “Enforce: [Pending] deny-tests in `functions/test/firestore_rules.test.mjs`: changed-value update `assertFails`, identical replay `assertSucc”; `learning_tracker/functions/test/firestore_rules.test.mjs:337` — “describe('streak_events — owner write, tutor read, delete denied', () => {”; `learning_tracker/firestore.rules:254` — “allow create, update: if isOwner(uid);”; `learning_tracker/firestore.rules:38` — “// deny `update` and `delete`. Snapshot collections deny `delete` and gate”; `learning_tracker/firestore.rules:227` — “allow create, update: if isOwner(uid)”; `learning_tracker/firestore.rules:266` — “allow create, update: if isOwner(uid);”; `learning_tracker/firestore.rules:276` — “allow create, update: if isOwner(uid);”
- **Fix:** For each of completions/streak_events/learning_ledger/points_ledger, add a test that seeds a doc then attempts an owner update with a changed field value and asserts it fails; pair with a firestore.rules change adding `request.resource.data == resource.data` as an allowed alternative to full validation on update.
- **Done when:** firestore_rules.test.mjs adds one assertFails case per SR-1 collection where an owner updates an existing doc with a changed field value · `make test-rules` fails against today's firestore.rules and passes once firestore.rules adds an identical-replay branch for each SR-1 collection · docs/coding-standards.md SR-1 Enforce line flips from [Pending] to [Enforced] once the test lands
- **Labels:** security, child-data-integrity, SR-1, test-coverage, P0 · merged 1 duplicate report(s) · co-discovered by 2 batches

#### AUD-docs-02 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Add SR-2/SR-3/SR-4/SR-5 + TQ-9 ruleCoverage pending hardening tests to firestore_rules.test.mjs
- **Rule:** SR-2/SR-3/SR-4/SR-5/TQ-9 · **Effort:** L · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** coding-standards.md (2026-07-02) lists SR-2..SR-5 and TQ-9's ruleCoverage clause as [Pending], each with an 'Enforce' line naming the exact test pattern this file should carry. None exist. (1) SR-2: the only type/size check anywhere is `points: '50'` on completions (line 318) — no oversized-string test, no wrong-type test on any other field in any of the 12 hasOnly/open-bag collections. (2) SR-3: streak_events/learning_ledger/points_ledger accept a timestamp field of any value including far-future dates with zero test coverage — the deprecated test/firestore-rules/ suite used to test exactly this for 2 of these 3 collections before the schema migration; that coverage was lost, not carried forward. (3) SR-4: the file's own Firestore import list (line 33-40) never imports `getDocs`/`query` — it is structurally impossible for any test here to issue a list/collection query, so an owner or active tutor enumerating a child's entire event history in one unbounded query is completely untested. (4) SR-5: beforeEach (line 106-122) always seeds an 'active' tutor_grants/tutor_active_access pair; no test seeds a revoked or expired grant to prove tutor access is actually cut off, so a bug in the Cloud Function that deletes tutor_active_access on revoke would go undetected. (5) TQ-9: the emulator's own `ruleCoverage` report (flags rule expressions never evaluated by any test) is never fetched or asserted anywhere in the repo (zero grep hits for 'ruleCoverage'), so dead/unreachable branches in the 447-line rules file can accumulate silently.
- **Evidence:** `docs/coding-standards.md:298` — “SR-2 — Validate value types and cap string sizes in rules (`is timestamp`, `is number`, `s.size() <= N`), not just key sets via `hasOnly()`.”; `docs/coding-standards.md:303` — “SR-3 — Every event create requires a server-bounded timestamp: present, `is timestamp`, and `<= request.time`.”; `docs/coding-standards.md:308` — “SR-4 — Cap `list` queries on per-profile event collections: `allow list: if <cond> && request.query.limit <= 500`.”; `docs/coding-standards.md:313` — “SR-5 — Tutor cross-user access checks state and expiry in the rule itself (`state == 'active' && expires_at > request.time`...).”; `learning_tracker/functions/test/firestore_rules.test.mjs:36` — “setDoc,”
- **Fix:** Track as a backlog against SR-2..SR-5 + TQ-9: each lands its named assertFails/assertSucceeds pattern in firestore_rules.test.mjs; SR-4/SR-5 additionally need firestore.rules changes (an allow-list split with a limit cap, and a state/expires_at field) since nothing in the current rule is testable yet; TQ-9's ruleCoverage check is a Makefile/ci.yml addition that curls the emulator's coverage endpoint after the suite runs.
- **Done when:** SR-2: a test asserts a large string and a wrong-typed field are denied on at least one hasOnly-guarded and one open-bag collection · SR-3: streak_events, learning_ledger and points_ledger each gain a future-timestamp assertFails test mirroring completions' · SR-4: a test issues `limit(500)` (succeeds) and `limit(1000)`/unbounded (fails) against one event collection after firestore.rules adds an allow-list cap · SR-5: a test seeds a revoked/expired tutor_active_access scenario and asserts tutor read is denied · TQ-9: CI fetches the emulator's ruleCoverage report and fails the job on any never-evaluated rule expression
- **Labels:** security, test-coverage, SR-2, SR-3, SR-4, SR-5, TQ-9, P2 · verifier corrections: Bundles 5 distinct rule IDs (SR-2..SR-5, TQ-9) into one finding tagged 'sites: 5' — digest's consolidation rule (#4) is meant for the same defect repeated at N sites, not N different rules glued together. #### AUD-docs-08 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Fix docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md's LWW tie-break rule — it contradicts the implemented and tested behavior
- **Rule:** AG-8 (doc/code parity); FB-2/FB-3 (LWW ordering, clock-skew handling) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The canonical doc says ties are dropped in favor of local (strict `remoteTimestamp > localTimestamp`) and never mentions a clock-skew window. The actual implementation and its exhaustive, intentional test coverage do the opposite for the common case: outside a ±5s skew window ties do stay local, but *inside* the window — the realistic case for near-simultaneous writes from a user's own two devices — an exact tie goes to REMOTE (code comment: 'prefer remote... converge instead of bouncing'), and a `synced_at` server-timestamp tie-break exists that the doc never describes at all. An engineer implementing a new merger or debugging a 'my edit got overwritten' report will read the doc, get the tie-break backwards for the realistic case, and either mis-implement a new merger or chase a phantom bug.
- **Evidence:** `docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md:30` — “> strictly newer timestamp wins. If both timestamps are equal the remote row
> is silently dropped (the LWW rule is `remoteTimestamp > local”; `learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/drift_merge_store.dart:148` — “// The one true tie (equal `updated_at`, no decisive server timestamp) is
    // resolved by preferring remote so two devices that wrote the”; `learning_tracker/test/sync/merge/lww_symmetric_test.dart:1228` — “test('exactly identical timestamps, no synced_at → remote wins', () {”
- **Fix:** Rewrite the 'Push/pull invariant' section to describe the actual 3-tier rule in DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer: (1) outside ±5s skew, strict remote>local wins and ties stay local; (2) inside ±5s skew with both sides carrying synced_at, the server timestamp decides; (3) inside the window with no decisive synced_at, remote wins to force convergence. Point the doc at drift_merge_store.dart:113-152 so future changes are easy to diff against it.
- **Done when:** docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md's tie-break wording matches lib/core/sync/merge/drift_merge_store.dart:113-152 exactly, confirmed by re-reading both side by side · the doc states the ±5s clock-skew window and the synced_at tie-break, matching DriftMergeStore.clockSkewTieBreakWindow
- **Labels:** docs, sync, lww, correctness-adjacent

#### AUD-docs-22 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Update or disclaim docs/scenarios/stitch-prompts/{03-mode-selection,04-curriculum-selection,06-dashboard}.md — describe a product IA the shipped app doesn't have
- **Rule:** Tier-4 triage AREA NOTE — presents-as-current classification; egregious contradiction with reality · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 3 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** These prompts are literal AI-image-generation inputs for the WDS/Stitch design workflow (docs/index.md calls the folder 'AI-generated UI design prompts'; see the bmad-wds-stitch-generation skill) — their whole purpose is to be re-run to produce mockups. Unlike every file in the dashboard-redesign-set and evolution-set, none of the 7 stitch-prompts carry any staleness/inspiration-only disclaimer, so re-running them today would generate polished mockups for the wrong information architecture.

- **Fix:** Update 03-mode-selection.md, 04-curriculum-selection.md, and 06-dashboard.md to match the current onboarding (child/adult mode), the full 9-curriculum roster, and the real 4-tab nav — or add a one-line 'early concept, not current IA' disclaimer to the whole stitch-prompts set the way dashboard-redesign-set and evolution/ already do.

### platform  (6 findings — 0 P0 / 1 P1 / 0 P2 / 5 P3)

#### AUD-platform-01 · **P1** · CONFIRMED · Fix unverifiable Android App Link intent-filters for sign-in/invite deep links (AndroidManifest.xml)
- **Rule:** Tier-2 correctness (no numbered rule ID; auth/deep-link infra consistency) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [3x3]
- **Why:** Live verification (2026-07-03): https://torah-study-tracker.firebaseapp.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json returns HTTP 404, the domain root '/' returns HTTP 404, and '/sign-in' returns HTTP 404 — only Firebase's built-in /__/auth/action handler responds. Neither firebase.json (root or learning_tracker/) declares a "hosting" block, so nothing can ever serve assetlinks.json or these custom paths as currently configured. Android only honors autoVerify="true" intent-filters after validating that file, so it never marks the app as the verified handler for /sign-in or /invite. A parent tapping 'finish sign-in' in their email, or a tutor tapping an invite link (PP-7 wave-B, AndroidManifest.xml:57), gets sent to the system browser instead of the app — which then also 404s, since no Hosting deployment serves those paths either. Both flows dead-end on an error page.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:48` — “<intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">”; `learning_tracker/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:54` — “android:host="torah-study-tracker.firebaseapp.com"”; `learning_tracker/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:64` — “android:host="torah-study-tracker.firebaseapp.com"”; `firebase.json:1` — “{ "firestore": { "rules": "firestore.rules", ... } }”; `learning_tracker/firebase.json:1` — “{ "functions": { "source": "functions", "runtime": "nodejs22" },”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/account/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:86` — “continueUrl: '$_linkDomain/sign-in',”
- **Fix:** Either deploy Firebase Hosting with a committed .well-known/assetlinks.json (declaring package name + release SHA-256 cert fingerprint) and add the "hosting" block to firebase.json in the same change, or drop the autoVerify/pathPrefix App Links approach for a mechanism that doesn't need host-level verification. Add a deploy/CI smoke check that curls the assetlinks URL and fails the pipeline on non-200.

#### AUD-platform-02 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Drop dead UIBackgroundModes (fetch, remote-notification) from ios/Runner/Info.plist — no backing implementation exists
- **Rule:** Tier-2 config correctness / dead-target directive (no numbered coding-standards.md rule; general dead-code + AG posture) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** Info.plist declares both `fetch` and `remote-notification` background modes, but AppDelegate.swift (6-18) implements no `application(_:performFetchWithCompletionHandler:)` or `application(_:didReceiveRemoteNotification:fetchCompletionHandler:)` override and never calls `registerForRemoteNotifications()`; pubspec.yaml has no `firebase_messaging` dependency; every reminder in NotificationGateway is scheduled locally via `zonedSchedule`. The keys were added wholesale in the initial iOS scaffold (b9d3a8b0) and never exercised. Concrete cost: Apple App Review Guideline 2.5.4 explicitly targets apps that declare background modes without a corresponding implementation (submission friction/rejection risk), and the stale declaration will mislead whoever next builds real push notifications into thinking server-side delivery already exists.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/ios/Runner/Info.plist:56` — “<string>fetch</string>
						<string>remote-notification</string>”; `learning_tracker/ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift:7` — “_ application: UIApplication,
    didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions:”; `learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/domain/services/notification_gateway.dart:184` — “await _plugin.zonedSchedule(”
- **Fix:** Remove the `UIBackgroundModes` key (and its two entries) from Info.plist since notification delivery is 100% local today. If server push is genuinely planned, land the capability declaration in the same change as the `firebase_messaging` dependency, the AppDelegate handler(s), and `registerForRemoteNotifications()` — not ahead of the implementation.
- **Done when:** Info.plist has no UIBackgroundModes key, or each remaining mode has a matching handler in AppDelegate.swift referenced by a Linear ticket. · grep -A2 'UIBackgroundModes' learning_tracker/ios/Runner/Info.plist returns nothing (or only modes with matching AppDelegate.swift handlers) — usable as a Rule-0 grep checker.
- **Labels:** ios, config, dead-code, tier2, AG · verifier corrections: Lowered P2->P3: the stated 'concrete cost' (App Review rejection) is unlikely in practice for fetch+remote-notification specifically; only the maintenance/misleading-signal cost is solidly concrete, which fits P3 hygiene

#### AUD-platform-03 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Fail fast on missing key.properties instead of silently debug-signing release Android builds (build.gradle.kts)
- **Rule:** Tier-2 area note (security) — AG-11-adjacent CI guardrail soft-skip · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1] · filed P2, revised
- **Why:** When KEYSTORE_BASE64 is unset (misconfigured secret, or a maintainer manually dispatches the 'Build APK' workflow with build_type=release before secrets are wired up), build.yml prints a warning but does not fail — it proceeds to 'flutter build apk --release'. Because key.properties was never written, Gradle's fallback here silently signs the 'release' APK with the shared, publicly-known Flutter debug keystore, then uploads it as a GitHub Actions artifact literally named learning-tracker-release-apk. Anyone who installs that artifact believing it's a genuine release build gets a debug-signed binary; since the debug key is identical across virtually all Flutter/Android-Studio installs, another developer's debug-signed build could later 'update' over it without Android's signature check objecting.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/android/app/build.gradle.kts:54` — “signingConfig = if (keystorePropertiesFile.exists()) {”; `learning_tracker/android/app/build.gradle.kts:57` — “signingConfigs.getByName("debug")”; `.github/workflows/build.yml:87` — “echo "Warning: KEYSTORE_BASE64 secret not set."”; `.github/workflows/build.yml:106` — “run: flutter build apk --release”
- **Fix:** Make the release signingConfig fail fast (e.g. error("release build requested but key.properties is missing")) instead of silently substituting debug signing, or at minimum have build.yml's keystore-decode step exit 1 when build_type == 'release' and the secret is empty instead of only warning.
- **Done when:** flutter build apk --release (or ./gradlew assembleRelease) fails loudly when key.properties/keystore secret is absent, instead of producing a debug-signed 'release' artifact. · build.yml's release job aborts (non-zero exit) when KEYSTORE_BASE64 is empty and build_type=release.
- **Labels:** android, signing, ci, security · verifier corrections: docs/deployment-guide.md:25 documents the debug-signing fallback as intentional design ('falls back to debug signing if absent'), undercutting the 'silently' framing and the primary fail-hard-Gradle recommendation, which

#### AUD-platform-04 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Fix invalid ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GENERATE_SWIFT_ASSET_SYMBOL_EXTENSIONS value in Debug/Release Xcode configs (project.pbxproj)
- **Rule:** Tier-2 area note (drift between duplicated configs) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** This is a Boolean Xcode build setting; 'AppIcon' is not a valid YES/NO value — it reads as a copy-paste bleed from the neighboring ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME = AppIcon setting a few lines away. Debug and Release (the two configurations used for every local dev run and every shipped build) diverge from Profile, which has the correct YES. Currently inert since nothing in this small app consumes generated Swift asset symbols, but it produces an Xcode build warning today and will silently break (compiles only in Profile) the moment someone adds Swift code that references a generated asset symbol.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:314` — “ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GENERATE_SWIFT_ASSET_SYMBOL_EXTENSIONS = YES;”; `learning_tracker/ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:434` — “ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GENERATE_SWIFT_ASSET_SYMBOL_EXTENSIONS = AppIcon;”; `learning_tracker/ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:491` — “ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GENERATE_SWIFT_ASSET_SYMBOL_EXTENSIONS = AppIcon;”
- **Fix:** Set ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GENERATE_SWIFT_ASSET_SYMBOL_EXTENSIONS to the same valid YES/NO value across Debug, Release, and Profile.
- **Done when:** All three XCBuildConfiguration blocks for ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GENERATE_SWIFT_ASSET_SYMBOL_EXTENSIONS use the same valid YES/NO value. · xcodebuild -showBuildSettings (or an xcodeproj lint script) shows no divergence between Debug/Release/Profile for this key.
- **Labels:** ios, xcode, config-drift

#### AUD-platform-05 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Pin distributionSha256Sum in android/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties
- **Rule:** Tier-2 area note (security/supply-chain) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 1 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** The wrapper properties file has no distributionSha256Sum key. Without it, gradlew's bootstrap download of the Gradle distribution has no integrity check beyond TLS — a compromised mirror/CDN or a MITM on a misconfigured proxy could substitute a malicious Gradle distribution that every subsequent local build and CI run would silently execute.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/android/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties:5` — “distributionUrl=https\://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-8.14-all.zip”
- **Fix:** Run `./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version 8.14 --distribution-type all` (or add distributionSha256Sum manually from Gradle's published checksums page) so the wrapper verifies the download and fails closed on mismatch.
- **Done when:** gradle-wrapper.properties contains a distributionSha256Sum line matching the official checksum for gradle-8.14-all.zip. · A deliberately-wrong checksum causes ./gradlew to fail the download instead of proceeding.
- **Labels:** android, gradle, supply-chain

#### AUD-l10n-01 · **P2** · CONFIRMED · Deduplicate 5 shadowed top-level keys in app_he.arb/app_en.arb — one silently kills a zero-task notification branch
- **Rule:** Rule 0 gap (no duplicate-key checker for ARB files) · **Effort:** M · **Sites:** 5 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** JSON's last-key-wins behavior is confirmed against the generated Dart output: lib/l10n/app_localizations_he.dart's todaysLearning(count), errorLoadingTasks(error) and notificationReminderBody(taskCount, curriculumCount) all match the SECOND (later) ARB definition, not the first. No checker anywhere (make audit, arb-parity, flutter analyze) catches a duplicate top-level key within a single ARB file, so 3 of the 5 duplicate pairs carry genuinely different text: an editor who fixes the first (now-dead) copy of todaysLearning or errorLoadingTasks has the fix silently discarded. Worse, notificationReminderBody's line-1765 definition had a deliberately-written zero-task branch (he: 'אין משימות להיום — שמרו על הרצף!' / en: 'No tasks today — stay on track!'); a later duplicate insertion at line 2636/2834 (identical pattern in app_en.arb) replaced it with a two-way plural that has no zero case at all. It is not live-broken today only because the sole caller, lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart:517, has an unrelated 'D2 fix' guard (`if (taskCount == 0) { cancel; return; }`) that happens to prevent taskCount=0 from ever reaching the l10n call — if that guard is ever removed or a second caller is added, Intl.pluralLogic falls to `other` and produces 'You have 0 tasks…' instead of the friendly copy that still sits, unused, in the file. The identical 5-key duplicate set exists in app_en.arb too, confirming this is a systemic missing-checker gap, not a one-off typo.
- **Evidence:** `learning_tracker/lib/l10n/app_he.arb:15` — “"todaysLearning": "הלימוד של היום",”; `learning_tracker/lib/l10n/app_he.arb:1154` — “"todaysLearning": "לימוד היום ({count})",”; `learning_tracker/lib/l10n/app_he.arb:320` — “"errorLoadingTasks": "שגיאה בטעינת המשימות: {error}",”; `learning_tracker/lib/l10n/app_he.arb:1765` — “"notificationReminderBody": "{taskCount,plural, =0{אין משימות להיום — שמרו על הרצף!} …}",”; `learning_tracker/lib/l10n/app_he.arb:2636` — “"notificationReminderBody": "יש לכם {taskCount, plural, =1{…} other{…}} …",”; `learning_tracker/lib/l10n/app_he.arb:356` — “"today": "היום",”
- **Fix:** Add a Rule-0 checker (tool/ script or a test/l10n/ test) that fails when any top-level key string appears more than once in app_en.arb or app_he.arb, wired into make audit/ci. Then resolve the 5 duplicates: keep todaysLearning's parameterized form (matches its @todaysLearning metadata), keep errorLoadingTasks's live copy or fix the grammar deliberately, and decide whether notificationReminderBody's zero-task branch should be restored (and its caller's guard removed) or the dead ARB text deleted — don't leave orphaned content either way.
- **Done when:** A new checker/test fails when a top-level ARB key is duplicated, and is part of make audit or make ci. · app_en.arb and app_he.arb each contain todaysLearning, errorLoadingTasks, today, notificationReminderTitle, and notificationReminderBody exactly once. · notificationReminderBody's zero-task branch is either wired to a real caller or its vestigial ARB text is removed — no orphaned/unused ICU branch remains.
- **Labels:** l10n, arb, data-integrity

#### AUD-repo-05 · **P3** · CONFIRMED · Remove the inert .gitattributes merge=beads directive for a gitignored path
- **Rule:** AG-1 (dead guardrail config) · **Effort:** S · **Sites:** 2 · **Verified:** [1x1]
- **Why:** `.beads/` is git-ignored at the repo root, and `git ls-files | grep beads` confirms `.beads/issues.jsonl` has never been tracked. A `merge=` custom-merge-driver attribute only ever activates during a git merge of a tracked file, so this line can never fire. Even setting that aside, no `merge.beads.driver` command is registered anywhere in the repo (no hooks/, tool/, or doc sets it via `git config`) — so even a force-added copy of the file would hit 'unable to find custom merge driver beads' rather than actually merging. This is dead scaffolding for a workflow (the beads issue tracker) that isn't wired into this repo.
- **Evidence:** `.gitattributes:3` — “.beads/issues.jsonl merge=beads”; `.gitignore:5` — “.beads/”
- **Fix:** Either delete the .gitattributes line (if beads isn't used here), or un-ignore .beads/issues.jsonl and add a committed setup step that registers `git config merge.beads.driver`.
- **Done when:** Either .gitattributes no longer references a driver that's never registered, or the driver is registered by a committed script and the target path is tracked.
- **Labels:** hygiene, dead-config, git · verifier corrections: '.beads/issues.jsonl has never been tracked' is false: commit 34643e55 added it and commit 8aa6c1dd ('chore: Remove beads in favor of gastown') deliberately removed it. It's leftover scaffolding from a deprecated tool sw

## 4. Roadmap — sequenced by risk retired per unit effort

Waves are ordered so each one makes the next cheaper to verify. Tidy-first waves (0, 4) change no behavior; behavioral waves (1–3) ride on the guardrails wave 0 restores. Every item cites register IDs; the ticket pass should lift them 1:1.

### Wave 0 — Repair the enforcement machinery (do first; small, high leverage)
The fence gets its wire back. Nothing else in this roadmap can be trusted "done" until the checkers that prove it run again.
- Repair custom_lint toolchain (analyzer-9 compat) and make CI run it hard-fail — AUD-guardrails-03.
- Fix the dead check-15 awk; align Rule 2's barrel convention doc↔code — AUD-guardrails-02, AUD-learning-* (barrel reconcile).
- Add `Goals` to `tool/schema_check.dart`; wire `packages/custom_lints/test/` into CI; add the AG-7 codegen freshness gate; commit the 3 stale `.g.dart` — AUD-guardrails-01, AUD-guardrails-17, AUD-core-labels-03.
- Kill the dead error-handler twin; one canonical bootstrap installation path — AUD-core-logging-01.
- Repo hygiene sweep: root `coding-standards.md`, `build/`, `clear`, `_bmad-output/` — AUD-docs-04, AUD-repo-*.

### Wave 1 — Data integrity & privacy (the P0 band; behavioral, test-first)
Every fix lands with its red-first regression test (TQ-8) and, where checkable, its Rule-0 checker.
- profileId scoping: `LearningOrderDao` scoping, FK+CASCADE on the 6 tables, `UNIQUE(profileId, ulid)` on points tables, export/import scoped deletes — AUD-core-database-02, AUD-core-database-01, AUD-core-database-03, AUD-settings-03.
- Privacy: constrain `logEvent` to the `AnalyticsEvent` catalog; strip `entity_key` from dead-letter events; redact email bodies — AUD-core-analytics-01, AUD-core-sync-* (dead-letter), AUD-core-email-01.
- Tutor trust chain: verify `emailVerified`/invite token in `inviteTutor`; check `TutorGrantResult` before reporting success; surface swallowed tutor-write failures — AUD-firebase-01, AUD-tutoring-*, AUD-profiles-02.
- The archive-wipes-data flow and its test — AUD-profiles-01.
- Offline-account lifecycle: outbox-drain guard before `removeCloudFromDevice`; the AU-family supplemental set — AUD-account-01, AUD-account-*.
- Firestore rules: SR-1 append-only deny-tests, SR-2 value validation, SR-4 list caps — AUD-docs-01 (rules-tests), AUD-firebase-*.

### Wave 2 — Sync correctness under failure (behavioral)
- Server timestamps for LWW ordering; `hasPendingWrites`/`isFromCache` echo guards — AUD-core-sync-13, AUD-core-sync-* (FB-3).
- Outbox resilience: per-row decode isolation, single-flight generation token, atomic merge-store upsert+timestamp — AUD-core-sync-* (outbox/merge cluster).
- Fix `deleteUserData`'s wrong Firestore paths; codec safety (`as int?` casts, ISO-string dates) — AUD-core-sync-* (gateway/codec).
- Error-as-values at the boundary: stable codes on `SyncStatus.error`/`RestoreStatus.error`; stop surfacing `e.toString()` (BulkMark, restore, sacred_time, tracks hub) — AUD-sync-*, AUD-app-*, AUD-onboarding-*.

### Wave 3 — i18n & state-management debt (mechanical, high count)
- The 21 AX-2 localization clusters (onboarding, content_browsing, settings, tracks wizard, core widgets, scheduler picker…) — AUD-*-AX-2 set; land the AX-2 string-literal lint with the sweep.
- SM-4 `ref.mounted` guards (14 clusters) and SM-2 build-side-effect providers (7) — AUD-notifications-*, AUD-gamification-*, AUD-account-*, AUD-dashboard-*; land the SM-4 custom lint with it.
- DB-2 transaction wraps (7) and DB-3 batch conversions (4) — AUD-core-database-*, AUD-learning-*, AUD-onboarding-*.

### Wave 4 — Test-suite hardening & structure (tidy-first)
- TQ-8 register: rewrite tautological/stale-copy/dead-code-pinning tests (102 findings, start with the ones guarding Wave-1 fixes) — AUD-t-* set.
- TQ-6: clock injection + the 377-site wall-clock backlog as a ratchet; kill real sleeps/network in tests — AUD-t-*, meta TQ-6.
- AG-3 (327 files) and AG-5 (537 unmirrored) as warn→fail ratchets; AG-4 renames (7 dup names + provider dup) — meta-recommendations, AUD-tutoring-* (dup provider).
- Docs refresh wave: architecture graph + schema/version claims, firestore-collection-layout, AG-8 pairing checker — AUD-docs-15, AUD-docs-*, meta AG-8.

### Defer (file, don't schedule)
PF polish beyond the lazy-list P1s, theme-token `Colors.*` statics (extend the lint first or document statics-allowed), naming-convention drift, `_codec.dart` suffix documentation, remaining P3 hygiene. They're in the register with IDs; they should ride along with area work, not lead it.

### B. Coverage & method statistics

- Manifest: 4,431 git-tracked files → Tier 1: 1,640 · Tier 2: 184 · Tier 3 (generated): 80 · Tier 4 (docs): 239 · Excluded: 2,288. Every file has a ledger row (`_LEDGER.md`); **zero UNAUDITED**.
- Per-file verdicts (audited tiers): 783 SOUND · 957 ISSUES · 157 DEFECTIVE · 166 POINT-IN-TIME.
- Find phase: 120 batch finders + 5 critic-triggered supplemental finders (Sonnet), full-file reads, ~556k lines audited. 1,008 raw findings incl. 7 orchestrator-seeded.
- Verification: every finding adversarially verified. P0/P1: 3 skeptics each (evidence-fidelity / behavior / novelty-severity lenses), majority to survive, 116 findings × 3 votes. P2/P3: grouped single skeptic (174 chunks) **plus** a 150-finding second-opinion sweep: 147/150 re-upheld (98% inter-verifier agreement); 33 severities revised downward/upward by verifiers; 19 killed overall (~2%).
- Calibration note (Part G expects 20–40% kills): the raw stream was pre-filtered by a strict novelty filter, a clean `flutter analyze` baseline, and schema-forced evidence — the 98% second-opinion agreement and a manual chair re-read of all 10 P0s support finder precision over verifier leniency. Disclosed rather than tuned.
- Completeness critic: independently reconciled all 2,368 non-audited tracked files to legitimate exclusion reasons; flagged 5 under-covered rule families → supplemental round (25 additional verified findings, incl. 1 P0 + 3 P1).
- Quota resilience: two mid-run quota outages; all completed work harvested from workflow journals, zero loss, ~1,140 agents total.
